printed: {printed:?}\\nparsed:\\n{report}\");\n    }\n\n    /// 🧊️ Cold twin of [`assert_op_text_binary_equivalence`]; `retire` takes exact ownership of\n    /// every operation this helper decodes (one from the text lane, one from the binary lane).\n    pub fn assert_op_text_binary_equivalence_cold<Op>(operation: &Op, mut retire: impl FnMut(Op))\n    where\n        Op: OpText + OpBinary + PartialEq + std::fmt::Debug,\n    {\n        assert_op_line_round_trip_cold(operation, &mut retire);\n        let encoded = operation.encode_op().unwrap_or_else(|error| panic!(\"op encode failed: {error}\"));\n        let encoded_again = operation.encode_op().unwrap_or_else(|error| panic!(\"op re-encode failed: {error}\"));\n        assert_eq!(encoded, encoded_again, \"op binary encoding is not deterministic\");\n        let decoded = Op::decode_op(&encoded).unwrap_or_else(|error| panic!(\"op decode failed: {error}\"));\n        let matches = decoded == *operation;\n        let report = matches.then(String::new).unwrap_or_else(|| format!(\"{decoded:?}\"));\n        retire(decoded);\n        assert!(matches, \"op-binary round trip diverged from source operation\\ndecoded:\\n{report}\");\n    }\n\n    /// ⚖️ Asserts op text and op binary are two encodings of the SAME operation:\n    /// `decode_op(encode_op(op)) == parse_op(print_op(op)) == op`, and the binary encoding is\n    /// deterministic. The compile-time validation ground truth for\n    /// `ArtifactCommand`'s text/binary pair — the command-level mirror of\n    /// `assert_op_text_binary_equivalence`.\n    pub async fn assert_command_text_binary_equivalence<P, Op>(command: &ArtifactCommand<Op>)\n    where\n        Op: OpText + OpBinary + self::Mutation<P> + PartialEq + std::fmt::Debug,\n    {\n        let printed = print_command(command).await.unwrap_or_else(|error| panic!(\"command print failed: {error}\"));\n        let parsed: ArtifactCommand<Op> = parse_command::<P, Op>(&printed).await.unwrap_or_else(|error| panic!(\"command parse failed: {error}\"));\n        assert_eq!(&parsed, command, \"command text round trip diverged; printed:\\n{printed}\");\n        let encoded = command.encode_command().unwrap_or_else(|error| panic!(\"command encode failed: {error}\"));\n        let encoded_again = command.encode_command().unwrap_or_else(|error| panic!(\"command re-encode failed: {error}\"));\n        assert_eq!(encoded, encoded_again, \"command binary encoding is not deterministic\");\n        let decoded: ArtifactCommand<Op> = ArtifactCommand::<Op>::decode_command::<P>(&encoded).unwrap_or_else(|error| panic!(\"command decode failed: {error}\"));\n        assert_eq!(&decoded, command, \"command binary round trip diverged from source command\");\n    }\n\n    /// 📄️ Asserts that printing a store's envelope to text and parsing it back keeps its whole shared log — every edit\n    /// and every history transition — and hydrates to the canonical trunk tip (the `.ops` text is the shared log and\n    /// carries no viewer head, ticket 26/10/01 PER-VIEWER-ALTERNATIVE-HEAD); a store on the trunk tip gets back exactly the\n    /// envelope and live snapshot it holds. snapshot\");\n        }\n        retire_parsed_document(parsed);\n    }\n\n    /// 🧹️ Bounded retirement for a parse-produced document that belongs to no store.\n    /// Every terminal shell below struct RoundTripValueRetirement<T>(Option<T>);\n\n    impl<T: Send> ErasedSnapshotRetirement for RoundTripValueRetirement<T> {\n        fn close_step(&mut self, maximum_items: usize, _maximum_bytes: usize) -> Result<SnapshotRetirementStep, semio_framework_value::ValueError> {\n            if maximum_items == 0 {\n                return Ok(SnapshotRetirementStep::Pending { released_items: 0, released_bytes: 0 });\n            }\n            if self.0.take().is_some() {\n                return Ok(SnapshotRetirementStep::Pending { released_items: 1, released_bytes: 0 });\n            }\n ErasedSnapshotRetirement> {\n            Box::new(RoundTripValueRetirement(Some(value)))\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// 🗄️ Asserts a full pack-based document round trip: mirrors\n    /// storage formats must never diverge on the same store.\n    pub async fn assert_document_pack_round_trip<P, Mutation>(store: &ArtifactStore<P, Mutation>)\n    where\n        P: Clone + ArtifactDsl + assert_eq!(parsed_pack.snapshot, live, \"document-pack round trip diverged from store snapshot\");\n\n        let text_files = print_document_text(store.envelope()).await.expect(\"print document text\");\n        let parsed_text: ParsedDocumentText<P, Mutation> = parse_document_text(&text_files.dsl, &text_files.ops).await.unwrap_or_else(|error| panic!(\"parse document text failed: {error}\"));\n        assert_eq!(parsed_pack.snapshot, parsed_text.snapshot, \"document-pack path diverged from document-text path\");\n        retire_parsed_document(parsed_pack);\n        retire_parsed_document(parsed_text);\n    }\n\n    /// ✉️ Asserts that converting an `Edit<Mutation>` into `crate::os_spr::MutationEnvelope`s\n    /// (`protocol_causal`'s canonical wire/causal into an\n    /// `Edit` (unlike `encode_pack`/`decode_pack`, there is no `envelope_to_edit` inverse — vcs's OWN\n    /// `edit_from_operation_envelope` recovers a *whole edit* from vcs's own, self::Mutation<P> + PartialEq + std::fmt::Debug + OpBinary,\n    {\n        let envelopes = crate::os_spr::mutation_envelope_from_edit::<P, Mutation>(edit, document_id, schema).unwrap_or_else(|error| panic!(\"mutation_envelope_from_edit must succeed for a well-formed edit: {error}\"));\n        assert_eq!(envelopes.len(), edit.forwards.len(), \"one envelope must be produced per forward operation\");\n        for (index, envelope) in envelopes.iter().enumerate() {\n            assert_eq!(envelope.document_id, *document_id, \"document id did not survive the envelope conversion\");\n \"explicit operation id did not survive the envelope conversion\");\n                }\n                assert_eq!(envelope.dependencies, meta.dependencies, \"explicit dependencies did not survive the envelope conversion\");\n                if let Some(author_id) = &meta.author_id {\n                    assert_eq!(&envelope.actor, author_id, \"explicit author id did not survive the envelope conversion\");\n                }\n                assert_eq!(envelope.timestamp, meta.timestamp, \"explicit timestamp did not survive the envelope conversion\");\n            }\n            let Some(backward) => {\n                    let recovered_backward = Mutation::decode_op(&envelope.inverse.payload).unwrap_or_else(|error| panic!(\"envelope inverse payload must decode back into an equal operation: {error}\"));\n                    assert_eq!(&recovered_backward, backward, \"envelope inverse payload did not decode back into an equal backward operation\");\n                }\n Hand-written rather than derived because the private fields\n/// are `ManuallyDrop` (the staged group root must be adopted or retired before `Drop`), which no\n/// derive can see through.\n#[cfg(test)]\nimpl Serialize for ArtifactCursor {\n    fn serialize<S: serde::Serializer>(&self, serializer: S) -> Result<S::Ok, S::Error> {\n        Serialize::serialize(&**self, serializer)\n    }\n}\n\n/// 🌉️ Mirror of the `Serialize` twin directly above — also test-only.\n#[cfg(test)]\nimpl<'de> Deserialize<'de> for ArtifactCursor {\n    fn deserialize<D: serde::Deserializer<'de>>(deserializer: D) -> Result<Self, D::Error> {\n        ArtifactCursorOwners::deserialize(deserializer).map(Self::from_owners)\n    }\n}\n\nimpl Drop for ArtifactCursor {\n    fn drop(&mut self) {\n        assert!(std::thread::panicking() || (self.group.is_none()), \"artifact cursor reached Drop before its exact staged root was adopted or returned for retirement\");\n        unsafe { std::mem::ManuallyDrop::drop(&mut self.owners) };\n    }\n}\n\n//#region 🔖️HistoryLane\n/// 🛤️ Which undo/redo cursor a recorded edit belongs to. `Document` is the default — the\n/// ordinary main history `Undo`/`Redo` travels. See ticket\n/// `26/08/14/FIRST-CLASS-HOVER-AND-SELECTION-MECHANISM/📋️master.md` decision 1.\n#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq, ToValue, FromValue)]\n#[value(rename_all = \"camelCase\")]\npub enum HistoryLane {\n    #[default]\n    Document,\n    Interaction,\n}\n\nimpl HistoryLane {\n    async fn is_document(&self) -> bool {\n        matches!(self, HistoryLane::Document)\n    }\n}\n//#endregion 🔖️HistoryLane\n\n#[derive(Debug, PartialEq)]\npub struct ArtifactEnvelopeOwners<P, Mutation> {\n    pub schema: String,\n    pub id: String,\n    pub vcs: ArtifactVcs<P, Mutation>,\n    pub backbone: Option<ArtifactBackboneRef>,\n    pub active_alternative_id: Option<String>,\n    /// 🎯️ Undo/redo/checkout position, present only once a store has synced it (see\n    /// `ArtifactStore::sync_cursor`) — absent for a freshly-constructed envelope or one loaded\n    /// from a source that predates this field, in which case position stays runtime-only exactly\n    /// as before.\n    pub cursor: Option<ArtifactCursor>,\n    /// 🗣️ The dialect this envelope's `vcs.initial_snapshot` (and every replayed edit) is\n    /// currently in — absent for envelopes minted before dialect-tracking existed, or for document\n    /// kinds that never adopted more than one dialect. See `26/08/10` D4 evolution slice; nothing\n    /// in `ArtifactStore::dispatch` reads or writes this yet (that wiring is later scope) — it is\n    /// purely a persisted fact a future migration-aware caller can act on.\n    pub dialect: Option<crate::os_io::ArtifactDialect>,\n    /// 🧬️ Set once, the first time this envelope's snapshot was produced by migrating a\n    /// prior document's dialect (see `migrate_document` below) rather than being authored directly\n    /// in `dialect`. Placed on\n    /// the CHILD's own envelope (not only on the parent's `ArtifactChild` handle) so ownership is\n    /// queryable directly from the child side — e.g. \"is this document embeddable standalone, or\n    /// does deleting it require going through its owner\". Absent for every independent artifact\n    /// (the overwhelming majority) and for every envelope minted before this ticket.\n    pub owner: Option<OwnerRef>,\n    /// 🛤️ Sparse `Edit.id → HistoryLane` ledger: only entries recorded under a NON-`Document`\n    /// lane are ever inserted (an ordinary document edit never gets a map entry at all), so an id\n    /// absent from this map is `HistoryLane::Document` by construction — see\n    /// `ArtifactStore::edit_lane`. Lives on the envelope (not on `Edit<Mutation>`\n    /// itself, which this crate's per-technology `Mutation` types don't own) so it survives a plain\n    /// JSON round trip (`ArtifactStore::envelope_json`) alongside `cursor`/`owner`/`dialect`.\n    pub lanes: BTreeMap<String, HistoryLane>,\n    /// 👁 Explicit checkpoint this viewer is looking at. `None` is the tip of the active line.\n    /// Local to this replica: a collaborator's checkout does not write it.\n    pub viewer_checkpoint_id: Option<String>,\n    pub edit_messages: ArtifactEditMessageLedger,\n    pub conflicts: Vec<crate::os_spr::Conflict>,\n    /// 🔀️ Every structural history event — undo, redo, checkpoint commit, branch, checkout,\n    /// repin — as one causal `crate::os_spr::HISTORY_TRANSITION_SCHEMA` envelope, in HLC order.\n    /// Together with `vcs.edits` this is the document's complete semantic event log. The\n    /// change/checkpoint/alternative ledgers are its projection. `active_alternative_id` and\n    /// `viewer_checkpoint_id` are this replica's head, persisted local-only, not that projection.\n    pub transitions: Vec<crate::os_spr::MutationEnvelope>,\n    /// 🗂️ The transitions this history holds ([`crate::os_spr::HistoryShape`]): a config store's history holds undo and\n    /// redo only, so its store refuses every other transition at dispatch and at remote admission — the same law its\n    /// retained loader applies.\n    pub history_shape: crate::os_spr::HistoryShape,\n    /// 🎐️ The tool transaction whose edit is open in `vcs.edits` ([`ArtifactCommand::AppendTransaction`]). it before its commit, so an abort or a lost session leaves\n    /// no trace.\n    pub open_transaction: Option<OpenToolTransaction>,\n}\n\n/// 📸️ One immutable envelope observation; cursor and every the key when the option is `None`/the map is empty.\nimpl<P: ToValue, Mutation: ToValue> ToValue for ArtifactEnvelopeRead<'_, P, Mutation> {\n    fn to_value(&self) -> DslValue {\n        let mut entries = vec![(\"schema\".to_string(), self.schema.to_value()), (\"id\".to_string(), self.id.to_value()), (\"vcs\".to_string(), self.vcs.to_value())];\n        if let Some(backbone) = self.backbone {\n            entries.push((\"backbone\".to_string(), backbone.to_value()));\n        }\n        if let Some(active_alternative_id) = self.active_alternative_id {\n            entries.push((\"activeAlternativeId\".to_string(), active_alternative_id.to_value()));\n        }\n        if let Some(cursor) = self.cursor {\n            entries.push((\"cursor\".to_string(), cursor.to_value()));\n        }\n        if let Some(dialect) = self.dialect {\n            entries.push((\"dialect\".to_string(), dialect.to_value()));\n        }\n        if let Some(migrated_from) = self.migrated_from {\n            entries.push((\"migratedFrom\".to_string(), migrated_from.to_value()));\n        }\n        if let Some(owner) = self.owner {\n            entries.push((\"owner\".to_string(), owner.to_value()));\n        }\n        if !self.lanes.is_empty() {\n            entries.push((\"lanes\".to_string(), self.lanes.to_value()));\n        }\n entries.push((\"editMessages\".to_string(), self.edit_messages.to_value()));\n        entries.push((\"conflicts\".to_string(), self.conflicts.to_value()));\n        DslValue::Object(entries)\n    }\n}\n\nimpl<P, Mutation> ArtifactEnvelopeOwners<P, Mutation> {\n    /// 🖇️ Whether `edit_id` is committed history: every edit but the open tool transaction's, which the shared log and\n    /// every persisted form leave out until its commit.\n    pub fn holds_committed_edit(&self, edit_id: &str) -> bool {\n        self.open_transaction.as_ref().is_none_or(|open| open.edit_id != edit_id)\n    }\n\n    /// 📸️ Captures read roots before any serializer can cross a shared group decision.\n    pub fn capture_read(&self) -> Result<ArtifactEnvelopeRead<'_, P, Mutation>, &'static str> {\n        let history_visibility = self.vcs.group_visibility().map_err(|()| \"envelope history contains different group authorities\")?;\n        let cursor_visibility = self.cursor.as_ref().and_then(ArtifactCursor::group_visibility);\n        if history_visibility.zip(cursor_visibility).is_some_and(|(history, cursor)| !std::ptr::eq(history, cursor)) {\n            return Err(\"envelope cursor and history have different group authorities\");\n        }\n        let decision = captured group authority\")?;\n        let cursor = self.cursor.as_ref().map(|cursor| cursor.read_group(decision.as_ref())).transpose().map_err(|()| \"envelope cursor lost its captured group authority\")?;\n        Ok(ArtifactEnvelopeRead {\n            schema: &self.schema,\n            id: &self.id,\n            vcs,\n            backbone: self.backbone.as_ref(),\n conflicts: &self.conflicts,\n        })\n    }\n}\n\n/// 🛡️ Terminal shell for one exact document record. Deep fields are ManuallyDrop from\n/// birth and can leave the shell only through the bounded store/completed-record owner protocols.\npub struct ArtifactEnvelope<P, Mutation> {\n    owners: std::mem::ManuallyDrop<ArtifactEnvelopeOwners<P, Mutation>>,\n    owners_detached: bool,\n}\n\nimpl<P, Mutation> ArtifactEnvelope<P, Mutation> {\n    pub fn from_owners(owners: ArtifactEnvelopeOwners<P, Mutation>) -> Self {\n        Self { owners: std::mem::ManuallyDrop::new(owners), owners_detached: false }\n    }\n\n    /// 🧺️ Consumes the terminal shell and hands back its owners. This is the ONLY way a caller\n    /// outside this module can read an envelope's fields: the shell's `Drop` asserts that its owners\n    /// were detached first, so reading fields by reference and letting the shell fall out of scope\n    /// aborts at runtime (\"terminal shell reached Drop before ... detached every nested owner\").\n    /// `🖥️host`'s `BackboneDocument` construction goes through here for exactly that reason.\n    pub fn into_owners(mut self) -> ArtifactEnvelopeOwners<P, Mutation> {\n        assert!(!self.owners_detached, \"artifact envelope owners were detached twice\");\n        self.owners_detached = true;\n        unsafe { std::mem::ManuallyDrop::take(&mut self.owners) }\n    }\n\n    /// 🧹️ Retires a candidate envelope that no store adopted. {@link into_owners} hands back\n    /// fixed ledgers (`vcs.edits`/`changes`/`checkpoints`/`alternatives`, `edit_messages`) that each\n    /// carry their own terminal-empty `Drop` witness, so dropping a POPULATED candidate aborts the\n    /// process on that witness instead of surfacing the refusal. Every entry is popped here, in the\n    /// same tail-first order {@link ArtifactStore::close_take_final_envelope_retirement} leaves the\n    /// ledgers in, and nothing else about the refusal changes. The initial snapshot and every popped\n    /// edit are retired through the technology's own vocabulary, never dropped: a procedural\n    /// snapshot's `OrderedMap` layout and its operations' roots abort the guest on a bare drop (hub\n    /// genesis of `3d.generation`, 2026-09-28, ticket 26/09/23 slice S19).\n    pub fn retire_unadopted(self)\n    where\n        Mutation: self::Mutation<P>,\n    {\n        let ArtifactEnvelopeOwners { schema, id, vcs, backbone, active_alternative_id, cursor, dialect, migrated_from, owner, lanes, viewer_checkpoint_id, mut edit_messages, conflicts, transitions, history_shape: _, open_transaction: _ } =\n            self.into_owners();\n        let ArtifactVcs { initial_snapshot, mut edits, mut changes, mut checkpoints, mut alternatives } = vcs;\n        while let Some(edit) = edits.pop() {\n            retire_scratch_edits::<P, Mutation>([edit]);\n        }\n        while changes.pop().is_some() {}\n        while checkpoints.pop().is_some() {}\n        while alternatives.pop().is_some() {}\n        while edit_messages.pop().is_some() {}\n        drop((schema, id, edits, changes, checkpoints, alternatives, backbone, active_alternative_id, cursor, dialect, migrated_from, owner, lanes, viewer_checkpoint_id, edit_messages, conflicts, transitions));\n        retire_replayed_projection::<P, Mutation>(initial_snapshot);\n    }\n\n    /// 🌱️ Moves the sole snapshot from a decoder-proven fresh envelope. Rejection\n    /// returns the exact shell untouched; accepted metadata is definitionally bounded and empty.\n    pub fn try_into_fresh_snapshot(self) -> Result<P, Self> {\n        if self.schema.len() > 256\n            || self.id.len() > 256\n            || !self.vcs.edits.is_empty()\n            || !self.vcs.changes.is_empty()\n            || !self.vcs.checkpoints.is_empty()\n            || !self.vcs.alternatives.is_empty()\n            || self.backbone.is_some()\n            || self.active_alternative_id.is_some()\n            || self.cursor.is_some()\n            || self.dialect.is_some()\n            || self.migrated_from.is_some()\n            || self.owner.is_some()\n            || !self.lanes.is_empty()\n            || self.viewer_checkpoint_id.is_some()\n            || !self.edit_messages.is_empty()\n            || !self.conflicts.is_empty()\n            || !self.transitions.is_empty()\n        {\n            return Err(self);\n        }\n        let ArtifactEnvelopeOwners { schema, id, vcs, backbone, active_alternative_id, cursor, dialect, migrated_from, owner, lanes, viewer_checkpoint_id, edit_messages, conflicts, transitions, history_shape: _, open_transaction: _ } =\n            self.into_owners();\n        let ArtifactVcs { initial_snapshot, edits, changes, checkpoints, alternatives } = vcs;\n        drop((schema, id, edits, changes, checkpoints, alternatives, backbone, active_alternative_id, cursor, dialect, migrated_from, owner, lanes, viewer_checkpoint_id, edit_messages, conflicts, transitions));\n        Ok(initial_snapshot)\n crate::os_io::ArtifactDialect,\n    #[value(default, skip_serializing_if = \"Option::is_none\")]\n    pub checkpoint_id: Option<String>,\n    pub migrated_at: String,\n}\n\n#[derive(Clone, Debug, Undo,\n    Redo,\n    UndoWithPolicy {\n        policy: UndoPolicy,\n        #[value(default, skip_serializing_if = \"Option::is_none\")]\n        semantic_command: Ordinal\n    /// 15 — frozen, appended after `PruneDrafts`.\n    SetMergePolicy {\n        policy: crate::os_spr::MergePolicy,\n    },\n    /// ⚔️ Resolves an `Open` `crate::os_spr::Conflict` by id — see\n    /// `ArtifactStore::resolve_conflict` for what `Accept`/`Discard` do for each conflict kind.\n    /// Ordinal 16 — frozen.\n    ResolveConflict {\n        conflict_id: String,\n        resolution: crate::os_spr::ConflictResolution,\n    },\n    /// ✏️ Supersedes the effective input of applied operations, non-destructively: each input replaces its target's\n    /// input (`None` withdraws it) in every alternative, or only within the alternative `scope`. Ordinal 18.\n    CreateAlternativeWithSupersede {\n        name: String,\n        inputs: Vec<SupersedeInput<Mutation>>,\n    },\n    /// 🎞️ Appends `mutations` to the open edit of the tool transaction `transaction`, opening it with its first append:\n    /// a streamed tool's ticks become one edit, every operation stamped with the ref and none announced before\n    /// `CommitTransaction`. Ordinal 21.\n    AbortTransaction {\n        transaction_id: String,\n    },\n}\n\n/// 🎞️ The tool transaction a store holds open ([`ArtifactCommand::AppendTransaction`]): its ref and the one edit its\n/// appends grow, kept at the tail of the local applied history until its commit announces it or its abort removes it.\n#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)]\npub struct OpenToolTransaction {\n    pub transaction: protocol::TransactionRef,\n    pub edit_id: String,\n}\n\n/// 🐢️ A history change this store admitted but has not adopted yet (design §16.6): the remote `transitions` it admitted\n/// turn; the replay\n/// restarts whenever the history it started from changed (the content revision it names).\nstruct PendingReprojection<P, Mutation>\nwhere\n    Mutation: self::Mutation<P>,\n{\n    transitions: Vec<crate::os_spr::MutationEnvelope>,\n    local: Option<PendingLocalStep>,\n    replay: Option<([u8; 32], EditReplay<P, Mutation>)>,\n}\n\nimpl<P, Mutation> PendingReprojection<P, Mutation>\nwhere\n    Mutation: self::Mutation<P>,\n{\n    /// 🫗️ Nothing admitted yet.\n    fn empty() -> Self {\n        Self { transitions: Vec::new(), local: None, replay: None }\n    }\n}\n\n/// 🪃️ A local history step whose Report replay outlasts its dispatch: the transitions it authored (neither recorded nor\n/// announced yet), the head `(line, checkpoint)` it moves this replica to, and whether it finalizes a supersession — whose\n/// report must not block finalizing, or the step is refused with nothing of it recorded.\nstruct PendingLocalStep {\n    envelopes: Vec<crate::os_spr::MutationEnvelope>,\n    head: (Option<String>, Option<String>),\n    finalizing: bool,\n}\n\n/// ⏩️ Where one advance of a deferred reprojection left it.\nenum ReprojectionAdvance {\n    Pending(ReplayProgress),\n    Adopted(Vec<crate::os_spr::EditMessages>),\n}\n\n/// ⏱️ How far one turn of a deferred reprojection replays (design §7: ≤ 4 ms slices): until the turn's wall deadline on\n/// `now_us` — `wall_us` after the turn began, or the runtime's own turn deadline ([`ArtifactStore::step_reprojection`]) —\n/// and at most `operations` operations, whichever comes first; every turn replays at least one operation. `now_us` is the\n/// job clock ([`semio_framework_job::default_now_us`]); laws inject their own.\n#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug)]\npub struct ReplayTurnBudget {\n    pub wall_us: u64,\n    pub operations: usize,\n    pub now_us: fn() -> Option<u64>,\n}\n\nimpl ReplayTurnBudget {\n    /// 🕓️ `wall_us` of the job clock per turn, with `operations` as the secondary cap.\n    pub fn wall(wall_us: u64, operations: usize) -> Self {\n        Self { wall_us, operations, now_us: semio_framework_job::default_now_us }\n    }\n\n    /// 🔢️ `operations` per turn and no wall limit: what a law that counts operations replays with.\n    pub fn operations(operations: usize) -> Self {\n        Self { wall_us: u64::MAX, operations, now_us: semio_framework_job::default_now_us }\n    }\n\n    /// ⌛️ The turn's deadline on `now_us`: the runtime's `deadline_us`, else `wall_us` from now (now when the clock cannot\n    /// be read); `None` without a wall limit.\n    fn turn_deadline(&self, deadline_us: Option<u64>) -> Option<u64> {\n        deadline_us.or_else(|| (self.wall_us != u64::MAX).then(|| (self.now_us)().map_or(0, |now| now.saturating_add(self.wall_us))))\n    }\n\n    /// 🛎️ Whether a turn that replayed `replayed` operations ends: its cap is reached or its deadline passed on `now_us`\n    /// (an unreadable clock ends it).\n    fn turn_ends(&self, replayed: usize, deadline_us: Option<u64>) -> bool {\n        replayed >= self.operations || deadline_us.is_some_and(|deadline| (self.now_us)().is_none_or(|now| now >= deadline))\n    }\n}\n\n/// ✏️ One input of [`ArtifactCommand::Supersede`]: the superseded operation and the replacement it folds as from now\n/// on (`None` withdraws it).\n#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, ToValue, FromValue)]\n#[value(rename_all = \"camelCase\")]\npub struct SupersedeInput<Mutation> {\n    pub target: MutationId,\n    #[value(default, skip_serializing_if = \"Option::is_none\")]\n    pub replacement: Option<Mutation>,\n}\n\nimpl<Mutation> ArtifactCommand<Mutation> {\n    /// 🔮️ Names the projection-invalidating transition this command performs, if it has one.\n    pub async fn projection_cause(&self) -> Option<ArtifactProjectionCause> {\n        match self {\n            Self::Apply { .. } | Self::ApplyInLane { .. } => Some(ArtifactProjectionCause::Apply),\n            Self::IngestRemote { .. } => Some(ArtifactProjectionCause::RemoteIngest),\n            Self::Undo | Self::UndoWithPolicy { .. } | Self::UndoInLane { .. } => Some(ArtifactProjectionCause::Undo),\n            Self::Redo | Self::RedoInLane { .. } => Some(ArtifactProjectionCause::Redo),\n            Self::CheckoutCheckpoint { .. } | Self::CreateAlternative { .. } | Self::SwitchAlternative { .. } => Some(ArtifactProjectionCause::Checkout),\n            Self::CommitCheckpoint { .. } => Some(ArtifactProjectionCause::Checkpoint),\n            Self::PruneDrafts => Some(ArtifactProjectionCause::PruneDrafts),\n            Self::SetMergePolicy { .. } => Some(ArtifactProjectionCause::PolicyChange),\n            Self::ResolveConflict { .. } => Some(ArtifactProjectionCause::RemoteIngest),\n            Self::Supersede { .. } | Self::CreateAlternativeWithSupersede { .. } => Some(ArtifactProjectionCause::Replay),\n            Self::AppendTransaction { .. } | Self::CommitTransaction { .. } => Some(ArtifactProjectionCause::Apply),\n            Self::AbortTransaction { .. } => Some(ArtifactProjectionCause::Undo),\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// 🚦️ Whether this command moves history positions — an undo, redo, checkpoint, alternative, checkout, supersession or\n    /// conflict resolution: what a store whose local history step still replays refuses ([`VcsError::HistoryReplaying`]).\n    pub fn moves_history(&self) -> bool {\n        !self.history_transition_kinds().is_empty() || matches!(self, Self::ResolveConflict { .. })\n    }\n\n    /// 🏷️ Every kind of history transition this command may author, in authoring order: what the store's\n    /// [`crate::os_spr::HistoryShape`] must admit before the command runs.\n    pub fn history_transition_kinds(&self) -> &'static [crate::os_spr::HistoryTransitionKind] {\n        use crate::os_spr::HistoryTransitionKind::{Branch, Checkout, Commit, Reinstate, Revert, Supersede};\n        match self {\n            Self::Undo | Self::UndoWithPolicy { .. } | Self::UndoInLane { .. } => &[Revert],\n            Self::Redo | Self::RedoInLane { .. } => &[Reinstate],\n &[Checkout],\n            Self::Supersede { .. } => &[Supersede],\n            Self::CreateAlternativeWithSupersede { .. } => &[Commit, Branch, Supersede],\n            Self::Apply { .. }\n 🔖️Composition\n// 🧩️ Composable-vs-referenceable artifact primitives (ticket `26/08/12/UNIFIED-COMPOSABLE-\n// ARTIFACT-SYSTEM` `📓️design-full-plan.md` §\"1. Kernel primitives\"). Two structurally distinct\n// relationships between artifacts:\n// - a **CHILD** (`ArtifactChild<S>` on the parent's snapshot / `OwnerRef` on the child's own\n//   envelope): the parent creates and deletes it, it has exactly one owner, no pin, no\n//   independent lifecycle, and nests inline in UI — but it is still its OWN `ArtifactEnvelope`\n//   with its own `ArtifactVcs` history and store, never an inline subtree (this crate's own doc\n//   comment / the design doc's \"Child = own envelope\" decision). Consequently a parent's diff\n//   NEVER embeds a child diff.\n// - a **LINK** (`ArtifactLink`/`LinkPin`): an independent lifecycle of its own, a PIN (so it can\n//   be frozen to a specific `Head`/`Checkpoint`/content-addressed `Snapshot`), and renders as a\n//   chip, never nested inline.\n//\n// `ArtifactRefs` lets a snapshot type declare its own children/links (defaulted to none, so a\n// leaf artifact needs zero boilerplate); `LinkResolver`/`ChildStoreFactory` are the host-side\n// seams that turn those declarations into real bytes/stores. `CompositionCoordinator` (its own\n// `🔖️CompositionCoordinator` region, after `🔖️Space` below) orchestrates atomic multi-store\n// dispatch across a parent and its children on top of these types.\n\n/// 🧸️ Ownership handle a parent SNAPSHOT embeds for one owned child slot (e.g. a plugin's\n/// generated field `mesh_child: ArtifactChild<MeshSnapshot>`). `S` is a compile-time-only phantom\n/// naming which snapshot type the child is expected to materialize as — it never appears on the\n/// wire and never constrains this type's own capabilities. `Clone`/`Debug`/`PartialEq` are\n/// hand-implemented below (not `#[derive(..)]`'d): deriving them on a `PhantomData<S>`-carrying\n/// struct adds an unwanted `S: Trait` bound to every impl even though `S` never appears in any\n/// stored/compared data, so those three derives would silently fail to work \"for any `S`\" (the\n/// task's own requirement) the moment a caller picked an `S` that itself didn't implement\n/// `Clone`/`Debug`/`PartialEq`. `Serialize`/`Deserialize` avoid the same trap via `#[serde(bound =\n/// \"\")]` instead of a hand impl — the standard serde idiom for a `PhantomData<S>` field, since\n/// serde's derive macro honors an explicit empty bound list rather than inferring one from `S`.\n/// `local_owner` is a serialization-skipped, immutable materialization retained by this exact\n/// handle; it is intentionally absent from equality, debug, DSL, pack, and JSON identity. No pin,\n/// no independent lifecycle: see the region doc's CHILD-vs-LINK split.\nstruct ArtifactChildLocalText(Arc<str>);\n\n/// 🚫️ Why an owned child's local materialization cannot be read at a typed boundary.\n#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum ArtifactChildMaterializationError {\n    Absent,\n    WrongType,\n}\n\nimpl std::fmt::Display for ArtifactChildMaterializationError {\n    fn fmt(&self, formatter: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {\n        match self {\n            Self::Absent => formatter.write_str(\"artifact child is not materialized\"),\n            Self::WrongType => formatter.write_str(\"artifact child materialization has a different exact type\"),\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nimpl std::error::Error for ArtifactChildMaterializationError {}\n\n/// 🆔️ The content-addressed id of a composed child or persisted scene: `<prefix>-` + the first 16 lowercase hex digits\n/// of SHA-256 over `bytes` (the child schema's `ContentId`). Specified, stable across processes, platforms and\n/// toolchains, and reproducible by any implementation — unlike a `std` hasher, whose algorithm Rust leaves unspecified.\n/// A site that addresses several fields joins them with U+001F. TypeScript twin: `contentId` (`🪆️child/🧬️schema/🟦️.ts`).\npub fn content_id(prefix: &str, bytes: &[u8]) -> String {\n    format!(\"{prefix}-{}\", semio_framework_hash::hex_lower(&semio_framework_hash::Sha256::digest(bytes)[..8]))\n}\n\npub struct ArtifactChild<S> {\n    pub child_id: String,\n    pub target: crate::os_io::ArtifactRef,\n    local_owner: Option<Arc<dyn std::any::Any + Send + Sync>>,\n    _snapshot: PhantomData<S>,\n}\n\nimpl<S> ArtifactChild<S> {\n    /// 🏗️ Constructs a handle, threading the phantom marker for the caller.\n    pub fn new(child_id: String, target: crate::os_io::ArtifactRef) -> Self {\n        Self { child_id, target, local_owner: None, _snapshot: PhantomData }\n    }\n\n    /// 🪆 Attaches an immutable local-only materialization to this owned child handle.\n    pub fn with_local_owner<T: std::any::Any + Send + Sync>(mut self, owner: Arc<T>) -> Self {\n        self.local_owner = Some(owner);\n        self\n    }\n\n    /// 🪆 Replaces this handle's immutable local-only materialization owner.\n    pub fn set_local_owner<T: std::any::Any + Send + Sync>(&mut self, owner: Arc<T>) {\n        self.local_owner = Some(owner);\n    }\n\n    /// 🧵 Retains a type-checked local-only materialization without cloning its payload.\n    pub fn local_owner<T: std::any::Any + Send + Sync>(&self) -> Option<Arc<T>> {\n        Arc::downcast::<T>(self.local_owner.clone()?).ok()\n    }\n\n    /// 📤️ Requires the exact local materialization at content-reading boundaries. Exporters must\n    /// propagate this failure instead of serializing the handle or substituting default content.\n    pub fn require_local_owner<T: std::any::Any + Send + Sync>(&self) -> Result<Arc<T>, ArtifactChildMaterializationError> {\n        let owner = self.local_owner.clone().ok_or(ArtifactChildMaterializationError::Absent)?;\n        Arc::downcast::<T>(owner).map_err(|_| ArtifactChildMaterializationError::WrongType)\n    }\n\n    /// 📤️ Transfers the exact typed local owner; a type mismatch retains the untouched owner.\n    pub fn take_local_owner<T: std::any::Any + Send + Sync>(&mut self) -> Result<Option<Arc<T>>, &'static str> {\n        let Some(owner) = self.local_owner.take() else {\n            return Ok(None);\n        };\n        match Arc::downcast::<T>(owner) {\n            Ok(owner) => Ok(Some(owner)),\n            Err(owner) => {\n                self.local_owner = Some(owner);\n                Err(\"artifact child local owner has a different exact type\")\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// 🪆 Attaches immutable local-only text to this owned child handle.\n    pub fn with_local_text(mut self, text: Arc<str>) -> Self {\n        self.local_owner = Some(Arc::new(ArtifactChildLocalText(text)));\n        self\n    }\n\n    /// 🪆 Replaces this handle's immutable local-only text owner.\n    pub fn set_local_text(&mut self, text: Arc<str>) {\n        self.local_owner = Some(Arc::new(ArtifactChildLocalText(text)));\n    }\n\n    /// 🔎 Borrows this handle's local-only text when the child has been materialized.\n    pub fn local_text(&self) -> Option<&str> {\n        self.local_owner.as_deref()?.downcast_ref::<ArtifactChildLocalText>().map(|owner| owner.0.as_ref())\n    }\n\n    /// 🧵 Retains this handle's local-only text owner without copying its bytes.\n    pub fn local_text_owner(&self) -> Option<Arc<str>> {\n        self.local_owner.as_deref()?.downcast_ref::<ArtifactChildLocalText>().map(|owner| owner.0.clone())\n    }\n\n    /// 🪪️ Drops the compile-time-only `S` phantom, producing the type-erased projection\n    /// `ArtifactRefs::child_refs` returns.\n    pub async fn to_child_ref(&self, slot: &str) -> ChildRef {\n        ChildRef { slot: slot.to_string(), child_id: self.child_id.clone(), target: self.target.clone() }\n    }\n}\n\nimpl<S> Clone for ArtifactChild<S> {\n    fn clone(&self) -> Self {\n        Self { child_id: self.child_id.clone(), target: self.target.clone(), local_owner: self.local_owner.clone(), _snapshot: PhantomData }\n    }\n}\n\nimpl<S> semio_framework_schema_composition::ChildFieldRefs for ArtifactChild<S> {\n    const MANY: bool = false;\n    fn visit_child_field<'a, V: semio_framework_schema_composition::ChildRefVisitor<'a>>(&'a self, slot: &'static str, visitor: &mut V) -> Result<(), V::Error> {\n        visitor.step()?;\n        visitor.child(\n            slot,\n            semio_framework_schema_composition::ChildRefFields {\n                child_id: &self.child_id,\n                artifact_id: &self.target.artifact_id,\n                artifact_kind: std::fmt::Debug for ArtifactChild<S> {\n    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {\n        f.debug_struct(\"ArtifactChild\").field(\"child_id\", |control| {\n            control.scoped_stage(|control| {\n                control.begin_stage(2)?;\n                let mut fields = protocol::value::DecodedValue::new(control.allocate_vec::<(String, DslValue)>(2)?, |fields: Vec<(String, DslValue)>| {\n                    for (_, value) in fields {\n                        <DslValue as FromValue>::retire_decoded(value);\n                    }\n error.under(\"childId\"))?;\n                fields.get_mut().push((key, child_id));\n                control.step()?;\n                let key = control.copy_text(\"target\")?;\n                let target = ToValue::to_value_controlled(&self.target, control).map_err(|error| error.under(\"target\"))?;\n                fields.get_mut().push((key, target));\n                control.step()?;\n                Ok(DslValue::Object(fields.take()))\n            })\n        })\n    }\n}\n\nimpl<S> FromValue for ArtifactChild<S> {\n    fn from_value(value: DslValue) -> Result<Self, ValueError> {\n {value:?}\")));\n        };\n        let mut child_id = None;\n        let mut target = None;\n        for (key, entry) in fields {\n            match key.as_str() {\n                \"childId\" => child_id = Some(String::from_value(entry).map_err(|e| e.under(\"childId\"))?),\n                \"target\" => target = Some(crate::os_io::ArtifactRef::from_value(entry).map_err(|e| e.under(\"target\"))?),\n                _ => return Err(ValueError::new(semio_framework_value::ValueRefusalKind::InvalidValue, format!(\"ArtifactChild has unknown field {key}\"))),\n            }\n        }\n        Ok(ArtifactChild {\n            child_id: child_id.ok_or_else(|| ValueError::new(semio_framework_value::ValueRefusalKind::InvalidValue, \"ArtifactChild missing childId\"))?,\n PhantomData,\n        })\n    }\n    fn from_value_controlled(value: &DslValue, control: &mut protocol::value::NativeDecodeControl<'_>) -> Result<Self, ValueError> {\n        let DslValue::Object(fields) = value else { return Err(ValueError::new(semio_framework_value::ValueRefusalKind::InvalidValue, \"expected an object for ArtifactChild\")) };\n        control.scoped_depth(64, |control| {\n            control.scoped_stage(|control| {\n                control.begin_stage(fields.len())?;\n                let mut child_id = None;\n                let mut target = None;\n                for (key, entry) in fields {\n                    match key.as_str() {\n                        \"childId\" => child_id = Some(String::from_value_controlled(entry, control).map_err(|error| error.under(\"childId\"))?),\n                        \"target\" => target = Some(crate::os_io::ArtifactRef::from_value_controlled(entry, control).map_err(|error| error.under(\"target\"))?),\n                        _ => return Err(ValueError::new(semio_framework_value::ValueRefusalKind::InvalidValue, \"ArtifactChild has an unknown field\")),\n                    }\n                    control.step()?;\n                }\n                control.checkpoint()?;\n                Ok(Self {\n                    child_id: child_id.ok_or_else(|| ValueError::new(semio_framework_value::ValueRefusalKind::InvalidValue, \"ArtifactChild missing childId\"))?,\n                    target: target.ok_or_else(|| ValueError::new(semio_framework_value::ValueRefusalKind::InvalidValue, \"ArtifactChild missing target\"))?,\n                    local_owner: None,\n                    _snapshot: PhantomData,\n                })\n            })\n        })\n    }\n}\n\n/// 🪪️ Type-erased projection of one `ArtifactChild<S>` field, dropping the compile-time-only\n/// `S` phantom so `ArtifactRefs::child_refs` can return a single homogeneous `Vec` across however\n/// many differently-`S`-typed child slots a snapshot declares.\n#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, ToValue, FromValue)]\n#[value(rename_all = \"camelCase\")]\npub struct ChildRef {\n    pub slot: String,\n    pub child_id: String,\n    pub target: crate::os_io::ArtifactRef,\n}\n\n/// 📏️ Fixed restore admission bounds; sparse container walks consume their own step budget.\npub const CHILD_RESTORE_MAXIMUM_REFERENCES: usize = 64;\npub const CHILD_RESTORE_MAXIMUM_FIELD_BYTES: usize = 256;\npub const CHILD_RESTORE_MAXIMUM_VISIT_STEPS: usize = 256;\n\n/// 🛑️ Exact loaded-parent projection failures, before opening or publishing any child store.\n#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum ChildRestoreProjectionError {\n    InvalidSlot,\n    InvalidReference,\n    DuplicateChild,\n    SingularSlot,\n    ReferenceLimit,\n    TraversalLimit,\n    IncompleteSet,\n}\n\nimpl std::fmt::Display for ChildRestoreProjectionError {\n    fn fmt(&self, formatter: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {\n        write!(formatter, \"child restore projection: {self:?}\")\n    }\n}\n\nimpl std::error::Error for ChildRestoreProjectionError {}\n\n/// 🌳️ Bounded borrowed authority derived only from the loaded parent's declared child fields.\n#[derive(Debug)]\npub struct ChildRestoreProjection<'a> {\n    slots: &'static [semio_framework_schema_composition::ChildSlotSpec],\n    rows: [Option<(&'static str, semio_framework_schema_composition::ChildRefFields<'a>)>; CHILD_RESTORE_MAXIMUM_REFERENCES],\n    length: usize,\n    steps: usize,\n}\n\nimpl<'a> ChildRestoreProjection<'a> {\n    /// 🔎️ Visits actual typed snapshot fields without cloning handles, leases or child content.\n    pub fn from_snapshot<S: semio_framework_schema_composition::ArtifactCompositionFields>(snapshot: &'a S) -> Result<Self, ChildRestoreProjectionError> {\n        let slots = S::child_slots();\n        if slots.len() > CHILD_RESTORE_MAXIMUM_REFERENCES {\n            return Err(ChildRestoreProjectionError::ReferenceLimit);\n        }\n        for (index, slot) in slots.iter().enumerate() {\n            if slot.name.is_empty()\n                || slot.name.len() > CHILD_RESTORE_MAXIMUM_FIELD_BYTES\n                || slot.kind.len() > CHILD_RESTORE_MAXIMUM_FIELD_BYTES\n                || !crate::os_io::is_canonical_artifact_kind(slot.kind)\n                || slots[..index].iter().any(|prior| prior.name == slot.name)\n            {\n                return Err(ChildRestoreProjectionError::InvalidSlot);\n            }\n        }\n        let mut projection = Self { slots, rows: [None; CHILD_RESTORE_MAXIMUM_REFERENCES], length: 0, steps: 0 };\n        snapshot.visit_child_refs(&mut projection)?;\n        Ok(projection)\n    }\n\n    /// 🧮️ Number of exact child references carried by this loaded parent.\n    pub fn len(&self) -> usize {\n        self.length\n    }\n\n    /// 🍃️ Whether this projection has no populated child fields.\n    pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {\n        self.length == 0\n    }\n\n    /// 🌿️ Reads one admitted typed child row without copying handles or payload owners.\n    pub fn get(&self, index: usize) -> Option<(&'static str, semio_framework_schema_composition::ChildRefFields<'a>)> {\n        self.rows.get(index).copied().flatten()\n    }\n\n    /// 🪪️ Checks one member against the actual loaded parent, without treating it as a full batch.\n    pub fn admits_member(&self, slot: &str, expected: &crate::os_io::ArtifactRef) -> bool {\n        self.rows[..self.length]\n            .iter()\n            .flatten()\n            .any(|(name, fields)| *name == slot && fields.artifact_id == expected.artifact_id && fields.artifact_kind == expected.dialect.artifact_kind && fields.standard == expected.dialect.standard && fields.subset == expected.dialect.subset)\n    }\n\n    /// ⚖️ Admits exactly one unordered complete set: no omission, substitution or duplicate.\n    pub fn admit_complete<'b>(&self, incoming: impl IntoIterator<Item = (&'b str, semio_framework_schema_composition::ChildRefFields<'b>)>) -> Result<(), ChildRestoreProjectionError> {\n        let mut seen = [false; CHILD_RESTORE_MAXIMUM_REFERENCES];\n        let mut count = 0;\n        for (slot, fields) in incoming {\n            if count == CHILD_RESTORE_MAXIMUM_REFERENCES {\n                return Err(ChildRestoreProjectionError::ReferenceLimit);\n            }\n            let index = self.rows[..self.length].iter().position(|entry| entry.as_ref().is_some_and(|(name, expected)| *name == slot && *expected == fields)).ok_or(ChildRestoreProjectionError::IncompleteSet)?;\n            if seen[index] {\n                return Err(ChildRestoreProjectionError::DuplicateChild);\n            }\n            seen[index] = true;\n            count += 1;\n        }\n        if count != self.length {\n            return Err(ChildRestoreProjectionError::IncompleteSet);\n        }\n        Ok(())\n    }\n}\n\nimpl<'a> semio_framework_schema_composition::ChildRefVisitor<'a> for ChildRestoreProjection<'a> {\n    type Error = ChildRestoreProjectionError;\n    fn step(&mut self) -> Result<(), Self::Error> {\n        if self.steps == CHILD_RESTORE_MAXIMUM_VISIT_STEPS {\n semio_framework_schema_composition::ChildRefFields<'a>) -> Result<(), Self::Error> {\n        if self.length == CHILD_RESTORE_MAXIMUM_REFERENCES {\n            return Err(Self::Error::ReferenceLimit);\n        }\n        let spec = self.slots.iter().find(|spec| spec.name == slot).ok_or(Self::Error::InvalidSlot)?;\n        if fields.artifact_kind != spec.kind || [fields.child_id, fields.artifact_id, fields.artifact_kind, fields.standard, fields.subset].iter().any(|field| field.is_empty() || field.len() > CHILD_RESTORE_MAXIMUM_FIELD_BYTES) {\n The caller's `Mutation` impl is expected to route\n    /// through the framework's `next_hover` pure fn before landing here.\n    pub async fn apply(&mut self, mutations: &[Mutation]) -> crate::os_spr::MutationApplyResult<()> {\n        let mut candidate = self.hover.clone();\n        for mutation in mutations {\n            candidate = mutation.diff(&candidate).diff().apply(&candidate)?;\n        }\n        if !mutations.is_empty() {\n            self.hover = candidate;\n            self.generation = self.generation.wrapping_add(1);\n        }\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    /// 🔄️ Discards hover — a host clears this when a view/window closes (nothing left to hover).\n    pub async fn reset(&mut self, hover: S) {\n        self.hover = hover;\n        self.generation = self.generation.wrapping_add(1);\n    }\n\n    /// 🔢️ Bumps on every local hover change; drives the same broadcast-coalescing signal as\n    /// `PresenceStore::generation`.\n    pub async fn generation(&self) -> u64 {\n        self.generation\n    }\n}\n//#endregion 🔖️InteractionStore\n//#endregion 🔖️EphemeralLanes\n//#endregion 🔖️Authority\n\n//#region 🔖️Text\n//#region 🔖️Text\n/// 📍️ 1-based line/column position inside DSL or op-log source text. debt: usize,\n}\n\nimpl<T> BoundedArtifactValueRetirement<T> {\n    fn new(value: T) -> Self {\n        Self { value: std::mem::ManuallyDrop::new(Some(value)), debt: 0 }\n    }\n}\n\nimpl<T: Send + 'static> ErasedSnapshotRetirement for BoundedArtifactValueRetirement<T> {\n    fn close_step(&mut self, maximum_items: usize, maximum_bytes: usize) -> Result<SnapshotRetirementStep, }\n        if self.debt > 0 {\n            let paid = self.debt.min(maximum_bytes);\n            self.debt -= paid;\n            return Ok(SnapshotRetirementStep::Pending { released_items: 0, released_bytes: paid });\n        }\n        if let Some(value) = self.value.take() {\n            drop(value);\n            let paid = ARTIFACT_ENVELOPE_DECODE_PAGE_BYTES.min(maximum_bytes);\n         let mutations: Vec<Mutation> = if ops_vec.is_empty() {\n                    Vec::new()\n                } else {\n                    let op_blobs = crate::os_spr::decode_ops_vec(ops_vec).map_err(|error| VcsError::Deserialize(error.to_string()))?;\n                    let mut decoded = Vec::with_capacity(op_blobs.len());\n                    for bytes in &op_blobs {\n                        decoded.push(Mutation::decode_op(bytes).map_err(|error| VcsError::Deserialize(error.to_string()))?);\n                    }\n                    decoded\n                };\n                if mutations.is_empty() {\n                    if pack.is_empty() && spr.is_empty() {\n                        return Ok((Vec::new(), Vec::new(), String::new()));\n                    }\n                    let parsed = parse_document_pack::<P, Mutation>(pack, spr).await.map_err(|error| VcsError::Deserialize(error.to_string()))?;\n                    let envelope = parsed.into_envelope();\n                    let printed = print_document_pack(&envelope).await;\n                    envelope.retire_unadopted();\n                    let files = printed?;\n                    return Ok((files.pack, files.spr, files.ops));\n                }\n                let mut store = if pack.is_empty() && spr.is_empty() {\n                    return Err(VcsError::Deserialize(\"apply_ops_binary: lane has no pack+spr baseline\".into()));\n                } else {\n                    let parsed = parse_document_pack::<P, Mutation>(pack, spr).await.map_err(|error| VcsError::Deserialize(error.to_string()))?;\n                    let mut envelope = parsed.into_envelope();\n                    let (applied, redo) = match &envelope.cursor {\n                        Some(cursor) => (cursor.applied_edit_ids.clone(), cursor.redo_edit_ids.clone()),\n                        None => (envelope.vcs.edits.iter().map(|edit| edit.id.clone()).collect(), crate::os_vcs::HistoryPageStack::new()),\n                    };\n                    envelope.cursor = Some(ArtifactCursor::new(applied, redo, envelope.cursor.as_ref().and_then(|cursor| cursor.checkpoint_id.clone())));\n                    let mut store = ArtifactStore::new(envelope).await?;\n                    store.install_document_store_owners_exact(bounded_artifact_store_owners::<P, Mutation>());\n                    store\n                };\n                let applied = store.dispatch_apply_exact(mutations, None).await;\n                let printed = match &applied {\n                    Ok(_) => print_document_pack(&store.envelope).await,\n                    Err(_) => Err(VcsError::ValidationFailed(\"artifact codec apply skipped print after a failed reduction\".into())),\n                };\n                let closed = close_codec_reduction_store(store);\n                applied?;\n                closed?;\n                let files = printed?;\n                Ok((files.pack, files.spr, files.ops))\n            })\n        }\n\n        fn replay_envelopes_impl<'a, P, Mutation>(pack: &'a [u8], spr: &'a [u8], envelopes: &'a [u8]) -> ArtifactCodecApplyFuture<'a>\n        where\n            P: Clone + ToValue + FromValue + ArtifactDsl + ArtifactPack + Send + Sync + 'static,\n            Mutation: Clone + ToValue + FromValue + OpText + OpBinary + self::Mutation<P> + Send + Sync + 'static,\n        {\n            Box::pin(async move {\n                let files = replay_envelopes_onto_pair::<P, Mutation>(pack, spr, envelopes, bounded_artifact_store_owners::<P, Mutation>).await?;\n                Ok((files.pack, files.spr, files.ops))\n            })\n        }\n\n        fn edit_text_from_envelope_impl<'a, P, Mutation>(envelope: &'a crate::os_spr::MutationEnvelope) -> std::pin::Pin<Box<dyn std::future::Future<Output = Result<String, VcsError>> + 'a>>\n        where\n            Mutation: OpText + OpBinary,\n        {\n            Box::pin(async move {\n                let edit = edit_from_operation_envelope::<Mutation>(envelope).await?;\n                print_edit_lines(&edit).await\n            })\n        }\n\n        Self {\n            schema: schema.into(),\n            extension: P::EXTENSION,\n            snapshot_sqlite: P::sqlite_snapshot_codec(),\n            pack_schema_hash: match P::record_spec() {\n                Some(spec) => crate::os_pack::schema_hash(&spec),\n                None => [0u8; 32],\n            },\n            compile_dsl: compile_dsl_impl::<P, Mutation>,\n            print_mirror: print_mirror_impl::<P, Mutation>,\n            edit_text_from_envelope: edit_text_from_envelope_impl::<P, Mutation>,\n            apply_ops_binary: apply_ops_binary_impl::<P, Mutation>,\n            replay_envelopes: replay_envelopes_impl::<P, Mutation>,\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nstatic DOCUMENT_CODEC_REGISTRY: std::sync::OnceLock<std::sync::RwLock<BTreeMap<String, ArtifactCodec>>> = std::sync::OnceLock::new();\n\nfn document_codec_registry() -> &'static std::sync::RwLock<BTreeMap<String, ArtifactCodec>> {\n    DOCUMENT_CODEC_REGISTRY.get_or_init(|| std::sync::RwLock::new(BTreeMap::new()))\n}\n\n/// ⚠️ A document schema already has a codec owner. The established codec is never replaced.\n#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub struct DocumentCodecRegistryConflict {\n    pub schema: String,\n}\n\n/// ⚠️ Document-codec registration cannot replace an owner or use an unavailable registry.\n#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum DocumentCodecRegistryError {\n    Conflict(DocumentCodecRegistryConflict),\n    Unavailable,\n}\n\nimpl std::fmt::Display for DocumentCodecRegistryError {\n    fn fmt(&self, formatter: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {\n        match self {\n            Self::Conflict(error) => write!(formatter, \"document codec registration conflicts for schema {}\", error.schema),\n            Self::Unavailable => formatter.write_str(\"document codec registry unavailable\"),\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nimpl std::error::Error for DocumentCodecRegistryError {}\n\nfn same_document_codec(left: &ArtifactCodec, right: &ArtifactCodec) -> bool {\n    left.schema == right.schema\n        && left.extension == right.extension\n        && match (left.snapshot_sqlite.as_ref(), right.snapshot_sqlite.as_ref()) {\n            (Some(left), Some(right)) => left.identical_to(right),\n            (None, None) => true,\n            _ => false,\n        }\n        && left.pack_schema_hash == right.pack_schema_hash\n        && std::ptr::fn_addr_eq(left.compile_dsl, right.compile_dsl)\n        && std::ptr::fn_addr_eq(left.print_mirror, right.print_mirror)\n        && std::ptr::fn_addr_eq(left.edit_text_from_envelope, right.edit_text_from_envelope)\n        && std::ptr::fn_addr_eq(left.apply_ops_binary, right.apply_ops_binary)\n        && std::ptr::fn_addr_eq(left.replay_envelopes, right.replay_envelopes)\n}\n\nfn validate_document_codecs(registry: &BTreeMap<String, ArtifactCodec>, codecs: &[ArtifactCodec]) -> Result<(), DocumentCodecRegistryError> {\n    let mut proposed: BTreeMap<&str, &ArtifactCodec> = BTreeMap::new();\n    for codec in codecs {\n        match proposed.get(codec.schema.as_str()) {\n            Some(existing) if same_document_codec(existing, codec) => {}\n            Some(_) => return Err(DocumentCodecRegistryError::Conflict(DocumentCodecRegistryConflict { schema: codec.schema.clone() })),\n            None => {\n                proposed.insert(codec.schema.as_str(), codec);\n            }\n        }\n    }\n    for (schema, codec) in proposed {\n        match registry.get(schema) {\n            Some(existing) if same_document_codec(existing, codec) => {}\n            Some(_) => return Err(DocumentCodecRegistryError::Conflict(DocumentCodecRegistryConflict { schema: schema.to_string() })),\n            None => {}\n        }\n    }\n    Ok(())\n}\n\n/// 🔬️ Verifies document codecs against all established schemas without mutating the registry.\n#[must_use]\npub async fn preflight_document_codecs(codecs: &[ArtifactCodec]) -> Result<(), DocumentCodecRegistryError> {\n    let assembly = begin_artifact_assembly().map_err(|_| DocumentCodecRegistryError::Unavailable)?;\n    preflight_document_codecs_in_assembly(&assembly, codecs)\n}\n\n/// 🔬️ Verifies document codecs while one artifact assembly owns the shared publication barrier.\n#[must_use]\npub fn preflight_document_codecs_in_assembly(_assembly: &ArtifactAssemblyTransaction, codecs: &[ArtifactCodec]) -> Result<(), DocumentCodecRegistryError> {\n    let registry = document_codec_registry().read().map_err(|_| DocumentCodecRegistryError::Unavailable)?;\n    validate_document_codecs(&registry, codecs)\n}\n\n/// 📝️ Registers one schema codec exactly once. Collisions fail deterministically before any\n/// replacement can occur, so registration order never changes decoding behavior.\n#[must_use]\npub fn register_document_codec(codec: ArtifactCodec) -> Result<(), DocumentCodecRegistryError> {\n    register_document_codecs(vec![codec])\n}\n\n/// 📝️ Registers document codecs only when every descriptor and executable is conflict-free.\n#[must_use]\npub fn register_document_codecs(codecs: Vec<ArtifactCodec>) -> Result<(), DocumentCodecRegistryError> {\n    let assembly = begin_artifact_assembly().map_err(|_| DocumentCodecRegistryError::Unavailable)?;\n    register_document_codecs_in_assembly(&assembly, codecs)\n}\n\n/// 📝️ Publishes preflighted document codecs while one artifact assembly owns the shared barrier.\n#[must_use]\npub fn register_document_codecs_in_assembly(_assembly: &ArtifactAssemblyTransaction, codecs: Vec<ArtifactCodec>) -> Result<(), DocumentCodecRegistryError> {\n    let mut registry = document_codec_registry().write().map_err(|_| DocumentCodecRegistryError::Unavailable)?;\n    validate_document_codecs(&registry, &codecs)?;\n    for codec in codecs {\n        if !registry.contains_key(&codec.schema) {\n            registry.insert(codec.schema.clone(), codec);\n        }\n    }\n    Ok(())\n}\n\n/// 🔎️ Looks up the codec registered for `schema`, if any.\n#[must_use]\npub async fn document_codec(schema: &str) -> Result<Option<ArtifactCodec>, DocumentCodecRegistryError> {\n    let registry = document_codec_registry().read().map_err(|_| DocumentCodecRegistryError::Unavailable)?;\n    Ok(registry.get(schema).cloned())\n}\n\n/// 🧬️ A component codec answer still in flight. `Send` natively, where document owners run on\n/// the shared worker pool; the browser's single isolate needs no `Send`.\n#[cfg(not(target_arch = \"wasm32\"))]\npub type ComponentDocumentCodecFuture<'a, T> = std::pin::Pin<Box<dyn std::future::Future<Output = Result<T, VcsError>> + Send + 'a>>;\n\n#[cfg(target_arch = \"wasm32\")]\npub type ComponentDocumentCodecFuture<'a, T> = std::pin::Pin<Box<dyn std::future::Future<Output = Result<T, VcsError>> + 'a>>;\n\n/// 🧬️ One document kind's codec as the COMPONENT that owns the kind answers it — the\n/// `world actor` `codec` interface (ticket 26/09/18 slice TC3b) — installed by the host that mounted\n/// that component. A process that links no Rust codec for a kind identifies and validates its documents\n/// through this, exactly as the hub's trusted catalog does for a package it links no codec for\n/// (`🌎️hub/🗿️artifact-authority/🔏️trusted-catalog`'s `VerifiedNativeArtifactCodec`: its linked `codec`,\n/// else its component `guest`).\npub trait ComponentDocumentCodec: Send + Sync {\n    /// 🏷️ The document schema the component owns.\n    fn schema(&self) -> &str;\n    /// 🧬️ `codec.pack-schema-hash`: the kind's structural snapshot fingerprint.\n    fn pack_schema_hash(&self) -> ComponentDocumentCodecFuture<'_, [u8; 32]>;\n    /// 📥️ `codec.print-mirror`: the pair's text mirror, which is also its validation fence.\n    fn print_mirror<'a>(&'a self, pack: &'a [u8], spr: &'a [u8]) -> ComponentDocumentCodecFuture<'a, ArtifactTextFiles>;\n}\n\n/// 🧭️ The one codec a document owner resolves for a schema: the Rust codec this binary links\n/// when it links one, else the component codec installed for the mounted component that owns the kind.\n#[derive(Clone)]\npub enum DocumentKindCodec {\n    Linked(ArtifactCodec),\n    Component(Arc<dyn ComponentDocumentCodec>),\n}\n\nimpl DocumentKindCodec {\n    /// 🧬️ The kind's structural snapshot fingerprint.\n    pub async fn pack_schema_hash(&self) -> Result<[u8; 32], VcsError> {\n        match self {\n            Self::Linked(codec) => Ok(codec.pack_schema_hash),\n            Self::Component(codec) => codec.pack_schema_hash().await,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// 📥️ The pair's text mirror; an `Err` means the pair is not a document of this kind.\n    pub async fn print_mirror(&self, pack: &[u8], spr: &[u8]) -> Result<ArtifactTextFiles, VcsError> {\n        match self {\n            Self::Linked(codec) => (codec.print_mirror)(pack, spr).await,\n            Self::Component(codec) => codec.print_mirror(pack, spr).await,\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nstatic COMPONENT_DOCUMENT_CODEC_REGISTRY: std::sync::OnceLock<std::sync::RwLock<BTreeMap<String, Arc<dyn ComponentDocumentCodec>>>> = std::sync::OnceLock::new();\n\nfn component_document_codec_registry() -> &'static std::sync::RwLock<BTreeMap<String, Arc<dyn ComponentDocumentCodec>>> {\n    COMPONENT_DOCUMENT_CODEC_REGISTRY.get_or_init(|| std::sync::RwLock::new(BTreeMap::new()))\n}\n\n/// 📝️ Installs a mounted component's codec for the schema it owns. A later mount of that kind's\n/// owner replaces an earlier one: in this process the component a host mounted IS the kind's owner.\n#[must_use]\npub fn register_component_document_codec(codec: Arc<dyn ComponentDocumentCodec>) -> Result<(), DocumentCodecRegistryError> {\n    let mut registry = component_document_codec_registry().write().map_err(|_| DocumentCodecRegistryError::Unavailable)?;\n    registry.insert(codec.schema().to_string(), codec);\n    Ok(())\n}\n\n/// 🔎️ Resolves `schema` to the one codec a document owner uses — see [`DocumentKindCodec`].\n#[must_use]\npub async fn document_kind_codec(schema: &str) -> Result<Option<DocumentKindCodec>, DocumentCodecRegistryError> {\n    if let Some(codec) = document_codec(schema).await? {\n        return Ok(Some(DocumentKindCodec::Linked(codec)));\n    }\n    let registry = component_document_codec_registry().read().map_err(|_| DocumentCodecRegistryError::Unavailable)?;\n    Ok(registry.get(schema).cloned().map(DocumentKindCodec::Component))\n}\n\n/// 📜️ Reads the document schema id from an encoded `.spr` history log.\npub async fn lane_schema_from_spr(spr: &[u8]) -> Option<String> {\n    if spr.is_empty() {\n        return None;\n    }\n    crate::os_spr::decode_history(spr, &crate::os_spr::DecodeOptions::default()).await.ok().map(|log| log.schema).filter(|schema| !schema.is_empty())\n}\n//#endregion 🔖️CodecRegistry\n\n//#region 🔖️DialectMigration\n/// 🧬️ One registered lossy/lossless pack-bytes transform between two dialects of the SAME\n/// artifact kind (`from.artifact_kind == to.artifact_kind` is a convention this registry doesn't\n/// itself enforce — callers key by the exact `(from, to)` pair they registered). `migrate_pack` is\n/// a bare `fn` pointer (same non-capturing-bridge-function shape `ArtifactCodec::of` already uses\n/// for `compile_dsl`/`print_mirror`/etc above) so a migration can be a plain top-level fn with zero\n/// closure-capture ceremony. Additive-only: nothing in `ArtifactCodec`/`document_codec`/\n/// `ArtifactStore::dispatch` reads this registry yet — see `26/08/10` D4 evolution slice scope note.\n#[derive(Clone)]\npub struct DialectMigration {\n    pub from: crate::os_io::ArtifactDialect,\n    pub to: crate::os_io::ArtifactDialect,\n    pub lossless: bool,\n    pub migrate_pack: fn(&[u8]) -> Result<Vec<u8>, String>,\n}\n\nstatic DIALECT_MIGRATION_REGISTRY: std::sync::OnceLock<std::sync::RwLock<BTreeMap<(crate::os_io::ArtifactDialect, crate::os_io::ArtifactDialect), DialectMigration>>> = std::sync::OnceLock::new();\n\nfn dialect_migration_registry() -> &'static std::sync::RwLock<BTreeMap<(crate::os_io::ArtifactDialect, crate::os_io::ArtifactDialect), DialectMigration>> {\n    DIALECT_MIGRATION_REGISTRY.get_or_init(|| std::sync::RwLock::new(BTreeMap::new()))\n}\n\n/// ⚠️ Dialect-migration registration cannot overwrite an owner or cross artifact kinds.\n#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum DialectMigrationRegistryError {\n    CrossArtifactKind { from: crate::os_io::ArtifactDialect, to: crate::os_io::ArtifactDialect },\n    Conflict { from: crate::os_io::ArtifactDialect, to: crate::os_io::ArtifactDialect },\n    Unavailable,\n}\n\nimpl std::fmt::Display for DialectMigrationRegistryError {\n    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {\n        match self {\n            Self::CrossArtifactKind { from, to } => write!(f, \"dialect migration crosses artifact kinds from {from:?} to {to:?}\"),\n            Self::Conflict { from, to } => write!(f, \"dialect migration conflict from {from:?} to {to:?}\"),\n            Self::Unavailable => write!(f, \"dialect migration registry unavailable\"),\n        }\n    }\n}\nimpl std::error::Error for DialectMigrationRegistryError {}\n\n/// 🚫️ A migration was unavailable or the registered executable rejected its input.\n#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum DialectMigrationError {\n    Missing { from: crate::os_io::ArtifactDialect, to: crate::os_io::ArtifactDialect },\n    Unavailable,\n    Rejected(String),\n}\n\nfn same_dialect_migration(left: &DialectMigration, right: &DialectMigration) -> bool {\n    left.from == right.from && left.to == right.to && left.lossless == right.lossless && std::ptr::fn_addr_eq(left.migrate_pack, right.migrate_pack)\n}\n\nfn validate_dialect_migrations(registry: &BTreeMap<(crate::os_io::ArtifactDialect, crate::os_io::ArtifactDialect), DialectMigration>, migrations: &[DialectMigration]) -> Result<(), DialectMigrationRegistryError> {\n    let mut proposed: BTreeMap<(crate::os_io::ArtifactDialect, crate::os_io::ArtifactDialect), &DialectMigration> = BTreeMap::new();\n    for migration in migrations {\n        if migration.from.artifact_kind != migration.to.artifact_kind {\n            return Err(DialectMigrationRegistryError::CrossArtifactKind { from: migration.from.clone(), to: migration.to.clone() });\n        }\n        let key = (migration.from.clone(), migration.to.clone());\n        match proposed.get(&key) {\n            Some(existing) if same_dialect_migration(existing, migration) => {}\n            Some(_) => return Err(DialectMigrationRegistryError::Conflict { from: key.0, to: key.1 }),\n            None => {\n                proposed.insert(key, migration);\n            }\n        }\n    }\n    for (key, migration) in proposed {\n        match registry.get(&key) {\n            Some(existing) if same_dialect_migration(existing, migration) => {}\n            Some(_) => return Err(DialectMigrationRegistryError::Conflict { from: key.0, to: key.1 }),\n            None => {}\n        }\n    }\n    Ok(())\n}\n\n/// 🔬️ Verifies a migration set against established dialect pairs without mutation.\n#[must_use]\npub async fn preflight_dialect_migrations(migrations: &[DialectMigration]) -> Result<(), DialectMigrationRegistryError> {\n    let assembly = begin_artifact_assembly().map_err(|_| DialectMigrationRegistryError::Unavailable)?;\n    preflight_dialect_migrations_in_assembly(&assembly, migrations).await\n}\n\n/// 🔬️ Verifies migrations while one artifact assembly owns the shared publication barrier.\n#[must_use]\npub async fn preflight_dialect_migrations_in_assembly(_assembly: &ArtifactAssemblyTransaction, migrations: &[DialectMigration]) -> Result<(), DialectMigrationRegistryError> {\n    let registry = dialect_migration_registry().read().map_err(|_| DialectMigrationRegistryError::Unavailable)?;\n    validate_dialect_migrations(&registry, migrations)\n}\n\n/// 📝️ Registers a migration only when its full descriptor and executable identity match.\n#[must_use]\npub fn register_dialect_migration(migration: DialectMigration) -> Result<(), DialectMigrationRegistryError> {\n    register_dialect_migrations(vec![migration])\n}\n\n/// 📝️ Registers migrations only when every candidate pair is conflict-free.\n#[must_use]\npub fn register_dialect_migrations(migrations: Vec<DialectMigration>) -> Result<(), DialectMigrationRegistryError> {\n    let assembly = begin_artifact_assembly().map_err(|_| DialectMigrationRegistryError::Unavailable)?;\n    register_dialect_migrations_in_assembly(&assembly, migrations)\n}\n\n/// 📝️ Publishes preflighted migrations while one artifact assembly owns the shared barrier.\n#[must_use]\npub fn register_dialect_migrations_in_assembly(_assembly: &ArtifactAssemblyTransaction, migrations: Vec<DialectMigration>) -> Result<(), DialectMigrationRegistryError> {\n    let mut registry = dialect_migration_registry().write().map_err(|_| DialectMigrationRegistryError::Unavailable)?;\n    validate_dialect_migrations(&registry, &migrations)?;\n    for migration in migrations {\n        let key = (migration.from.clone(), migration.to.clone());\n        registry.entry(key).or_insert(migration);\n    }\n    Ok(())\n}\n\n/// 🔁️ Looks up the exact `(from, to)` migration and runs its `migrate_pack` over\n/// `pack_bytes`, or a clear `Err` naming both dialect coordinates when none is registered.\n#[must_use]\npub async fn migrate_document(from: &crate::os_io::ArtifactDialect, to: &crate::os_io::ArtifactDialect, pack_bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<Vec<u8>, DialectMigrationError> {\n    let registry = dialect_migration_registry().read().map_err(|_| DialectMigrationError::Unavailable)?;\n    let migration = registry.get(&(from.clone(), to.clone())).ok_or_else(|| DialectMigrationError::Missing { from: from.clone(), to: to.clone() })?;\n    (migration.migrate_pack)(pack_bytes).map_err(DialectMigrationError::Rejected)\n}\n\n/// 🧷️ All writable store registries held before an artifact assembly can publish anything.\npub struct ArtifactAssemblyStoreRegistryGuards<'assembly> {\n    document_codecs: std::sync::RwLockWriteGuard<'static, BTreeMap<String, ArtifactCodec>>,\n    dialect_migrations: std::sync::RwLockWriteGuard<'static, BTreeMap<(crate::os_io::ArtifactDialect, crate::os_io::ArtifactDialect), DialectMigration>>,\n    _assembly: &'assembly ArtifactAssemblyTransaction,\n}\n\n/// 🚫️ A staged store registry assembly cannot be preflighted or committed.\n#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum ArtifactAssemblyStoreRegistryError {\n    DocumentCodec(DocumentCodecRegistryError),\n    DialectMigration(DialectMigrationRegistryError),\n}\n\nimpl std::fmt::Display for ArtifactAssemblyStoreRegistryError {\n    fn fmt(&self, formatter: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {\n        match self {\n            Self::DocumentCodec(error) => error.fmt(formatter),\n            Self::DialectMigration(error) => error.fmt(formatter),\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nimpl std::error::Error for ArtifactAssemblyStoreRegistryError {}\n\n/// 🧷️ Acquires every store registry write lock before an assembly validates or mutates state.\n#[must_use]\npub fn acquire_artifact_assembly_store_registry_guards<'assembly>(assembly: &'assembly ArtifactAssemblyTransaction) -> Result<ArtifactAssemblyStoreRegistryGuards<'assembly>, ArtifactAssemblyStoreRegistryError> {\n    let document_codecs = document_codec_registry().write().map_err(|_| ArtifactAssemblyStoreRegistryError::DocumentCodec(DocumentCodecRegistryError::Unavailable))?;\n    let dialect_migrations = dialect_migration_registry().write().map_err(|_| ArtifactAssemblyStoreRegistryError::DialectMigration(DialectMigrationRegistryError::Unavailable))?;\n    Ok(ArtifactAssemblyStoreRegistryGuards { document_codecs, dialect_migrations, _assembly: assembly })\n}\n\n/// 🔬️ Verifies all staged store rows while every affected write lock is already held.\n#[must_use]\npub fn preflight_artifact_assembly_store_registry_guards(guards: &ArtifactAssemblyStoreRegistryGuards<'_>, document_codecs: &[ArtifactCodec], dialect_migrations: &[DialectMigration]) -> Result<(), ArtifactAssemblyStoreRegistryError> {\n    validate_document_codecs(&guards.document_codecs, document_codecs).map_err(ArtifactAssemblyStoreRegistryError::DocumentCodec)?;\n    validate_dialect_migrations(&guards.dialect_migrations, dialect_migrations).map_err(ArtifactAssemblyStoreRegistryError::DialectMigration)\n}\n\n/// 📌️ Publishes rows proven safe by `preflight_artifact_assembly_store_registry_guards`.\npub fn commit_artifact_assembly_store_registry_guards(guards: &mut ArtifactAssemblyStoreRegistryGuards<'_>, document_codecs: Vec<ArtifactCodec>, dialect_migrations: Vec<DialectMigration>) {\n    for codec in document_codecs {\n        guards.document_codecs.entry(codec.schema.clone()).or_insert(codec);\n    }\n    for migration in dialect_migrations {\n        let key = (migration.from.clone(), migration.to.clone());\n        guards.dialect_migrations.entry(key).or_insert(migration);\n    }\n}\n//#endregion 🔖️DialectMigration\n\n//#region 🔖️MergeHelpers\n/// 🌳️ Walks `checkpoint_id`'s ancestor chain via `parent_id` back to the root, nearest-first\n/// (`checkpoint_id` itself is the first entry). Cycle-guarded (a malformed/adversarial parent chain\n/// stops instead of looping forever) — every well-formed chain built by `reconcile_alternative`/\n/// `CommitCheckpoint` is already acyclic, this is defense in depth, not a documented invariant break.\nasync fn checkpoint_ancestors<P, Mutation>(envelope: &ArtifactEnvelope<P, Mutation>, checkpoint_id: &str) -> Vec<String> {\n    let mut chain = Vec::new();\n    let mut seen = HashSet::new();\n    let mut current = Some(checkpoint_id.to_string());\n    while let Some(id) = current {\n        if !seen.insert(id.clone()) {\n            break;\n        }\n        let parent = envelope.vcs.checkpoints.iter().find(|checkpoint| checkpoint.id == id).and_then(|checkpoint| checkpoint.parent_id.clone());\n        chain.push(id);\n        current = parent;\n    }\n    chain\n}\n\n/// 🌳️ The merge-base of checkpoints `a` and `b`: the nearest checkpoint common to both\n/// ancestor chains (via `parent_id`), or `None` if their histories share no common ancestor.\n/// Supports branch-merge tooling that needs to know \"everything since the fork point\" on either\n/// side. `b`'s chain is walked nearest-to-farthest so the FIRST hit in `a`'s ancestor set is the\n/// nearest (not merely *a*) common ancestor.\npub async fn merge_base<P, Mutation>(envelope: &ArtifactEnvelope<P, Mutation>, a: &str, b: &str) -> Option<String> {\n    let ancestors_a: HashSet<String> = checkpoint_ancestors(envelope, a).await.into_iter().collect();\n    checkpoint_ancestors(envelope, b).await.into_iter().find(|id| ancestors_a.contains(id))\n}\n\n/// 🌀️ `alternative_id` is both cloned and returned below — a future can only be awaited once\n/// (R10 shape 2), so it is resolved to a plain `String` here.\n///\n/// 🌀️ Same reasoning as `alternative_id` above — resolved once, before it is borrowed AND moved.\n///\n/// 🎯️ `&[]`: reconcile-alternative checkpoints carry no composition pins yet — the\n/// `CompositionCoordinator` that populates real `CompositionPin`s on commit is a later wave.\npub async fn reconcile_alternative<P, Mutation>(envelope: &mut ArtifactEnvelope<P, Mutation>, alternative_name: &str, checkpoint_message: Option<String>, authors: Vec<Author>) -> Result<String, VcsError>\nwhere\n    P: Clone + ToValue + FromValue,\n    Mutation: Clone + ToValue + FromValue,\n{\n    if envelope.vcs.checkpoints.is_empty() {\n        return Err(VcsError::NoCheckpoint);\n    }\n    let checkpoint_id = envelope.vcs.checkpoints.last().map(|checkpoint| checkpoint.id.clone()).ok_or(VcsError::NoCheckpoint)?;\n    let alternative_id = mint_alternative_id(alternative_name, std::slice::from_ref(&checkpoint_id)).await;\n    envelope.vcs.alternatives.try_push(Alternative { id: alternative_id.clone(), name: alternative_name.to_string(), checkpoint_ids: vec![checkpoint_id] }).map_err(|_| VcsError::ValidationFailed(\"alternative history ledger is saturated\".into()))?;\n    if let Some(message) = checkpoint_message {\n        let change = Change { id: mint_change_id(&[], Some(&message)).await, edit_ids: Vec::new(), description: Some(message), saved_at: now_iso() };\n        let parent = envelope.vcs.checkpoints.last();\n        let parent_id = parent.map(|checkpoint| checkpoint.id.clone());\n        let mut change_ids = parent.map(|checkpoint| checkpoint.change_ids.clone()).unwrap_or_default();\n        change_ids.push(change.id.clone());\n        envelope.vcs.changes.try_push(change).map_err(|_| VcsError::ValidationFailed(\"change history ledger is saturated\".into()))?;\n        let timestamp = now_iso();\n        let checkpoint_message = Some(\"reconciled\".to_string());\n        let id = content_addressed_checkpoint_id(parent_id.as_deref(), &change_ids, &envelope.vcs.changes, checkpoint_message.as_deref(), &authors, &timestamp, &[]).await;\n        envelope\n            .vcs\n            .checkpoints\n            .try_push(Checkpoint { id, change_ids, parent_id, authors, message: checkpoint_message, timestamp, composition_pins: Vec::new() })\n            .map_err(|_| VcsError::ValidationFailed(\"checkpoint history ledger is saturated\".into()))?;\n    }\n    Ok(alternative_id)\n}\n//#endregion 🔖️MergeHelpers\n\n//#region 🔖️Config\npub type ConfigEnvelope<C, ConfigMutation> = ArtifactEnvelope<C, ConfigMutation>;\npub type ConfigStore<C, ConfigMutation> = ArtifactStore<C, ConfigMutation>;\n\n/// 🎚️ A config store's envelope: a document envelope whose history holds undo and redo only\n/// ([`crate::os_spr::HistoryShape::Config`]).\npub async fn create_config_envelope<C, ConfigMutation>(schema: &str, id: &str, initial_snapshot: C, backbone: Option<ArtifactBackboneRef>) -> ConfigEnvelope<C, ConfigMutation>\nwhere\n    C: Clone,\n{\n    let mut envelope = create_document_envelope(schema, id, initial_snapshot, backbone);\n    envelope.history_shape = crate::os_spr::HistoryShape::Config;\n    envelope\n}\n\n/// 🧮️ Config snapshots use the same DSL law as documents — `ConfigRecord` marks config types.\npub trait ConfigRecord: ArtifactDsl {}\n\n/// 🎯️ Marks `$ty` as whole-record (no field-level diff — an operation replaces the entire\n/// config) with the trivial `ConfigRecord` + `MutationDiff<Self>` pair every hand-rolled\n/// `impl crate::os_store::ConfigRecord for XConfig {}` + `impl crate::os_spr::MutationDiff<XConfig> for XConfig {\n/// fn apply(...) -> XConfig { self.clone() } fn absorb(...) { *self = other; } }` duo repeated\n/// (~33 crates) — `impl_whole_record_config!(XConfig);` replaces both. The orphan rule still\n/// requires the macro invoked from `$ty`'s own crate (relies on the caller already having\n/// `protocol` in scope by name, exactly as every hand-rolled impl this replaces already did).\n#[macro_export]\nmacro_rules! impl_whole_record_config {\n    ($ty:ty) => {\n        impl $crate::ConfigRecord for $ty {}\n        impl ::protocol::MutationDiff<$ty> for $ty {\n            fn apply(&self, _base: &$ty) -> ::protocol::MutationApplyResult<$ty> {\n                Ok(self.clone())\n            }\n            fn absorb(&mut self, other: Self) {\n                *self =
