parse failed: {error}\"));\n        assert_eq!(&via_pack, snapshot, \"pack round trip diverged from source snapshot\");\n        assert_eq!(&via_dsl, snapshot, \"dsl round trip diverged from source snapshot\");\n        assert_eq!(via_pack, via_dsl, \"pack and dsl round trips diverged from each other\");\n    }\n\n    /// 🧊️ Cold twin of [`assert_dsl_pack_equivalence`] for a projection that failed: {error}\"));\n        let via_dsl = P::parse_dsl(&snapshot.print_dsl()).unwrap_or_else(|error| panic!(\"dsl parse failed: {error}\"));\n        let pack_matches = via_pack == *snapshot;\n The compile-time validation ground\n    /// truth for every technology's `🔖️OpText` region — call this once per `Mutation` variant.\n    pub fn assert_op_line_round_trip<Op>(operation: &Op)\n    where\n        Op: OpText + PartialEq + std::fmt::Debug,\n    {\n        let printed = operation.print_op();\n        assert!(!printed.contains('\\n'), \"print_op must be one line, got: {printed:?}\");\n        let parsed = Op::parse_op(&printed).unwrap_or_else(|error| panic!(\"op parse failed: {error}\"));\n        assert_eq!(&parsed, operation, \"op-text round trip diverged; printed: {printed:?}\");\n    }\n\n    /// 🧾️ Asserts a committed language-agnostic wire witness (`…/🧾️wire-witness/🦠️mutation/🔣️.json`) IS the canonical\n    /// Rust wire of its operation: `FromValue` decodes it and `ToValue` re-encodes exactly the committed JSON under the\n    /// independent `serde_json` oracle (key order free, number spelling exact — `3.0` for an `f64`). The owner-side half of\n    /// the `schema-mutation-payload-parity` witness rule; the lint validates the same file against the leaf schema.\n    pub fn assert_wire_witness<Op>(witness: &str) -> Op\n    where\n        Op: FromValue + ToValue,\n    {\n        let committed: serde_json::Value = serde_json::from_str(witness).unwrap_or_else(|error| panic!(\"wire witness is not JSON: {error}\\n{witness}\"));\n        let operation = Op::from_value(committed.clone().into()).unwrap_or_else(|error| panic!(\"wire witness does not decode: {error}\\n{witness}\"));\n        assert_eq!(serde_json::Value::from(operation.to_value()), committed, \"wire witness is not the canonical Rust wire\");\n        operation\n    }\n\n    /// 🧊️ Cold twin of [`assert_op_line_round_trip`] for an operation that REJECTS a bare drop —\n    /// one carrying an `OrderedMap` root or a retirement ladder (`🧰️framework/🔨️modules/🌱️value/🗂️ordered/🦀️.rs:81`),\n    /// e.g. a mutation payload holding a `neural_engine::Dictionary`. Every operation this helper\n    /// decodes is handed to `retire` instead of being dropped, so the law can be asserted without\n    /// tripping a destructor guard. The op-level mirror of [`assert_dsl_round_trip_cold`].\n    pub fn assert_op_line_round_trip_cold<Op>(operation: &Op, retire: impl FnOnce(Op))\n    where\n        Op: OpText + PartialEq + std::fmt::Debug,\n    {\n        let printed = operation.print_op();\n        assert!(!printed.contains('\\n'), \"print_op must be one line, got: {printed:?}\");\n        let parsed = Op::parse_op(&printed).unwrap_or_else(|error| panic!(\"op parse failed: {error}\"));\n        let matches = parsed == *operation;\n        let report = matches.then(String::new).unwrap_or_else(|| format!(\"{parsed:?}\"));\n        retire(parsed);\n        assert!(matches, \"op-text round trip diverged; printed: {printed:?}\\nparsed:\\n{report}\");\n    }\n\n    /// 🧊️ Cold twin of [`assert_op_text_binary_equivalence`]; `retire` takes exact ownership of\n    /// every operation this helper decodes (one from the text lane, one from the binary lane).\n    pub fn assert_op_text_binary_equivalence_cold<Op>(operation: &Op, mut retire: impl FnMut(Op))\n    where\n        Op: OpText + OpBinary + PartialEq + std::fmt::Debug,\n    {\n        assert_op_line_round_trip_cold(operation, &mut retire);\n        let encoded = operation.encode_op().unwrap_or_else(|error| panic!(\"op encode failed: {error}\"));\n        let encoded_again = operation.encode_op().unwrap_or_else(|error| panic!(\"op re-encode failed: {error}\"));\n        assert_eq!(encoded, encoded_again, \"op binary encoding is not deterministic\");\n        let decoded = Op::decode_op(&encoded).unwrap_or_else(|error| panic!(\"op decode failed: {error}\"));\n        let matches = decoded == *operation;\n        let report = matches.then(String::new).unwrap_or_else(|| format!(\"{decoded:?}\"));\n        retire(decoded);\n        assert!(matches, \"op-binary round trip diverged from source operation\\ndecoded:\\n{report}\");\n    }\n\n    /// ⚖️ Asserts op text and op binary are two encodings of the SAME operation:\n    /// `decode_op(encode_op(op)) == parse_op(print_op(op)) == op`, and the binary encoding is\n    /// deterministic. The compile-time validation ground truth for every technology's `OpBinary`\n    /// impl — the op-level mirror of {@link assert_dsl_pack_equivalence}.\n    pub fn assert_op_text_binary_equivalence<Op>(operation: &Op)\n    where\n        Op: OpText + OpBinary + PartialEq + std::fmt::Debug,\n    {\n        assert_op_line_round_trip(operation);\n        let encoded = operation.encode_op().unwrap_or_else(|error| panic!(\"op encode failed: {error}\"));\n        let encoded_again = operation.encode_op().unwrap_or_else(|error| panic!(\"op re-encode failed: {error}\"));\n        assert_eq!(encoded, encoded_again, \"op binary encoding is not deterministic\");\n        let decoded = Op::decode_op(&encoded).unwrap_or_else(|error| panic!(\"op decode failed: {error}\"));\n        assert_eq!(&decoded, operation, \"op-binary round trip diverged from source operation\");\n    }\n\n    /// ⚖️ Asserts command text and command binary are two encodings of the SAME command:\n    /// `ArtifactCommand::decode_command(&c.encode_command()) == parse_command(print_command(c)) == c`, and the\n    /// binary encoding is deterministic. The compile-time validation ground truth for\n    /// `ArtifactCommand`'s text/binary pair — the command-level mirror of\n    /// `assert_op_text_binary_equivalence`.\n    pub async fn assert_command_text_binary_equivalence<P, Op>(command: &ArtifactCommand<Op>)\n    where\n        Op: OpText + OpBinary + self::Mutation<P> + PartialEq + std::fmt::Debug,\n    {\n        let printed = print_command(command).await.unwrap_or_else(|error| panic!(\"command print failed: {error}\"));\n        let parsed: ArtifactCommand<Op> = parse_command::<P, Op>(&printed).await.unwrap_or_else(|error| panic!(\"command parse failed: {error}\"));\n        assert_eq!(&parsed, command, \"command text round trip diverged; printed:\\n{printed}\");\n        let encoded = command.encode_command().unwrap_or_else(|error| panic!(\"command encode failed: {error}\"));\n        let encoded_again = command.encode_command().unwrap_or_else(|error| panic!(\"command re-encode failed: {error}\"));\n        assert_eq!(encoded, encoded_again, \"command binary encoding is not deterministic\");\n        let decoded: ArtifactCommand<Op> = ArtifactCommand::<Op>::decode_command::<P>(&encoded).unwrap_or_else(|error| panic!(\"command decode failed: {error}\"));\n        assert_eq!(&decoded, command, \"command binary round trip diverged from source command\");\n    }\n\n    /// 📄️ Asserts that printing a store's envelope to text and parsing it back keeps its whole shared log — every edit\n    /// and every history transition — and hydrates to the canonical trunk tip (the `.ops` text is the shared log and\n    /// carries no viewer head, ticket 26/10/01 PER-VIEWER-ALTERNATIVE-HEAD); a store on the trunk tip gets back exactly the\n    /// envelope and live snapshot it holds. The ground truth for {@link print_document_text}/{@link parse_document_text}\n    /// on any technology once it implements `ArtifactDsl` + `OpText`.\n    pub async fn assert_document_text_round_trip<P, Mutation>(store: &ArtifactStore<P, Mutation>)\n    where\n        P: Clone + ArtifactDsl + ArtifactPack + PartialEq + std::fmt::Debug + ToValue + FromValue + Send + 'static,\n        Mutation: Clone + OpText + self::Mutation<P> + PartialEq + ToValue + FromValue + OpBinary + Send + 'static,\n    {\n        let live = store.snapshot().expect(\"store snapshot\");\n        let files = print_document_text(store.envelope()).await.expect(\"print document text\");\n        let parsed: ParsedDocumentText<P, Mutation> = parse_document_text(&files.dsl, &files.ops).await.unwrap_or_else(|error| panic!(\"parse document text failed: {error}\"));\n        let shared = parsed.envelope.vcs.edits.iter().map(|edit| (&edit.id, &edit.forwards, &edit.mutation_meta)).eq(store.envelope().vcs.edits.iter().map(|edit| (&edit.id, &edit.forwards, &edit.mutation_meta)));\n        assert!(shared && parsed.envelope.transitions == store.envelope().transitions, \"document-text round trip lost shared history\");\n        assert!(parsed.envelope.active_alternative_id.is_none() && parsed.envelope.viewer_checkpoint_id.is_none(), \"document text hydrates to the canonical trunk tip\");\n        if store.envelope().active_alternative_id.is_none() && store.envelope().viewer_checkpoint_id.is_none() {\n            assert!(&parsed.envelope == store.envelope(), \"document-text round trip lost durable history\");\n            assert_eq!(parsed.snapshot, live, \"document-text round trip diverged from store snapshot\");\n        }\n        retire_parsed_document(parsed);\n    }\n\n    /// 🧹️ Bounded retirement for a parse-produced document that belongs to no store.\n    /// Every terminal shell below `ParsedDocumentText` (`ArtifactEnvelope`, its `ArtifactVcs`, the\n    /// history ledger, each `Edit`) asserts in `Drop` that its nested owners were retired through the\n    /// bounded protocol first, and only an `ArtifactStore` ever runs that protocol — so a helper that\n    /// parses an envelope purely to compare it must drive `ArtifactStoreEnvelopeRetirement` itself\n    /// rather than let the value fall out of scope.\n    pub fn retire_parsed_document<P, Mutation>(parsed: ParsedDocumentText<P, Mutation>)\n    where\n        P: Send + 'static,\n        Mutation: Send + 'static,\n    {\n        let ParsedDocumentText { envelope, snapshot } = parsed;\n        let mut retirement = ArtifactStoreEnvelopeRetirement::new(envelope, Arc::new(RoundTripValueRetirementFactory), Arc::new(RoundTripValueRetirementFactory));\n        for _ in 0..1_000_000 {\n            if retirement.terminal_is_empty() {\n                break;\n            }\n            ErasedSnapshotRetirement::close_step(&mut retirement, 1, 4_096).expect(\"parsed document retires within its exact grant\");\n        }\n        assert!(retirement.terminal_is_empty(), \"parsed document must reach its terminal-empty shell\");\n        drop(snapshot);\n    }\n\n    /// 🧪️ Retirement authorities for a test document whose snapshot and mutations are plain\n    /// data: every value retires in one bounded step, and the store closes through the real cursor\n    /// disposer — so a test store records history and closes exactly like a production member.\n    pub fn plain_document_store_owners<P, Mutation>() -> DocumentStoreOwners<P, Mutation>\n    where\n        P: Clone + ToValue + FromValue + ArtifactPack + Send + Sync + 'static,\n        Mutation: Clone + ToValue + FromValue + self::Mutation<P> + OpBinary + OpText + Send + 'static,\n    {\n        DocumentStoreOwners::new(Arc::new(RoundTripValueRetirementFactory), Arc::new(RoundTripValueRetirementFactory), Arc::new(RoundTripValueRetirementFactory), Box::new(ArtifactStoreCursorDisposer::<P, Mutation>::new()))\n    }\n\n    /// 🧪️ A store over `envelope` carrying [`plain_document_store_owners`].\n    pub async fn plain_test_store<P, Mutation>(envelope: ArtifactEnvelope<P, Mutation>) -> ArtifactStore<P, Mutation>\n    where\n        P: Clone + ToValue + FromValue + ArtifactPack + Send + Sync + 'static,\n        Mutation: Clone + ToValue + FromValue + self::Mutation<P> + OpBinary + OpText + Send + 'static,\n    {\n        let mut store = ArtifactStore::new(envelope).await.expect(\"test fixture history is valid\");\n        store.install_document_store_owners_exact(plain_document_store_owners());\n        store\n    }\n\n    /// 🧹️ Releases a test store's backbone and drives its owned close to the terminal-empty\n    /// witness its `Drop` requires.\n    pub fn close_plain_test_store<P, Mutation>(store: &mut ArtifactStore<P, Mutation>)\n    where\n        P: Clone + ToValue + FromValue + ArtifactPack + Send + Sync + 'static,\n        Mutation: Clone + ToValue + FromValue + self::Mutation<P> + OpBinary + OpText + Send + 'static,\n    {\n        drop(store.detach_backbone().expect(\"a closing test store releases its backbone\"));\n        for _ in 0..65_536 {\n            if store.close_owned_terminal_is_empty() {\n                return;\n            }\n            if store.close_owned_step(1, 4_096).expect(\"test store closes under its bounded owner grant\") == SnapshotRetirementStep::Complete {\n                return;\n            }\n        }\n        panic!(\"test store did not reach its exact terminal-empty witness\");\n    }\n\n    impl<P: Send + Sync + 'static> SnapshotRetirementFactory<P> for RoundTripValueRetirementFactory {\n        fn retire(&self, snapshot: Arc<P>) -> Box<dyn ErasedSnapshotRetirement> {\n            Box::new(RoundTripValueRetirement(Some(snapshot)))\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// 🧹️ One-value retirement used only by [`retire_parsed_document`] — a parsed comparison\n    /// document owns no domain resources, so releasing a value is exactly one bounded step.\n    struct RoundTripValueRetirement<T>(Option<T>);\n\n    impl<T: Send> ErasedSnapshotRetirement for RoundTripValueRetirement<T> {\n        fn close_step(&mut self, maximum_items: usize, _maximum_bytes: usize) -> Result<SnapshotRetirementStep, semio_framework_value::ValueError> {\n            if maximum_items == 0 {\n                return Ok(SnapshotRetirementStep::Pending { released_items: 0, released_bytes: 0 });\n            }\n            if self.0.take().is_some() {\n                return Ok(SnapshotRetirementStep::Pending { released_items: 1, released_bytes: 0 });\n            }\n            Ok(SnapshotRetirementStep::Complete)\n        }\n\n        fn terminal_is_empty(&self) -> bool {\n            self.0.is_none()\n        }\n    }\n\n    struct RoundTripValueRetirementFactory;\n\n    impl<T: Send + 'static> ArtifactOwnedValueRetirementFactory<T> for RoundTripValueRetirementFactory {\n        fn retire_owned(&self, value: T) -> Box<dyn ErasedSnapshotRetirement> {\n            Box::new(RoundTripValueRetirement(Some(value)))\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// 🗄️ Asserts a full pack-based document round trip: mirrors\n    /// `assert_document_text_round_trip` but via `print_document_pack`/`parse_document_pack`, and\n    /// additionally asserts the pack path's parsed snapshot agrees with the text path's — the two\n    /// storage formats must never diverge on the same store.\n    pub async fn assert_document_pack_round_trip<P, Mutation>(store: &ArtifactStore<P, Mutation>)\n    where\n        P: Clone + ArtifactDsl + ArtifactPack + PartialEq + std::fmt::Debug + ToValue + FromValue + Send + 'static,\n        Mutation: Clone + OpText + OpBinary + self::Mutation<P> + PartialEq + ToValue + FromValue + Send + 'static,\n    {\n        let live = store.snapshot().expect(\"store snapshot\");\n        let pack_files = print_document_pack(store.envelope()).await.expect(\"print document pack\");\n        let parsed_pack: ParsedDocumentText<P, Mutation> = parse_document_pack(&pack_files.pack, &pack_files.spr).await.unwrap_or_else(|error| panic!(\"parse document pack failed: {error}\"));\n        assert_eq!(parsed_pack.snapshot, live, \"document-pack round trip diverged from store snapshot\");\n\n        let text_files = print_document_text(store.envelope()).await.expect(\"print document text\");\n        let parsed_text: ParsedDocumentText<P, Mutation> = parse_document_text(&text_files.dsl, &text_files.ops).await.unwrap_or_else(|error| panic!(\"parse document text failed: {error}\"));\n        assert_eq!(parsed_pack.snapshot, parsed_text.snapshot, \"document-pack path diverged from document-text path\");\n        retire_parsed_document(parsed_pack);\n        retire_parsed_document(parsed_text);\n    }\n\n    /// ✉️ Asserts that converting an `Edit<Mutation>` into `crate::os_spr::MutationEnvelope`s\n    /// (`protocol_causal`'s canonical wire/causal representation, moved from `framework/core` in CW3,\n    /// via `crate::os_spr::mutation_envelope_from_edit`) preserves every operation's essential facts —\n    /// the causal-wire sibling of `assert_pack_round_trip`/`assert_dsl_round_trip` for the app\n    /// fan-out's \"pack laws\" cluster.\n    ///\n    /// `MutationEnvelope` is a runtime struct that is never itself re-serialized back into an\n    /// `Edit` (unlike `encode_pack`/`decode_pack`, there is no `envelope_to_edit` inverse — vcs's OWN\n    /// `edit_from_operation_envelope` recovers a *whole edit* from vcs's own, differently-shaped,\n    /// per-edit `semio_framework_replication::MutationEnvelope`, not from this per-operation\n    /// `protocol_causal` one), so a byte-level encode-then-decode law is not meaningful here.\n    /// Instead this checks the two LAWS that actually matter for this bridge: (1) whatever\n    /// `edit.mutation_meta` explicitly recorded for a slot (the ground-truth source\n    /// `mutation_envelope_from_edit` prefers over its own `Mutation`-trait/structural fallbacks —\n    /// see that function's own doc comment) survives unchanged onto the envelope's\n    /// `mutation_id`/`dependencies`/`actor`/`timestamp`; and (2) `envelope.diff.payload`/\n    /// `envelope.inverse.inverse_diff` decode back (via `Mutation`'s own `Deserialize` impl) into\n    /// operations equal to `edit.forwards[i]`/`edit.inverse[i]` — the part a hand-rolled\n    /// `Serialize`/`Deserialize` pair can silently break. Deliberately does NOT recompute the\n    /// envelope's fallback chain (id/actor/deps when `mutation_meta` is absent) itself, since doing\n    /// so would just re-run `mutation_envelope_from_edit`'s own logic against itself and always\n    /// agree — see this function's `🧪️Tests` sibling for a deliberately lossy `Mutation` impl that\n    /// trips law (2).\n    pub async fn assert_command_envelope_round_trip<P, Mutation>(edit: &Edit<Mutation>, document_id: &ArtifactId, schema: &SchemaId)\n    where\n        P: Clone + PartialEq + std::fmt::Debug,\n        Mutation: self::Mutation<P> + PartialEq + std::fmt::Debug + OpBinary,\n    {\n        let envelopes = crate::os_spr::mutation_envelope_from_edit::<P, Mutation>(edit, document_id, schema).unwrap_or_else(|error| panic!(\"mutation_envelope_from_edit must succeed for a well-formed edit: {error}\"));\n        assert_eq!(envelopes.len(), edit.forwards.len(), \"one envelope must be produced per forward operation\");\n        for (index, envelope) in envelopes.iter().enumerate() {\n            assert_eq!(envelope.document_id, *document_id, \"document id did not survive the envelope conversion\");\n            if let Some(meta) = edit.mutation_meta.get(index) {\n                if let Some(mutation_id) = &meta.mutation_id {\n                    assert_eq!(&envelope.mutation_id, mutation_id, \"explicit operation id did not survive the envelope conversion\");\n                }\n                assert_eq!(envelope.dependencies, meta.dependencies, \"explicit dependencies did not survive the envelope conversion\");\n                if let Some(author_id) = &meta.author_id {\n                    assert_eq!(&envelope.actor, author_id, \"explicit author id did not survive the envelope conversion\");\n                }\n                assert_eq!(envelope.timestamp, meta.timestamp, \"explicit timestamp did not survive the envelope conversion\");\n            }\n            let assert_eq!(&recovered_forward, &edit.forwards[index], \"envelope diff payload did not decode back into an equal forward operation\");\n            match edit.inverse.get(index) {\n operation: {error}\"));\n                    assert_eq!(&recovered_backward, backward, \"envelope inverse payload did not decode back into an equal backward operation\");\n                }\n Call after arbitrary command sequences (apply/amend/undo/redo/checkpoint/switch\n    /// interleavings) in a tech's own tests to confirm the incremental fast paths never diverge from\n    /// the replay ground truth.\n    pub async fn assert_live_equals_replay<P, Mutation>(store: &ArtifactStore<P, Mutation>)\n    where\n        P: Clone + ArtifactPack + PartialEq + std::fmt::Debug + ToValue + FromValue + Send + 'static,\n        Mutation: Clone + ToValue + FromValue + self::Mutation<P> + OpBinary + OpText + Send + 'static,\n    {\n        let live = store.snapshot().expect(\"store snapshot\");\n        let replayed = materialize_document_snapshot(store.envelope(), store.applied_edit_ids()).await.expect(\"replay\");\n        assert_eq!(live, replayed, \"store's live snapshot diverged from full-replay materialization\");\n    }\n\n    /// 🎚️ Strongest achieved native IO fidelity for export/reimport laws (S8).\n    #[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]\n    pub enum IoFidelityClass {\n        Exact,\n        Canonical,\n        Semantic,\n        Lossy,\n    }\n\n    /// 🗂️ Vendored real-world example input for subset integrated roundtrip harnesses.\n    pub struct ExampleAsset<'a> {\n        pub bytes: &'a [u8],\n        pub text: Option<&'a str>,\n        pub provenance: &'a str,\n    }\n\n    /// 🪆 Subset-facing surface the integrated harness needs. type Mutation: Clone + PartialEq + std::fmt::Debug + ToValue + FromValue + Mutation<Self::Snapshot> + OpText + OpBinary;\n        type Inference: Clone + PartialEq + std::fmt::Debug + Default;\n        async fn dialect() -> crate::os_io::ArtifactDialect;\n        async fn fidelity() -> IoFidelityClass;\n        async fn drops() -> &'static [&'static str];\n        async fn parse_native(asset: &ExampleAsset<'_>) -> Result<Self::Snapshot, String>;\n        async fn export_native(snapshot: &Self::Snapshot) -> Result<Vec<u8>, String>;\n        async fn reimport_native(bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<Self::Snapshot, String>;\n        async fn infer(snapshot: &Self::Snapshot) -> Self::Inference;\n        async fn sample_mutations(snapshot: &Self::Snapshot) -> Vec<Self::Mutation>;\n        async fn validate_payload(bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<(), Vec<String>>;\n        async fn validate_negative(bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<Vec<String>, String>;\n        async fn is_derived() -> bool {\n            false\n        }\n    }\n\n    async fn skip_stage(error: &str) -> bool {\n        error.starts_with(\"SKIP:\")\n    }\n\n    async fn skip_validation(codes: &[String]) -> bool {\n        codes.len() == 1 && skip_stage(&codes[0]).await\n    }\n\n    /// 🧪 Assert import/export byte fidelity matches the declared class at the raw-byte layer.\n    pub async fn fidelity requires byte-identical export\"),\n            IoFidelityClass::Canonical | IoFidelityClass::Semantic | IoFidelityClass::Lossy => {}\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// 🎯 Assert two inference runs are identical (determinism law S6).\n    pub async fn assert_inference_determinism<I: PartialEq + std::fmt::Debug>(a: &I, b: &I) {\n        assert_eq!(a, b, \"inference is not deterministic across two runs on the same snapshot\");\n    }\n\n    /// 🔁 Drive S0–S10 subset roundtrip stages. S::fidelity().await {\n                        IoFidelityClass::Exact => {}\n                        IoFidelityClass::Canonical | IoFidelityClass::Semantic => {\n S::drops().await.is_empty() => {\n                            assert_eq!(&reimported, &snapshot, \"S8: lossy fidelity with empty drop set requires equal snapshot after reimport\");\n }\n\n        match S::validate_payload(example.bytes).await {\n            Ok(()) => {}\n            Err(codes) if skip_validation(&codes).await => {}\n            Err(codes) => panic!(\"S9 ArtifactPack>::encode_pack_with(&value, options)\n    }\n    fn decode_pack_with(bytes: &[u8], options: &PackDecodeOptions) -> Result<Self, PackError> {\n        let value = <DslValue as ArtifactPack>::decode_pack_with(bytes, options)?;\n        <Self as FromValue>::from_value(value).map_err(|error: ValueError| PackError::Schema(error.to_string()))\n    }\n}\n//#endregion Deep fields are ManuallyDrop from\n/// birth and can leave the shell only through the bounded store/completed-record owner protocols.\npub struct ArtifactEnvelope<P, Mutation> {\n    owners: std::mem::ManuallyDrop<ArtifactEnvelopeOwners<P, Mutation>>,\n    owners_detached: bool,\n}\n\nimpl<P, Mutation> ArtifactEnvelope<P, Mutation> {\n    pub fn from_owners(owners: ArtifactEnvelopeOwners<P, Mutation>) -> Self {\n        Self { owners: std::mem::ManuallyDrop::new(owners), owners_detached: false }\n    }\n\n    /// 🧺️ Consumes the terminal shell and hands back its owners. FromValue)]\n#[value(rename_all = \"camelCase\")]\npub struct MigrationProvenance {\n    pub document_id: String,\n    pub dialect: crate::os_io::ArtifactDialect,\n    #[value(default, skip_serializing_if = \"Option::is_none\")]\n    pub checkpoint_id: Option<String>,\n    pub migrated_at: String,\n}\n\n#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, ToValue, FromValue)]\n#[value(tag = \"kind\", on every operation's metadata and wire envelope.\n    Apply {\n        mutations: Vec<Mutation>,\n        #[value(skip_serializing_if = \"Option::is_none\")]\n        description: Option<String>,\n UndoPolicy,\n        #[value(default, skip_serializing_if = \"Option::is_none\")]\n        semantic_command: Option<Box<ArtifactCommand<Mutation>>>,\n    },\n    /// 🛤️ `Apply`'s lane-tagged twin — records the resulting edit under `lane` (via\n    /// `ArtifactEnvelope.lanes`) instead of the implicit `HistoryLane::Document` a plain `Apply`\n    /// gets.\n    ApplyInLane {\n        mutations: Vec<Mutation>,\n        #[value(skip_serializing_if = \"Option::is_none\")]\n        description: Option<String>,\n        #[value(default)]\n        lane: HistoryLane,\n        #[value(default, skip_serializing_if = \"Option::is_none\")]\n        transaction: Option<protocol::TransactionRef>,\n    },\n    /// 🛤️ Explicit lane-scoped undo: mirrors plain `Undo`'s selective (own-author) semantics\n    /// but searches `applied_edit_ids` for the nearest local entry whose `HistoryLane` is exactly\n    /// `lane`, instead of `HistoryLane::Document`. Lets a caller walk a non-`Document` lane on\n    /// purpose — the completing half of \"default `Undo`/`Redo` skip non-`Document` lanes\" (see\n    /// `ArtifactStore::dispatch`'s `Undo` arm).\n    UndoInLane {\n        lane: HistoryLane,\n    },\n    /// 🛤️ `UndoInLane`'s redo-direction sibling — mirrors plain `Redo`, but pops the\n    /// nearest-to-top `redo_edit_ids` entry whose `HistoryLane` is exactly `lane`.\n    RedoInLane {\n        lane: HistoryLane,\n    },\n    CommitCheckpoint {\n        #[value(skip_serializing_if = \"Option::is_none\")]\n        message: Option<String>,\n        #[value(default, skip_serializing_if = \"Vec::is_empty\")]\n        authors: Vec<Author>,\n    },\n    CreateAlternative {\n        name: String,\n    },\n    SwitchAlternative {\n        alternative_id: String,\n    },\n    CheckoutCheckpoint {\n        #[value(rename = \"checkpointId\")]\n        checkpoint_id: String,\n    },\n    /// 🕸️ Feeds a remote MutationEnvelope through the causal DAG into the edit timeline.\n    IngestRemote {\n        #[value(serialize_with = \"operation_envelope_serde::to_value\", deserialize_with = \"operation_envelope_serde::from_value\")]\n        envelope: crate::os_spr::MutationEnvelope,\n    },\n    /// 🧹 Clears volatile draft-lane history that must never enter a Change/Checkpoint.\n    PruneDrafts,\n    /// ⚖️ Sets this store's local `crate::os_spr::MergePolicy` — authority-local state, never\n    /// carried on a `crate::os_spr::MutationEnvelope`/`BackboneMessage`, never part of shared\n    /// history (`26/08/16/MUTATION-OUTCOMES-MERGE-POLICIES-AND-FIRST-CLASS-CONFLICTS` §C6). Ordinal\n    /// 15 — frozen, appended after `PruneDrafts`.\n    SetMergePolicy {\n        policy: crate::os_spr::MergePolicy,\n    },\n    /// ⚔️ Resolves an `Open` `crate::os_spr::Conflict` by id — see\n    /// `ArtifactStore::resolve_conflict` for what `Accept`/`Discard` do for each conflict kind.\n    /// Ordinal 16 — frozen.\n    ResolveConflict {\n        conflict_id: String,\n        resolution: crate::os_spr::ConflictResolution,\n    },\n    /// ✏️ Supersedes the effective input of applied operations, non-destructively: each input replaces its target's\n    /// input (`None` withdraws it) in every alternative, or only within the alternative `scope`. Ordinal 18.\n    CreateAlternativeWithSupersede {\n        name: String,\n        inputs: Vec<SupersedeInput<Mutation>>,\n    },\n    /// 🎞️ Appends `mutations` to the open edit of the tool transaction `transaction`, opening it with its first append:\n    /// a streamed tool's ticks become one edit, every operation stamped with the ref and none announced before\n    /// `CommitTransaction`. While it is open the store refuses every command but its appends, its commit or abort, a remote\n    /// ingest and a merge-policy change (`VcsError::TransactionOpen`). Ordinal 19.\n    AppendTransaction {\n        mutations: Vec<Mutation>,\n        transaction: protocol::TransactionRef,\n    },\n    /// ✅️ Closes the open edit of the tool transaction `transaction_id` and announces every operation it holds. Ordinal 20.\n    CommitTransaction {\n        transaction_id: String,\n    },\n    /// 🧨️ Reverts the open edit of the tool transaction `transaction_id` with zero trace: no edit, no operation, no\n    /// announcement, the projection and revision of before its first append. Ordinal 21.\n    AbortTransaction {\n        transaction_id: String,\n    },\n}\n\n/// 🎞️ The tool transaction a store holds open ([`ArtifactCommand::AppendTransaction`]): its ref and the one edit its\n/// appends grow, kept at the tail of the local applied history until its commit announces it or its abort removes it.\n#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)]\npub struct OpenToolTransaction {\n    pub transaction: protocol::TransactionRef,\n    pub edit_id: String,\n}\n\n/// 🐢️ A history change this store admitted but has not adopted yet (design §16.6): the remote `transitions` it admitted\n/// ([`ArtifactStore::defer_remote_replays`]) and at most one `local` step this replica authored\n/// ([`ArtifactStore::defer_local_replays`]) wait outside the log while their Report replay steps turn by turn; the replay\n/// restarts whenever the history it started from changed (the content revision it names).\nstruct PendingReprojection<P, Mutation>\nwhere\n    Mutation: self::Mutation<P>,\n{\n    transitions: Vec<crate::os_spr::MutationEnvelope>,\n    local: Option<PendingLocalStep>,\n    replay: Option<([u8; 32], EditReplay<P, Mutation>)>,\n}\n\nimpl<P, Mutation> PendingReprojection<P, Mutation>\nwhere\n    Mutation: self::Mutation<P>,\n{\n    /// 🫗️ Nothing admitted yet.\n    fn empty() -> Self {\n        Self { transitions: Vec::new(), local: None, replay: None }\n    }\n}\n\n/// 🪃️ A local history step whose Report replay outlasts its dispatch: the transitions it authored (neither recorded nor\n/// announced yet), the head `(line, checkpoint)` it moves this replica to, and whether it finalizes a supersession — whose\n/// report must not block finalizing, or the step is refused with nothing of it recorded.\nstruct PendingLocalStep {\n    envelopes: Vec<crate::os_spr::MutationEnvelope>,\n    head: (Option<String>, Option<String>),\n    finalizing: bool,\n}\n\n/// ⏩️ Where one advance of a deferred reprojection left it.\nenum ReprojectionAdvance {\n    Pending(ReplayProgress),\n    Adopted(Vec<crate::os_spr::EditMessages>),\n}\n\n/// ⏱️ How far one turn of a deferred reprojection replays (design §7: ≤ 4 ms slices): until the turn's wall deadline on\n/// `now_us` — `wall_us` after the turn began, or the runtime's own turn deadline ([`ArtifactStore::step_reprojection`]) —\n/// and at most `operations` operations, whichever comes first; every turn replays at least one operation. `now_us` is the\n/// job clock ([`semio_framework_job::default_now_us`]); laws inject their own.\n#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug)]\npub struct ReplayTurnBudget {\n    pub wall_us: u64,\n    pub operations: usize,\n    pub now_us: fn() -> Option<u64>,\n}\n\nimpl ReplayTurnBudget {\n    /// 🕓️ `wall_us` of the job clock per turn, with `operations` as the secondary cap.\n    pub fn wall(wall_us: u64, operations: usize) -> Self {\n        Self { wall_us, operations, now_us: semio_framework_job::default_now_us }\n    }\n\n    /// 🔢️ `operations` per turn and no wall limit: what a law that counts operations replays with.\n    pub fn operations(operations: usize) -> Self {\n        Self { wall_us: u64::MAX, operations, now_us: semio_framework_job::default_now_us }\n    }\n\n    /// ⌛️ The turn's deadline on `now_us`: the runtime's `deadline_us`, else `wall_us` from now (now when the clock cannot\n    /// be read); `None` without a wall limit.\n    fn turn_deadline(&self, deadline_us: Option<u64>) -> Option<u64> {\n        deadline_us.or_else(|| (self.wall_us != u64::MAX).then(|| (self.now_us)().map_or(0, |now| now.saturating_add(self.wall_us))))\n    }\n\n    /// 🛎️ Whether a turn that replayed `replayed` operations ends: its cap is reached or its deadline passed on `now_us`\n    /// (an unreadable clock ends it).\n    fn turn_ends(&self, replayed: usize, deadline_us: Option<u64>) -> bool {\n        replayed >= self.operations || deadline_us.is_some_and(|deadline| (self.now_us)().is_none_or(|now| now >= deadline))\n    }\n}\n\n/// ✏️ One input of [`ArtifactCommand::Supersede`]: the superseded operation and the replacement it folds as from now\n/// on (`None` withdraws it).\n#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, ToValue, FromValue)]\n#[value(rename_all = \"camelCase\")]\npub struct SupersedeInput<Mutation> {\n    pub target: MutationId,\n    #[value(default, skip_serializing_if = \"Option::is_none\")]\n    pub replacement: Option<Mutation>,\n}\n\nimpl<Mutation> ArtifactCommand<Mutation> {\n    /// 🔮️ Names the projection-invalidating transition this command performs, if it has one.\n    pub async fn projection_cause(&self) -> Option<ArtifactProjectionCause> {\n        match self {\n            Self::Apply { .. } | Self::ApplyInLane { .. } => Some(ArtifactProjectionCause::Apply),\n            Self::IngestRemote { .. } => Some(ArtifactProjectionCause::RemoteIngest),\n            Self::Undo | Self::UndoWithPolicy { .. } | Self::UndoInLane { .. } => Some(ArtifactProjectionCause::Undo),\n            Self::Redo | Self::RedoInLane { .. } => Some(ArtifactProjectionCause::Redo),\n            Self::CheckoutCheckpoint { .. } | Self::CreateAlternative { .. } | Self::SwitchAlternative { .. } => Some(ArtifactProjectionCause::Checkout),\n            Self::CommitCheckpoint { .. } => Some(ArtifactProjectionCause::Checkpoint),\n            Self::PruneDrafts => Some(ArtifactProjectionCause::PruneDrafts),\n            Self::SetMergePolicy { .. } => Some(ArtifactProjectionCause::PolicyChange),\n            Self::ResolveConflict { .. } => Some(ArtifactProjectionCause::RemoteIngest),\n            Self::Supersede { .. } | Self::CreateAlternativeWithSupersede { .. } => Some(ArtifactProjectionCause::Replay),\n            Self::AppendTransaction { .. } | Self::CommitTransaction { .. } => Some(ArtifactProjectionCause::Apply),\n            Self::AbortTransaction { .. } => Some(ArtifactProjectionCause::Undo),\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// 🚦️ Whether this command moves history positions — an undo, redo, checkpoint, alternative, checkout, supersession or\n    /// conflict resolution: what a store whose local history step still replays refuses ([`VcsError::HistoryReplaying`]).\n    pub fn moves_history(&self) -> bool {\n        !self.history_transition_kinds().is_empty() || matches!(self, Self::ResolveConflict { .. })\n    }\n\n    /// 🏷️ Every kind of history transition this command may author, in authoring order: what the store's\n    /// [`crate::os_spr::HistoryShape`] must admit before the command runs.\n    pub fn history_transition_kinds(&self) -> &'static [crate::os_spr::HistoryTransitionKind] {\n        use crate::os_spr::HistoryTransitionKind::{Branch, Checkout, Commit, Reinstate, Revert, Supersede};\n        match self {\n            Self::Undo | Self::UndoWithPolicy { .. } | Self::UndoInLane { .. } => &[Revert],\n            Self::Redo | Self::RedoInLane { .. } => &[Reinstate],\n            Self::CommitCheckpoint { .. } => &[Commit],\n            Self::CreateAlternative { .. } => &[Commit, Branch],\n            Self::SwitchAlternative { .. } | Self::CheckoutCheckpoint { .. } => &[Checkout],\n            Self::Supersede { .. } => &[Supersede],\n            Self::CreateAlternativeWithSupersede { .. } => &[Commit, Branch, Supersede],\n            Self::Apply { .. }\n | Self::AppendTransaction { .. }\n            | Self::CommitTransaction { .. }\n            | Self::AbortTransaction { .. } => &[],\n        }\n    }\n}\n//#endregion 🔖️Schemas\n\n//#region 🔖️Composition\n// 🧩️ Composable-vs-referenceable artifact primitives (ticket `26/08/12/UNIFIED-COMPOSABLE-\n// ARTIFACT-SYSTEM` `📓️design-full-plan.md` §\"1. Kernel primitives\"). Two structurally distinct\n// relationships between artifacts:\n// - a **CHILD** (`ArtifactChild<S>` on the parent's snapshot / `OwnerRef` on the child's own\n//   envelope): the parent creates and deletes it, it has exactly one owner, no pin, no\n//   independent lifecycle, and nests inline in UI — but it is still its OWN `ArtifactEnvelope`\n//   with its own `ArtifactVcs` history and store, never an inline subtree (this crate's own doc\n//   comment / the design doc's \"Child = own envelope\" decision). Consequently a parent's diff\n//   NEVER embeds a child diff.\n// - a **LINK** (`ArtifactLink`/`LinkPin`): an independent lifecycle of its own, a PIN (so it can\n//   be frozen to a specific `Head`/`Checkpoint`/content-addressed `Snapshot`), and renders as a\n//   chip, never nested inline.\n//\n// `ArtifactRefs` lets a snapshot type declare its own children/links (defaulted to none, so a\n// leaf artifact needs zero boilerplate); `LinkResolver`/`ChildStoreFactory` are the host-side\n// seams that turn those declarations into real bytes/stores. `CompositionCoordinator` (its own\n// `🔖️CompositionCoordinator` region, after `🔖️Space` below) orchestrates atomic multi-store\n// dispatch across a parent and its children on top of these types.\n\n/// 🧸️ Ownership handle a parent SNAPSHOT embeds for one owned child slot (e.g. a plugin's\n/// generated field `mesh_child: ArtifactChild<MeshSnapshot>`). `S` is a compile-time-only phantom\n/// naming which snapshot type the child is expected to materialize as — it never appears on the\n/// wire and never constrains this type's own capabilities. `Clone`/`Debug`/`PartialEq` are\n/// hand-implemented below (not `#[derive(..)]`'d): deriving them on a `PhantomData<S>`-carrying\n/// struct adds an unwanted `S: Trait` bound to every impl even though `S` never appears in any\n/// stored/compared data, so those three derives would silently fail to work \"for any `S`\" (the\n/// task's own requirement) the moment a caller picked an `S` that itself didn't implement\n/// `Clone`/`Debug`/`PartialEq`. `Serialize`/`Deserialize` avoid the same trap via `#[serde(bound =\n/// \"\")]` instead of a hand impl — the standard serde idiom for a `PhantomData<S>` field, since\n/// serde's derive macro honors an explicit empty bound list rather than inferring one from `S`.\n/// `local_owner` is a serialization-skipped, immutable materialization retained by this exact\n/// handle; it is intentionally absent from equality, debug, DSL, pack, and JSON identity. No pin,\n/// no independent lifecycle: see the region doc's CHILD-vs-LINK split.\nstruct ArtifactChildLocalText(Arc<str>);\n\n/// 🚫️ Why an owned child's local materialization cannot be read at a typed boundary.\n#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum ArtifactChildMaterializationError {\n    Absent,\n    WrongType,\n}\n\nimpl std::fmt::Display for ArtifactChildMaterializationError {\n    fn fmt(&self, formatter: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {\n        match self {\n            Self::Absent => formatter.write_str(\"artifact child is not materialized\"),\n            Self::WrongType => formatter.write_str(\"artifact child materialization has a different exact type\"),\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nimpl std::error::Error for ArtifactChildMaterializationError {}\n\n/// 🆔️ The content-addressed id of a composed child or persisted scene: `<prefix>-` + the first 16 lowercase hex digits\n/// of SHA-256 over `bytes` (the child schema's `ContentId`). Specified, stable across processes, platforms and\n/// toolchains, and reproducible by any implementation — unlike a `std` hasher, whose algorithm Rust leaves unspecified.\n/// A site that addresses several fields joins them with U+001F. TypeScript twin: `contentId` (`🪆️child/🧬️schema/🟦️.ts`).\npub fn content_id(prefix: &str, bytes: &[u8]) -> String {\n    format!(\"{prefix}-{}\", semio_framework_hash::hex_lower(&semio_framework_hash::Sha256::digest(bytes)[..8]))\n}\n\npub struct ArtifactChild<S> {\n    pub child_id: String,\n    pub target: crate::os_io::ArtifactRef,\n    local_owner: Option<Arc<dyn std::any::Any + Send + Sync>>,\n    _snapshot: PhantomData<S>,\n}\n\nimpl<S> ArtifactChild<S> {\n    /// 🏗️ Constructs a handle, threading the phantom marker for the caller.\n    pub fn new(child_id: String, target: crate::os_io::ArtifactRef) -> Self {\n        Self { child_id, target, local_owner: None, _snapshot: PhantomData }\n    }\n\n    /// 🪆 Attaches an immutable local-only materialization to this owned child handle.\n    pub fn with_local_owner<T: std::any::Any + Send + Sync>(mut self, owner: Arc<T>) -> Self {\n        self.local_owner = Some(owner);\n        self\n    }\n\n    /// 🪆 Replaces this handle's immutable local-only materialization owner.\n    pub fn set_local_owner<T: std::any::Any + Send + Sync>(&mut self, owner: Arc<T>) {\n        self.local_owner = Some(owner);\n    }\n\n    /// 🧵 Retains a type-checked local-only materialization without cloning its payload.\n    pub fn local_owner<T: std::any::Any + Send + Sync>(&self) -> Option<Arc<T>> {\n        Arc::downcast::<T>(self.local_owner.clone()?).ok()\n    }\n\n    /// 📤️ Requires the exact local materialization at content-reading boundaries. Exporters must\n    /// propagate this failure instead of serializing the handle or substituting default content.\n    pub fn require_local_owner<T: std::any::Any + Send + Sync>(&self) -> Result<Arc<T>, ArtifactChildMaterializationError> {\n        let owner = self.local_owner.clone().ok_or(ArtifactChildMaterializationError::Absent)?;\n        Arc::downcast::<T>(owner).map_err(|_| ArtifactChildMaterializationError::WrongType)\n    }\n\n    /// 📤️ Transfers the exact typed local owner; a type mismatch retains the untouched owner.\n    pub fn take_local_owner<T: std::any::Any + Send + Sync>(&mut self) -> Result<Option<Arc<T>>, &'static str> {\n        let Some(owner) = self.local_owner.take() else {\n            return Ok(None);\n        };\n        match Arc::downcast::<T>(owner) {\n            Ok(owner) => Ok(Some(owner)),\n            Err(owner) => {\n                self.local_owner = Some(owner);\n                Err(\"artifact child local owner has a different exact type\")\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// 🪆 Attaches immutable local-only text to this owned child handle.\n    pub fn with_local_text(mut self, text: Arc<str>) -> Self {\n        self.local_owner = Some(Arc::new(ArtifactChildLocalText(text)));\n        self\n    }\n\n    /// 🪆 Replaces this handle's immutable local-only text owner.\n    pub fn set_local_text(&mut self, text: Arc<str>) {\n        self.local_owner = Some(Arc::new(ArtifactChildLocalText(text)));\n    }\n\n    /// 🔎 Borrows this handle's local-only text when the child has been materialized.\n    pub fn local_text(&self) -> Option<&str> {\n        self.local_owner.as_deref()?.downcast_ref::<ArtifactChildLocalText>().map(|owner| owner.0.as_ref())\n    }\n\n    /// 🧵 Retains this handle's local-only text owner without copying its bytes.\n    pub fn local_text_owner(&self) -> Option<Arc<str>> {\n        self.local_owner.as_deref()?.downcast_ref::<ArtifactChildLocalText>().map(|owner| owner.0.clone())\n    }\n\n    /// 🪪️ Drops the compile-time-only `S` phantom, producing the type-erased projection\n    /// `ArtifactRefs::child_refs` returns.\n    pub async fn to_child_ref(&self, slot: &str) -> ChildRef {\n        ChildRef { slot: slot.to_string(), child_id: self.child_id.clone(), target: self.target.clone() }\n    }\n}\n\nimpl<S> Clone for ArtifactChild<S> {\n    fn clone(&self) -> Self {\n        Self { child_id: self.child_id.clone(), target: self.target.clone(), local_owner: self.local_owner.clone(), _snapshot: PhantomData }\n    }\n}\n\nimpl<S> semio_framework_schema_composition::ChildFieldRefs for ArtifactChild<S> {\n    const MANY: bool = false;\n    fn visit_child_field<'a, V: semio_framework_schema_composition::ChildRefVisitor<'a>>(&'a self, slot: &'static str, visitor: &mut V) -> Result<(), V::Error> {\n        visitor.step()?;\n        visitor.child(\n            slot,\n            semio_framework_schema_composition::ChildRefFields {\n                child_id: &self.child_id,\n                artifact_id: &self.target.artifact_id,\n                artifact_kind: &self.target.dialect.artifact_kind,\n                standard: &self.target.dialect.standard,\n                subset: &self.target.dialect.subset,\n            },\n        )\n    }\n}\n\nimpl<S> child_id=ToValue::to_value_controlled(&self.child_id,control).map_err(|error|error.under(\"childId\"))?;fields.get_mut().push((key,child_id));control.step()?;\n            let {value:?}\")));\n        };\n        let mut child_id = None;\n        let mut target = None;\n        for (key, entry) in fields {\n            match key.as_str() {\n                \"childId\" => child_id = Some(String::from_value(entry).map_err(|e| e.under(\"childId\"))?),\n                \"target\" => target = Some(crate::os_io::ArtifactRef::from_value(entry).map_err(|e| e.under(\"target\"))?),\n                _ => return Err(ValueError::new(semio_framework_value::ValueRefusalKind::InvalidValue, format!(\"ArtifactChild has unknown field {key}\"))),\n            }\n from_value_controlled(value:&DslValue,control:&mut protocol::value::NativeDecodeControl<'_>)->Result<Self,ValueError>{\n        let DslValue::Object(fields)=value else{return \"target\"=>target=Some(crate::os_io::ArtifactRef::from_value_controlled(entry,control).map_err(|error|error.under(\"target\"))?),\n                    _=>return control.checkpoint()?;\n            Ok(Self{child_id:child_id.ok_or_else(||ValueError::new(semio_framework_value::ValueRefusalKind::InvalidValue, \"ArtifactChild missing childId\"))?,target:target.ok_or_else(||ValueError::new(semio_framework_value::ValueRefusalKind::InvalidValue, \"ArtifactChild missing target\"))?,local_owner:None,_snapshot:PhantomData})\n        }))\n    }\n\n}\n\n/// 🪪️ Type-erased projection of one `ArtifactChild<S>` field, dropping the compile-time-only\n/// `S` phantom so `ArtifactRefs::child_refs` can return a single homogeneous `Vec` across however\n/// many differently-`S`-typed child slots a snapshot declares.\n#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, ToValue, FromValue)]\n#[value(rename_all = \"camelCase\")]\npub struct ChildRef {\n CHILD_RESTORE_MAXIMUM_REFERENCES: usize = 64;\npub const CHILD_RESTORE_MAXIMUM_FIELD_BYTES: usize = 256;\npub const CHILD_RESTORE_MAXIMUM_VISIT_STEPS: usize = 256;\n\n/// 🛑️ Exact loaded-parent projection failures, before opening or publishing any child store.\n#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum ChildRestoreProjectionError {\n    InvalidSlot,\n    InvalidReference,\n    DuplicateChild,\n    SingularSlot,\n    ReferenceLimit,\n    TraversalLimit,\n    IncompleteSet,\n}\n\nimpl std::fmt::Display for ChildRestoreProjectionError {\n    fn fmt(&self, formatter: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {\n        write!(formatter, \"child restore projection: {self:?}\")\n    }\n}\n\nimpl std::error::Error for ChildRestoreProjectionError {}\n\n/// 🌳️ Bounded borrowed authority derived only from the loaded parent's declared child fields.\n#[derive(Debug)]\npub struct ChildRestoreProjection<'a> {\n    slots: &'static [semio_framework_schema_composition::ChildSlotSpec],\n    rows: [Option<(&'static str, semio_framework_schema_composition::ChildRefFields<'a>)>; CHILD_RESTORE_MAXIMUM_REFERENCES],\n    length: usize,\n    steps: usize,\n}\n\nimpl<'a> ChildRestoreProjection<'a> {\n    /// 🔎️ Visits actual typed snapshot fields without cloning handles, leases or child content.\n    pub fn from_snapshot<S: semio_framework_schema_composition::ArtifactCompositionFields>(snapshot: &'a S) -> Result<Self, ChildRestoreProjectionError> {\n        let slots = S::child_slots();\n        if slots.len() > CHILD_RESTORE_MAXIMUM_REFERENCES {\n            return Err(ChildRestoreProjectionError::ReferenceLimit);\n        }\n        for (index, slot) in slots.iter().enumerate() {\n            if slot.name.is_empty()\n                || slot.name.len() > CHILD_RESTORE_MAXIMUM_FIELD_BYTES\n                || slot.kind.len() > CHILD_RESTORE_MAXIMUM_FIELD_BYTES\n                || !crate::os_io::is_canonical_artifact_kind(slot.kind)\n                || slots[..index].iter().any(|prior| prior.name == slot.name)\n            {\n                return Err(ChildRestoreProjectionError::InvalidSlot);\n            }\n        }\n        let mut projection = Self { slots, rows: [None; CHILD_RESTORE_MAXIMUM_REFERENCES], length: 0, steps: 0 };\n        snapshot.visit_child_refs(&mut projection)?;\n        Ok(projection)\n    }\n\n    /// 🧮️ Number of exact child references carried by this loaded parent.\n    pub fn len(&self) -> usize {\n        self.length\n    }\n\n    /// 🍃️ Whether this projection has no populated child fields.\n    pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {\n        self.length == 0\n    }\n\n    /// 🌿️ Reads one admitted typed expected: &crate::os_io::ArtifactRef) -> bool {\n        self.rows[..self.length].iter().flatten().any(|(name, fields)| {\n            *name == slot\n                && fields.artifact_id == expected.artifact_id\n                && fields.artifact_kind == expected.dialect.artifact_kind\n                && fields.standard == expected.dialect.standard\n                && fields.subset == expected.dialect.subset\n        })\n    }\n\n    /// ⚖️ Admits exactly one unordered complete set: no omission, substitution or duplicate.\n    pub fn admit_complete<'b>(&self, incoming: impl IntoIterator<Item = (&'b str, semio_framework_schema_composition::ChildRefFields<'b>)>) -> Result<(), ChildRestoreProjectionError> {\n        let mut seen = [false; CHILD_RESTORE_MAXIMUM_REFERENCES];\n        let mut count = 0;\n        for (slot, fields) in incoming {\n            if count == CHILD_RESTORE_MAXIMUM_REFERENCES {\n                return Err(ChildRestoreProjectionError::ReferenceLimit);\n            }\n            let index = self.rows[..self.length].iter().position(|entry| entry.as_ref().is_some_and(|(name, expected)| *name == slot && *expected == fields)).ok_or(ChildRestoreProjectionError::IncompleteSet)?;\n            if seen[index] {\n                return Err(ChildRestoreProjectionError::DuplicateChild);\n            }\n spec.kind\n            || [fields.child_id, fields.artifact_id, fields.artifact_kind, fields.standard, fields.subset].iter().any(|field| field.is_empty() || field.len() > embeddable standalone, or does deleting it require going through its\n/// owner\". `child_id` matches the owning `ArtifactChild<S>.child_id`/`ChildRef.child_id` exactly.\n#[path = \"🪆️child/🏠️owner/🧬️schema/🦀️.rs\"]\nmod artifact_child_owner_schema;\npub use artifact_child_owner_schema::OwnerRef;\n\n#[path = \"🔗️link/🧬️schema/🦀️.rs\"]\nmod artifact_link_schema;\npub use A UI/renderer calls this only\n/// when it actually needs to show/open the linked content.\npub trait LinkResolver {\n    async fn resolve(&self, link: &ArtifactLink) -> LinkState;\n}\n\n/// 🗂️ The read-only directory a `MemberLinkResolver` resolves against — whatever holds the\n/// live members (a `SpaceHost`, or a test fixture). using.\npub enum NoBlobStore {}\n\nimpl BlobStore for NoBlobStore {\n    async fn put(&self, _bytes: &[u8], _media_type: &str) -> Result<BlobRef, VcsError> {\n        match *self {}\n    }\n\n }\n\n    async fn delete(&self, _hash: &str) -> Result<(), VcsError> {\n        match *self {}\n    }\n}\n\npub struct MemberLinkResolver<D, B = NoBlobStore> {\n    directory: D,\n    blobs: resolved {\n                    Some(pack_bytes) => LinkState::Resolved { pack_bytes, dialect },\n                    None => LinkState::PinnedOnly { blob: blob.clone() },\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// 🏭️ Generic genesis-construction helper every `space_members!`-generated `MemberFactory::\n/// create` arm calls — the composition sibling of child\n/// without consulting the parent.\npub async fn open_member_store<P, Mutation>(schema: &str, expected: &crate::os_io::ArtifactRef, owner: Option<&OwnerRef>, envelope_pack: &[u8]) -> self::Mutation<P> + OpBinary + OpText + Send + 'static,\n{\n    if owner.is_some_and(|owner| owner.child_id != expected.artifact_id) {\n        return Err(VcsError::Deserialize(\"member owner child parse_decoded_document_spr::<P, Mutation>(&pack, history).await.map_err(|error| VcsError::Deserialize(error.to_string()))?;\n    let mut store = ArtifactStore::new(parsed.envelope).await?;\n dialect_matches = persisted_dialect.is_some_and(|(kind, standard, subset)| kind == &expected.dialect.artifact_kind && standard == &expected.dialect.standard && subset == &expected.dialect.subset);\n crate::os_io::ArtifactRef::parse_uri(parent).is_ok_and(|parent| parent == owner.parent),\n        _ => false,\n    };\n    if history.doc_id != expected.artifact_id || history.schema != schema || !dialect_matches || !owner_matches {\n        return Err(VcsError::Deserialize(\"member envelope does not match requested identity, schema, dialect and ownership\".into()));\n    }\n    Ok(())\n}\n\n//#region 🔖️CompositionDsl\n/// 🧬️ Hand-crafted `crate::os_dsl::DslField` records for `ArtifactChild`/`OwnerRef`/`ArtifactLink`/\n/// `LinkPin` (P6 idiom, the same one `BackboneMessage`'s `OpText`/`OpBinary` impls near\n/// `🔖️Backbone` below use) — NOT new `Shape` variants: the design doc's deviation D1 deliberately\n/// keeps `Shape` closed (it is exhaustively matched in ~20 files) and represents every new value\n/// type here as an ordinary `Shape::Record`. Targets use the canonical literal\n/// `crate::os_io::ArtifactRef` record so each owned reference component remains independent.\n// 🚫️async: E4 fn-pointer slot — value stored in `Shape::Record(fn() -> RecordSpec)`\nfn artifact_child_spec() -> crate::os_dsl::RecordSpec {\n    crate::os_dsl::RecordSpec::new(None, crate::os_dsl::RecordLayout::Inline, vec![crate::os_dsl::FieldSpec::new(0, \"child_id\", crate::os_dsl::Shape::Text), crate::os_dsl::FieldSpec::new(1, \"target\", <crate::os_io::ArtifactRef as crate::os_dsl::DslField>::shape())])\n}\n\nfn artifact_child_spec_controlled<C:crate::os_dsl::NativeSchemaControl>(control:&mut C)->Result<crate::os_dsl::RecordSpec,semio_framework_value::ValueError>{\n    control.scoped_stage(|control|{\n        control.begin_stage(2)?;let mut fields=control.allocate_vec::<crate::os_dsl::FieldSpec>(2)?;\n        fields.push(crate::os_dsl::schema::producer::field(0,\"child_id\",crate::os_dsl::Shape::Text,control)?);control.step()?;\n        let target=<crate::os_io::ArtifactRef as crate::os_dsl::DslField>::shape_controlled(control)?;\n        fields.push(crate::os_dsl::schema::producer::field(1,\"target\",target,control)?);control.step()?;\n        crate::os_dsl::schema::producer::record(None,crate::os_dsl::RecordLayout::Inline,fields,control)\n    })\n}\n\nfn artifact_child_spec_producer()->crate::os_dsl::RecordSpecProducer{\n    crate::os_dsl::RecordSpecProducer{ordinary:artifact_child_spec,decoding:|control|artifact_child_spec_controlled(control),encoding:|control|artifact_child_spec_controlled(control)}\n}\n\n// 🚫️async: E1 pure — record conversion with no suspension point, consumed by the sync\n// `DslField::to_value` impl below. See R9.\nfn artifact_child_to_record<S>(child: &ArtifactChild<S>) -> crate::os_dsl::RecordValue {\n    let mut record = crate::os_dsl::RecordValue::default();\n    record.fields.insert(0, crate::os_dsl::FieldValue::Text(child.child_id.clone()));\n    record.fields.insert(1, <crate::os_io::ArtifactRef as crate::os_dsl::DslField>::to_value(&child.target));\n    record\n}\n\n// 🚫️async: E1 pure — same sync consumer as `artifact_child_to_record`. See R9.\n/// 🧱️ Constructs the persisted child identity and literal target without a local owner.\nfn artifact_child_from_record<S>(record: &crate::os_dsl::RecordValue) -> Result<ArtifactChild<S>, String> {\n    if record.fields.len()!=2||record.fields.keys().any(|id|*id>1){return Err(\"artifact child requires its two literal fields\".into());}\n    let child_id = match record.get(0) {\n        Some(crate::os_dsl::FieldValue::Text(s)) => s.clone(),\n        other => return Err(format!(\"expected child_id, found {other:?}\")),\n    };\n    let target=<crate::os_io::ArtifactRef as crate::os_dsl::DslField>::from_value(record.get(1).ok_or(\"missing artifact child target\")?)?;\n    Ok(ArtifactChild { child_id, target, local_owner: None, _snapshot: PhantomData })\n}\n\nimpl<S> crate::os_dsl::DslField for ArtifactChild<S> {\n    /// 🚫️async: E4 — see `DslField::shape`'s tag on the trait.\n    fn shape() -> crate::os_dsl::Shape {\n        crate::os_dsl::Shape::Record(artifact_child_spec_producer())\n    }\n    fn shape_controlled<C:crate::os_dsl::NativeSchemaControl>(control:&mut crate::os_dsl::NativeEncodeControl<'_>)->Result<crate::os_dsl::FieldValue,semio_framework_value::ValueError>{\n        <Self as crate::os_dsl::DslField>::to_record_controlled(self,control).map(crate::os_dsl::FieldValue::Record)\n    }\n    fn to_record_controlled(&self,control:&mut crate::os_dsl::NativeEncodeControl<'_>)->Result<crate::os_dsl::RecordValue,semio_framework_value::ValueError>{\n        control.scoped_depth(64,|control|control.scoped_stage(|control|{\n            control.begin_stage(2)?;let mut record=crate::os_dsl::native_encoding::EncodedRecord::new(2,control)?;\n usize = 64;\npub const PRESENCE_PEER_ID_BYTES: usize = 256;\n\n#[derive(Debug)]\nstruct PresencePeerEntry<P> {\n    actor: std::mem::ManuallyDrop<String>,\n    presence: fixed byte authority\".into());\n        }\n        let mut next = self.clone_aliases();\n        let mut index = 0usize;\n        while index < next.len && next.entries[index].as_ref().is_some_and(|entry| entry.actor.as_str() < actor.as_str()) {\n            index += 1;\n        }\n        if next.entries.get(index).and_then(Option::as_ref).is_some_and(|entry| entry.actor.as_str() == actor.as_str()) {\n            let retired = next.entries[index].replace(Arc::new(PresencePeerEntry::new(actor, Arc::new(presence), received_at_ms)));\n            return Ok((next, retired));\n        }\n        if next.len == next.entries[cursor + 1] = next.entries[cursor].take();\n        }\n        next.entries[index] = Some(Arc::new(PresencePeerEntry::new(actor, Arc::new(presence), received_at_ms)));\n        next.len += 1;\n        Ok((next, None))\n    }\n\n    fn remove(&self, actor: &str) -> (Self, Option<Arc<PresencePeerEntry<P>>>) {\n        let mut next = self.clone_aliases();\n        let Some(index) = next.entries[..next.len].iter().position(|entry| entry.as_ref().is_some_and(|entry| entry.actor.as_str() == actor)) else {\n            return (next, None);\n        };\n        let retired = next.entries[index].take();\n        for cursor in index..next.len.saturating_sub(1) {\n            next.entries[cursor] = next.entries[cursor + 1].take();\n        }\n        next.len = next.len.saturating_sub(1);\n        next.entries[next.len] = None;\n        (next, retired)\n    }\n\n    fn remove_at(&self, index: usize) -> (Self, Option<Arc<PresencePeerEntry<P>>>) {\n        if index >= self.len {\n            return (self.clone_aliases(), None);\n        }\n        let mut next = self.clone_aliases();\n        let retired = next.entries[index].take();\n        for cursor in index..next.len.saturating_sub(1) {\n            next.entries[cursor] = next.entries[cursor + 1].take();\n        }\n        next.len = next.len.saturating_sub(1);\n        next.entries[next.len] = None;\n        (next, retired)\n    }\n\n    fn retain_received(&self, oldest_allowed_ms: i64) -> (Self, PresencePeersRetiredEntries<P>) {\n        let mut next = Self::empty();\n        let mut retired = PresencePeersRetiredEntries::empty();\n        for entry in self.entries[..self.len].iter().filter_map(Option::as_ref) {\n            if entry.received_at_ms >= oldest_allowed_ms {\n retired.len += 1;\n            }\n        }\n        (next, retired)\n    }\n}\n\n#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub struct PresencePeersCapacityError;\n\npub struct append(&mut self, other: &mut Self) -> Result<(), PresencePeersCapacityError> {\n        if self.len.saturating_add(other.len) > PRESENCE_PEER_SLOTS {\n            return generation_after: self.generation })\n    }\n\n    pub fn peers_root(&self) -> Arc<PresencePeersRoot<P>> {\n        Arc::clone(&self.peers)\n    }\n\n    pub fn install_peer_retirement_factory(&mut retirement factory is already installed\".into());\n        }\n        self.peer_retirement_factory = Some(factory);\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    pub fn peer_retirement_available(&self) -> bool {\n factory.clone()))\n    }\n\n    pub fn publish_peer_commit(&mut self, commit: PresencePeersCommit<P>) -> Result<Option<PresencePeersRetirement<P>>, PresencePeersCommit<P>>\n    where\n        P: Send + Sync + 'static,\n    {\n        if self.close_started || !Arc::ptr_eq(&self.peers, &commit.base_root) || !self.peer_retirement_factory.as_ref().is_some_and(|factory| Arc::ptr_eq(factory, self.generation\n    }\n\n    /// 🪪️ Reads the event-maintained generation at an already-owned operation boundary.\n    pub fn generation_now(&self) -> u64 {\n        self.generation\n    }\n}\n\n/// If a value must survive a reload it belongs in `config`; if a peer must see it, in\n/// `presence`; if it is document content, in the artifact (or its draft).\npub struct TransientStore<P, Mutation> owned_retirement_factory: Arc<dyn ArtifactOwnedValueRetirementFactory<P>>,\n    ) -> Result<ArtifactEphemeralOneItemPublication<P, Mutation>, ArtifactEphemeralOneItemAdmissionRejected<Mutation>>\n -> u64 {\n        self.generation\n    }\n\n    /// ♻️ Detaches this store's exact root/read registry and installs a fresh terminal root.\n    pub fn begin_retirement(&mut self, terminal: P, factory: Arc<dyn ArtifactOwnedValueRetirementFactory<P>>) -> TransientStoreRetirement<P>\n    where\n        P: Send + Sync + 'static,\n    {\n        let next_generation = self.generation.wrapping_add(1);\n transient root plus every returned/live tracked read.\npub struct TransientStoreRetirement<P> {\n    root: std::mem::ManuallyDrop<Option<Arc<P>>>,\n    reads: std::mem::ManuallyDrop<Option<Arc<SnapshotReadLeaseRegistry>>>,\n    active_returned: std::mem::ManuallyDrop<Option<Box<dyn ErasedSnapshotRetirement>>>,\n    active_root: std::mem::ManuallyDrop<Option<Box<dyn ErasedSnapshotRetirement>>>,\n    factory: Option<Arc<dyn ArtifactOwnedValueRetirementFactory<P>>>,\n}\n\nimpl<P> TransientStoreRetirement<P> {\n    fn new<Mutation>(store: TransientStore<P, Mutation>, factory: Arc<dyn ArtifactOwnedValueRetirementFactory<P>>) -> Self {\n        let store = std::mem::ManuallyDrop::new(store);\n        Self {\n            root: std::mem::ManuallyDrop::new(Some(unsafe { std::ptr::read(&store.current) })),\n            reads: std::mem::ManuallyDrop::new(Some(unsafe { std::ptr::read(&store.reads) })),\n            active_returned: std::mem::ManuallyDrop::new(unsafe { std::ptr::read(&store.active_returned_read) }),\n            active_root: std::mem::ManuallyDrop::new(None),\n            factory: Some(factory),\n        }\n    }\n\n    pub fn terminal_is_empty(&self) -> bool {\n        self.root.is_none() && self.reads.is_none() && self.active_returned.is_none() && self.active_root.is_none() && self.factory.is_none()\n    }\n}\n\nimpl<P: Send + Sync + 'static> TransientStoreRetirement<P> {\n    pub fn close_step(&mut self, maximum_items: usize, maximum_bytes: usize) -> Result<SnapshotRetirementStep, semio_framework_value::ValueError> {\n        if maximum_items == 0 {\n            return Ok(SnapshotRetirementStep::Pending { released_items: 0, released_bytes: 0 });\n        }\n        if let Some(reads) = self.reads.as_ref() {\n            if self.active_returned.is_some() || reads.has_returned() {\n                return advance_returned_snapshot_read(reads, &mut self.active_returned, self.factory.as_ref().ok_or_else(|| semio_framework_value::ValueError::new(semio_framework_value::ValueRefusalKind::InvariantViolated, \"transient retirement lost its owned factory\"))?, 1, maximum_bytes);\n            }\n        }\n        if let Some(active) = self.active_root.as_mut() {\n            return match active.close_step(1, maximum_bytes)? {\n                SnapshotRetirementStep::Complete if active.terminal_is_empty() => {\n                    drop(self.active_root.take());\n                    Ok(SnapshotRetirementStep::Pending { released_items: 1, released_bytes: 0 })\n                }\n                SnapshotRetirementStep::Complete => Err(semio_framework_value::ValueError::new(semio_framework_value::ValueRefusalKind::InvariantViolated, \"transient root completed without its exact empty witness\")),\n                SnapshotRetirementStep::Pending { released_items, released_bytes } if released_items > 1 || released_bytes > maximum_bytes => Err(semio_framework_value::ValueError::new(semio_framework_value::ValueRefusalKind::InvariantViolated, \"transient root exceeded its exact grant\")),\n                step => Ok(step),\n            };\n        }\n        if let Some(root) = self.root.take() {\n            *self.active_root = Some(Box::new(ReturnedSnapshotReadRetirement::new(root, }\n}\n\n//#region 🔖️InteractionStore\n/// 🕹️ Ephemeral LOCAL-ONLY lane for the framework interaction mechanism's hover half — the\n/// `PresenceStore`/`TransientStore` sibling for `InteractionState.hover`.\n///\n/// 🎯️ Only hover lives here. Selection + `active_mode`/`active_granularity` are\n/// **persisted-local** (`InteractionState`'s other three fields) and already flow through the\n/// ordinary `ConfigStore` (`ArtifactStore<Config, ConfigMutation>`) via `ArtifactCommand::\n/// ApplyInLane { lane: HistoryLane::Interaction, .. }` — no new store type needed for that half,\n/// it is the ENTIRE point of the `HistoryLane` mechanism above. The caller's `Mutation` impl is expected to route\n    /// through the framework's `next_hover` pure fn before landing here.\n    pub async fn apply(&mut self, mutations: &[Mutation]) -> crate::os_spr::MutationApplyResult<()> {\n        let mut candidate = self.hover.clone();\n        for mutation in mutations {\n            candidate = mutation.diff(&candidate).diff().apply(&candidate)?;\n        }\n        if !mutations.is_empty() {\n            self.hover = candidate;\n            self.generation = self.generation.wrapping_add(1);\n        }\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    /// 🔄️ Discards hover — a host clears this when a view/window closes (nothing left to hover).\n    pub async fn reset(&mut self, hover: S) {\n        self.hover = hover;\n        self.generation = self.generation.wrapping_add(1);\n    }\n\n    /// 🔢️ Bumps on every local hover change; drives the same broadcast-coalescing signal as\n    /// `PresenceStore::generation`.\n    pub async fn generation(&self) -> u64 {\n        self.generation\n    }\n}\n//#endregion 🔖️InteractionStore\n//#endregion 🔖️EphemeralLanes\n//#endregion 🔖️Authority\n\n//#region 🔖️Text\n//#region 🔖️Text\n/// 📍️ 1-based line/column position inside DSL or op-log source text. debt: usize,\n}\n\nimpl<T> BoundedArtifactValueRetirement<T> {\n    fn new(value: T) -> Self {\n        Self { value: std::mem::ManuallyDrop::new(Some(value)), debt: 0 }\n    }\n}\n\nimpl<T: Send + 'static> ErasedSnapshotRetirement for BoundedArtifactValueRetirement<T> {\n    fn close_step(&mut self, maximum_items: usize, maximum_bytes: usize) -> Result<SnapshotRetirementStep, semio_framework_value::ValueError> {\n        if maximum_items == 0 || maximum_bytes == 0 {\n            return Ok(SnapshotRetirementStep::Pending { released_items: 0, released_bytes: 0 });\n        }\n        if self.debt > 0 {\n            let paid = self.debt.min(maximum_bytes);\n            self.debt -= paid;\n            return Ok(SnapshotRetirementStep::Pending { released_items: 0, released_bytes: paid });\n        }\n        if let Some(value) = self.value.take() {\n            drop(value);\n            let paid = ARTIFACT_ENVELOPE_DECODE_PAGE_BYTES.min(maximum_bytes);\n Ok(SnapshotRetirementStep::Complete)\n    }\n\n    fn terminal_is_empty(&self) -> bool {\n        self.value.is_none() && self.debt == 0\n    }\n}\n\nimpl<T> Drop for BoundedArtifactValueRetirement<T> {\n    fn drop(&mut self) {\n        assert!(std::thread::panicking() || (self.value.is_none() && self.debt == 0), \"bounded artifact value retirement reached Drop before exact terminal emptiness\");\n    }\n}\n\nstruct BoundedArtifactRetirementFactory<T>(PhantomData<fn() -> T>);\n\nimpl<T> BoundedArtifactRetirementFactory<T> {\n    fn new() -> Self {\n        Self(PhantomData)\n Arc::new(BoundedArtifactRetirementFactory::<P>::new()),\n        Arc::new(BoundedArtifactRetirementFactory::<P>::new()),\n        Arc::new(BoundedArtifactRetirementFactory::<Mutation>::new()),\n The enclosing `of<P, Mutation>` already requires `'static` of both, so\n        /// saying it here costs nothing and lets the coercion succeed.\n        fn compile_dsl_impl<'a, P, Mutation>(dsl: &'a str, ops: &'a str) -> std::pin::Pin<Box<dyn std::future::Future<Output = Result<(ArtifactPackFiles, String), VcsError>> + Send + 'a>>\n        where\n            P: Clone + ArtifactDsl + ArtifactPack + Send + Sync + 'static,\n            Mutation: OpText + OpBinary + self::Mutation<P> + Send + Sync + 'static,\n        {\n            Box::pin(async move {\n                let parsed: ParsedDocumentText<P, Mutation> = parse_document_text(dsl, ops).await.map_err(|error| VcsError::Deserialize(error.to_string()))?;\n                let envelope = parsed.into_envelope();\n                let pack_files = print_document_pack(&envelope).await;\n                let dsl_mirror = envelope.vcs.initial_snapshot.print_dsl();\n                envelope.retire_unadopted();\n                Ok((pack_files?, dsl_mirror))\n            })\n        }\n\n        /// 🕰️`'static`, not `'a`. The enclosing `of<P, Mutation>` already requires `'static` of both, so\n        /// saying it here costs nothing and lets the coercion succeed.\n        fn print_mirror_impl<'a, P, Mutation>(pack: &'a [u8], spr: &'a [u8]) -> std::pin::Pin<Box<dyn std::future::Future<Output = Result<ArtifactTextFiles, VcsError>> + Send + 'a>>\n        where\n            P: Clone + ArtifactDsl + ArtifactPack + Send + Sync + 'static,\n            Mutation: OpText + OpBinary + self::Mutation<P> + Send + Sync + 'static,\n        {\n            Box::pin(async move {\n                let parsed: ParsedDocumentText<P, Mutation> = parse_document_pack(pack, spr).await.map_err(|error| VcsError::Deserialize(error.to_string()))?;\n                let envelope = parsed.into_envelope();\n                let mirror = print_document_text(&envelope).await;\n                envelope.retire_unadopted();\n                mirror\n            })\n        }\n\n        /// 🎯️ `encode_ops_vec(&[])` is a NON-empty framed header, not a zero-length byte\n        /// slice — the empty-batch fast path must key off the DECODED mutation count, or an\n        /// empty gesture builds a store, hits `EmptyApply`, and (before TC5) aborted in Drop.\n        ///\n        /// 🛂️ The throwaway reduction store gets the framework's own bounded owner\n        /// catalogue. `ArtifactStore::new` installs NONE, and an uninstalled store cannot\n        /// retire: the close cursor below answers `artifact store has no owner-supplied\n        /// bounded disposer` for the first nonempty batch through a LINKED Rust codec —\n        /// the path stdio and gis take on a hub. The guest twin\n        /// (`plugin_runtime::artifact_app_apply_ops`) installs the APP's own catalogue\n        /// there, which this thunk has no app type to ask for; the framework catalogue is\n        /// the exact equivalent for a store that lives only for one reduction (ticket\n        /// 26/09/18 slices TC3e §7d, TC4 §2).\n        ///\n        /// 🗄️ Never `?` while `store` is live: `ArtifactStore`'s Drop asserts a terminal\n        /// shallow shell, so an early return here aborts the process instead of reporting the\n        /// fault. ArtifactPack + Send + Sync + 'static,\n            Mutation: ToValue + FromValue + OpText + OpBinary + self::Mutation<P> + Send + Sync + 'static,\n        {\n            Box::pin(async move {\n {\n                        Some(cursor) => (cursor.applied_edit_ids.clone(), cursor.redo_edit_ids.clone()),\n                        None => (envelope.vcs.edits.iter().map(|edit| edit.id.clone()).collect(), crate::os_vcs::HistoryPageStack::new()),\n                    };\n                    envelope.cursor = Some(ArtifactCursor::new(applied, redo, store.install_document_store_owners_exact(bounded_artifact_store_owners::<P, Mutation>());\n                    store\n                };\n                let applied = replay_envelopes_impl<'a, P, Mutation>(pack: &'a [u8], spr: &'a [u8], envelopes: &'a [u8]) -> ArtifactCodecApplyFuture<'a>\n        where\n            P: Clone + ToValue + FromValue + ArtifactDsl + files.ops))\n            })\n        }\n\n        fn edit_text_from_envelope_impl<'a, P, Mutation>(envelope: &'a crate::os_spr::MutationEnvelope) -> std::pin::Pin<Box<dyn std::future::Future<Output = std::sync::RwLock::new(BTreeMap::new()))\n}\n\n/// ⚠️ A document schema already has a codec owner. The established codec is never replaced.\n#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub struct DocumentCodecRegistryConflict {\n    pub schema: String,\n}\n\n/// ⚠️ Document-codec registration cannot replace an owner or use an unavailable registry.\n#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum DocumentCodecRegistryError {\n    Conflict(DocumentCodecRegistryConflict),\n    Unavailable,\n}\n\nimpl std::fmt::Display for DocumentCodecRegistryError {\n    fn fmt(&self, formatter: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {\n        match self {\n            Self::Conflict(error) => write!(formatter, \"document codec registration conflicts for schema {}\", error.schema),\n            Self::Unavailable => formatter.write_str(\"document codec registry unavailable\"),\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nimpl std::error::Error for DocumentCodecRegistryError {}\n\nfn same_document_codec(left: &ArtifactCodec, right: &ArtifactCodec) -> bool {\n    left.schema == right.schema\n        && left.extension == right.extension\n        && match (left.snapshot_sqlite.as_ref(), right.snapshot_sqlite.as_ref()) {\n            (Some(left), Some(right)) => left.identical_to(right),\n            (None, None) => true,\n            _ => false,\n        }\n        && left.pack_schema_hash == right.pack_schema_hash\n        && std::ptr::fn_addr_eq(left.compile_dsl, right.compile_dsl)\n        && std::ptr::fn_addr_eq(left.print_mirror, right.print_mirror)\n        && std::ptr::fn_addr_eq(left.edit_text_from_envelope, right.edit_text_from_envelope)\n        && std::ptr::fn_addr_eq(left.apply_ops_binary, right.apply_ops_binary)\n        && std::ptr::fn_addr_eq(left.replay_envelopes, right.replay_envelopes)\n}\n\nfn validate_document_codecs(registry: &BTreeMap<String, ArtifactCodec>, codecs: &[ArtifactCodec]) -> Result<(), DocumentCodecRegistryError> {\n    let mut proposed: BTreeMap<&str, &ArtifactCodec> = BTreeMap::new();\n    for codec in codecs {\n        match proposed.get(codec.schema.as_str()) {\n            Some(existing) if same_document_codec(existing, codec) => {}\n            Some(_) => return Err(DocumentCodecRegistryError::Conflict(DocumentCodecRegistryConflict { schema: codec.schema.clone() })),\n            None => {\n                proposed.insert(codec.schema.as_str(), codec);\n            }\n        }\n    }\n    for (schema, codec) in proposed {\n        match registry.get(schema) {\n            Some(existing) if same_document_codec(existing, codec) => {}\n            Some(_) => return Err(DocumentCodecRegistryError::Conflict(DocumentCodecRegistryConflict { schema: schema.to_string() })),\n            None => {}\n        }\n    }\n    Ok(())\n}\n\n/// 🔬️ Verifies document codecs against all established schemas without mutating the registry.\n#[must_use]\npub async fn preflight_document_codecs(codecs: &[ArtifactCodec]) -> Result<(), DocumentCodecRegistryError> {\n    let assembly = begin_artifact_assembly().map_err(|_| DocumentCodecRegistryError::Unavailable)?;\n    preflight_document_codecs_in_assembly(&assembly, codecs)\n}\n\n/// 🔬️ Verifies document codecs while one artifact assembly owns the shared publication barrier.\n#[must_use]\npub fn preflight_document_codecs_in_assembly(_assembly: &ArtifactAssemblyTransaction, codecs: &[ArtifactCodec]) -> Result<(), DocumentCodecRegistryError> {\n    let registry = document_codec_registry().read().map_err(|_| DocumentCodecRegistryError::Unavailable)?;\n    validate_document_codecs(&registry, codecs)\n}\n\n/// 📝️ Registers one schema codec exactly once.
