Collisions fail deterministically before any\n/// replacement can occur, so registration order never changes decoding behavior.\n#[must_use]\npub fn register_document_codec(codec: ArtifactCodec) -> Result<(), DocumentCodecRegistryError> {\n    register_document_codecs(vec![codec])\n}\n\n/// 📝️ Registers document codecs only when every descriptor and executable is conflict-free.\n#[must_use]\npub fn register_document_codecs(codecs: Vec<ArtifactCodec>) -> Result<(), DocumentCodecRegistryError> {\n    let assembly = begin_artifact_assembly().map_err(|_| DocumentCodecRegistryError::Unavailable)?;\n    register_document_codecs_in_assembly(&assembly, codecs)\n}\n\n/// 📝️ Publishes preflighted document codecs while one artifact assembly owns the shared barrier.\n#[must_use]\npub fn register_document_codecs_in_assembly(_assembly: &ArtifactAssemblyTransaction, codecs: Vec<ArtifactCodec>) -> Result<(), DocumentCodecRegistryError> {\n    let mut registry = document_codec_registry().write().map_err(|_| DocumentCodecRegistryError::Unavailable)?;\n    validate_document_codecs(&registry, &codecs)?;\n    for codec in codecs {\n        if !registry.contains_key(&codec.schema) {\n            registry.insert(codec.schema.clone(), codec);\n        }\n    }\n    Ok(())\n}\n\n/// 🔎️ Looks up the codec registered for `schema`, if any.\n#[must_use]\npub async fn document_codec(schema: &str) -> Result<Option<ArtifactCodec>, DocumentCodecRegistryError> {\n    let registry = document_codec_registry().read().map_err(|_| DocumentCodecRegistryError::Unavailable)?;\n    Ok(registry.get(schema).cloned())\n}\n\n/// 🧬️ A component codec answer still in flight. `Send` natively, where document owners run on\n/// the shared worker pool; the browser's single isolate needs no `Send`.\n#[cfg(not(target_arch = \"wasm32\"))]\npub type ComponentDocumentCodecFuture<'a, T> = std::pin::Pin<Box<dyn std::future::Future<Output = Result<T, VcsError>> + Send + 'a>>;\n\n#[cfg(target_arch = \"wasm32\")]\npub type ComponentDocumentCodecFuture<'a, T> = std::pin::Pin<Box<dyn std::future::Future<Output = Result<T, VcsError>> + 'a>>;\n\n/// 🧬️ One document kind's codec as the COMPONENT that owns the kind answers it — the\n/// `world actor` `codec` interface (ticket 26/09/18 slice TC3b) — installed by the host that mounted\n/// that component. A process that links no Rust codec for a kind identifies and validates its documents\n/// through this, exactly as the hub's trusted catalog does for a package it links no codec for\n/// (`🌎️hub/🗿️artifact-authority/🔏️trusted-catalog`'s `VerifiedNativeArtifactCodec`: its linked `codec`,\n/// else its component `guest`).\npub trait ComponentDocumentCodec: Send + Sync {\n    /// 🏷️ The document schema the component owns.\n    fn schema(&self) -> &str;\n    /// 🧬️ `codec.pack-schema-hash`: the kind's structural snapshot fingerprint.\n    fn pack_schema_hash(&self) -> ComponentDocumentCodecFuture<'_, [u8; 32]>;\n    /// 📥️ `codec.print-mirror`: the pair's text mirror, which is also its validation fence.\n    fn print_mirror<'a>(&'a self, pack: &'a [u8], spr: &'a [u8]) -> ComponentDocumentCodecFuture<'a, ArtifactTextFiles>;\n}\n\n/// 🧭️ The one codec a document owner resolves for a schema: the Rust codec this binary links\n/// when it links one, else the component codec installed for the mounted component that owns the kind.\n#[derive(Clone)]\npub enum DocumentKindCodec {\n    Linked(ArtifactCodec),\n    Component(Arc<dyn ComponentDocumentCodec>),\n}\n\nimpl DocumentKindCodec {\n    /// 🧬️ The kind's structural snapshot fingerprint.\n    pub async fn pack_schema_hash(&self) -> Result<[u8; 32], VcsError> {\n        match self {\n            Self::Linked(codec) => Ok(codec.pack_schema_hash),\n            Self::Component(codec) => codec.pack_schema_hash().await,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// 📥️ The pair's text mirror; an `Err` means the pair is not a document of this kind.\n    pub async fn print_mirror(&self, pack: &[u8], spr: &[u8]) -> Result<ArtifactTextFiles, VcsError> {\n        match self {\n            Self::Linked(codec) => (codec.print_mirror)(pack, spr).await,\n            Self::Component(codec) => codec.print_mirror(pack, spr).await,\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nstatic COMPONENT_DOCUMENT_CODEC_REGISTRY: std::sync::OnceLock<std::sync::RwLock<BTreeMap<String, Arc<dyn ComponentDocumentCodec>>>> = std::sync::OnceLock::new();\n\nfn component_document_codec_registry() -> &'static std::sync::RwLock<BTreeMap<String, Arc<dyn ComponentDocumentCodec>>> {\n    COMPONENT_DOCUMENT_CODEC_REGISTRY.get_or_init(|| std::sync::RwLock::new(BTreeMap::new()))\n}\n\n/// 📝️ Installs a mounted component's codec for the schema it owns. A later mount of that kind's\n/// owner replaces an earlier one: in this process the component a host mounted IS the kind's owner.\n#[must_use]\npub fn register_component_document_codec(codec: Arc<dyn ComponentDocumentCodec>) -> Result<(), DocumentCodecRegistryError> {\n    let mut registry = component_document_codec_registry().write().map_err(|_| DocumentCodecRegistryError::Unavailable)?;\n    registry.insert(codec.schema().to_string(), codec);\n    Ok(())\n}\n\n/// 🔎️ Resolves `schema` to the one codec a document owner uses — see [`DocumentKindCodec`].\n#[must_use]\npub async fn document_kind_codec(schema: &str) -> Result<Option<DocumentKindCodec>, DocumentCodecRegistryError> {\n    if let Some(codec) = document_codec(schema).await? {\n        return Ok(Some(DocumentKindCodec::Linked(codec)));\n    }\n    let registry = component_document_codec_registry().read().map_err(|_| DocumentCodecRegistryError::Unavailable)?;\n    Ok(registry.get(schema).cloned().map(DocumentKindCodec::Component))\n}\n\n/// 📜️ Reads the document schema id from an encoded `.spr` history log.\npub async fn lane_schema_from_spr(spr: &[u8]) -> Option<String> {\n    if spr.is_empty() {\n        return None;\n    }\n    crate::os_spr::decode_history(spr, &crate::os_spr::DecodeOptions::default()).await.ok().map(|log| log.schema).filter(|schema| !schema.is_empty())\n}\n//#endregion 🔖️CodecRegistry\n\n//#region 🔖️DialectMigration\n/// 🧬️ One registered lossy/lossless pack-bytes transform between two dialects of the SAME\n/// artifact kind (`from.artifact_kind == to.artifact_kind` is a convention this registry doesn't\n/// itself enforce — callers key by the exact `(from, to)` pair they registered). `migrate_pack` is\n/// a bare `fn` pointer (same non-capturing-bridge-function shape `ArtifactCodec::of` already uses\n/// for `compile_dsl`/`print_mirror`/etc above) so a migration can be a plain top-level fn with zero\n/// closure-capture ceremony. Additive-only: nothing in `ArtifactCodec`/`document_codec`/\n/// `ArtifactStore::dispatch` reads this registry yet — see `26/08/10` D4 evolution slice scope note.\n#[derive(Clone)]\npub struct DialectMigration {\n    pub from: crate::os_io::ArtifactDialect,\n    pub to: crate::os_io::ArtifactDialect,\n    pub lossless: bool,\n    pub migrate_pack: fn(&[u8]) -> Result<Vec<u8>, String>,\n}\n\nstatic DIALECT_MIGRATION_REGISTRY: std::sync::OnceLock<std::sync::RwLock<BTreeMap<(crate::os_io::ArtifactDialect, crate::os_io::ArtifactDialect), DialectMigration>>> = std::sync::OnceLock::new();\n\nfn dialect_migration_registry() -> &'static std::sync::RwLock<BTreeMap<(crate::os_io::ArtifactDialect, crate::os_io::ArtifactDialect), DialectMigration>> {\n    DIALECT_MIGRATION_REGISTRY.get_or_init(|| std::sync::RwLock::new(BTreeMap::new()))\n}\n\n/// ⚠️ Dialect-migration registration cannot overwrite an owner or cross artifact kinds.\n#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum DialectMigrationRegistryError {\n    CrossArtifactKind { from: crate::os_io::ArtifactDialect, to: crate::os_io::ArtifactDialect },\n    Conflict { from: crate::os_io::ArtifactDialect, to: crate::os_io::ArtifactDialect },\n    Unavailable,\n}\n\nimpl std::fmt::Display for DialectMigrationRegistryError {\n    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {\n        match self {\n            Self::CrossArtifactKind { from, to } => write!(f, \"dialect migration crosses artifact kinds from {from:?} to {to:?}\"),\n            Self::Conflict { from, to } => write!(f, \"dialect migration conflict from {from:?} to {to:?}\"),\n            Self::Unavailable => write!(f, \"dialect migration registry unavailable\"),\n        }\n    }\n}\nimpl std::error::Error for DialectMigrationRegistryError {}\n\n/// 🚫️ A migration was unavailable or the registered executable rejected its input.\n#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum DialectMigrationError {\n    Missing { from: crate::os_io::ArtifactDialect, to: crate::os_io::ArtifactDialect },\n    Unavailable,\n    Rejected(String),\n}\n\nfn same_dialect_migration(left: &DialectMigration, right: &DialectMigration) -> bool {\n    left.from == right.from && left.to == right.to && left.lossless == right.lossless && std::ptr::fn_addr_eq(left.migrate_pack, right.migrate_pack)\n}\n\nfn validate_dialect_migrations(registry: &BTreeMap<(crate::os_io::ArtifactDialect, crate::os_io::ArtifactDialect), DialectMigration>, migrations: &[DialectMigration]) -> Result<(), DialectMigrationRegistryError> {\n    let mut proposed: BTreeMap<(crate::os_io::ArtifactDialect, crate::os_io::ArtifactDialect), &DialectMigration> = BTreeMap::new();\n    for migration in migrations {\n        if migration.from.artifact_kind != migration.to.artifact_kind {\n            return Err(DialectMigrationRegistryError::CrossArtifactKind { from: migration.from.clone(), to: migration.to.clone() });\n        }\n        let key = (migration.from.clone(), migration.to.clone());\n        match proposed.get(&key) {\n            Some(existing) if same_dialect_migration(existing, migration) => {}\n            Some(_) => return Err(DialectMigrationRegistryError::Conflict { from: key.0, to: key.1 }),\n            None => {\n                proposed.insert(key, migration);\n            }\n        }\n    }\n    for (key, migration) in proposed {\n        match registry.get(&key) {\n            Some(existing) if same_dialect_migration(existing, migration) => {}\n            Some(_) => return Err(DialectMigrationRegistryError::Conflict { from: key.0, to: key.1 }),\n            None => {}\n        }\n    }\n    Ok(())\n}\n\n/// 🔬️ Verifies a migration set against established dialect pairs without mutation.\n#[must_use]\npub async fn preflight_dialect_migrations(migrations: &[DialectMigration]) -> Result<(), DialectMigrationRegistryError> {\n    let assembly = begin_artifact_assembly().map_err(|_| DialectMigrationRegistryError::Unavailable)?;\n    preflight_dialect_migrations_in_assembly(&assembly, migrations).await\n}\n\n/// 🔬️ Verifies migrations while one artifact assembly owns the shared publication barrier.\n#[must_use]\npub async fn preflight_dialect_migrations_in_assembly(_assembly: &ArtifactAssemblyTransaction, migrations: &[DialectMigration]) -> Result<(), DialectMigrationRegistryError> {\n    let registry = dialect_migration_registry().read().map_err(|_| DialectMigrationRegistryError::Unavailable)?;\n    validate_dialect_migrations(&registry, migrations)\n}\n\n/// 📝️ Registers a migration only when its full descriptor and executable identity match.\n#[must_use]\npub fn register_dialect_migration(migration: DialectMigration) -> Result<(), DialectMigrationRegistryError> {\n    register_dialect_migrations(vec![migration])\n}\n\n/// 📝️ Registers migrations only when every candidate pair is conflict-free.\n#[must_use]\npub fn register_dialect_migrations(migrations: Vec<DialectMigration>) -> Result<(), DialectMigrationRegistryError> {\n    let assembly = begin_artifact_assembly().map_err(|_| DialectMigrationRegistryError::Unavailable)?;\n    register_dialect_migrations_in_assembly(&assembly, migrations)\n}\n\n/// 📝️ Publishes preflighted migrations while one artifact assembly owns the shared barrier.\n#[must_use]\npub fn register_dialect_migrations_in_assembly(_assembly: &ArtifactAssemblyTransaction, migrations: Vec<DialectMigration>) -> Result<(), DialectMigrationRegistryError> {\n    let mut registry = dialect_migration_registry().write().map_err(|_| DialectMigrationRegistryError::Unavailable)?;\n    validate_dialect_migrations(&registry, &migrations)?;\n    for migration in migrations {\n        let key = (migration.from.clone(), migration.to.clone());\n        registry.entry(key).or_insert(migration);\n    }\n    Ok(())\n}\n\n/// 🔁️ Looks up the exact `(from, to)` migration and runs its `migrate_pack` over\n/// `pack_bytes`, or a clear `Err` naming both dialect coordinates when none is registered.\n#[must_use]\npub async fn migrate_document(from: &crate::os_io::ArtifactDialect, to: &crate::os_io::ArtifactDialect, pack_bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<Vec<u8>, DialectMigrationError> {\n    let registry = dialect_migration_registry().read().map_err(|_| DialectMigrationError::Unavailable)?;\n    let migration = registry.get(&(from.clone(), to.clone())).ok_or_else(|| DialectMigrationError::Missing { from: from.clone(), to: to.clone() })?;\n    (migration.migrate_pack)(pack_bytes).map_err(DialectMigrationError::Rejected)\n}\n\n/// 🧷️ All writable store registries held before an artifact assembly can publish anything.\npub struct ArtifactAssemblyStoreRegistryGuards<'assembly> {\n    document_codecs: std::sync::RwLockWriteGuard<'static, BTreeMap<String, ArtifactCodec>>,\n    dialect_migrations: std::sync::RwLockWriteGuard<'static, BTreeMap<(crate::os_io::ArtifactDialect, crate::os_io::ArtifactDialect), DialectMigration>>,\n    _assembly: &'assembly ArtifactAssemblyTransaction,\n}\n\n/// 🚫️ A staged store registry assembly cannot be preflighted or committed.\n#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum ArtifactAssemblyStoreRegistryError {\n    DocumentCodec(DocumentCodecRegistryError),\n    DialectMigration(DialectMigrationRegistryError),\n}\n\nimpl std::fmt::Display for ArtifactAssemblyStoreRegistryError {\n    fn fmt(&self, formatter: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {\n        match self {\n            Self::DocumentCodec(error) => error.fmt(formatter),\n            Self::DialectMigration(error) => error.fmt(formatter),\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nimpl std::error::Error for ArtifactAssemblyStoreRegistryError {}\n\n/// 🧷️ Acquires every store registry write lock before an assembly validates or mutates state.\n#[must_use]\npub fn acquire_artifact_assembly_store_registry_guards<'assembly>(assembly: &'assembly ArtifactAssemblyTransaction) -> Result<ArtifactAssemblyStoreRegistryGuards<'assembly>, ArtifactAssemblyStoreRegistryError> {\n    let document_codecs = document_codec_registry().write().map_err(|_| ArtifactAssemblyStoreRegistryError::DocumentCodec(DocumentCodecRegistryError::Unavailable))?;\n    let dialect_migrations = dialect_migration_registry().write().map_err(|_| ArtifactAssemblyStoreRegistryError::DialectMigration(DialectMigrationRegistryError::Unavailable))?;\n    Ok(ArtifactAssemblyStoreRegistryGuards { document_codecs, dialect_migrations, _assembly: assembly })\n}\n\n/// 🔬️ Verifies all staged store rows while every affected write lock is already held.\n#[must_use]\npub fn preflight_artifact_assembly_store_registry_guards(guards: &ArtifactAssemblyStoreRegistryGuards<'_>, document_codecs: &[ArtifactCodec], dialect_migrations: &[DialectMigration]) -> Result<(), ArtifactAssemblyStoreRegistryError> {\n    validate_document_codecs(&guards.document_codecs, document_codecs).map_err(ArtifactAssemblyStoreRegistryError::DocumentCodec)?;\n    validate_dialect_migrations(&guards.dialect_migrations, dialect_migrations).map_err(ArtifactAssemblyStoreRegistryError::DialectMigration)\n}\n\n/// 📌️ Publishes rows proven safe by `preflight_artifact_assembly_store_registry_guards`.\npub fn commit_artifact_assembly_store_registry_guards(guards: &mut ArtifactAssemblyStoreRegistryGuards<'_>, document_codecs: Vec<ArtifactCodec>, dialect_migrations: Vec<DialectMigration>) {\n    for codec in document_codecs {\n        guards.document_codecs.entry(codec.schema.clone()).or_insert(codec);\n    }\n    for migration in dialect_migrations {\n        let key = (migration.from.clone(), migration.to.clone());\n        guards.dialect_migrations.entry(key).or_insert(migration);\n    }\n}\n//#endregion 🔖️DialectMigration\n\n//#region 🔖️MergeHelpers\n/// 🌳️ Walks `checkpoint_id`'s ancestor chain via `parent_id` back to the root, nearest-first\n/// (`checkpoint_id` itself is the first entry). Cycle-guarded (a malformed/adversarial parent chain\n/// stops instead of looping forever) — every well-formed chain built by `reconcile_alternative`/\n/// `CommitCheckpoint` is already acyclic, this is defense in depth, not a documented invariant break.\nasync fn checkpoint_ancestors<P, Mutation>(envelope: &ArtifactEnvelope<P, Mutation>, checkpoint_id: &str) -> Vec<String> {\n    let mut chain = Vec::new();\n    let mut seen = HashSet::new();\n    let mut current = Some(checkpoint_id.to_string());\n    while let Some(id) = current {\n        if !seen.insert(id.clone()) {\n            break;\n        }\n        let parent = envelope.vcs.checkpoints.iter().find(|checkpoint| checkpoint.id == id).and_then(|checkpoint| checkpoint.parent_id.clone());\n        chain.push(id);\n        current = parent;\n    }\n    chain\n}\n\n/// 🌳️ The merge-base of checkpoints `a` and `b`: the nearest checkpoint common to both\n/// ancestor chains (via `parent_id`), or `None` if their histories share no common ancestor.\n/// Supports branch-merge tooling that needs to know \"everything since the fork point\" on either\n/// side. `b`'s chain is walked nearest-to-farthest so the FIRST hit in `a`'s ancestor set is the\n/// nearest (not merely *a*) common ancestor.\npub async fn merge_base<P, Mutation>(envelope: &ArtifactEnvelope<P, Mutation>, a: &str, b: &str) -> Option<String> {\n    let ancestors_a: HashSet<String> = checkpoint_ancestors(envelope, a).await.into_iter().collect();\n    checkpoint_ancestors(envelope, b).await.into_iter().find(|id| ancestors_a.contains(id))\n}\n\n/// 🌀️ `alternative_id` is both cloned and returned below — a future can only be awaited once\n/// (R10 shape 2), so it is resolved to a plain `String` here.\n///\n/// 🌀️ Same reasoning as `alternative_id` above — resolved once, before it is borrowed AND moved.\n///\n/// 🎯️ `&[]`: reconcile-alternative checkpoints carry no composition pins yet — the\n/// `CompositionCoordinator` that populates real `CompositionPin`s on commit is a later wave.\npub async fn reconcile_alternative<P, Mutation>(envelope: &mut ArtifactEnvelope<P, Mutation>, alternative_name: &str, checkpoint_message: Option<String>, authors: Vec<Author>) -> Result<String, VcsError>\nwhere\n    P: Clone + ToValue + FromValue,\n    Mutation: Clone + ToValue + FromValue,\n{\n    if envelope.vcs.checkpoints.is_empty() {\n        return Err(VcsError::NoCheckpoint);\n    }\n    let checkpoint_id = envelope.vcs.checkpoints.last().map(|checkpoint| checkpoint.id.clone()).ok_or(VcsError::NoCheckpoint)?;\n    let alternative_id = mint_alternative_id(alternative_name, std::slice::from_ref(&checkpoint_id)).await;\n    envelope.vcs.alternatives.try_push(Alternative { id: alternative_id.clone(), name: alternative_name.to_string(), checkpoint_ids: vec![checkpoint_id] }).map_err(|_| VcsError::ValidationFailed(\"alternative history ledger is saturated\".into()))?;\n    if let Some(message) = checkpoint_message {\n        let change = Change { id: mint_change_id(&[], Some(&message)).await, edit_ids: Vec::new(), description: Some(message), saved_at: now_iso() };\n        let parent = envelope.vcs.checkpoints.last();\n        let parent_id = parent.map(|checkpoint| checkpoint.id.clone());\n        let mut change_ids = parent.map(|checkpoint| checkpoint.change_ids.clone()).unwrap_or_default();\n        change_ids.push(change.id.clone());\n        envelope.vcs.changes.try_push(change).map_err(|_| VcsError::ValidationFailed(\"change history ledger is saturated\".into()))?;\n        let timestamp = now_iso();\n        let checkpoint_message = Some(\"reconciled\".to_string());\n        let id = content_addressed_checkpoint_id(parent_id.as_deref(), &change_ids, &envelope.vcs.changes, checkpoint_message.as_deref(), &authors, &timestamp, &[]).await;\n        envelope\n            .vcs\n            .checkpoints\n            .try_push(Checkpoint { id, change_ids, parent_id, authors, message: checkpoint_message, timestamp, composition_pins: Vec::new() })\n            .map_err(|_| VcsError::ValidationFailed(\"checkpoint history ledger is saturated\".into()))?;\n    }\n    Ok(alternative_id)\n}\n//#endregion 🔖️MergeHelpers\n\n//#region 🔖️Config\npub type ConfigEnvelope<C, ConfigMutation> = ArtifactEnvelope<C, ConfigMutation>;\npub type ConfigStore<C, ConfigMutation> = ArtifactStore<C, ConfigMutation>;\n\n/// 🎚️ A config store's envelope: a document envelope whose history holds undo and redo only\n/// ([`crate::os_spr::HistoryShape::Config`]).\npub async fn create_config_envelope<C, ConfigMutation>(schema: &str, id: &str, initial_snapshot: C, backbone: Option<ArtifactBackboneRef>) -> ConfigEnvelope<C, ConfigMutation>\nwhere\n    C: Clone,\n{\n    let mut envelope = create_document_envelope(schema, id, initial_snapshot, backbone);\n    envelope.history_shape = crate::os_spr::HistoryShape::Config;\n    envelope\n}\n\n/// 🧮️ Config snapshots use the same DSL law as documents — `ConfigRecord` marks config types.\npub trait ConfigRecord: ArtifactDsl {}\n\n/// 🎯️ Marks `$ty` as whole-record (no field-level diff — an operation replaces the entire\n/// config) with the trivial `ConfigRecord` + `MutationDiff<Self>` pair every hand-rolled\n/// `impl crate::os_store::ConfigRecord for XConfig {}` + `impl crate::os_spr::MutationDiff<XConfig> for XConfig {\n/// fn apply(...) -> XConfig { self.clone() } fn absorb(...) { *self = other; } }` duo repeated\n/// (~33 crates) — `impl_whole_record_config!(XConfig);` replaces both. The orphan rule still\n/// requires the macro invoked from `$ty`'s own crate (relies on the caller already having\n/// `protocol` in scope by name, exactly as every hand-rolled impl this replaces already did).\n#[macro_export]\nmacro_rules! impl_whole_record_config {\n    ($ty:ty) => {\n        impl $crate::ConfigRecord for $ty {}\n        impl ::protocol::MutationDiff<$ty> for $ty {\n            fn apply(&self, _base: &$ty) -> ::protocol::MutationApplyResult<$ty> {\n                Ok(self.clone())\n            }\n            fn absorb(&mut self, other: Self) {\n                *self = other;\n            }\n        }\n    };\n}\n\n// config_spec_* removed — ConfigSpec is UI (framework-core); avoids kernel↔core cycle\n//#endregion 🔖️Config\n\n//#region 🔖️Materialize\npub fn create_document_envelope<P, Mutation>(schema: &str, id: &str, initial_snapshot: P, backbone: Option<ArtifactBackboneRef>) -> ArtifactEnvelope<P, Mutation>\nwhere\n    P: Clone,\n{\n    ArtifactEnvelope::from_owners(ArtifactEnvelopeOwners {\n        schema: schema.into(),\n        id: id.into(),\n        vcs: ArtifactVcs { initial_snapshot, edits: ArtifactHistoryLedger::new(), changes: ArtifactHistoryLedger::new(), checkpoints: ArtifactHistoryLedger::new(), alternatives: ArtifactHistoryLedger::new() },\n        backbone,\n        active_alternative_id: None,\n        cursor: Some(ArtifactCursor::default()),\n        dialect: None,\n        migrated_from: None,\n        owner: None,\n        lanes: BTreeMap::new(),\n        edit_messages: ArtifactEditMessageLedger::new(),\n        conflicts: Vec::new(),\n        transitions: Vec::new(),\n        history_shape: crate::os_spr::HistoryShape::Document,\n        open_transaction: None,\n        viewer_checkpoint_id: None,\n    })\n}\n\npub async fn edit_ids_for_changes<P, Mutation>(envelope: &ArtifactEnvelope<P, Mutation>, change_ids: &[String]) -> Vec<String>\nwhere\n    Mutation: Clone,\n    P: Clone,\n{\n    let mut edit_ids = Vec::new();\n    for change_id in change_ids {\n        if let Some(change) = envelope.vcs.changes.iter().find(|entry| entry.id == *change_id) {\n            edit_ids.extend(change.edit_ids.iter().cloned());\n        }\n    }\n    edit_ids\n}\n\n/// 🔂️ Full raw fold of `initial_snapshot` over every `applied_edit_ids` edit's `forwards`.\n/// `crate::os_spr::command::Mutation::reconcile` and its diagnostic-bag-returning twin\n/// `materialize_document_snapshot_with_conflicts` are GONE\n/// (`26/08/16/MUTATION-OUTCOMES-MERGE-POLICIES-AND-FIRST-CLASS-CONFLICTS` §C6/C10) — concurrent-merge\n/// arbitration is now `ArtifactStore::ingest_remote`/`resolve_conflict`'s job against\n/// `📡️spr/⚔️conflict`'s first-class `Conflict`/`MergeReport`, not a post-materialization hook here.\npub async fn materialize_document_snapshot<P, Mutation, I, S>(envelope: &ArtifactEnvelopeOwners<P, Mutation>, applied_edit_ids: I) -> Result<P, VcsError>\nwhere\n    P: Clone,\n    Mutation: self::Mutation<P> + OpBinary,\n    I: IntoIterator<Item = S>,\n    S: AsRef<str>,\n{\n    let supersessions = fold_envelope_history(envelope)?.supersessions;\n    let mut snapshot = ReplayProjection::<P, Mutation>::new(envelope.vcs.initial_snapshot.clone());\n    for edit_id in applied_edit_ids {\n        let edit_id = edit_id.as_ref();\n        let edit = envelope.vcs.edits.find_near(|entry| entry.id == edit_id).ok_or_else(|| VcsError::UnknownEdit(edit_id.to_string()))?;\n        fold_effective_edit(&mut snapshot, edit, &envelope.schema, &supersessions, usize::MAX);\n    }\n    Ok(snapshot.into_inner())\n}\n\n/// 🕰️ Single timestamp source for `Edit.started_at`/`Checkpoint.timestamp` — re-exported so\n/// callers outside this crate (e.g. the framework session command log) stamp entries in the\n/// exact same format.\npub fn now_iso() -> String {\n    format!(\"{}\", now_ms())\n}\n\n/// 🪪️ A Store's replica clock: its `actor` is fresh platform entropy per Store instance, the\n/// identity every edit and operation id this Store mints is namespaced by. Refusing to construct\n/// without entropy is deliberate — a constant replica makes two sessions' first edits collide.\nfn fresh_replica_clock() -> HybridLogicalTimestamp {\n    HybridLogicalTimestamp::new(crate::os_identity::entropy_u64().expect(\"artifact store replica identity requires platform entropy\"), now_ms())\n}\n\nfn now_ms() -> u64 {\n    #[cfg(any(not(target_arch = \"wasm32\"), target_env = \"p2\"))]\n    {\n        use std::time::{SystemTime, UNIX_EPOCH};\n        SystemTime::now().duration_since(UNIX_EPOCH).map_or(0, |duration| duration.as_millis() as u64)\n    }\n    #[cfg(all(target_arch = \"wasm32\", not(target_env = \"p2\")))]\n    {\n        js_sys::Date::now() as u64\n    }\n}\n\n/// 🩺️ Defense in depth, NOT the fix for the id-domain discontinuity itself (see {@link\n/// stamp_primary_operation_identity}, which is): every id this returns is about to become a\n/// `Change.edit_ids` entry, so if one isn't backed by a real `envelope.vcs.edits` entry, a much\n/// louder and more specific `debug_assert!` here beats discovering it two calls later as\n/// `validate_durable_history`'s cryptic \"invalid edit reference\". Deliberately does NOT filter the\n/// id out in release builds — silently shrinking the checkpoint would drop a real edit out of\n/// history without a trace, exactly the failure mode `checkpoint_after_ingesting_a_remote_edit_\n/// stays_valid_once_the_sender_s_own_checkpoint_snapshot_arrives`'s doc comment warns against.\nasync fn uncommitted_edit_ids<P, Mutation, I, S>(envelope: &ArtifactEnvelope<P, Mutation>, applied_edit_ids: I) -> Vec<String>\nwhere\n    Mutation: Clone,\n    P: Clone,\n    I: IntoIterator<Item = S>,\n    S: AsRef<str>,\n{\n    let committed: HashSet<String> = envelope.vcs.changes.iter().flat_map(|change| change.edit_ids.iter().cloned()).collect();\n    applied_edit_ids\n        .into_iter()\n        .map(|id| id.as_ref().to_string())\n        .filter(|id| !committed.contains(id))\n        .inspect(|id| debug_assert!(envelope.vcs.edits.iter().any(|edit| edit.id == *id), \"uncommitted_edit_ids: {id} is applied but has no backing envelope.vcs.edits entry — the checkpoint about to reference it will fail validate_durable_history\"))\n        .collect()\n}\n\n/// 🪪️ For a SINGLE-op edit only, overrides its sole `mutation_meta[0].mutation_id` with the edit's\n/// own real `id` — preserving a SINGLE global edit-id domain across the wire for the dominant case\n/// (one atomic user action, one forward op). `replay_mutations` always pre-fills\n/// `mutation_meta[i].mutation_id` (`mutation.mutation_id().unwrap_or_else(mint_mutation_id` of the\n/// raw op bytes), so by the time an `Edit` exists it is never absent — a plain `is_none()` guard\n/// would never fire. `mutation_id()` has exactly one implementor repo-wide (the\n/// `crate::os_spr::Mutation<P>` trait's own `None` default — confirmed zero overrides), so op 0\n/// always carries `mint_mutation_id`'s hash of the raw op bytes and its replica clock tick: an identity that shares\n/// nothing with `edit.id` (`mint_edit_id`'s replica+sequence+full-fingerprint hash) by construction of\n/// the two different formulas — not merely \"sometimes absent\". For a single-op edit, op 0 IS the\n/// edit's entire wire identity (`crate::os_spr::mutation_ids_for_edit`'s only entry for it), so\n/// overriding it to the edit's real id means `edit_from_operation_envelope` reconstructs an EXACT\n/// id match on every receiving store, instead of a content-hash id that never existed locally and\n/// cannot resolve a history transition naming it. MUST NOT extend to a genuine multi-op edit\n/// (`forwards.len() > 1`): `ingest_remote` reconstructs one local single-forward `Edit` per WIRE op,\n/// so giving op 0 the parent edit's bare id would make that receiver's one-forward edit share its\n/// id with the author's N-forward edit. Multi-op ops keep their content-hash ids.\n/// Called from every fresh-edit constructor (`apply_command`); a streamed transaction tick always\n/// appends beyond index 0 of its open edit, so it never qualifies. See\n/// `checkpoint_after_ingesting_a_remote_edit_stays_valid_once_the_sender_s_own_checkpoint_snapshot_arrives`\n/// > for the regression this fixes.\nfn stamp_primary_operation_identity<Mutation>(edit: &mut Edit<Mutation>) {\n    if edit.forwards.len() != 1 {\n        return;\n    }\n    if let Some(first) = edit.mutation_meta.first_mut() {\n        first.mutation_id = Some(MutationId(edit.id.clone()));\n    }\n}\n\n/// 🕊️ `CommitCheckpoint`'s \"nothing uncommitted\" rejection message — a `pub const`, not an inline\n/// literal, so a caller (e.g. `VcsArtifactApp::dispatch_action` in `🔌️plugin/🦀️.rs`) can\n/// recognize this SPECIFIC, benign outcome by value rather than duplicating the string. Genuinely\n/// benign, not just here to silence an error: after a `CommitCheckpoint` dispatch's own `pump()`\n/// absorbs a peer's checkpoint that already covers every edit this store has applied (a real,\n/// expected outcome of full convergence — see\n/// `checkpoint_after_ingesting_a_remote_edit_stays_valid_once_the_sender_s_own_checkpoint_snapshot_arrives`'s\n/// sibling scenario), there is truly nothing left to commit — the same \"requested but nothing to\n/// do\" shape as `VcsError::NothingToUndo`/`NothingToRedo`, just without a dedicated variant.\npub const EMPTY_CHECKPOINT_MESSAGE: &str = \"cannot create an empty checkpoint\";\n\n//#endregion 🔖️Materialize\n\n//#region 🔖️TextFormat\n//#region 🔖️TextFormat\n/// 📄️ The two files a textual VCS document is made of: the DSL text (initial snapshot) and\n/// the append-only op log (every edit ever created, forwards-only — see {@link parse_document_text}).\n#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub struct ArtifactTextFiles {\n    pub dsl: String,\n    pub ops: String,\n}\n\n/// 🧩️ The result of loading a document from text: the reconstructed envelope plus the live\n/// snapshot folded from every edit, so a caller never has to replay again after loading.\n#[derive(Debug, PartialEq)]\npub struct ParsedDocumentText<P, Mutation> {\n    pub envelope: ArtifactEnvelope<P, Mutation>,\n    pub snapshot: P,\n}\n\nimpl<P, Mutation: self::Mutation<P>> ParsedDocumentText<P, Mutation> {\n    /// 🧊️ Takes the envelope and RETIRES the replayed projection beside it. Every load path wants the\n    /// envelope only — the store rebuilds its own head projection from the cursor — and a bare\n    /// `parsed.envelope` partial move leaves `snapshot` to drop, which aborts the process for any\n    /// artifact whose projection owns a fail-closed root (`🌱️value/🗂️ordered/🦀️.rs`'s `Drop`). That is\n    /// what killed every `.pack`/`.spr` load of a generation3d document\n    /// (ticket 26/09/09/PROCEDURAL-3D-END-TO-END).\n    pub fn into_envelope(self) -> ArtifactEnvelope<P, Mutation> {\n        let Self { envelope, snapshot } = self;\n        retire_replayed_projection::<P, Mutation>(snapshot);\n        envelope\n    }\n\n    /// 🔭️ The mirror of [`Self::into_envelope`]: takes the LIVE replayed projection and discards the\n    /// history beside it through the same bounded path a refused parse already uses. For a reader\n    /// that wants to LOOK at a document it will never edit — an inference computing over the\n    /// artifact a caller named, which owns no store to put an envelope in — and which must not let\n    /// the envelope fall out of scope, because every terminal shell below it asserts in `Drop` that\n    /// its owners were retired first.\n    pub fn into_snapshot(self) -> P {\n        let Self { envelope, snapshot } = self;\n        discard_parsed_envelope::<P, Mutation>(envelope);\n        snapshot\n    }\n}\n\n//#region 🔖️OpsHeaderGrammar\n/// 🖋️ One `by=[...]` list entry on a `commit` line: id then name, both positional\n/// (bare-preferred, quoted only when needed — e.g. a name containing a space), then the optional\n/// avatar — every field the transition's content-addressed id covers.\n#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, DslRecord)]\nstruct OpsAuthor {\n    #[dsl(positional)]\n    id: String,\n    #[dsl(positional)]\n    name: String,\n    avatar: Option<String>,\n}\n\nimpl From<&Author> for OpsAuthor {\n    fn from(author: &Author) -> Self {\n        Self { id: author.id.clone(), name: author.name.clone(), avatar: author.avatar.clone() }\n    }\n}\n\nimpl From<OpsAuthor> for Author {\n    fn from(author: OpsAuthor) -> Self {\n        Self { id: author.id, name: author.name, avatar: author.avatar }\n    }\n}\n\n/// 📌️ One `pins=[...]` entry on a `repin` line: child artifact uri, then its checkpoint.\n#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, DslRecord)]\nstruct OpsPin {\n    #[dsl(positional)]\n    child: String,\n    #[dsl(positional)]\n    checkpoint: String,\n}\n\n/// ✏️ One `inputs=[...]` entry on a `supersede` line: the superseded operation, then its\n/// replacement — `schema` plus the base64 `OpBinary` `payload`, or neither for a withdrawal.\n#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, DslRecord)]\nstruct OpsSupersededInput {\n    #[dsl(positional)]\n    target: String,\n    schema: Option<String>,\n    payload: Option<String>,\n}\n\nimpl From<crate::os_spr::SupersededInput> for OpsSupersededInput {\n    fn from(input: crate::os_spr::SupersededInput) -> Self {\n        match input.replacement {\n            crate::os_spr::InputReplacement::Input { schema, payload } => Self { target: input.target.0, schema: Some(schema), payload: Some(semio_framework_io_base64::base64_standard_encode(&payload)) },\n            crate::os_spr::InputReplacement::Withdrawn => Self { target: input.target.0, schema: None, payload: None },\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nimpl TryFrom<OpsSupersededInput> for crate::os_spr::SupersededInput {\n    type Error = String;\n\n    fn try_from(input: OpsSupersededInput) -> Result<Self, String> {\n        let replacement = match (input.schema, input.payload) {\n            (Some(schema), Some(payload)) => crate::os_spr::InputReplacement::Input { schema, payload: semio_framework_io_base64::base64_standard_decode(&payload).map_err(|error| format!(\"supersede input {} payload: {error}\", input.target))? },\n            (None, None) => crate::os_spr::InputReplacement::Withdrawn,\n            _ => return Err(format!(\"supersede input {} needs both schema and payload, or neither\", input.target)),\n        };\n        Ok(Self { target: MutationId(input.target), replacement })\n    }\n}\n\n/// 🧾️ One `.ops` header/structural line — `doc`/`edit` and one line per history transition\n/// (`revert`/`reinstate`/`commit`/`branch`/`checkout`/`repin`/`supersede`) — re-derived directly on the `dsl_schema` grammar engine (`#[derive(DslOps)]` generates\n/// `OpText::parse_op`/`print_op` from this declaration; see {@link print_edit_lines}/\n/// {@link print_document_text}/{@link parse_document_text}, its only callers). Sigil-free lowercase\n/// keywords (bare `doc`, never `@doc` — `@` is reserved for connection points everywhere else in the\n/// unified DSL syntax); `id` is always the first positional field on every line; every other field is\n/// a plain `key=value` attribute that is simply OMITTED when absent (no more `-` placeholder\n/// sentinel); `operations`/`after`/`by`/`pins` are real DSL lists (`by=[ u1 \"Ueli Saluz\" ]`), not\n/// comma-joined, percent-escaped strings.\n#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, DslOps)]\nenum OpsHeaderLine {\n    Doc {\n        #[dsl(positional)]\n        id: String,\n        schema: String,\n    },\n    Edit {\n        #[dsl(positional)]\n        id: String,\n        sequence: i32,\n        started: String,\n        actor: Option<String>,\n        finished: Option<String>,\n        description: Option<String>,\n        verb: Option<String>,\n        line: Vec<String>,\n    },\n    /// ⏪️ A `Revert` transition: `clock` is the HLC as `physical.logical.actor`, `after` its\n    /// causal dependencies; every transition line carries both so its envelope id re-derives exactly.\n    Revert {\n        #[dsl(positional)]\n        id: String,\n        actor: String,\n        clock: String,\n        after: Vec<String>,\n        operations: Vec<String>,\n    },\n    /// ⏩️ A `Reinstate` transition.\n    Reinstate {\n        #[dsl(positional)]\n        id: String,\n        actor: String,\n        clock: String,\n        after: Vec<String>,\n        operations: Vec<String>,\n    },\n    /// 🚩️ A `Commit` transition with the change and checkpoint facts it introduces.\n    Commit {\n        #[dsl(positional)]\n        id: String,\n        actor: String,\n        clock: String,\n        after: Vec<String>,\n        checkpoint: String,\n        parent: Option<String>,\n        change: String,\n        operations: Vec<String>,\n        description: Option<String>,\n        saved: String,\n        by: Vec<OpsAuthor>,\n        message: Option<String>,\n        at: String,\n        line: Vec<String>,\n    },\n    /// 🌿️ A `Branch` transition.\n    Branch {\n        #[dsl(positional)]\n        id: String,\n        actor: String,\n        clock: String,\n        after: Vec<String>,\n        alternative: String,\n        name: String,\n        checkpoint: String,\n    },\n    /// 🎯️ A `Checkout` transition.\n    Checkout {\n        #[dsl(positional)]\n        id: String,\n        actor: String,\n        clock: String,\n        after: Vec<String>,\n        checkpoint: String,\n        alternative: Option<String>,\n    },\n    /// 🧩️ A `Repin` transition.\n    Repin {\n        #[dsl(positional)]\n        id: String,\n        actor: String,\n        clock: String,\n        after: Vec<String>,\n        checkpoint: String,\n        pinned: String,\n        pins: Vec<OpsPin>,\n    },\n    /// ✏️ A `Supersede` transition: every input it replaces, document-wide or within `scope`, and the newest foreign\n    /// operation its author had `observed` (its grading frontier at the hub).\n    Supersede {\n        #[dsl(positional)]\n        id: String,\n        actor: String,\n        clock: String,\n        after: Vec<String>,\n        scope: Option<String>,\n        inputs: Vec<OpsSupersededInput>,\n        observed: Option<String>,\n    },\n    /// 🔙️ One edit's complete inverse sequence, encoded with the operation's own text grammar.\n    Inverse { edit: String, ops: Vec<String> },\n    /// 🪪️ One authoritative metadata record for a forward operation.\n    Metadata { edit: String, index: u32, data: String },\n    /// 📨️ One durable diagnostic ledger entry, explicitly owned by an edit.\n    Message { edit: String, data: String },\n    /// ⚔️ One first-class conflict, including its content-addressed identity and lifecycle.\n    Conflict { data: String },\n}\n\n/// 🌿️ A text record explicitly carries zero trunk/unknown or one authored branch identity.\nfn ops_line_provenance(mut lines: Vec<String>) -> Result<Option<String>, TextError> {\n    if lines.len() > 1 { return Err(crate::os_dsl::__rt::field_error(\"history line admits zero or one identity\")); }\n    Ok(lines.pop())\n}\n\n//#region 🔖️OpCodec\n/// 🎞️ Handcrafted OpText (P6).\nimpl OpText for OpsHeaderLine {\n    fn parse_op(line: &str) -> Result<Self, TextError> {\n        let variants = <Self as crate::os_dsl::DslVariants>::variants();\n        for (keyword, spec_fn) in &variants {\n            let probe = format!(\"{} \", keyword);\n            if line == keyword.as_str() || line.starts_with(&probe) {\n                let record = crate::os_dsl::parse(line, &(spec_fn.ordinary)(), &crate::os_dsl::ParseOptions { limits: semio_framework_diagnostic::Limits::default(), mode: crate::os_dsl::SourceMode::Inline })?;\n                return <Self as crate::os_dsl::DslVariants>::from_named_record(keyword, &record);\n            }\n        }\n        Err(crate::os_dsl::__rt::field_error(format!(\"unknown operation line '{line}'\")))\n    }\n    fn print_op(&self) -> String {\n        let (keyword, record) = <Self as crate::os_dsl::DslVariants>::to_named_record(self);\n        let variants = <Self as crate::os_dsl::DslVariants>::variants();\n        let spec_fn = variants.iter().find(|(k, _)| k == &keyword).map(|(_, s)| *s).expect(\"variant spec must exist for its own keyword\");\n        crate::os_dsl::print(&record, &(spec_fn.ordinary)(), crate::os_dsl::JoinMode::Inline)\n    }\n}\n\n/// 🎯️ Handcrafted OpBinary (P6).\nimpl OpBinary for OpsHeaderLine {\n    fn encode_op(&self) -> Result<Vec<u8>, crate::os_spr::ProtocolError> {\n        const OP_BINARY_FORMAT: u8 = 1;\n        let (keyword, record) = <Self as crate::os_dsl::DslVariants>::to_named_record(self);\n        let variants = <Self as crate::os_dsl::DslVariants>::variants();\n        let ordinal = variants.iter().position(|(k, _)| *k == keyword).ok_or(crate::os_spr::ProtocolError::Malformed { what: \"op variant\", offset: 0, detail: format!(\"keyword {keyword:?} is not a declared variant\") })?;\n        let spec = (variants[ordinal].1.ordinary)();\n        let body = crate::os_pack::encode_record_body(&spec, &record, &PackEncodeOptions::default()).map_err(crate::os_spr::ProtocolError::from)?;\n        let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(body.len() + 3);\n        out.push(OP_BINARY_FORMAT);\n        crate::os_pack::write_varint_u64(&mut out, ordinal as u64);\n        out.extend_from_slice(&body);\n        Ok(out)\n    }\n    fn decode_op(bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<Self, crate::os_spr::ProtocolError> {\n        const OP_BINARY_FORMAT: u8 = 1;\n        let mut reader = crate::os_pack::ByteReader::new(bytes);\n        let format = reader.read_u8()?;\n        if format != OP_BINARY_FORMAT {\n            return Err(crate::os_spr::ProtocolError::Malformed { what: \"op format\", offset: 0, detail: format!(\"unsupported op format {format}\") });\n        }\n        let ordinal = reader.read_varint_u64()?;\n        let variants = <Self as crate::os_dsl::DslVariants>::variants();\n        let (keyword, spec_fn) = variants.get(ordinal as usize).ok_or(crate::os_spr::ProtocolError::Malformed { what: \"op variant\", offset: 1, detail: format!(\"ordinal {ordinal} out of range for {} declared variants\", variants.len()) })?;\n        let spec = (spec_fn.ordinary)();\n        let body = &bytes[reader.position()..];\n        let (record, _report) = crate::os_pack::decode_record_body(body, &spec, &PackDecodeOptions::default()).map_err(crate::os_spr::ProtocolError::from)?;\n        let record_offset = reader.position() as u64;\n        <Self as crate::os_dsl::DslVariants>::from_named_record(keyword, &record).map_err(|error| crate::os_spr::ProtocolError::Malformed { what: \"op record\", offset: record_offset, detail: error.to_string() })\n    }\n}\n//#endregion 🔖️OpCodec\n\n//#endregion 🔖️OpsHeaderGrammar\n\n/// 📤️ Prints one edit as the complete hot-path append unit: `edit ...` header, one\n/// two-space-indented `print_op` line per forward operation, then the matching inverse record and\n/// one authoritative metadata record per forward — what `append_ops` / `replay_ops` require. The\n/// metadata records carry only persisted facts, like `.spr`: the semantic kind and label every load\n/// re-derives from the operation stay out of the text mirror.\npub async fn print_edit_lines<Mutation: OpText>(edit: &Edit<Mutation>) -> Result<String, VcsError> {\n    if edit.mutation_meta.len() != edit.forwards.len() {\n        return Err(VcsError::ValidationFailed(format!(\"edit {} has {} metadata entries for {} forward operations\", edit.id, edit.mutation_meta.len(), edit.forwards.len())));\n    }\n    let header = OpsHeaderLine::Edit {\n        id: edit.id.clone(),\n        sequence: edit.sequence_number,\n        started: edit.started_at.clone(),\n        actor: edit.actor.clone(),\n        finished: edit.finished_at.clone(),\n        description: edit.description.clone(),\n        verb: edit.verb.clone(),\n        line: edit.line.iter().cloned().collect(),\n    };\n    let mut out = header.print_op();\n    out.push('\\n');\n    for operation in &edit.forwards {\n        let printed = operation.print_op();\n        if printed.contains('\\n') {\n            return Err(VcsError::Serialize(\"op-text print_op must not contain a newline\".into()));\n        }\n        out.push_str(\"  \");\n        out.push_str(&printed);\n        out.push('\\n');\n    }\n    let mut inverse: Vec<String> = Vec::with_capacity(edit.inverse.len());\n    for operation in &edit.inverse {\n        let text = operation.print_op();\n        if text.contains('\\n') {\n            return Err(VcsError::Serialize(\"op-text print_op must not contain a newline\".into()));\n        }\n        inverse.push(text);\n    }\n    out.push_str(&OpsHeaderLine::Inverse { edit: edit.id.clone(), ops: inverse }.print_op());\n    out.push('\\n');\n    for (index, meta) in edit.mutation_meta.iter().enumerate() {\n        let data = semio_framework_pack_json::to_json_string(&MutationMeta { semantic_kind: None, label: None, ..meta.clone() });\n        out.push_str(&OpsHeaderLine::Metadata { edit: edit.id.clone(), index: index as u32, data }.print_op());\n        out.push('\\n');\n    }\n    Ok(out)\n}\n\n/// 📤️ Builds just the op-log half of a textual/pack document — `doc` header, every edit ever\n/// created as an `edit` block, then `change`/`checkpoint`/`alternative`/`active` records. Shared by\n/// `print_document_text` and `print_document_pack`: the op-log grammar never touches\n/// `initial_snapshot`, so it is provably format-invariant and both printers thin out to this plus\n/// their own initial-snapshot encoding. Every replay-critical value is explicit: forward and\n/// inverse operations, operation metadata, message ledger, conflicts, and cursor.\n/// ⏰️ `physical.logical.actor` — the textual HLC every transition line carries.\nfn print_clock(timestamp: &HybridLogicalTimestamp) -> String {\n    format!(\"{}.{}.{}\", timestamp.physical_ms, timestamp.logical, timestamp.actor)\n}\n\nfn parse_clock(text: &str) -> Result<HybridLogicalTimestamp, String> {\n    let mut parts = text.split('.').map(str::parse::<u64>);\n    match (parts.next(), parts.next(), parts.next(), parts.next()) {\n        (Some(Ok(physical_ms)), Some(Ok(logical)), Some(Ok(actor)), None) => Ok(HybridLogicalTimestamp { actor, physical_ms, logical }),\n        _ => Err(format!(\"invalid transition clock {text}\")),\n    }\n}\n\nfn operation_ids(ids: &[MutationId]) -> Vec<String> {\n    ids.iter().map(|id| id.0.clone()).collect()\n}\n\nfn mutation_ids(ids: Vec<String>) -> Vec<MutationId> {\n    ids.into_iter().map(MutationId).collect()\n}\n\n/// 🖨️ One transition envelope as its semantic `.ops` line.\nfn ops_line_from_transition(envelope: &crate::os_spr::MutationEnvelope) -> Result<OpsHeaderLine, VcsError> {\n    let transition = crate::os_spr::history_transition_from_envelope(envelope).map_err(|error| VcsError::Serialize(error.to_string()))?.ok_or_else(|| VcsError::Serialize(format!(\"{} is not a history transition\", envelope.mutation_id.0)))?;\n    let id = envelope.mutation_id.0.clone();\n    let actor = envelope.actor.0.clone();\n    let clock = print_clock(&envelope.timestamp);\n    let after = operation_ids(&envelope.dependencies);\n    Ok(match transition {\n        crate::os_spr::HistoryTransition::Revert { mutation_ids } => OpsHeaderLine::Revert { id, actor, clock, after, operations: operation_ids(&mutation_ids) },\n        crate::os_spr::HistoryTransition::Reinstate { mutation_ids } => OpsHeaderLine::Reinstate { id, actor, clock, after, operations: operation_ids(&mutation_ids) },\n        crate::os_spr::HistoryTransition::Commit(checkpoint) => OpsHeaderLine::Commit {\n            id,\n            actor,\n            clock,\n            after,\n            checkpoint: checkpoint.checkpoint_id,\n            parent: checkpoint.parent_id,\n            change: checkpoint.change_id,\n            operations: operation_ids(&checkpoint.mutation_ids),\n            description: checkpoint.description,\n            saved: checkpoint.saved_at,\n            by: checkpoint.authors.into_iter().map(|author| OpsAuthor { id: author.id, name: author.name, avatar: author.avatar }).collect(),\n            message: checkpoint.message,\n            at: checkpoint.timestamp,\n            line: checkpoint.line_id.into_iter().collect(),\n        },\n        crate::os_spr::HistoryTransition::Branch { alternative_id, name, checkpoint_id } => OpsHeaderLine::Branch { id, actor, clock, after, alternative: alternative_id, name, checkpoint: checkpoint_id },\n        crate::os_spr::HistoryTransition::Checkout { checkpoint_id, alternative_id } => OpsHeaderLine::Checkout { id, actor, clock, after, checkpoint: checkpoint_id, alternative: alternative_id },\n        crate::os_spr::HistoryTransition::Repin { checkpoint_id, pinned_checkpoint_id, pins } => {\n            OpsHeaderLine::Repin { id, actor, clock, after, checkpoint: checkpoint_id, pinned: pinned_checkpoint_id, pins: pins.into_iter().map(|pin| OpsPin { child: pin.child_uri, checkpoint: pin.checkpoint_id }).collect() }\n        }\n        crate::os_spr::HistoryTransition::Supersede(supersede) => {\n            OpsHeaderLine::Supersede { id, actor, clock, after, scope: supersede.scope, inputs: supersede.inputs.into_iter().map(OpsSupersededInput::from).collect(), observed: envelope.observed.as_ref().map(|observed| observed.0.clone()) }\n        }\n    })\n}\n\n/// 🧾️ Rebuilds the transition envelope a `.ops` transition line describes, refusing a line\n/// whose printed id is not the content-addressed id of what it states.\nfn transition_from_ops_line(document_id: &str, id: String, actor: String, clock: &str, after: Vec<String>, transition: crate::os_spr::HistoryTransition) -> Result<crate::os_spr::MutationEnvelope, String> {\n    let envelope = crate::os_spr::history_transition_envelope(&transition, &ArtifactId(document_id.to_string()), &ActorId(actor), mutation_ids(after), parse_clock(clock)?);\n    if envelope.mutation_id.0 != id {\n        return Err(format!(\"transition line {id} does not match its content-addressed id {}\", envelope.mutation_id.0));\n    }\n    Ok(envelope)\n}\n\n/// 📚️ Materializes everything an envelope's event log projects to — change/checkpoint/\n/// alternative ledgers, the active alternative and the cursor — from [`fold_envelope_history`].\n/// The loaders call it right after reading the persisted events, which are all a document stores.\nfn project_envelope_history<P, Mutation>(envelope: &mut ArtifactEnvelope<P, Mutation>) -> Result<EffectiveSupersessions, VcsError>\nwhere\n    Mutation: self::Mutation<P>,\n{\n    let fold = fold_envelope_history(envelope)?;\n    let changes = fold.changes.into_iter().map(|change| Change { id: change.id, edit_ids: change.edit_ids, description: change.description, saved_at: change.saved_at }).collect();\n    let mut checkpoints = Vec::with_capacity(fold.checkpoints.len());\n    for checkpoint in fold.checkpoints {\n        let mut composition_pins = Vec::with_capacity(checkpoint.pins.len());\n        for pin in checkpoint.pins {\n            composition_pins.push(crate::os_vcs::CompositionPin { child_ref: crate::os_io::ArtifactRef::parse_uri(&pin.child_uri).map_err(VcsError::Deserialize)?, checkpoint_id: pin.checkpoint_id });\n        }\n        let authors = checkpoint.authors.into_iter().map(|author| Author { id: author.id, name: author.name, avatar: author.avatar }).collect();\n        checkpoints.push(Checkpoint { id: checkpoint.id, change_ids: checkpoint.change_ids, parent_id: checkpoint.parent_id, authors, message: checkpoint.message, timestamp: checkpoint.timestamp, composition_pins });\n    }\n    let alternatives = fold.alternatives.into_iter().map(|alternative| Alternative { id: alternative.id, name: alternative.name, checkpoint_ids: alternative.checkpoint_ids }).collect();\n    envelope.vcs.changes = ArtifactHistoryLedger::try_from_preflighted(changes).map_err(|_| VcsError::ValidationFailed(\"history change capacity exceeded\".into()))?;\n    envelope.vcs.checkpoints = ArtifactHistoryLedger::try_from_preflighted(checkpoints).map_err(|_| VcsError::ValidationFailed(\"history checkpoint capacity exceeded\".into()))?;\n    envelope.vcs.alternatives = ArtifactHistoryLedger::try_from_preflighted(alternatives).map_err(|_| VcsError::ValidationFailed(\"history alternative capacity exceeded\".into()))?;\n    envelope.active_alternative_id = fold.alternative;\n    envelope.cursor = Some(ArtifactCursor::new(fold.applied, fold.redo, fold.checkpoint));\n    Ok(fold.supersessions)\n}\n\n/// ✏️ Settles a loaded history: persisted inverses and messages of applied edits are derived caches a later supersession\n/// or re-projection may have left stale (an append-only log never rewrites the edit record), so every load recomputes\n/// them with one Report replay from the genesis — an operation that no longer applies is recorded as a `Fatal` no-op\n/// whether or not supersessions exist — and every supersession envelope regains the conflict target its record does not\n/// persist. Answers the replayed head projection.\nfn replay_loaded_history<P, Mutation, I, S>(envelope: &mut ArtifactEnvelope<P, Mutation>, applied: I, supersessions: EffectiveSupersessions) -> Result<P, VcsError>\nwhere\n    P: Clone,\n    Mutation: self::Mutation<P> + OpBinary,\n    I: IntoIterator<Item = S>,\n    S: AsRef<str>,\n{\n    let mut replay = loaded_history_replay(envelope, applied, supersessions)?;\n    replay.step(&envelope.vcs.edits, &mut || false)?;\n    adopt_loaded_replay(envelope, replay.finish()?)\n}\n\n/// ⏪️ The Report replay every load settles its applied history with ([`replay_loaded_history`]): from the genesis, under\n/// the fold's effective supersessions. A retained loader steps it under its own deadline.\nfn loaded_history_replay<P, Mutation, I, S>(envelope: &ArtifactEnvelope<P, Mutation>, applied: I, supersessions: EffectiveSupersessions) -> Result<EditReplay<P, Mutation>, VcsError>\nwhere\n    P: Clone,\n    Mutation: self::Mutation<P> + OpBinary,\n    I: IntoIterator<Item = S>,\n    S: AsRef<str>,\n{\n    let order = applied.into_iter().map(|edit_id| edit_id.as_ref().to_string()).collect();\n    EditReplay::new(ReplayMode::Report, Arc::new(envelope.vcs.initial_snapshot.clone()), order, 0, &envelope.schema, supersessions, &envelope.vcs.edits)\n}\n\n/// ✍️ Writes a finished load replay into `envelope` — every applied edit's rebased inverse and messages, every supersession\n/// envelope's conflict target — and answers the replayed head projection.\nfn adopt_loaded_replay<P, Mutation>(envelope: &mut ArtifactEnvelope<P, Mutation>, mut result: EditReplayResult<P, Mutation>) -> Result<P, VcsError>\nwhere\n    P: Clone,\n    Mutation: self::Mutation<P> + OpBinary,\n{\n    fill_supersession_targets::<P, Mutation>(envelope)?;\n    for (edit_id, inverse) in result.take_rebased_inverse() {\n        match envelope.vcs.edits.iter_mut().find(|edit| edit.id == edit_id) {\n            Some(edit) => retire_scratch_operations::<P, Mutation>(std::mem::replace(&mut edit.inverse, inverse)),\n            None => retire_scratch_operations::<P, Mutation>(inverse),\n        }\n    }\n    for entry in result.take_replayed() {\n        if entry.messages.is_empty() {\n            envelope.edit_messages.remove_id(&entry.edit_id);\n            continue;\n        }\n        match envelope.edit_messages.get_mut_by_id(&entry.edit_id) {\n            Some(established) => *established = entry,\n            None => envelope.edit_messages.admit(entry).map_err(|rejected| VcsError::ValidationFailed(format!(\"replayed messages of edit {} exceed the message ledger\", rejected.edit_id)))?,\n        }\n    }\n    let state = result.take_state().ok_or_else(|| VcsError::ValidationFailed(\"history replay lost its reached projection\".into()))?;\n    match Arc::try_unwrap(state) {\n        Ok(state) => Ok(state),\n        Err(shared) => {\n            let state = (*shared).clone();\n            retire_shared_projection::<P, Mutation>(shared);\n            Ok(state)\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// 🎯️ Re-derives the conflict target of every supersession envelope that carries none — the persisted transition record\n/// does not — from the superseded and replacing operations ([`supersession_address`]).\nfn fill_supersession_targets<P, Mutation>(envelope: &mut ArtifactEnvelope<P, Mutation>) -> Result<(), VcsError>\nwhere\n    Mutation: self::Mutation<P> + OpBinary,\n{\n    let mut originals: HashMap<MutationId, &Mutation> = HashMap::new();\n    for edit in envelope.vcs.edits.iter() {\n        originals.extend(crate::os_spr::mutation_ids_for_edit::<P, Mutation>(edit).into_iter().zip(edit.forwards.iter()));\n    }\n    let mut targets = Vec::new();\n    for (index, transition) in envelope.transitions.iter().enumerate() {\n        if !transition.target.is_empty() {\n            continue;\n        }\n        if let Some(crate::os_spr::HistoryTransition::Supersede(supersede)) = crate::os_spr::history_transition_from_envelope(transition).map_err(|error| VcsError::Deserialize(error.to_string()))? {\n            targets.push((index, supersession_address::<P, Mutation>(&supersede, &envelope.schema, |target| originals.get(target).copied())));\n        }\n    }\n    drop(originals);\n    for (index, target) in targets {\n        envelope.transitions[index].target = target;\n    }\n    Ok(())\n}\n\n/// 🎯️ The address a supersession writes: the longest prefix every superseded operation's and every admitted\n/// replacement's conflict target share — the same law authoring stamps and loading re-derives. A replacement breaking\n/// the supersede law ([`admit_replacement`]) writes nothing beyond its target.\nfn supersession_address<'a, P, Mutation>(supersede: &protocol::TransitionSupersede, schema: &str, original: impl Fn(&MutationId) -> Option<&'a Mutation>) -> Vec<String>\nwhere\n    Mutation: self::Mutation<P> + OpBinary + 'a,\n{\n    let mut address: Option<Vec<String>> = None;\n    for input in &supersede.inputs {\n        let operation = original(&input.target);\n        let mut written = operation.map(self::Mutation::<P>::conflict_target).unwrap_or_default();\n        if let Some(Ok(Some(replacement))) = operation.map(|operation| admit_replacement::<P, Mutation>(operation, &input.replacement, schema)) {\n            written = common_address(&written, &replacement.conflict_target());\n            self::Mutation::<P>::retire_cold(replacement);\n        }\n        address = Some(match address {\n            Some(known) => common_address(&known, &written),\n            None => written,\n        });\n    }\n    address.unwrap_or_default()\n}\n\n/// 🎯️ The longest address prefix `left` and `right` share.\nfn common_address(left: &[String], right: &[String]) -> Vec<String> {\n    left.iter().zip(right.iter()).take_while(|(left, right)| left == right).map(|(segment, _)| segment.clone()).collect()\n}\n\nasync fn print_ops_log<P, Mutation>(envelope: &ArtifactEnvelopeOwners<P, Mutation>) -> Result<String, VcsError>\nwhere\n    Mutation: OpText,\n{\n    let mut ops = String::new();\n    ops.push_str(&OpsHeaderLine::Doc { id: envelope.id.clone(), schema: envelope.schema.clone() }.print_op());\n    ops.push('\\n');\n    for edit in envelope.vcs.edits.iter().filter(|edit| envelope.holds_committed_edit(&edit.id)) {\n        ops.push_str(&print_edit_lines(edit).await?);\n    }\n    for transition in &envelope.transitions {\n        ops.push_str(&ops_line_from_transition(transition)?.print_op());\n        ops.push('\\n');\n    }\n    for entry in envelope.edit_messages.iter().filter(|entry| envelope.holds_committed_edit(&entry.edit_id)) {\n        if !envelope.vcs.edits.iter().any(|edit| edit.id == entry.edit_id) {\n            return Err(VcsError::ValidationFailed(format!(\"message ledger references unknown edit {}\", entry.edit_id)));\n        }\n        for message in &entry.messages {\n            let data = semio_framework_pack_json::to_json_string(message);\n            ops.push_str(&OpsHeaderLine::Message { edit: entry.edit_id.clone(), data }.print_op());\n            ops.push('\\n');\n        }\n    }\n    for conflict in &envelope.conflicts {\n        let data = semio_framework_pack_json::to_json_string(conflict);\n        ops.push_str(&OpsHeaderLine::Conflict { data }.print_op());\n        ops.push('\\n');\n    }\n    Ok(ops)\n}\n\n/// 📤️ Prints the full textual VCS document: the DSL text (initial snapshot) and the complete\n/// event log (`doc` header, every edit with its inverse/meta/message records, every history\n/// transition, every conflict) — events only; positions are re-derived by folding on load.\n/// Replaces the JSON envelope as the canonical persisted form.\npub async fn print_document_text<P, Mutation>(envelope: &ArtifactEnvelopeOwners<P, Mutation>) -> Result<ArtifactTextFiles, VcsError>\nwhere\n    P: ArtifactDsl,\n    Mutation: OpText,\n{\n    let dsl = envelope.vcs.initial_snapshot.print_dsl();\n    let ops = print_ops_log(envelope).await?;\n    Ok(ArtifactTextFiles { dsl, ops })\n}\n\n/// 🎞️ `crate::os_spr::UndoPolicy` ordinal, matching `HistoryOpMeta.undo_policy`'s wire shape —\n/// distinct from `undo_policy_ordinal` above, which maps THIS crate's `ArtifactCommand`-facing\n/// `UndoPolicy` (currently `semio_framework_replication::UndoPolicy`; the two enums have identical\n/// variants and will merge in the kernel-unification wave, see `protocol_core`'s own doc note).\n// 🚫️async: E1 pure ordinal mapping, consumed by `history_op_meta_from_operation_meta` which is\n// itself consumed only through `Iterator::map` fn-item arguments — see R9.\nfn protocol_undo_policy_ordinal(policy: UndoPolicy) -> u8 {\n    match policy {\n        UndoPolicy::ExactBaseOnly => 0,\n        UndoPolicy::TransformAgainstConcurrent => 1,\n        UndoPolicy::SemanticUndo => 2,\n        UndoPolicy::CompensatingAction => 3,\n    }\n}\n\n// 🚫️async: E1 pure ordinal mapping, consumed by `mutation_meta_from_history_op_meta` — see R9.\nfn protocol_undo_policy_from_ordinal(ordinal: u8) -> UndoPolicy {\n    match ordinal {\n        1 => UndoPolicy::TransformAgainstConcurrent,\n        2 => UndoPolicy::SemanticUndo,\n        3 => UndoPolicy::CompensatingAction,\n        _ => UndoPolicy::ExactBaseOnly,\n    }\n}\n\n// 🚫️async: E1 pure field-copy, consumed only through `Iterator::map` fn-item arguments — see R9.\nfn history_message_from_mutation_message(message: &crate::os_spr::MutationMessage) -> crate::os_spr::history::HistoryMessage {\n    crate::os_spr::history::HistoryMessage { level: message.level.as_u8(), code: message.code.0.clone(), message: message.message.clone(), target: message.target.clone(), op_index: message.op_index }\n}\n\n// 🚫️async: E1 pure field-copy, consumed only through `Iterator::map` fn-item arguments — see R9.\nfn mutation_message_from_history_message(message: crate::os_spr::history::HistoryMessage) -> Result<crate::os_spr::MutationMessage, String> {\n    let level = semio_framework_diagnostic::Severity::from_u8(message.level).ok_or_else(|| format!(\"unknown mutation message severity {}\", message.level))?;\n    Ok(crate::os_spr::MutationMessage { level, code: semio_framework_diagnostic::FaultCode(message.code), message: message.message, target: message.target, op_index: message.op_index })\n}\n\n// 🚫️async: E1 pure field-copy, consumed only through `Iterator::map` fn-item arguments — see R9.\nfn history_op_meta_from_operation_meta(meta: &MutationMeta, messages: impl IntoIterator<Item = crate::os_spr::history::HistoryMessage>) -> crate::os_spr::HistoryOpMeta {\n    crate::os_spr::HistoryOpMeta {\n        op_id: meta.mutation_id.as_ref().map(|id| id.0.clone()),\n        dependencies: meta.dependencies.iter().map(|id| id.0.clone()).collect(),\n        base_version: meta.base_version,\n        author_id: meta.author_id.as_ref().map(|id| id.0.clone()),\n        hlt: Some((meta.timestamp.actor, meta.timestamp.physical_ms as i64, meta.timestamp.logical)),\n        undo_policy: protocol_undo_policy_ordinal(meta.undo_policy),\n        payload_hash: meta.payload_hash.as_ref().map(|hash| hash.0),\n        group_id: meta.group_id.clone(),\n        origin: meta.origin.clone(),\n        transaction: meta.transaction.clone(),\n        messages: messages.into_iter().collect(),\n    }\n}\n\n// 🚫️async: E1 pure field-copy, consumed by `mutation_meta_from_history_op_meta`'s own caller\n// (§) without `.await` — see R9.\nfn mutation_meta_from_history_op_meta(meta: crate::os_spr::HistoryOpMeta) -> Result<(MutationMeta, Vec<crate::os_spr::MutationMessage>), String> {\n    let (actor, physical_ms, logical) = meta.hlt.ok_or_else(|| \"history operation metadata has no hybrid-clock timestamp\".to_string())?;\n    let physical_ms = u64::try_from(physical_ms).map_err(|_| \"history operation metadata has a negative hybrid-clock physical time\".to_string())?;\n    if meta.op_id.as_ref().is_none_or(|id| id.trim().is_empty()) {\n        return Err(\"history operation metadata has no stable operation identity\".to_string());\n    }\n    let messages = meta.messages.into_iter().map(mutation_message_from_history_message).collect::<Result<Vec<_>, _>>()?;\n    Ok((\n        MutationMeta {\n            mutation_id: meta.op_id.map(MutationId),\n            dependencies: meta.dependencies.into_iter().map(MutationId).collect(),\n            base_version: meta.base_version,\n            author_id: meta.author_id.map(ActorId),\n            timestamp: HybridLogicalTimestamp { actor, physical_ms, logical },\n            undo_policy: protocol_undo_policy_from_ordinal(meta.undo_policy),\n            payload_hash: meta.payload_hash.map(crate::os_spr::PayloadHash),\n            semantic_kind: None,\n            label: None,\n            group_id: meta.group_id,\n            origin: meta.origin,\n            transaction: meta.transaction,\n        },\n        messages,\n    ))\n}\n\n/// ⚖️ Persistence admits exactly the frozen outcome vocabulary ([`protocol::OUTCOME_CODES`] plus the\n/// `mutation.apply.<detail>` family), each code at the one level it fixes.\nasync fn expected_mutation_message_level(code: &str) -> Option<semio_framework_diagnostic::Severity> {\n    protocol::outcome_code_level(code)\n}\n\nasync fn validate_persisted_message(message: &crate::os_spr::MutationMessage, operation_count: Option<usize>) -> Result<(), VcsError> {\n    let Some(expected_level) = expected_mutation_message_level(&message.code.0).await else {\n        return Err(VcsError::ValidationFailed(format!(\"history carries unknown mutation message code {}\", message.code.0)));\n    };\n    if message.level != expected_level || message.message.trim().is_empty() || message.target.iter().any(|target| target.trim().is_empty()) {\n        return Err(VcsError::ValidationFailed(format!(\"history carries malformed mutation message {}\", message.code.0)));\n    }\n    if let Some(operation_count) = operation_count {\n        if message.op_index.is_none_or(|index| index as usize >= operation_count) {\n            return Err(VcsError::ValidationFailed(format!(\"history carries an invalid operation index for mutation message {}\", message.code.0)));\n        }\n    }\n    Ok(())\n}\n\nasync fn stable_mutation_ids_for_edit<Mutation>(edit: &Edit<Mutation>) -> Result<Vec<MutationId>, VcsError> {\n    if edit.mutation_meta.len() != edit.forwards.len() {\n        return Err(VcsError::ValidationFailed(format!(\"edit {} does not carry one operation identity per forward mutation\", edit.id)));\n    }\n    edit.mutation_meta.iter().map(|meta| meta.mutation_id.clone().filter(|id| !id.0.trim().is_empty()).ok_or_else(|| VcsError::ValidationFailed(format!(\"edit {} has an operation without a stable identity\", edit.id)))).collect()\n}\n\nasync fn conflict_messages_for_edits<Mutation>(edits: &[Edit<Mutation>], replayed: &[crate::os_spr::EditMessages]) -> Result<Vec<crate::os_spr::MutationMessage>, VcsError> {\n    let replayed_by_edit: HashMap<&str, &crate::os_spr::EditMessages> = replayed.iter().map(|entry| (entry.edit_id.as_str(), entry)).collect();\n    if replayed_by_edit.len() != replayed.len() {\n        return Err(VcsError::ValidationFailed(\"conflict messages repeat an edit owner\".to_string()));\n    }\n    let mut messages = Vec::new();\n    let mut offset = 0u32;\n    for edit in edits {\n        if let Some(entry) = replayed_by_edit.get(edit.id.as_str()) {\n            for message in &entry.messages {\n                validate_persisted_message(message, Some(edit.forwards.len())).await?;\n                let mut message = message.clone();\n                let index = message.op_index.ok_or_else(|| VcsError::ValidationFailed(format!(\"conflict message {} has no operation index\", message.code.0)))?;\n                message.op_index = Some(offset.checked_add(index).ok_or_else(|| VcsError::ValidationFailed(\"conflict operation index overflow\".to_string()))?);\n                messages.push(message);\n            }\n        }\n        offset = offset\n            .checked_add(u32::try_from(edit.forwards.len()).map_err(|_| VcsError::ValidationFailed(format!(\"edit {} has too many operations\", edit.id)))?)\n            .ok_or_else(|| VcsError::ValidationFailed(\"conflict operation index overflow\".to_string()))?;\n    }\n    Ok(messages)\n}\n\nasync fn canonical_conflict_actors(actors: impl IntoIterator<Item = ActorId>) -> Vec<ActorId> {\n    let mut actors: Vec<ActorId> = actors.into_iter().collect();\n    actors.sort_by(|left, right| left.0.cmp(&right.0));\n    actors.dedup_by(|left, right| left.0 == right.0);\n    actors\n}\n\n/// 🎯️ A conflict's messages index its kind-specific flattened operation sequence: wire\n/// envelopes in `Quarantined` order, or every forward operation of `Degraded` edits in\n/// `edit_ids` order. This makes `op_index` globally unambiguous for a conflict rather\n/// than accidentally treating every message as if it belonged to its first edit.\nasync fn validate_persisted_conflicts<P, Mutation>(envelope: &ArtifactEnvelopeOwners<P, Mutation>) -> Result<(), VcsError> {\n    let mut conflict_ids = HashSet::new();\n    let known_edits: HashMap<&str, &Edit<Mutation>> = envelope.vcs.edits.iter().map(|edit| (edit.id.as_str(), edit)).collect();\n    for conflict in &envelope.conflicts {\n        if conflict.id.0.trim().is_empty() || !conflict_ids.insert(conflict.id.0.as_str()) || conflict.messages.is_empty() {\n            return Err(VcsError::ValidationFailed(format!(\"history repeats or omits conflict identity {}\", conflict.id.0)));\n        }\n        if conflict.actors.is_empty() || conflict.actors.iter().any(|actor| actor.0.trim().is_empty()) || conflict.actors != canonical_conflict_actors(conflict.actors.clone()).await {\n            return Err(VcsError::ValidationFailed(format!(\"conflict {} has malformed actor identities\", conflict.id.0)));\n        }\n        let (mutation_ids, operation_count) = match &conflict.kind {\n            crate::os_spr::ConflictKind::Quarantined { envelopes } => {\n                if envelopes.is_empty() {\n                    return Err(VcsError::ValidationFailed(format!(\"quarantined conflict {} has no mutation envelopes\", conflict.id.0)));\n                }\n                let mut mutation_ids = Vec::with_capacity(envelopes.len());\n                let expected_actors = canonical_conflict_actors(envelopes.iter().map(|remote| remote.actor.clone())).await;\n                if conflict.actors != expected_actors {\n                    return Err(VcsError::ValidationFailed(format!(\"quarantined conflict {} has actors inconsistent with its envelopes\", conflict.id.0)));\n                }\n                for remote in envelopes {\n                    let mut dependencies = HashSet::new();\n                    if remote.document_id.0 != envelope.id\n                        || remote.diff.schema.0 != envelope.schema\n                        || remote.inverse.schema != remote.diff.schema\n                        || remote.mutation_id.0.trim().is_empty()\n                        || remote.actor.0.trim().is_empty()\n                        || remote.dependencies.iter().any(|dependency| dependency.0.trim().is_empty() || dependency == &remote.mutation_id || !dependencies.insert(dependency.0.as_str()))\n                    {\n                        return Err(VcsError::ValidationFailed(format!(\"quarantined conflict {} has invalid mutation envelopes\", conflict.id.0)));\n                    }\n                    if conflict.timestamp < remote.timestamp {\n                        return Err(VcsError::ValidationFailed(format!(\"quarantined conflict {} predates its mutation envelope\", conflict.id.0)));\n                    }\n                    mutation_ids.push(remote.mutation_id.clone());\n                }\n                let mut ids = HashSet::new();\n                if mutation_ids.iter().any(|mutation_id| !ids.insert(mutation_id.0.as_str())) {\n                    return Err(VcsError::ValidationFailed(format!(\"quarantined conflict {} repeats a mutation identity\", conflict.id.0)));\n                }\n                (mutation_ids, envelopes.len())\n            }\n            crate::os_spr::ConflictKind::Degraded { edit_ids } => {\n                if edit_ids.is_empty() {\n                    return Err(VcsError::ValidationFailed(format!(\"degraded conflict {} has no edit references\", conflict.id.0)));\n                }\n                let mut ids = HashSet::new();\n                let mut mutation_ids = Vec::new();\n                let mut expected_actors = Vec::new();\n                for edit_id in edit_ids {\n                    if !ids.insert(edit_id.as_str()) {\n                        return Err(VcsError::ValidationFailed(format!(\"degraded conflict {} repeats edit reference {edit_id}\", conflict.id.0)));\n                    }\n                    let edit = known_edits.get(edit_id.as_str()).ok_or_else(|| VcsError::ValidationFailed(format!(\"degraded conflict {} references unknown edit {edit_id}\", conflict.id.0)))?;\n                    let timestamp = edit.mutation_meta.first().map(|meta| meta.timestamp).ok_or_else(|| VcsError::ValidationFailed(format!(\"degraded conflict {} references edit {edit_id} without operation metadata\", conflict.id.0)))?;\n                    if conflict.timestamp < timestamp {\n                        return Err(VcsError::ValidationFailed(format!(\"degraded conflict {} predates edit {edit_id}\", conflict.id.0)));\n                    }\n                    expected_actors.push(ActorId(edit.actor.clone().ok_or_else(|| VcsError::ValidationFailed(format!(\"degraded conflict {} references actorless edit {edit_id}\", conflict.id.0)))?));\n                    mutation_ids.extend(stable_mutation_ids_for_edit(edit).await.map_err(|_| VcsError::ValidationFailed(format!(\"degraded conflict {} references edit {edit_id} without stable operation identities\", conflict.id.0)))?);\n                }\n                if conflict.actors != canonical_conflict_actors(expected_actors).await {\n                    return Err(VcsError::ValidationFailed(format!(\"degraded conflict {} has actors inconsistent with its edits\", conflict.id.0)));\n                }\n                let operation_count = mutation_ids.len();\n                (mutation_ids, operation_count)\n            }\n        };\n        for message in &conflict.messages {\n            validate_persisted_message(message, Some(operation_count)).await?;\n        }\n        if conflict.id != crate::os_spr::ConflictId::new(&conflict.kind, &ArtifactId(envelope.id.clone()), &mutation_ids, &conflict.timestamp).await {\n            return Err(VcsError::ValidationFailed(format!(\"conflict {} does not match its content-addressed identity\", conflict.id.0)));\n        }\n    }\n    Ok(())\n}\n\n/// 🧱️ Validates the complete durable history graph at every persistence boundary.\n/// Deliberately free of store construction bounds: codecs must reject malformed history before a\n/// caller needs to construct an `ArtifactStore`.\nasync fn validate_durable_history<P, Mutation>(envelope: &ArtifactEnvelope<P, Mutation>) -> Result<(), VcsError> {\n    let mut edit_ids = HashSet::new();\n    let mut edit_sequences = HashSet::new();\n    for edit in &envelope.vcs.edits {\n        if !edit_ids.insert(edit.id.as_str()) {\n            return Err(VcsError::ValidationFailed(format!(\"history repeats authoritative edit {}\", edit.id)));\n        }\n        if edit.sequence_number < 0 || !edit_sequences.insert(edit.sequence_number) {\n            return Err(VcsError::ValidationFailed(format!(\"history has an invalid edit sequence {} for {}\", edit.sequence_number, edit.id)));\n        }\n    }\n    let mut message_edit_ids = HashSet::new();\n    for entry in &envelope.edit_messages {\n        if !message_edit_ids.insert(entry.edit_id.as_str()) || !edit_ids.contains(entry.edit_id.as_str()) {\n            return Err(VcsError::ValidationFailed(format!(\"history has an invalid message ledger for edit {}\", entry.edit_id)));\n        }\n        let operation_count = envelope.vcs.edits.find_near(|edit| edit.id == entry.edit_id).map(|edit| edit.forwards.len()).ok_or_else(|| VcsError::ValidationFailed(format!(\"history has an invalid message ledger for edit {}\", entry.edit_id)))?;\n        let mut any_malformed = false;\n        for message in &entry.messages {\n            if validate_persisted_message(message, Some(operation_count)).await.is_err() {\n                any_malformed = true;\n                break;\n            }\n        }\n        if entry.messages.is_empty() || any_malformed {\n            return Err(VcsError::ValidationFailed(format!(\"history has malformed messages for edit {}\", entry.edit_id)));\n        }\n    }\n    validate_persisted_conflicts(envelope).await?;\n    let mut change_ids = HashSet::new();\n    for change in &envelope.vcs.changes {\n        if !change_ids.insert(change.id.as_str()) {\n            return Err(VcsError::ValidationFailed(format!(\"history repeats authoritative change {}\", change.id)));\n        }\n        let mut referenced_edits = HashSet::new();\n        for edit_id in
