self.snapshot_read_leases));\n            drop(std::mem::ManuallyDrop::take(&mut self.displaced_retirements));\n            drop(std::mem::ManuallyDrop::take(&mut self.owned_disposer));\n            drop(std::mem::ManuallyDrop::take(&mut self.one_item_preparation_factory));\n            drop(std::mem::ManuallyDrop::take(&mut self.one_item_wire_preparation_factory));\n            drop(std::mem::ManuallyDrop::take(&mut self.pending_report));\n            drop(std::mem::ManuallyDrop::take(&mut self.durable_group_root));\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nasync fn preflight_merge_by_id<T: PartialEq>(local: &[T], remote: &[T], id_of: impl Fn(&T) -> &String) -> Result<(), VcsError> {\n    let existing: HashMap<&str, &T> = local.iter().map(|item| (id_of(item).as_str(), item)).collect();\n    for item in remote {\n        let id = id_of(item).clone();\n        match existing.get(id.as_str()) {\n            Some(established) if *established == item => {}\n            Some(_) => return Err(VcsError::ValidationFailed(format!(\"remote history conflicts with established record {id}\"))),\n            None => {}\n        }\n    }\n    Ok(())\n}\n\nasync fn merge_by_id<T: Clone + PartialEq>(local: &mut Vec<T>, remote: Vec<T>, id_of: impl Fn(&T) -> &String) -> Result<(), VcsError> {\n    preflight_merge_by_id(local, &remote, &id_of).await?;\n    let mut existing: HashSet<String> = local.iter().map(|item| id_of(item).clone()).collect();\n    for item in remote {\n        if existing.insert(id_of(&item).clone()) {\n            local.push(item);\n        }\n    }\n    Ok(())\n}\n\n// 🎯️ W6 kernel unification: this crate's own `mutation_envelope_from_edit` (whole-edit-per-\n// envelope, JSON payload) is DELETED — `flush_outbound` now calls `crate::os_spr::\n// mutation_envelope_from_edit` directly (one `crate::os_spr::MutationEnvelope` per forward op,\n// `OpBinary`-encoded payloads — W5's frozen-contract signature). `hash_bytes`'s import above this\n// region stays needed elsewhere in this file (`replay_mutations`'s `payload_hash`, unaffected).\n\n/// 📦️ Recovers a single-op `Edit` from one causal wire envelope. `crate::os_spr::causal::\n/// MutationEnvelope` carries exactly one op per envelope (W5's binary reshape) — the receiving-\n/// side half of the per-op fan-out `crate::os_spr::mutation_envelope_from_edit` performs when sending\n/// (see `flush_outbound`). `sequence_number`/`started_at` are placeholders `ingest_envelope`\n/// overwrites (mirroring the local-edit convention: `self.edit_sequence += 1` then `now_iso()`).\n/// `undo_policy` defaults to `ExactBaseOnly` — not a lossy conversion: `crate::os_spr::causal::\n/// MutationEnvelope` carries no undo_policy at all (only the local `Edit`/`MutationMeta` shape\n/// does), and a remote edit is always foreign, so this field is never consulted for it anyway\n/// (`edit_is_local` gates undo eligibility on authorship, not `undo_policy`).\npub async fn edit_from_operation_envelope<Mutation: OpBinary>(envelope: &crate::os_spr::MutationEnvelope) -> Result<Edit<Mutation>, VcsError> {\n    let forward = Mutation::decode_op(&envelope.diff.payload).map_err(|error| VcsError::Deserialize(error.to_string()))?;\n    let inverse = if envelope.inverse.payload.is_empty() { Vec::new() } else { vec![Mutation::decode_op(&envelope.inverse.payload).map_err(|error| VcsError::Deserialize(error.to_string()))?] };\n    Ok(Edit {\n        id: envelope.mutation_id.0.clone(),\n        actor: Some(envelope.actor.0.clone()),\n        forwards: vec![forward],\n        inverse,\n        mutation_meta: vec![MutationMeta {\n            mutation_id: Some(envelope.mutation_id.clone()),\n            dependencies: envelope.dependencies.clone(),\n            base_version: 0,\n            author_id: Some(envelope.actor.clone()),\n            timestamp: envelope.timestamp,\n            undo_policy: UndoPolicy::ExactBaseOnly,\n            payload_hash: None,\n            semantic_kind: None,\n            label: None,\n            group_id: None,\n            origin: Default::default(),\n            transaction: envelope.transaction.clone(),\n        }],\n        description: None, verb: envelope.verb.clone(), line: envelope.line.clone(),\n        sequence_number: 0,\n        started_at: String::new(),\n        finished_at: None,\n    })\n}\n\n/// 🧊️ Retires one SCRATCH projection a history fold displaced, through the technology's own diff\n/// vocabulary. Every replay seam below walks `base → mid₁ → … → head` and throws each intermediate\n/// away; an artifact whose projection owns a fail-closed root (an `OrderedMap`, a neural\n/// `Dictionary`) aborts the process on that bare drop, which is what made `undo`/`redo` and every\n/// `.pack`/`.spr` reload kill the app (ticket 26/09/09/PROCEDURAL-3D-END-TO-END).\nfn retire_replayed_projection<P, Mutation>(projection: P)\nwhere\n    Mutation: self::Mutation<P>,\n{\n    <Mutation::Diff as MutationDiff<P>>::retire_projection(projection);\n}\n\n/// 🧊️ The live intermediate of a history fold, which retires itself on EVERY exit path. A fold walks\n/// `base → mid₁ → … → head`; its loop body already retires the projection each step displaces, but an\n/// early return — an unknown edit id, a `MutationDiff::apply` refusal, a saturated owner queue —\n/// carried the still-live one straight into a bare drop, and an artifact whose projection owns a\n/// fail-closed root (an `OrderedMap`, a neural `Dictionary`) aborts the guest there. That is why\n/// 🖨️raster's `redo` kept trapping after its `retire_projection`/`retire_cold` overrides landed:\n/// `undo` answers from the tail cache and folds nothing, while `redo` re-applies the reinstated\n/// edit's forwards in `ArtifactStore::project_applied` (since folded into [`ArtifactStore::reproject`]) and meets the `?`\n/// (measured 2026-09-20).\n/// Holding the intermediate here makes the retirement STRUCTURAL — a fold that grows a new early\n/// return cannot silently miss it, and no technology has to override anything extra to be safe.\nstruct ReplayProjection<P, Mutation>\nwhere\n    Mutation: self::Mutation<P>,\n{\n    projection: Option<P>,\n    technology: std::marker::PhantomData<fn() -> Mutation>,\n}\n\nimpl<P, Mutation> ReplayProjection<P, Mutation>\nwhere\n    Mutation: self::Mutation<P>,\n{\n    /// 🌱️ Takes ownership of a fold's base projection.\n    fn new(projection: P) -> Self {\n        Self { projection: Some(projection), technology: std::marker::PhantomData }\n    }\n\n    /// ▶️ Installs the next projection and retires the one it displaces.\n    fn advance(&mut self, next: P) {\n        let displaced = self.projection.replace(next).expect(\"a live replay projection is present until it is handed out\");\n        retire_replayed_projection::<P, Mutation>(displaced);\n    }\n\n    /// 🎁️ Hands the finished projection to the caller, who owns its retirement from here on.\n    fn into_inner(mut self) -> P {\n        self.projection.take().expect(\"a live replay projection is handed out exactly once\")\n    }\n}\n\nimpl<P, Mutation> std::ops::Deref for ReplayProjection<P, Mutation>\nwhere\n    Mutation: self::Mutation<P>,\n{\n    type Target = P;\n    fn deref(&self) -> &P {\n        self.projection.as_ref().expect(\"a live replay projection is present until it is handed out\")\n    }\n}\n\nimpl<P, Mutation> Drop for ReplayProjection<P, Mutation>\nwhere\n    Mutation: self::Mutation<P>,\n{\n    fn drop(&mut self) {\n        if let Some(projection) = self.projection.take() {\n            retire_replayed_projection::<P, Mutation>(projection);\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// 🧊️ Cold-retires scratch operations (a rebased or discarded inverse): an operation may own a\n/// fail-closed root, so a displaced copy never reaches `Drop` owning it.\nfn retire_scratch_operations<P, Mutation>(operations: Vec<Mutation>)\nwhere\n    Mutation: self::Mutation<P>,\n{\n    for operation in operations {\n        self::Mutation::<P>::retire_cold(operation);\n    }\n}\n\n/// 🧊️ Cold-retires a scratch edit copy — a decoded arrival that history already holds, a replay\n/// lookup clone, a conflict listing — through its operations' [`Mutation::retire_cold`].\n/// 🕸️ Every transition among `transitions` that `refused` names or that causally depends — through `dependencies`,\n/// transitively — on one that does, as ids in log order: what one refusal retracts. One law for a store's event log and a\n/// persisted `.spr` log ([`retract_history_transitions_from_spr`]), so both retract exactly the same transitions.\npub fn transition_retraction_closure<'a, T>(transitions: &'a [T], identity: impl Fn(&'a T) -> &'a str, dependencies: impl Fn(&'a T) -> Vec<&'a str>, refused: &[String]) -> Vec<String> {\n    let mut retracted: HashSet<&'a str> = transitions.iter().map(&identity).filter(|id| refused.iter().any(|name| name == id)).collect();\n    loop {\n        let before = retracted.len();\n        for transition in transitions {\n            if dependencies(transition).into_iter().any(|dependency| retracted.contains(dependency)) {\n                retracted.insert(identity(transition));\n            }\n        }\n        if retracted.len() == before {\n            break;\n        }\n    }\n    transitions.iter().map(&identity).filter(|id| retracted.contains(id)).map(str::to_string).collect()\n}\n\n/// 🪒️ The `.spr` byte log without the transitions `refused` retracts ([`transition_retraction_closure`]) — what a sync\n/// actor persists after the hub refused them — and the retracted ids.\npub async fn retract_history_transitions_from_spr(spr: &[u8], refused: &[String]) -> Result<(Vec<u8>, Vec<String>), VcsError> {\n    let mut log = crate::os_spr::decode_history(spr, &crate::os_spr::DecodeOptions::default()).await.map_err(|error| VcsError::Deserialize(error.to_string()))?;\n    let retracted = transition_retraction_closure(&log.transitions, |record| record.id.as_str(), |record| record.dependencies.iter().map(String::as_str).collect(), refused);\n    log.transitions.retain(|record| !retracted.contains(&record.id));\n    let options = crate::os_spr::EncodeOptions { write_backwards_section: true, ..crate::os_spr::EncodeOptions::default() };\n    let bytes = crate::os_spr::encode_history(&log, &options).await.map_err(|error| VcsError::Serialize(error.to_string()))?;\n    Ok((bytes, retracted))\n}\n\n/// 📦️ `envelopes`, in authoring order, as the fewest document-backbone batches its declaration admits\n/// (`crate::os_spr::DOCUMENT_BACKBONE_BATCH_MAXIMUM_*`): a committed tool transaction of many operations leaves as several\n/// batches the hub takes one by one, never as one batch it refuses as undeclared.\nfn document_backbone_batches(envelopes: Vec<crate::os_spr::MutationEnvelope>) -> Vec<Vec<crate::os_spr::MutationEnvelope>> {\n    const FRAMING_BYTES: usize = 16;\n    let mut batches = Vec::new();\n    let mut batch: Vec<crate::os_spr::MutationEnvelope> = Vec::new();\n    let (mut bytes, mut dependencies, mut segments) = (FRAMING_BYTES, 0usize, 0usize);\n    for envelope in envelopes {\n        let mut encoded = Vec::new();\n        crate::os_spr::encode_envelope(&envelope, &mut encoded);\n        let full = bytes + encoded.len() > crate::os_spr::DOCUMENT_BACKBONE_BATCH_MAXIMUM_BYTES\n            || batch.len() == crate::os_spr::DOCUMENT_BACKBONE_BATCH_MAXIMUM_ENVELOPES\n            || dependencies + envelope.dependencies.len() > crate::os_spr::DOCUMENT_BACKBONE_BATCH_MAXIMUM_DEPENDENCIES\n            || segments + envelope.target.len() > crate::os_spr::DOCUMENT_BACKBONE_BATCH_MAXIMUM_TARGET_SEGMENTS;\n        if full && !batch.is_empty() {\n            batches.push(std::mem::take(&mut batch));\n            (bytes, dependencies, segments) = (FRAMING_BYTES, 0, 0);\n        }\n        bytes += encoded.len();\n        dependencies += envelope.dependencies.len();\n        segments += envelope.target.len();\n        batch.push(envelope);\n    }\n    if !batch.is_empty() {\n        batches.push(batch);\n    }\n    batches\n}\n\n/// 🫗️ Retires every typed replacement of a refused supersession's `inputs`, none of which was encoded.\nfn retire_supersede_inputs<P, Mutation>(inputs: Vec<SupersedeInput<Mutation>>)\nwhere\n    Mutation: self::Mutation<P>,\n{\n    for replacement in inputs.into_iter().filter_map(|input| input.replacement) {\n        self::Mutation::<P>::retire_cold(replacement);\n    }\n}\n\nfn retire_scratch_edits<P, Mutation>(edits: impl IntoIterator<Item = Edit<Mutation>>)\nwhere\n    Mutation: self::Mutation<P>,\n{\n    for edit in edits {\n        retire_scratch_operations::<P, Mutation>(edit.forwards);\n        retire_scratch_operations::<P, Mutation>(edit.inverse);\n    }\n}\n\n/// 🧮️ Folds an envelope's complete event log — its edits and its history transitions — into\n/// the history projection (`crate::os_spr::fold_history`). Quarantined edits (every edit owning an\n/// operation of a quarantined conflict that was not accepted) stay inactive.\npub fn fold_envelope_history<P, Mutation>(envelope: &ArtifactEnvelopeOwners<P, Mutation>) -> Result<crate::os_spr::HistoryFold, VcsError>\nwhere\n    Mutation: self::Mutation<P>,\n{\n    let head = envelope_viewer_head(envelope);\n    fold_event_log::<P, Mutation>(&envelope.id, &envelope.vcs.edits.iter().collect::<Vec<_>>(), &envelope.transitions, &envelope.conflicts, &head)\n}\n\n/// 👁 The head [`fold_history_for`] projects: this replica's alternative and explicit checkpoint.\n/// Absent alternative is the canonical trunk. `viewer_checkpoint_id` of `None` is that line's tip.\nfn envelope_viewer_head<P, Mutation>(envelope: &ArtifactEnvelopeOwners<P, Mutation>) -> crate::os_spr::ViewerHead {\n    let document_id = ArtifactId(envelope.id.clone());\n    let trunk = crate::os_spr::trunk_alternative_id(&document_id);\n    crate::os_spr::ViewerHead { line_id: envelope.active_alternative_id.clone().filter(|line| line != &trunk).unwrap_or(trunk), checkpoint_id: envelope.viewer_checkpoint_id.clone() }\n}\n\n/// 🧮️ [`fold_envelope_history`] over the bare event log: `edits`, `transitions` and the\n/// `conflicts` whose quarantine withholds edits — for document shapes that hold the log without a\n/// full envelope.\npub fn fold_event_log<P, Mutation>(document_id: &str, edits: &[&Edit<Mutation>], transitions: &[crate::os_spr::MutationEnvelope], conflicts: &[crate::os_spr::Conflict], head: &crate::os_spr::ViewerHead) -> Result<crate::os_spr::HistoryFold, VcsError>\nwhere\n    Mutation: self::Mutation<P>,\n{\n    let mut folded = Vec::with_capacity(edits.len());\n    let mut owners: HashMap<String, String> = HashMap::new();\n    for edit in edits.iter().copied() {\n        let mutation_ids = crate::os_spr::mutation_ids_for_edit::<P, Mutation>(edit);\n        for mutation_id in &mutation_ids {\n            owners.insert(mutation_id.0.clone(), edit.id.clone());\n        }\n        folded.push(crate::os_spr::FoldEdit { id: edit.id.clone(), actor: edit.actor.clone(), timestamp: edit_timestamp(edit), mutation_ids, line: edit.line.clone() });\n    }\n    let mut excluded = HashSet::new();\n    for conflict in conflicts {\n        if conflict.status == crate::os_spr::ConflictStatus::Accepted {\n            continue;\n        }\n        if let crate::os_spr::ConflictKind::Quarantined { envelopes, .. } = &conflict.kind {\n            excluded.extend(envelopes.iter().filter_map(|quarantined| owners.get(&quarantined.mutation_id.0).cloned()));\n        }\n    }\n    crate::os_spr::fold_history_for(&ArtifactId(document_id.to_string()), &folded, transitions, &excluded, head).map_err(|error| VcsError::ValidationFailed(error.to_string()))\n}\n\n/// 🗣️ `<document schema>#<semantic kind>` of the leaf `operation` is — what `MutationMeta.semantic_kind` records.\nfn operation_semantic_kind<P, Mutation: self::Mutation<P>>(operation: &Mutation, schema: &str) -> SchemaId {\n    SchemaId(format!(\"{schema}#{}\", operation.descriptor().semantic_kind))\n}\n\n/// 🗣️ Stamps every metadata record of `edit` with its operation's semantic kind and descriptor name — derived facts no\n/// persisted form carries, so every load and ingest path re-derives them.\nfn stamp_edit_semantics<P, Mutation: self::Mutation<P>>(edit: &mut Edit<Mutation>, schema: &str) {\n    for (meta, operation) in edit.mutation_meta.iter_mut().zip(edit.forwards.iter()) {\n        meta.semantic_kind = Some(operation_semantic_kind::<P, Mutation>(operation, schema));\n        meta.label = Some(operation.descriptor().display_name.to_string());\n    }\n}\n\n/// ⏰️ An edit's HLC: its first operation's stamped timestamp (the order key every fold uses).\nfn edit_timestamp<Mutation>(edit: &Edit<Mutation>) -> HybridLogicalTimestamp {\n    edit.mutation_meta.first().map_or(HybridLogicalTimestamp { actor: 0, physical_ms: 0, logical: 0 }, |meta| meta.timestamp)\n}\n\n/// 🧮️ Folds the genesis over the effective forwards of `applied_edit_ids` ([`fold_effective_edit`]).\nasync fn fold_history<P, Mutation, I, S>(envelope: &ArtifactEnvelope<P, Mutation>, applied_edit_ids: I, supersessions: &EffectiveSupersessions) -> Result<P, VcsError>\nwhere\n    P: Clone,\n    Mutation: self::Mutation<P> + OpBinary,\n    I: IntoIterator<Item = S>,\n    S: AsRef<str>,\n{\n    let mut snapshot = ReplayProjection::<P, Mutation>::new(envelope.vcs.initial_snapshot.clone());\n    let mut seen = HashSet::new();\n    for edit_id in applied_edit_ids {\n        let edit_id = edit_id.as_ref();\n        if !seen.insert(edit_id.to_string()) {\n            return Err(VcsError::ValidationFailed(format!(\"history repeats applied edit {edit_id}\")));\n        }\n        let edit = envelope.vcs.edits.find_near(|entry| entry.id == edit_id).ok_or_else(|| VcsError::UnknownEdit(edit_id.to_string()))?;\n        fold_effective_edit(&mut snapshot, edit, &envelope.schema, supersessions, usize::MAX);\n    }\n    Ok(snapshot.into_inner())\n}\n//#endregion 🔖️ArtifactStore\n\n//#region 🔖️EffectiveForwards\n/// 🪞️ The effective supersession of every superseded operation ([`protocol::HistoryFold::supersessions`]): the\n/// replacement input every fold site reads in place of the recorded forward, which is never modified.\npub type EffectiveSupersessions = BTreeMap<MutationId, protocol::EffectiveSupersession>;\n\n/// 🎭️ One forward operation as every fold site reads it: the recorded original, its decoded replacement, or nothing\n/// when withdrawn or when its supersession breaks the supersede law ([`admit_replacement`]). A decoded replacement\n/// retires itself through [`Mutation::retire_cold`].\npub struct EffectiveOperation<'a, P, Mutation>\nwhere\n    Mutation: self::Mutation<P>,\n{\n    pub op_index: u32,\n    pub mutation_id: MutationId,\n    original: &'a Mutation,\n    replacement: Option<Mutation>,\n    withdrawn: bool,\n    fault: Option<crate::os_spr::MutationMessage>,\n    marker: PhantomData<fn() -> P>,\n}\n\nimpl<P, Mutation> EffectiveOperation<'_, P, Mutation>\nwhere\n    Mutation: self::Mutation<P>,\n{\n    /// ▶️ The operation a fold applies, `None` when withdrawn or faulted.\n    pub fn operation(&self) -> Option<&Mutation> {\n        if self.withdrawn || self.fault.is_some() {\n            return None;\n        }\n        Some(self.replacement.as_ref().unwrap_or(self.original))\n    }\n\n    /// 🔀️ Whether a supersession replaced or withdrew the recorded forward (validly or not).\n    pub fn superseded(&self) -> bool {\n        self.withdrawn || self.replacement.is_some() || self.fault.is_some()\n    }\n\n    /// 🚫️ Whether a valid supersession withdrew the operation.\n    pub fn withdrawn(&self) -> bool {\n        self.withdrawn\n    }\n\n    /// 🧯️ The `Fatal` message of a supersession breaking the supersede law; the operation then folds as a no-op.\n    pub fn fault(&self) -> Option<&crate::os_spr::MutationMessage> {\n        self.fault.as_ref()\n    }\n}\n\nimpl<P, Mutation> Drop for EffectiveOperation<'_, P, Mutation>\nwhere\n    Mutation: self::Mutation<P>,\n{\n    fn drop(&mut self) {\n        if let Some(replacement) = self.replacement.take() {\n            self::Mutation::<P>::retire_cold(replacement);\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// 🔍️ The effective input of `operation` — operation `op_index` of its edit, identified as `mutation_id` — under\n/// `supersessions` in a document of `schema`. Total: a supersession breaking the supersede law ([`admit_replacement`])\n/// folds the operation as a no-op carrying one `Fatal` `mutation.invariant` message that targets the operation —\n/// identically at every fold site, so a garbage or foreign replacement never aborts a projection.\npub fn effective_operation<'a, P, Mutation>(operation: &'a Mutation, op_index: u32, mutation_id: MutationId, schema: &str, supersessions: &EffectiveSupersessions) -> EffectiveOperation<'a, P, Mutation>\nwhere\n    Mutation: self::Mutation<P> + OpBinary,\n{\n    let mut effective = EffectiveOperation { op_index, mutation_id, original: operation, replacement: None, withdrawn: false, fault: None, marker: PhantomData };\n    let Some(supersession) = supersessions.get(&effective.mutation_id) else { return effective };\n    match admit_replacement::<P, Mutation>(operation, &supersession.replacement, schema) {\n        Ok(Some(replacement)) => effective.replacement = Some(replacement),\n        Ok(None) => effective.withdrawn = true,\n        Err(reason) => {\n            let mut fault = crate::os_spr::MutationMessage::fatal(\"mutation.invariant\", format!(\"supersession {} of {} {reason}; the operation folds as a no-op\", supersession.transition_id, effective.mutation_id.0)).at([effective.mutation_id.0.clone()]);\n            fault.op_index = Some(op_index);\n            effective.fault = Some(fault);\n        }\n    }\n    effective\n}\n\n/// 🛂️ The supersede law every input obeys — authored, ingested, loaded or folded: `original` plans no foreign steps, and\n/// a replacement is an operation of `schema` in its canonical encoding planning no foreign steps. Answers the decoded\n/// replacement (`None` for a withdrawal) or why the input breaks the law.\npub fn admit_replacement<P, Mutation>(original: &Mutation, replacement: &protocol::InputReplacement, schema: &str) -> Result<Option<Mutation>, String>\nwhere\n    Mutation: self::Mutation<P> + OpBinary,\n{\n    if original.may_emit_foreign_steps() {\n        return Err(\"targets an operation that plans foreign steps\".to_string());\n    }\n    let protocol::InputReplacement::Input { schema: named, payload } = replacement else { return Ok(None) };\n    if named != schema {\n        return Err(format!(\"names schema {named}, not {schema}\"));\n    }\n    let decoded = Mutation::decode_op(payload).map_err(|error| format!(\"does not decode: {error}\"))?;\n    let refusal = match decoded.encode_op() {\n        Err(error) => Some(format!(\"does not re-encode: {error}\")),\n        Ok(recoded) if recoded != *payload => Some(\"is not canonically encoded\".to_string()),\n        Ok(_) if decoded.may_emit_foreign_steps() => Some(\"plans foreign steps\".to_string()),\n        Ok(_) => None,\n    };\n    match refusal {\n        None => Ok(Some(decoded)),\n        Some(reason) => {\n            self::Mutation::<P>::retire_cold(decoded);\n            Err(reason)\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// 📜️ `edit`'s effective forwards in operation order ([`effective_operation`]). The single accessor every fold site\n/// reads an edit through.\npub fn effective_forwards<'a, P, Mutation>(edit: &'a Edit<Mutation>, schema: &'a str, supersessions: &'a EffectiveSupersessions) -> impl Iterator<Item = EffectiveOperation<'a, P, Mutation>> + 'a\nwhere\n    P: 'a,\n    Mutation: self::Mutation<P> + OpBinary + 'a,\n{\n    let ids = crate::os_spr::mutation_ids_for_edit::<P, Mutation>(edit);\n    edit.forwards.iter().zip(ids).enumerate().map(move |(index, (operation, mutation_id))| effective_operation::<P, Mutation>(operation, index as u32, mutation_id, schema, supersessions))\n}\n\n/// 🪜️ A fold's running projection: what the next operation diffs against, and how its successor displaces it.\ntrait FoldProjection<P, Mutation> {\n    fn projection(&self) -> &P;\n    fn advance(&mut self, next: P);\n}\n\nimpl<P, Mutation> FoldProjection<P, Mutation> for ReplayProjection<P, Mutation>\nwhere\n    Mutation: self::Mutation<P>,\n{\n    fn projection(&self) -> &P {\n        self\n    }\n\n    fn advance(&mut self, next: P) {\n        ReplayProjection::advance(self, next);\n    }\n}\n\nimpl<P, Mutation> FoldProjection<P, Mutation> for Arc<P>\nwhere\n    Mutation: self::Mutation<P>,\n{\n    fn projection(&self) -> &P {\n        self\n    }\n\n    fn advance(&mut self, next: P) {\n        retire_shared_projection::<P, Mutation>(std::mem::replace(self, Arc::new(next)));\n    }\n}\n\n/// 🔂️ Folds the first `take` effective forwards of `edit` into `projection` with keep-and-record semantics\n/// ([`fold_operation`]) — the one loop every messageless fold site shares.\nfn fold_effective_edit<P, Mutation>(projection: &mut impl FoldProjection<P, Mutation>, edit: &Edit<Mutation>, schema: &str, supersessions: &EffectiveSupersessions, take: usize)\nwhere\n    Mutation: self::Mutation<P> + OpBinary,\n{\n    if supersessions.is_empty() {\n        for (index, operation) in edit.forwards.iter().enumerate().take(take) {\n            if let (Some(next), _) = fold_operation::<P, Mutation>(projection.projection(), operation, index as u32) {\n                projection.advance(next);\n            }\n        }\n        return;\n    }\n    for effective in effective_forwards::<P, Mutation>(edit, schema, supersessions).take(take) {\n        if let Some(operation) = effective.operation() {\n            if let (Some(next), _) = fold_operation::<P, Mutation>(projection.projection(), operation, effective.op_index) {\n                projection.advance(next);\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// 🎬️ One operation with [`protocol::MutationOutcome::apply_to`] semantics that never drops a projection: the next\n/// projection when its diff applied, and its op-stamped messages — an apply refusal becomes one `Fatal` message and\n/// folds as a no-op. The keep-and-record step every fold site, the retained initializers included, takes.\npub fn fold_operation<P, Mutation>(state: &P, operation: &Mutation, op_index: u32) -> (Option<P>, Vec<crate::os_spr::MutationMessage>)\nwhere\n    Mutation: self::Mutation<P>,\n{\n    let (diff, mut messages) = operation.diff(state).stamp_op_index(op_index).into_parts();\n    let applied = diff.apply(state);\n    <Mutation::Diff as MutationDiff<P>>::retire_cold(diff);\n    match applied {\n        Ok(next) => (Some(next), messages),\n        Err(error) => {\n            let mut fatal = crate::os_spr::MutationMessage::fatal(error.code, error.message).at(error.target);\n            fatal.op_index = Some(op_index);\n            messages.push(fatal);\n            (None, messages)\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// 📼️ Folds `applied[from..to]` onto `base` under `supersessions` with keep-and-record semantics, handing out the\n/// projection after every prefix length below `to` that is a multiple of `stride` (aliases of the running state, no\n/// copies). A failure retires the running state and everything recorded.\nfn fold_recorded<P, Mutation>(base: Arc<P>, applied: &[String], from: usize, to: usize, edits: &ArtifactHistoryLedger<Edit<Mutation>>, schema: &str, supersessions: &EffectiveSupersessions, stride: usize) -> Result<(Arc<P>, Vec<(usize, Arc<P>)>), VcsError>\nwhere\n    Mutation: self::Mutation<P> + OpBinary,\n{\n    let mut running = base;\n    let mut recorded: Vec<(usize, Arc<P>)> = Vec::new();\n    let mut failure = None;\n    for (offset, edit_id) in applied[from..to].iter().enumerate() {\n        let Some(edit) = edits.find_near(|edit| edit.id == *edit_id) else {\n            failure = Some(VcsError::UnknownEdit(edit_id.clone()));\n            break;\n        };\n        fold_effective_edit(&mut running, edit, schema, supersessions, usize::MAX);\n        let length = from + offset + 1;\n        if length < to && length % stride == 0 {\n            recorded.push((length, Arc::clone(&running)));\n        }\n    }\n    if let Some(error) = failure {\n        retire_shared_projection::<P, Mutation>(running);\n        for (_, snapshot) in recorded {\n            retire_shared_projection::<P, Mutation>(snapshot);\n        }\n        return Err(error);\n    }\n    Ok((running, recorded))\n}\n\n/// 🧊️ Releases one alias of a scratch projection: the last owner retires it ([`retire_replayed_projection`]), any\n/// other only drops its count — the owner that outlives it retires it.\nfn retire_shared_projection<P, Mutation>(projection: Arc<P>)\nwhere\n    Mutation: self::Mutation<P>,\n{\n    if let Ok(projection) = Arc::try_unwrap(projection) {\n        retire_replayed_projection::<P, Mutation>(projection);\n    }\n}\n\n/// 🔏️ Content digest of one effective supersession: which transition installed it and what it replaces the input with.\nfn supersession_digest(mutation_id: &MutationId, supersession: &protocol::EffectiveSupersession) -> [u8; 32] {\n    let (kind, schema, payload): (&[u8], &[u8], &[u8]) = match &supersession.replacement {\n        protocol::InputReplacement::Input { schema, payload } => (b\"input\", schema.as_bytes(), payload),\n        protocol::InputReplacement::Withdrawn => (b\"withdrawn\", b\"\", b\"\"),\n    };\n    CursorRevisionAccumulator::hash_record(b\"supersession\", &[mutation_id.0.as_bytes(), supersession.transition_id.as_bytes(), kind, schema, payload])\n}\n\n/// 🔐️ Digest of the supersessions in effect for `edit`'s operations, `None` when none is.\nfn edit_supersession_digest<P, Mutation>(edit: &Edit<Mutation>, supersessions: &EffectiveSupersessions) -> Option<[u8; 32]>\nwhere\n    Mutation: self::Mutation<P>,\n{\n    if supersessions.is_empty() {\n        return None;\n    }\n    let mut digest = None;\n    for (index, mutation_id) in crate::os_spr::mutation_ids_for_edit::<P, Mutation>(edit).iter().enumerate() {\n        if let Some(supersession) = supersessions.get(mutation_id) {\n            digest = Some(CursorRevisionAccumulator::hash_record(b\"edit-supersessions\", &[&digest.unwrap_or([0; 32]), &(index as u64).to_be_bytes(), &supersession_digest(mutation_id, supersession)]));\n        }\n    }\n    digest\n}\n\n/// 🤝️ How many leading ids `live` and `next` share.\nfn shared_prefix_len(live: &crate::os_vcs::HistoryPageStack<String>, next: &[String]) -> usize {\n    live.iter().zip(next).take_while(|(live, next)| live == next).count()\n}\n\n/// 🪞️ Rewrites `mirror` from position `dirty` on to `live`'s suffix ([`StackMirrorDirt`]); answers the ids it displaced.\nfn mirror_id_suffix(mirror: &mut crate::os_vcs::HistoryPageStack<String>, live: &crate::os_vcs::HistoryPageStack<String>, dirty: usize) -> Option<Vec<String>> {\n    let keep = dirty.min(live.len()).min(mirror.len());\n    let mut displaced = Vec::new();\n    while mirror.len() > keep {\n        displaced.push(mirror.pop().expect(\"a mirrored id remains present\"));\n    }\n    #[cfg(test)]\n    hot_path_census::count(|census| census.mirrored += live.len() - keep);\n    mirror.extend(live.iter_from(keep).cloned());\n    (!displaced.is_empty()).then_some(displaced)\n}\n\n/// 🧭️ Forwards-only effective prefix digests of `applied`: entry `i` names the projection after the first `i` edits by\n/// their ids, forward counts and effective supersessions — never the inverses, metadata or messages a replay rewrites.\nfn forward_prefix_digests<P, Mutation, I, S>(identity: [u8; 32], applied: I, edits: &ArtifactHistoryLedger<Edit<Mutation>>, supersessions: &EffectiveSupersessions) -> Result<Vec<[u8; 32]>, VcsError>\nwhere\n    Mutation: self::Mutation<P>,\n    I: IntoIterator<Item = S>,\n    S: AsRef<str>,\n{\n    let mut digest = CursorRevisionAccumulator::hash_record(b\"forward-prefix\", &[&identity]);\n    let mut digests = Vec::new();\n    digests.push(digest);\n    for edit_id in applied {\n        let edit_id = edit_id.as_ref();\n        #[cfg(test)]\n        hot_path_census::count(|census| census.digested += 1);\n        let edit = edits.find_near(|edit| edit.id == edit_id).ok_or_else(|| VcsError::UnknownEdit(edit_id.to_string()))?;\n        let superseded = edit_supersession_digest::<P, Mutation>(edit, supersessions).unwrap_or([0; 32]);\n        digest = CursorRevisionAccumulator::hash_record(b\"forward-prefix\", &[&digest, edit_id.as_bytes(), &(edit.forwards.len() as u64).to_be_bytes(), &superseded]);\n        digests.push(digest);\n    }\n    Ok(digests)\n}\n\n/// 🧮️ The applied positions of every edit owning an operation whose effective supersession differs between `previous`\n/// and `next`, ascending.\nfn superseded_positions<P, Mutation>(applied: &[String], edits: &ArtifactHistoryLedger<Edit<Mutation>>, previous: &EffectiveSupersessions, next: &EffectiveSupersessions) -> Result<Vec<usize>, VcsError>\nwhere\n    Mutation: self::Mutation<P>,\n{\n    let changed: HashSet<&MutationId> = previous.iter().filter(|(target, supersession)| next.get(*target) != Some(*supersession)).map(|(target, _)| target).chain(next.iter().filter(|(target, supersession)| previous.get(*target) != Some(*supersession)).map(|(target, _)| target)).collect();\n    if changed.is_empty() {\n        return Ok(Vec::new());\n    }\n    let mut positions = Vec::new();\n    for (position, edit_id) in applied.iter().enumerate() {\n        let edit = edits.find_near(|edit| edit.id == *edit_id).ok_or_else(|| VcsError::UnknownEdit(edit_id.clone()))?;\n        if crate::os_spr::mutation_ids_for_edit::<P, Mutation>(edit).iter().any(|mutation_id| changed.contains(mutation_id)) {\n            positions.push(position);\n        }\n    }\n    Ok(positions)\n}\n\n/// 📝️ `supersessions` with every draft replacement laid over it — the effective inputs a time-travel session previews.\npub fn draft_supersessions(supersessions: &EffectiveSupersessions, drafts: &BTreeMap<MutationId, protocol::InputReplacement>) -> EffectiveSupersessions {\n    let mut effective = supersessions.clone();\n    for (target, replacement) in drafts {\n        effective.insert(target.clone(), protocol::EffectiveSupersession { transition_id: DRAFT_SUPERSESSION_ID.to_string(), actor: String::new(), timestamp: HybridLogicalTimestamp::new(0, 0), scope: None, replacement: replacement.clone() });\n    }\n    effective\n}\n\n/// 🏷️ The transition id a not-yet-authored draft supersession carries inside a preview.\npub const DRAFT_SUPERSESSION_ID: &str = \"draft\";\n//#endregion 🔖️EffectiveForwards\n\n//#region 🔖️EditReplay\n/// ⚖️ How an [`EditReplay`] settles each edit. `Merge(policy)` is the policy-local ingest verdict: an edit whose worst\n/// message the policy rejects is quarantined and an apply refusal aborts the replay. `Report` keeps every edit, records\n/// every outcome and never aborts, so its result is policy-independent and identical on every replica.\n#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum ReplayMode {\n    Merge(crate::os_spr::MergePolicy),\n    Report,\n}\n\n/// 📚️ Where a replay reads the edits its order names.\npub trait ReplayEdits<Mutation> {\n    fn replay_edit(&self, edit_id: &str) -> Option<&Edit<Mutation>>;\n}\n\nimpl<Mutation> ReplayEdits<Mutation> for HashMap<String, Edit<Mutation>> {\n    fn replay_edit(&self, edit_id: &str) -> Option<&Edit<Mutation>> {\n        self.get(edit_id)\n    }\n}\n\nimpl<Mutation> ReplayEdits<Mutation> for ArtifactHistoryLedger<Edit<Mutation>> {\n    fn replay_edit(&self, edit_id: &str) -> Option<&Edit<Mutation>> {\n        self.find_near(|edit| edit.id == edit_id)\n    }\n}\n\n/// 📶️ `done` of `total` operations a replay folded.\n#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub struct ReplayProgress {\n    pub done: u32,\n    pub total: u32,\n}\n\n/// ⏯️ Where one [`EditReplay::step`] left its replay.\n#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum ReplayStep {\n    Pending(ReplayProgress),\n    Finished(ReplayProgress),\n}\n\n/// 🧲️ The previous projection a Report replay may converge onto. From prefix length `horizon` on every changed input\n/// has been replayed, so a prefix whose state equals the previous state after the same prefix leaves the whole tail\n/// unchanged: the previous head is spliced in and the replay stops. `checkpoints` ascend by prefix length and end with\n/// the previous head.\nstruct ReplayConvergence<P> {\n    horizon: usize,\n    checkpoints: Vec<(usize, Arc<P>)>,\n    equal: fn(&P, &P) -> bool,\n}\n\n/// ⏪️ Resumable replay of `order[from..]` over the projection after `order[..from]`, one operation per inner step:\n/// each operation's effective input is re-diffed and re-inverted against the running state and its messages are kept\n/// per mutation with their operation index. [`ArtifactStore::replay_suffix_partitioned`] drives a `Merge` replay to\n/// completion; history editing steps a `Report` replay under a deadline with progress. Cancelling is dropping it: the\n/// running projections, staged inverses and checkpoint aliases all retire.\npub struct EditReplay<P, Mutation>\nwhere\n    Mutation: self::Mutation<P>,\n{\n    mode: ReplayMode,\n    order: Vec<String>,\n    from: usize,\n    cursor: usize,\n    operation: usize,\n    edit_ids: Option<Vec<MutationId>>,\n    schema: String,\n    supersessions: EffectiveSupersessions,\n    state: Option<Arc<P>>,\n    candidate: Option<Arc<P>>,\n    edit_messages: Vec<crate::os_spr::MutationMessage>,\n    edit_inverse: Vec<Mutation>,\n    committed: Vec<String>,\n    quarantined: Vec<String>,\n    rebased_inverse: Vec<(String, Vec<Mutation>)>,\n    replayed: Vec<crate::os_spr::EditMessages>,\n    outcomes: Vec<protocol::MutationReplayOutcome>,\n    convergence: Option<ReplayConvergence<P>>,\n    converged_at: Option<usize>,\n    record_stride: usize,\n    recorded: Vec<(usize, Arc<P>)>,\n    drafts: BTreeMap<MutationId, protocol::InputReplacement>,\n    generation: u64,\n    revision: [u8; 32],\n    progress: ReplayProgress,\n    finished: bool,\n}\n\nimpl<P, Mutation> EditReplay<P, Mutation>\nwhere\n    Mutation: self::Mutation<P> + OpBinary,\n{\n    /// 🐣️ A replay of `order[from..]` starting from `base`, the projection after `order[..from]`, reading every\n    /// operation of a document of `schema` through `supersessions`. `edits` must hold every edit the suffix names.\n    pub fn new(mode: ReplayMode, base: Arc<P>, order: Vec<String>, from: usize, schema: &str, supersessions: EffectiveSupersessions, edits: &impl ReplayEdits<Mutation>) -> Result<Self, VcsError> {\n        let mut replay = Self {\n            mode,\n            order,\n            from,\n            cursor: from,\n            operation: 0,\n            edit_ids: None,\n            schema: schema.to_string(),\n            supersessions,\n            state: Some(base),\n            candidate: None,\n            edit_messages: Vec::new(),\n            edit_inverse: Vec::new(),\n            committed: Vec::new(),\n            quarantined: Vec::new(),\n            rebased_inverse: Vec::new(),\n            replayed: Vec::new(),\n            outcomes: Vec::new(),\n            convergence: None,\n            converged_at: None,\n            record_stride: usize::MAX,\n            recorded: Vec::new(),\n            drafts: BTreeMap::new(),\n            generation: 0,\n            revision: [0; 32],\n            progress: ReplayProgress::default(),\n            finished: false,\n        };\n        if replay.from > replay.order.len() {\n            return Err(VcsError::ValidationFailed(format!(\"edit replay starts at {} past its {}-edit order\", replay.from, replay.order.len())));\n        }\n        let mut total = 0u32;\n        for edit_id in &replay.order[replay.from..] {\n            let edit = edits.replay_edit(edit_id).ok_or_else(|| VcsError::UnknownEdit(edit_id.clone()))?;\n            total = total.saturating_add(u32::try_from(edit.forwards.len()).unwrap_or(u32::MAX));\n        }\n        replay.progress.total = total;\n        Ok(replay)\n    }\n\n    fn with_convergence(mut self, convergence: Option<ReplayConvergence<P>>) -> Self {\n        if let Some(previous) = std::mem::replace(&mut self.convergence, convergence) {\n            for (_, checkpoint) in previous.checkpoints {\n                retire_shared_projection::<P, Mutation>(checkpoint);\n            }\n        }\n        self\n    }\n\n    /// 🎙️ Keeps the projection after every replayed prefix whose length is a multiple of `stride`, for the prefix ring —\n    /// seeded with `prefixes`, the retained projections the base was folded through, and with the base itself when its\n    /// length is such a multiple.\n    fn recording(mut self, stride: usize, prefixes: Vec<(usize, Arc<P>)>) -> Self {\n        self.record_stride = stride.max(1);\n        self.recorded.extend(prefixes);\n        self.record();\n        self\n    }\n\n    /// 🔢️ Stamps the store generation and content revision this replay was started against — the freshness a finished\n    /// replay is committed under ([`ArtifactStore::commit_finished_replay`]).\n    pub fn with_base(mut self, generation: u64, revision: [u8; 32]) -> Self {\n        self.generation = generation;\n        self.revision = revision;\n        self\n    }\n\n    /// 🖊️ Records the draft inputs this replay previews, which a finalization authors as the supersession.\n    pub fn with_drafts(mut self, drafts: BTreeMap<MutationId, protocol::InputReplacement>) -> Self {\n        self.drafts = drafts;\n        self\n    }\n\n    /// 🆔️ The store generation this replay was started against.\n    pub fn generation(&self) -> u64 {\n        self.generation\n    }\n\n    /// 🗒️ The draft inputs this replay previews.\n    pub fn drafts(&self) -> &BTreeMap<MutationId, protocol::InputReplacement> {\n        &self.drafts\n    }\n\n    /// 📈️ Operations folded so far of the suffix total.\n    pub fn progress(&self) -> ReplayProgress {\n        self.progress\n    }\n\n    /// ⌛️ Whether every operation of the suffix was replayed (or the replay converged).\n    pub fn is_finished(&self) -> bool {\n        self.finished\n    }\n\n    /// ⏭️ Replays operations until the replay finishes or `deadline`, asked after every operation, answers `true`.\n    pub fn step(&mut self, edits: &impl ReplayEdits<Mutation>, deadline: &mut dyn FnMut() -> bool) -> Result<ReplayStep, VcsError> {\n        while !self.finished {\n            let Some(edit_id) = self.order.get(self.cursor) else {\n                self.finished = true;\n                break;\n            };\n            let edit = edits.replay_edit(edit_id).ok_or_else(|| VcsError::UnknownEdit(edit_id.clone()))?;\n            let edit_ids = match self.edit_ids.take() {\n                Some(edit_ids) => edit_ids,\n                None => crate::os_spr::mutation_ids_for_edit::<P, Mutation>(edit),\n            };\n            if self.operation < edit.forwards.len() {\n                let replayed = self.replay_operation(edit, &edit_ids);\n                self.edit_ids = Some(edit_ids);\n                replayed?;\n                self.operation += 1;\n                self.progress.done = self.progress.done.saturating_add(1);\n                if deadline() {\n                    return Ok(ReplayStep::Pending(self.progress));\n                }\n                continue;\n            }\n            self.close_edit(&edit.id);\n            self.cursor += 1;\n            self.operation = 0;\n            self.record();\n            self.converge();\n        }\n        Ok(ReplayStep::Finished(self.progress))\n    }\n\n    fn replay_operation(&mut self, edit: &Edit<Mutation>, edit_ids: &[MutationId]) -> Result<(), VcsError> {\n        let index = self.operation;\n        let mutation_id = edit_ids.get(index).cloned().unwrap_or_else(|| MutationId(format!(\"{}#{index}\", edit.id)));\n        let effective = effective_operation::<P, Mutation>(&edit.forwards[index], index as u32, mutation_id, &self.schema, &self.supersessions);\n        let mut messages: Vec<crate::os_spr::MutationMessage> = effective.fault().cloned().into_iter().collect();\n        if let Some(operation) = effective.operation() {\n            let base = match self.mode {\n                ReplayMode::Merge(_) => self.candidate.as_ref().or(self.state.as_ref()),\n                ReplayMode::Report => self.state.as_ref(),\n            }\n            .ok_or_else(|| VcsError::ValidationFailed(\"edit replay lost its running projection\".into()))?;\n            let mut back = operation.inverse(base);\n            back.reverse();\n            let next = match self.mode {\n                ReplayMode::Report => {\n                    let (next, operation_messages) = fold_operation::<P, Mutation>(base, operation, index as u32);\n                    messages = operation_messages;\n                    next\n                }\n                ReplayMode::Merge(_) => {\n                    let (diff, operation_messages) = operation.diff(base).stamp_op_index(index as u32).into_parts();\n                    let applied = diff.apply(base);\n                    <Mutation::Diff as MutationDiff<P>>::retire_cold(diff);\n                    messages = operation_messages;\n                    match applied {\n                        Ok(next) => Some(next),\n                        Err(error) => {\n                            retire_scratch_operations::<P, Mutation>(back);\n                            return Err(error.into());\n                        }\n                    }\n                }\n            };\n            match next {\n                Some(next) => {\n                    self.edit_inverse.extend(back);\n                    let next = Arc::new(next);\n                    let displaced = match self.mode {\n                        ReplayMode::Merge(_) => self.candidate.replace(next),\n                        ReplayMode::Report => self.state.replace(next),\n                    };\n                    if let Some(displaced) = displaced {\n                        retire_shared_projection::<P, Mutation>(displaced);\n                    }\n                }\n                None => retire_scratch_operations::<P, Mutation>(back),\n            }\n        }\n        let worst = crate::os_spr::worst_level(&messages);\n        self.edit_messages.extend(messages.iter().cloned());\n        self.outcomes.push(protocol::MutationReplayOutcome { mutation_id: effective.mutation_id.clone(), edit_id: edit.id.clone(), op_index: index as u32, worst, messages, superseded: effective.superseded(), withdrawn: effective.withdrawn() });\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    fn close_edit(&mut self, edit_id: &str) {\n        let mut messages = std::mem::take(&mut self.edit_messages);\n        if bound_edit_messages(edit_id, &mut messages) {\n            for outcome in self.outcomes.iter_mut().rev().take_while(|outcome| outcome.edit_id == edit_id) {\n                outcome.messages = messages.iter().filter(|message| message.op_index == Some(outcome.op_index)).cloned().collect();\n                outcome.worst = crate::os_spr::worst_level(&outcome.messages);\n            }\n        }\n        let inverse = std::mem::take(&mut self.edit_inverse);\n        let rejects = match self.mode {\n            ReplayMode::Merge(policy) => crate::os_spr::worst_level(&messages).is_some_and(|level| policy.rejects(level)),\n            ReplayMode::Report => false,\n        };\n        self.replayed.push(crate::os_spr::EditMessages { edit_id: edit_id.to_string(), messages });\n        if rejects {\n            if let Some(candidate) = self.candidate.take() {\n                retire_shared_projection::<P, Mutation>(candidate);\n            }\n            retire_scratch_operations::<P, Mutation>(inverse);\n            self.quarantined.push(edit_id.to_string());\n            return;\n        }\n        if let Some(candidate) = self.candidate.take() {\n            if let Some(previous) = self.state.replace(candidate) {\n                retire_shared_projection::<P, Mutation>(previous);\n            }\n        }\n        self.rebased_inverse.push((edit_id.to_string(), inverse));\n        self.committed.push(edit_id.to_string());\n    }\n\n    fn record(&mut self) {\n        if self.mode != ReplayMode::Report || self.cursor % self.record_stride != 0 || self.cursor >= self.order.len() {\n            return;\n        }\n        if let Some(state) = self.state.as_ref() {\n            self.recorded.push((self.cursor, Arc::clone(state)));\n        }\n    }\n\n    fn converge(&mut self) {\n        if self.mode != ReplayMode::Report {\n            return;\n        }\n        let Some(convergence) = self.convergence.as_ref() else { return };\n        if self.cursor < convergence.horizon || self.cursor >= self.order.len() {\n            return;\n        }\n        let (Some(state), Some((_, previous))) = (self.state.as_ref(), convergence.checkpoints.iter().find(|(length, _)| *length == self.cursor)) else { return };\n        if !(Arc::ptr_eq(state, previous) || (convergence.equal)(state, previous)) {\n            return;\n        }\n        let Some(head) = convergence.checkpoints.last().filter(|(length, _)| *length == self.order.len()).map(|(_, head)| Arc::clone(head)) else { return };\n        self.converged_at = Some(self.cursor);\n        self.finished = true;\n        self.progress.done = self.progress.total;\n        if let Some(previous) = self.state.replace(head) {\n            retire_shared_projection::<P, Mutation>(previous);\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// 🏁️ The finished replay's result; refused while operations remain.\n    pub fn finish(mut self) -> Result<EditReplayResult<P, Mutation>, VcsError> {\n        if !self.finished {\n            return Err(VcsError::ValidationFailed(\"edit replay has not finished\".into()));\n        }\n        let outcomes = std::mem::take(&mut self.outcomes);\n        let worst = outcomes.iter().filter_map(|outcome| outcome.worst).max();\n        Ok(EditReplayResult {\n            order: std::mem::take(&mut self.order),\n            from: self.from,\n            supersessions: std::mem::take(&mut self.supersessions),\n            drafts: std::mem::take(&mut self.drafts),\n            generation: self.generation,\n            revision: self.revision,\n            state: self.state.take(),\n            converged_at: self.converged_at,\n            committed: std::mem::take(&mut self.committed),\n            quarantined: std::mem::take(&mut self.quarantined),\n            rebased_inverse: std::mem::take(&mut self.rebased_inverse),\n            replayed: std::mem::take(&mut self.replayed),\n            recorded: std::mem::take(&mut self.recorded),\n            report: protocol::ReplayReport { from_position: u32::try_from(self.from).unwrap_or(u32::MAX), outcomes, worst },\n        })\n    }\n\n    /// 🛑️ Cancels the replay; every scratch owner it holds retires and nothing it computed is published.\n    pub fn cancel(self) {\n        drop(self);\n    }\n}\n\nimpl<P, Mutation> Drop for EditReplay<P, Mutation>\nwhere\n    Mutation: self::Mutation<P>,\n{\n    fn drop(&mut self) {\n        for projection in [self.state.take(), self.candidate.take()].into_iter().flatten() {\n            retire_shared_projection::<P, Mutation>(projection);\n        }\n        retire_scratch_operations::<P, Mutation>(std::mem::take(&mut self.edit_inverse));\n        for (_, inverse) in std::mem::take(&mut self.rebased_inverse) {\n            retire_scratch_operations::<P, Mutation>(inverse);\n        }\n        if let Some(convergence) = self.convergence.take() {\n            for (_, checkpoint) in convergence.checkpoints {\n                retire_shared_projection::<P, Mutation>(checkpoint);\n            }\n        }\n        for (_, recorded) in std::mem::take(&mut self.recorded) {\n            retire_shared_projection::<P, Mutation>(recorded);\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// 🎁️ What a finished [`EditReplay`] produced: the projection it reached, the edits it kept and quarantined, their\n/// rebased inverses and messages, and its per-mutation [`protocol::ReplayReport`]. Owners nobody took retire on drop.\npub struct EditReplayResult<P, Mutation>\nwhere\n    Mutation: self::Mutation<P>,\n{\n    order: Vec<String>,\n    from: usize,\n    supersessions: EffectiveSupersessions,\n    drafts: BTreeMap<MutationId, protocol::InputReplacement>,\n    generation: u64,\n    revision: [u8; 32],\n    state: Option<Arc<P>>,\n    converged_at: Option<usize>,\n    committed: Vec<String>,\n    quarantined: Vec<String>,\n    rebased_inverse: Vec<(String, Vec<Mutation>)>,\n    replayed: Vec<crate::os_spr::EditMessages>,\n    recorded: Vec<(usize, Arc<P>)>,\n    report: protocol::ReplayReport,\n}\n\nimpl<P, Mutation> EditReplayResult<P, Mutation>\nwhere\n    Mutation: self::Mutation<P>,\n{\n    /// ⏲️ The store generation the replay was started against.\n    pub fn generation(&self) -> u64 {\n        self.generation\n    }\n\n    /// 📃️ The draft inputs the replay previewed.\n    pub fn drafts(&self) -> &BTreeMap<MutationId, protocol::InputReplacement> {\n        &self.drafts\n    }\n\n    /// 🖼️ The projection the replay reached (the previous head when it converged).\n    pub fn state(&self) -> Option<&Arc<P>> {\n        self.state.as_ref()\n    }\n\n    /// 🎴️ Takes the reached projection; its retirement moves to the caller.\n    pub fn take_state(&mut self) -> Option<Arc<P>> {\n        self.state.take()\n    }\n\n    /// 🤝️ The prefix length at which the replay met the previous projection, if it did.\n    pub fn converged_at(&self) -> Option<usize> {\n        self.converged_at\n    }\n\n    /// ✅️ The edits the replay kept, in order.\n    pub fn committed(&self) -> &[String] {\n        &self.committed\n    }\n\n    /// 🚧️ The edits a `Merge` policy quarantined, in order.\n    pub fn quarantined(&self) -> &[String] {\n        &self.quarantined\n    }\n\n    /// 📨️ Every replayed edit's messages, in order.\n    pub fn replayed(&self) -> &[crate::os_spr::EditMessages] {\n        &self.replayed\n    }\n\n    /// 📊️ The per-mutation outcomes.\n    pub fn report(&self) -> &protocol::ReplayReport {\n        &self.report\n    }\n\n    /// 🪝️ Takes the per-mutation outcomes.\n    pub fn take_report(&mut self) -> protocol::ReplayReport {\n        std::mem::take(&mut self.report)\n    }\n\n    /// ☑️ Takes the kept edit ids.\n    pub fn take_committed(&mut self) -> Vec<String> {\n        std::mem::take(&mut self.committed)\n    }\n\n    /// 🪤️ Takes the quarantined edit ids.\n    pub fn take_quarantined(&mut self) -> Vec<String> {\n        std::mem::take(&mut self.quarantined)\n    }\n\n    /// 📬️ Takes the replayed edits' messages.\n    pub fn take_replayed(&mut self) -> Vec<crate::os_spr::EditMessages> {\n        std::mem::take(&mut self.replayed)\n    }\n\n    /// 🧳️ Takes the recorded prefix projections `(length, projection)`; their retirement moves to the caller.\n    pub fn take_recorded(&mut self) -> Vec<(usize, Arc<P>)> {\n        std::mem::take(&mut self.recorded)\n    }\n\n    /// 🔙️ Takes every kept edit's rebased inverse; their retirement moves to the caller.\n    pub fn take_rebased_inverse(&mut self) -> Vec<(String, Vec<Mutation>)> {\n        std::mem::take(&mut self.rebased_inverse)\n    }\n}\n\nimpl<P, Mutation> Drop for EditReplayResult<P, Mutation>\nwhere\n    Mutation: self::Mutation<P>,\n{\n    fn drop(&mut self) {\n        if let Some(state) = self.state.take() {\n            retire_shared_projection::<P, Mutation>(state);\n        }\n        for (_, inverse) in std::mem::take(&mut self.rebased_inverse) {\n            retire_scratch_operations::<P, Mutation>(inverse);\n        }\n        for (_, recorded) in std::mem::take(&mut self.recorded) {\n            retire_shared_projection::<P, Mutation>(recorded);\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// 🟰️ Whether two supersession maps install the same effective inputs — which transition installed them aside.\nfn same_effective_inputs(left: &EffectiveSupersessions, right: &EffectiveSupersessions) -> bool {\n    left.len() == right.len() && left.iter().zip(right.iter()).all(|((left_target, left), (right_target, right))| left_target == right_target && left.replacement == right.replacement)\n}\n\n/// 📸️ A retained projection after the first `length` applied edits, valid while `digest` names the live effective\n/// prefix ([`forward_prefix_digests`]).\nstruct PrefixSnapshot<P> {\n    length: usize,\n    digest: [u8; 32],\n    snapshot: Arc<P>,\n}\n\n/// 💍️ The most prefix projections a store retains, whatever its history length; the stride adapts so they spread over the\n/// whole applied history ([`ArtifactStore::prefix_ring_capacity`]).\nconst PREFIX_SNAPSHOT_RING_CAPACITY: usize = 16;\n\n/// 🪙️ The fewest prefix projections a store retains once its history is long enough to stride.\nconst PREFIX_SNAPSHOT_RING_FLOOR: usize = 8;\n\n/// 🎟️ Displaced owners one reprojection displaces besides its message entries and prefix projections: the tail\n/// snapshot and its id, `current`, the applied, redo and checkpoint owners, the supersessions, the revision bump and a\n/// full prefix-ring prune.\nconst REPROJECTION_OWNER_SLOTS: usize = 10 + PREFIX_SNAPSHOT_RING_CAPACITY;\n//#endregion 🔖️EditReplay\n\n//#region 🔖️Backbone\n//#region 🔖️Backbone\n/// 📨️ Wire message exchanged over an attached backbone channel. B-R6 \"kill hand-rolled binary\n/// codecs\": `#[derive(crate::os_dsl::DslOps)]` generates `OpBinary::encode_op`/`decode_op` (`format u8 (=1) |\n/// variant ordinal varint | record body`, `crate::os_dsl::op_rt`) — this is the one real binary encoding for\n/// every caller, including the wasm-sandbox `BackboneChannelPort` seam (see that trait's doc) — the\n/// WIT `backbone-send`/`backbone-poll` host functions carry these exact bytes as `list<u8>`.\n/// `Operations.envelopes` carries `crate::os_spr::encode_envelopes`/`decode_envelopes` bytes rather than a\n/// real `Vec<crate::os_spr::MutationEnvelope>` field: `MutationEnvelope` lives in `protocol_causal`,\n/// which sits BELOW `dsl` in the dependency graph (`dsl` → `protocol` → `protocol_causal`), so it\n/// cannot implement `crate::os_dsl::DslField` without a dependency cycle — the derive can only lower fields\n/// shaped from types it can see. `#[dsl(base64)]` marks each `Vec<u8>` field `Shape::Bytes64`\n/// (otherwise a bare `Vec<u8>` lowers to a `List<UInt>`, one DSL list element per byte).\n#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, DslOps)]\npub enum BackboneMessage {\n    /// 🧬️ The document's initial snapshot pack — its identity, never its current state. A\n    /// replica announces it before its event log; an empty persistence end adopts it as the genesis\n    /// it stores, every other end verifies it names the same document.\n    Genesis {\n        #[dsl(base64)]\n        pack: Vec<u8>,\n    },\n    /// ✉️ Semantic events — edit operations and history transitions — as causal envelopes.\n    Mutations {\n        #[dsl(base64)]\n        envelopes: Vec<u8>,\n    },\n    /// ✅️ Acknowledges inbound operations the store has ingested (store→actor). Lets a future actor\n    /// implement at-least-once redelivery with id-based dedupe — safe across store crashes/reloads.\n    Ack { op_ids: Vec<String> },\n    /// 🪆️ Semantic events authored on ONE composed member of this document, carrying that\n    /// member's exact `(slot, child_id)` lane identity. A composed document has exactly one replica\n    /// endpoint — the parent's backbone — so a child lane's edits can only cross under this tag, and\n    /// the receiving replica folds them into ITS own member of the same lane, never into the parent.\n    Member {\n        slot: String,\n        child_id: String,\n        #[dsl(base64)]\n        envelopes: Vec<u8>,\n    },\n    /// 🔙️ Retracts history transitions this replica authored and the hub refused (actor→store): each leaves the store's\n    /// event log with every local transition causally depending on it ([`transition_retraction_closure`]), and the\n    /// projection follows — the author converges with the hub, which never took them. No inverse exists for a\n    /// transition; a retraction is the refusal's exact compensation.\n    Retract { mutation_ids: Vec<String> },\n}\n\n//#region 🔖️OpCodec\n/// 🎞️ Handcrafted OpText (P6).\nimpl OpText for BackboneMessage {\n    fn parse_op(line: &str) -> Result<Self, TextError> {\n        let variants = <Self as crate::os_dsl::DslVariants>::variants();\n        for (keyword, spec_fn) in &variants {\n            let probe = format!(\"{} \", keyword);\n            if line == keyword.as_str() || line.starts_with(&probe) {\n                let record = crate::os_dsl::parse(line, &(spec_fn.ordinary)(), &crate::os_dsl::ParseOptions { limits: semio_framework_diagnostic::Limits::default(), mode: crate::os_dsl::SourceMode::Inline })?;\n                return <Self as crate::os_dsl::DslVariants>::from_named_record(keyword, &record);\n            }\n        }\n        Err(crate::os_dsl::__rt::field_error(format!(\"unknown operation line '{line}'\")))\n    }\n    fn print_op(&self) -> String {\n        let (keyword, record) = <Self as crate::os_dsl::DslVariants>::to_named_record(self);\n        let variants = <Self as crate::os_dsl::DslVariants>::variants();\n        let spec_fn = variants.iter().find(|(k, _)| k == &keyword).map(|(_, s)| *s).expect(\"variant spec must exist for its own keyword\");\n        crate::os_dsl::print(&record, &(spec_fn.ordinary)(), crate::os_dsl::JoinMode::Inline)\n    }\n}\n\n/// 🎯️ Handcrafted OpBinary (P6).\nimpl OpBinary for BackboneMessage {\n    fn encode_op(&self) -> Result<Vec<u8>, crate::os_spr::ProtocolError> {\n        crate::os_dsl::variants_binary::encode_op(self)\n    }\n\n    fn decode_op(bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<Self, crate::os_spr::ProtocolError> {\n        crate::os_dsl::variants_binary::decode_op(bytes)\n    }\n}\n//#endregion 🔖️OpCodec\n\npub const BACKBONE_HOT_MESSAGE_MAXIMUM_BYTES: usize = crate::os_spr::DOCUMENT_BACKBONE_BATCH_MAXIMUM_BYTES;\npub const BACKBONE_GENESIS_MESSAGE_MAXIMUM_BYTES: usize = 4 * 1024 * 1024;\npub const BACKBONE_CHANNEL_MAXIMUM_MESSAGES: usize = crate::os_spr::DOCUMENT_BACKBONE_PENDING_MAXIMUM_MESSAGES;\npub const BACKBONE_CHANNEL_MAXIMUM_BYTES: usize = crate::os_spr::DOCUMENT_BACKBONE_PENDING_MAXIMUM_BYTES;\n\npub fn decode_backbone_message_exact(bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<BackboneMessage, VcsError> {\n    if bytes.len() > BACKBONE_GENESIS_MESSAGE_MAXIMUM_BYTES {\n        return Err(VcsError::Deserialize(\"backbone message exceeds its fixed byte cap\".into()));\n    }\n    BackboneMessage::decode_op(bytes).map_err(|error| VcsError::Deserialize(error.to_string()))\n}\n\npub fn decode_hot_backbone_message_exact(bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<BackboneMessage, VcsError> {\n    if bytes.len() > BACKBONE_HOT_MESSAGE_MAXIMUM_BYTES {\n        return Err(VcsError::Deserialize(\"hot backbone message exceeds its fixed byte cap\".into()));\n    }\n    let message = decode_backbone_message_exact(bytes)?;\n    if matches!(message, BackboneMessage::Genesis { .. }) {\n        return Err(VcsError::ValidationFailed(\"hot backbone transport refuses genesis packs; a hot replica is bootstrapped through the cold document pair\".into()));\n    }\n    Ok(message)\n}\n\n/// 🧵️ Non-blocking, IO-free in-memory queue contract between a `ArtifactStore` and its\n/// sync actor. `send`/`receive` MUST return immediately: implementations only enqueue/dequeue\n/// `BackboneMessage`s — never HTTP, never filesystem, never a blocking wait. All IO (persistence,\n/// semio_hub sync, file watching, presence) lives behind this queue in `framework/sync`'s actor layer,\n/// which owns the other end; the store's `pump()`/`flush_outbound()` run synchronously on the\n/// caller's thread and must never be blocked by transport work.\n///\n/// URI schemes are resolved by the host actor (`framework/sync`): `temp://` (in-memory),\n/// `file://` (single JSON blob), `folder://` (sqlite `.semio/document.db`), `remote://` (OS semio_hub).\n// 🧵️ No `Send`/`Sync` supertrait bound (R7 coordinator ruling 2026-08-19): this crate is\n// guest-reachable and Send-ness comes structurally from the concrete `Backbones` enum at each spawn\n// site, never from a bound named here.\npub trait Backbone {\n    async fn descriptor(&self) -> ArtifactBackboneRef;\n    async fn send(&mut self, message: BackboneMessage) -> Result<(), VcsError>;\n    async fn receive(&mut self) -> Result<Vec<BackboneMessage>, VcsError>;\n}\n\npub trait BackbonePort {\n    async fn read(&self, uri: &str) -> Result<String, VcsError>;\n    async fn write(&self, uri: &str, payload: &str) -> Result<(), VcsError>;\n}\n\nstatic HOST_BACKBONE_PORT: Mutex<Option<Arc<BackbonePorts>>> = Mutex::new(None);\n\n/// 🔌️ Injects the browser or dev-server backbone port for wasm file/folder IO.\npub async fn set_host_backbone_port(port: Arc<BackbonePorts>) {\n    if let Ok(mut guard) = HOST_BACKBONE_PORT.lock() {\n        *guard = Some(port);\n    }\n}\n\nasync fn host_backbone_port() -> Option<Arc<BackbonePorts>> {\n    HOST_BACKBONE_PORT.lock().ok().and_then(|guard| guard.clone())\n}\n\n#[derive(Default)]\npub struct MemoryBackbonePort {\n    files: Mutex<HashMap<String, String>>,\n}\n\nimpl MemoryBackbonePort {\n    pub async fn new() -> Self {\n        Self::default()\n    }\n}\n\nimpl BackbonePort for MemoryBackbonePort {\n    async fn read(&self, uri: &str) -> Result<String, VcsError> {\n        self.files.lock().map_err(|_| VcsError::Backbone(\"lock poisoned\".into()))?.get(uri).cloned().ok_or_else(|| VcsError::Backbone(format!(\"missing backbone file {uri}\")))\n    }\n\n    async fn write(&self, uri: &str, payload: &str) -> Result<(), VcsError> {\n        self.files.lock().map_err(|_| VcsError::Backbone(\"lock poisoned\".into()))?.insert(uri.to_string(), payload.to_string());\n        Ok(())\n    }\n}\n\n#[cfg(all(target_arch = \"wasm32\", not(target_env = \"p2\")))]\nasync fn local_storage_backbone_key(uri: &str) -> String {\n    format!(\"semio:vcs:{uri}\")\n}\n\n/// 💾️ Browser `localStorage` backbone port with in-memory fallback for native tests.\n#[derive(Default)]\npub struct LocalStorageBackbonePort {\n    fallback: MemoryBackbonePort,\n}\n\nimpl LocalStorageBackbonePort {\n    pub async fn new() -> Self {\n        Self { fallback: MemoryBackbonePort::new().await }\n    }\n}\n\nimpl BackbonePort for LocalStorageBackbonePort {\n    async fn read(&self, uri: &str) -> Result<String, VcsError> {\n        if let Some(port) = host_backbone_port().await {\n            if let Ok(value) = Box::pin(port.read(uri)).await {\n                return Ok(value);\n            }\n        }\n        #[cfg(all(target_arch = \"wasm32\", not(target_env = \"p2\")))]\n        {\n            if let Some(window) = web_sys::window() {\n                if let Ok(Some(storage)) = window.local_storage() {\n                    if let Ok(Some(value)) = storage.get_item(&local_storage_backbone_key(uri).await) {\n                        return Ok(value);\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n        }\n        self.fallback.read(uri).await\n    }\n\n    async fn write(&self, uri: &str, payload: &str) -> Result<(), VcsError> {\n        self.fallback.write(uri, payload).await?;\n        if let Some(port) = host_backbone_port().await {\n            let _ = Box::pin(port.write(uri, payload)).await;\n        }\n        #[cfg(all(target_arch = \"wasm32\", not(target_env = \"p2\")))]\n        {\n            if let Some(window) = web_sys::window() {\n                if let Ok(Some(storage)) = window.local_storage() {\n                    let _ = storage.set_item(&local_storage_backbone_key(uri).await, payload);\n                }\n            }\n        }\n        Ok(())\n    }\n}\n\n/// 🧬️ Enum dispatch over every The trait stays as the contract; this enum\n/// implements it by match-delegation so 🪐️space's blanket `impl<T: BackbonePort>\n/// SpaceBackbonePort for T` keeps covering every concrete port through the enum too.\npub enum BackbonePorts {\n    Memory(MemoryBackbonePort),\n    LocalStorage(LocalStorageBackbonePort),\n}\n\nimpl BackbonePort for BackbonePorts {\n    async fn read(&self, uri: &str) -> Result<String, VcsError> {\n        match self {\n            Self::Memory(port) => port.read(uri).await,\n            Self::LocalStorage(port) => port.read(uri).await,\n        }\n    }\n\n    async fn write(&self, uri: &str, payload: &str) -> Result<(), VcsError> {\n        match self {\n            Self::Memory(port) => port.write(uri, payload).await,\n            Self::LocalStorage(port) => port.write(uri, payload).await,\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// 🕸️ Injectable duplex transport across the wasm sandbox boundary (program ↔ host process).\n/// `message`/the `poll` result are `BackboneMessage::encode_op`/`decode_op` (`crate::os_spr::OpBinary`) bytes.\npub trait BackboneChannelPort: Send + Sync {\n    async fn send(&self, uri: &str, message: &[u8]) -> Result<(), VcsError>;\n    async fn poll(&self, uri: &str) -> Result<Vec<Vec<u8>>, VcsError>;\n}\n\nstruct ActorBackboneChannelState {\n    uri: String,\n    inbound: VecDeque<Vec<u8>>,\n    outbound: VecDeque<Vec<u8>>,\n    inbound_bytes: usize,\n    outbound_bytes: usize,\n    accepting: bool,\n}\n\npub struct ActorBackboneChannelPort {\n    state: Arc<Mutex<ActorBackboneChannelState>>,\n}\n\n#[derive(Clone)]\npub struct ActorBackboneChannelOwner {\n    state: Arc<Mutex<ActorBackboneChannelState>>,\n}\n\nfn push_actor_backbone_outbound(state: &Arc<Mutex<ActorBackboneChannelState>>, uri: &str, message: &[u8]) -> Result<(), VcsError> {\n    decode_hot_backbone_message_exact(message)?;\n    let mut state = state.lock().map_err(|_| addressed to another URI\".into()));\n    }\n    let next_bytes = state.outbound_bytes.checked_add(message.len()).ok_or_else(|| VcsError::Backbone(\"actor backbone outbound byte accounting overflow\".into()))?;\n    if state.outbound.len() >= BACKBONE_CHANNEL_MAXIMUM_MESSAGES || next_bytes > BACKBONE_CHANNEL_MAXIMUM_BYTES {\n        return Err(VcsError::Backbone(\"actor backbone inbound_bytes: 0, outbound_bytes: 0, accepting: true }));\n        (Arc::new(BackboneChannelPorts::Actor(ActorBackboneChannelPort { state: state.clone() })), Self { state })\n    }\n\n    pub fn admits_same_channel(&self, other: &Self) -> bool {\n        Arc::ptr_eq(&self.state, &other.state)\n    }\n\n    pub fn push_inbound(&self, uri: &str, message: &[u8]) -> Result<(), VcsError> {\n        decode_hot_backbone_message_exact(message)?;\n        let mut state = self.state.lock().map_err(|_| VcsError::Backbone(\"actor backbone channel lock poisoned\".into()))?;\n        if !state.accepting || state.uri != uri {\n            return Err(VcsError::Backbone(\"actor backbone channel is retired or addressed to another URI\".into()));\n        }\n        let next_bytes = state.inbound_bytes.checked_add(message.len()).ok_or_else(|| VcsError::Backbone(\"actor backbone inbound byte accounting overflow\".into()))?;\n        if state.inbound.len() >= BACKBONE_CHANNEL_MAXIMUM_MESSAGES || next_bytes > BACKBONE_CHANNEL_MAXIMUM_BYTES {\n            return Err(VcsError::Backbone(\"actor backbone inbound queue is saturated\".into()));\n        }\n        state.inbound.push_back(message.to_vec());\n        state.inbound_bytes = next_bytes;\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    pub fn take_outbound(&self) -> Result<Option<Vec<u8>>, VcsError> {\n        let mut state = self.state.lock().map_err(|_| VcsError::Backbone(\"actor backbone channel lock poisoned\".into()))?;\n        let message = state.outbound.pop_front();\n        if let Some(message) = &message {\n            state.outbound_bytes = state.outbound_bytes.saturating_sub(message.len());\n        }\n        Ok(message)\n    }\n\n    #[cfg(test)]\n    pub fn push_outbound_for_test(&self, uri: &str, message: &[u8]) -> Result<(), VcsError> {\n        push_actor_backbone_outbound(&self.state, uri, message)\n    }\n\n    pub fn begin_retire(&self) -> Result<(), VcsError> {\n        let mut state = self.state.lock().map_err(|_| VcsError::Backbone(\"actor backbone channel lock poisoned\".into()))?;\n        state.accepting = false;\n        state.inbound.clear();\n        state.outbound.clear();\n        state.inbound_bytes = 0;\n        state.outbound_bytes = 0;\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    pub fn terminal_is_empty(&self) -> Result<bool, VcsError> {\n        let state = self.state.lock().map_err(|_| VcsError::Backbone(\"actor backbone channel lock poisoned\".into()))?;\n        Ok(!state.accepting && state.inbound.is_empty() && state.outbound.is_empty())\n    }\n}\n\npub enum BackboneChannelPorts {\n    Actor(ActorBackboneChannelPort),\n}\n\nimpl BackboneChannelPort for BackboneChannelPorts {\n    async fn send(&self, uri: &str, message: &[u8]) -> messages across the wasm sandbox boundary to the host process,\n/// which resolves the real `file://`/`folder://`/`remote://` backbone on its own (native) side. The\n/// channel is injected per instance via [`PortBackbone::with_channel`] — a pooled multi-instance\n/// actor cannot share one process-global channel (see `important.md`'s \"Replace, never wrap\" list,\n/// `set_host_backbone_channel`). {\n            messages.push(decode_hot_backbone_message_exact(&bytes)?);\n        }\n        Ok(messages)\n    }\n}\n\n/// 🔗️ Two crossed in-memory channel ends: whatever `a` sends, `b` receives, and vice versa.\npub struct MemoryBackbone {\n    uri: String,\n    inbox: Option<Arc<Mutex<VecDeque<BackboneMessage>>>>,\n    outbox: Option<Arc<Mutex<VecDeque<BackboneMessage>>>>,\n}\n\nimpl MemoryBackbone {\n    pub async fn pair(uri_a: &str, uri_b: &str) -> (Self, Self) {\n        let a_to_b = Arc::new(Mutex::new(VecDeque::new()));\n        let b_to_a = Arc::new(Mutex::new(VecDeque::new()));\n        (Self { uri: uri_a.to_string(), inbox: Some(b_to_a.clone()), outbox: Some(a_to_b.clone()) }, Self { uri: uri_b.to_string(), inbox: Some(a_to_b), outbox: Some(b_to_a) })\n    }\n}\n\nimpl Backbone for MemoryBackbone {\n    async fn descriptor(&self) -> ArtifactBackboneRef {\n        document_backbone_ref(&self.uri).await\n    }\n\n    async fn send(&mut self, message: BackboneMessage) -> Result<(), VcsError> {\n        self.outbox.as_ref().ok_or_else(|| VcsError::Backbone(\"memory backbone is closing\".into()))?.lock().map_err(|_| VcsError::Backbone(\"lock poisoned\".into()))?.push_back(message);\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    async fn receive(&mut self) -> Result<Vec<BackboneMessage>, VcsError> {\n        let mut inbox = self.inbox.as_ref().ok_or_else(|| VcsError::Backbone(\"memory backbone is closing\".into()))?.lock().map_err(|_| VcsError::Backbone(\"lock poisoned\".into()))?;\n        Ok(inbox.drain(..).collect())\n    }\n}\n\n/// 🔗️ The store-side end of a pair of crossed in-memory queues. Implements the non-blocking\n/// {@link Backbone} contract; the matching {@link ChannelBackboneRemote} is held by an external sync\n/// actor (built in `framework/sync`, a later workstream) that pushes inbound messages and drains the\n/// store's outbound ones. This crate only provides the queue plumbing — never the actor itself.\npub struct ChannelBackbone {\n    uri: String,\n    inbound: Option<Arc<Mutex<VecDeque<BackboneMessage>>>>,\n    outbound: Option<Arc<Mutex<VecDeque<BackboneMessage>>>>,\n    outbound_wake: Arc<std::sync::OnceLock<Arc<dyn Fn() + Send + Sync>>>,\n}\n\n/// 🎛️ The actor-side end paired with a {@link ChannelBackbone}: `push` delivers a message to\n/// the store's inbound queue, `try_pop_front` takes one exact outbound owner. Not a\n/// `Backbone` — this is the handle an IO-owning actor endpoint holds across the store boundary.\npub struct ChannelBackboneRemote {\n    uri: String,\n    inbound: Arc<Mutex<VecDeque<BackboneMessage>>>,\n    outbound: Arc<Mutex<VecDeque<BackboneMessage>>>,\n    outbound_wake: Arc<std::sync::OnceLock<Arc<dyn Fn() + Send + Sync>>>,\n}\n\nimpl ChannelBackbone {\n {\n            wake();\n        }\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    async fn receive(&mut self) -> Result<Vec<BackboneMessage>, VcsError> {\n        let mut inbound = self.inbound.as_ref().ok_or_else(|| VcsError::Backbone(\"channel backbone is closing\".into()))?.lock().map_err(|_| VcsError::Backbone(\"lock poisoned\".into()))?;\n        Ok(inbound.drain(..).collect())\n    }\n}\n\nimpl poisoned\".into()))?.push_back(message);\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    /// 🔔️ Installs the actor's wake: every store→actor send resumes the actor that drains it,\n    /// so an idle actor never sleeps Only the first install is kept.\n    pub fn set_outbound_wake(&self, wake: Arc<dyn Fn() + Send + Sync>) {\n        let _ = self.outbound_wake.set(wake);\n    }\n\n    /// 🪄️ Takes at most one store→actor message without a bulk collection or a\n    /// blocking lock wait; contention preserves the exact queued owner for a later worker turn.\n    pub fn try_pop_front(&self) -> released_bytes });\n        }\n        if let Some(message) = self.message.as_mut() {\n            match message {\n                BackboneMessage::Genesis { pack } => {\n                    if The\n/// `.spr` extension (`SpaceHistorySnapshot::EXTENSION`, `\"space-history\"`) is unchanged.\npub const S_SPACE_HISTORY_SCHEMA: &str = \"os.space.history\";\n\n#[path = \"📜️space-history/🧬️schema/📸️snapshot/🪶️sqlite/🦀️.rs\"]\npub mod space_history_sqlite;\n\n/// 🗄️ Snapshot of the `S_SPACE_HISTORY_SCHEMA` (`\"os.space.history\"`) meta-document: itself\n/// an ordinary `ArtifactVcs` document kind (dogfooded — no bespoke transport), holding the\n/// space-level checkpoint/alternative graph that `SpaceHost` composes on top of every registered\n/// member's own history.\n#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq, ToValue, FromValue)]\n#[value(rename_all = \"camelCase\")]\npub struct SpaceHistorySnapshot {\n    pub checkpoints: Vec<SpaceCheckpoint>,\n    /// 🌿️ Held in ASCENDING `id` order, not in creation order. Two facts force it: a branch\n    /// list is unordered in the product (nothing reads `alternatives[0]` as \"the first branch\"), and\n    /// only a canonical order makes `RemoveSpaceAlternative`'s inverse an exact inverse — re-adding\n    /// a removed alternative by appending put it back at the END, so undoing a removal changed the\n    /// document (`space_history_op_round_trips`: \"operation inverse did not restore pre-state\").
