panic!(\"dsl parse failed: {error}\"));\n        assert_eq!(&parsed, snapshot, \"dsl round trip diverged;\\nprinted:\\n{printed}\");\n    }\n\n    /// 🧊️ Cold twin of [`assert_dsl_round_trip`] for a projection that REJECTS a bare drop —\n    /// one owning an `OrderedMap` root or a retirement ladder (`🧰️framework/🔨️modules/🌱️value/🗂️ordered/🦀️.rs:81`).\n    /// The decoded value is handed to `retire` instead of being dropped, so the law can be asserted\n    /// without aborting the test binary in a destructor.\n    pub fn assert_dsl_round_trip_cold<P>(snapshot: &P, retire: impl FnOnce(P))\n    where\n        P: ArtifactDsl + PartialEq + std::fmt::Debug,\n    {\n        let printed = snapshot.print_dsl();\n        let parsed = P::parse_dsl(&printed).unwrap_or_else(|error| panic!(\"dsl parse failed: {error}\"));\n        let matches = parsed == *snapshot;\n        let report = matches.then(String::new).unwrap_or_else(|| format!(\"{parsed:?}\"));\n        retire(parsed);\n        assert!(matches, \"dsl round trip diverged;\\nprinted:\\n{printed}\\nparsed:\\n{report}\");\n    }\n\n    /// 🧮️ Config artifact twin of [`assert_dsl_round_trip`] — same law for `ConfigRecord` snapshots.\n    pub fn assert_config_round_trip<C>(snapshot: &C)\n    where\n        C: ConfigRecord + PartialEq + std::fmt::Debug,\n    {\n        assert_dsl_round_trip(snapshot);\n    }\n\n    /// 🧭️ Non-panicking twin of [`assert_dsl_round_trip`] for a repo-wide fixture-law SWEEP\n    /// (W6: `.🧬semio/🦑️repo/🎫️tickets/.../DSL-FIXTURE-LAW-SWEEP`): checks BOTH laws directly against real\n    /// shipped `📚️examples/**` fixture TEXT (not a hand-built in-memory value), which is exactly what\n    /// a single per-app round-trip test built on its own simpler hardcoded example can miss — a\n    /// printer/parser asymmetry only a real fixture's actual formatting (comment placement, field\n    /// order, quoting) would trip.\n    ///\n    /// **Law 1 — parse→print→reparse fixpoint**: `text` parses to `first`; printing then reparsing\n    /// `first` must recover an equal value (`second`) — the generic form of [`assert_dsl_round_trip`],\n    /// but starting from arbitrary fixture text instead of an already-canonical in-memory value.\n    ///\n    /// **Law 2 — canonicalize idempotence**: `canonicalize(x) := print_dsl(parse_dsl(x))`. For every\n    /// derive-generated `ArtifactDsl` impl this IS `crate::os_dsl::schema::canonicalize(x, spec, opts)`\n    /// (`__rt::print_document_record`/`parse_document_record` route straight through\n    /// `crate::os_dsl::schema::parse`/`print` in `JoinMode::Document`, the exact pair `canonicalize` composes)\n    /// — and it is the correct generalization for hand-rolled (Route A idiom) `ArtifactDsl` impls\n    /// that have no `RecordSpec` at all. `canonicalize(text) == printed_once`;\n    /// `canonicalize(printed_once) == printed_twice`; idempotence is `printed_once == printed_twice`.\n    ///\n    /// Returns `Ok(())` on success, `Err(description)` on the first law violated — never panics, so\n    /// a caller sweeping many fixture files can collect every failure before reporting.\n    pub fn check_dsl_fixture_text_laws<P>(text: &str) -> Result<(), String>\n    where\n        P: ArtifactDsl + PartialEq,\n    {\n        let first = P::parse_dsl(text).map_err(|error| format!(\"parse failed: {error}\"))?;\n        let printed_once = first.print_dsl();\n        let second = P::parse_dsl(&printed_once).map_err(|error| format!(\"reparse failed: {error}\\nprinted:\\n{printed_once}\"))?;\n        if first != second {\n            return Err(format!(\"parse->print->reparse fixpoint diverged;\\nprinted:\\n{printed_once}\"));\n        }\n        let printed_twice = second.print_dsl();\n        if printed_once != printed_twice {\n            return Err(format!(\"canonicalize is not idempotent;\\nonce:\\n{printed_once}\\ntwice:\\n{printed_twice}\"));\n        }\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    /// 📦️ Asserts a pack round trip: `P::decode_pack(&snapshot.encode_pack())` recovers an\n The compile-time validation ground\n    /// truth for every technology's `🔖️OpText` region — call this once per `Mutation` variant.\n    pub fn assert_op_line_round_trip<Op>(operation: &Op)\n    where\n        Op: OpText + PartialEq + std::fmt::Debug,\n    {\n        let printed = operation.print_op();\n        assert!(!printed.contains('\\n'), \"print_op must be one line, got: {printed:?}\");\n        let parsed = Op::parse_op(&printed).unwrap_or_else(|error| panic!(\"op parse failed: {error}\"));\n        assert_eq!(&parsed, operation, \"op-text round trip diverged; printed: {printed:?}\");\n    }\n\n    /// 🧾️ Asserts a committed language-agnostic wire witness (`…/🧾️wire-witness/🦠️mutation/🔣️.json`) IS the canonical\n    /// Rust wire of its operation: `FromValue` decodes it and `ToValue` re-encodes exactly the committed JSON under the\n    /// independent `serde_json` oracle (key order free, number spelling exact — `3.0` for an `f64`). The owner-side half of\n    /// the `schema-mutation-payload-parity` witness rule; the lint validates the same file against the leaf schema.\n    pub fn assert_wire_witness<Op>(witness: &str) -> Op\n    where\n        Op: FromValue + ToValue,\n    {\n        let committed: serde_json::Value = serde_json::from_str(witness).unwrap_or_else(|error| panic!(\"wire witness is not JSON: {error}\\n{witness}\"));\n        let operation = Op::from_value(committed.clone().into()).unwrap_or_else(|error| panic!(\"wire witness does not decode: {error}\\n{witness}\"));\n        assert_eq!(serde_json::Value::from(operation.to_value()), committed, \"wire witness is not the canonical Rust wire\");\n        operation\n    }\n\n    /// 🧊️ Cold twin of [`assert_op_line_round_trip`] for an operation that REJECTS a bare drop —\n    /// one carrying an `OrderedMap` root or a retirement ladder (`🧰️framework/🔨️modules/🌱️value/🗂️ordered/🦀️.rs:81`),\n    /// e.g. a mutation payload holding a `neural_engine::Dictionary`. printed: {printed:?}\\nparsed:\\n{report}\");\n    }\n\n    /// 🧊️ Cold twin of [`assert_op_text_binary_equivalence`]; `retire` takes exact ownership of\n    /// every operation this helper decodes (one from the text lane, one from the binary lane).\n    pub fn assert_op_text_binary_equivalence_cold<Op>(operation: &Op, mut retire: impl FnMut(Op))\n    where\n        Op: OpText + OpBinary + PartialEq + std::fmt::Debug,\n    {\n        assert_op_line_round_trip_cold(operation, &mut retire);\n        let encoded = operation.encode_op().unwrap_or_else(|error| panic!(\"op encode failed: {error}\"));\n        let encoded_again = operation.encode_op().unwrap_or_else(|error| panic!(\"op re-encode failed: {error}\"));\n        assert_eq!(encoded, encoded_again, \"op binary encoding is not deterministic\");\n        let decoded = Op::decode_op(&encoded).unwrap_or_else(|error| panic!(\"op decode failed: {error}\"));\n        let matches = decoded == *operation;\n        let report = matches.then(String::new).unwrap_or_else(|| format!(\"{decoded:?}\"));\n        retire(decoded);\n        assert!(matches, \"op-binary round trip diverged from source operation\\ndecoded:\\n{report}\");\n    }\n\n    /// ⚖️ Asserts op text and op binary are two encodings of the SAME operation:\n    /// `decode_op(encode_op(op)) == parse_op(print_op(op)) == op`, and the binary encoding is\n    /// deterministic. The compile-time validation ground truth for every technology's `OpBinary`\n    /// impl — the op-level mirror of {@link assert_dsl_pack_equivalence}.\n    pub fn assert_op_text_binary_equivalence<Op>(operation: &Op)\n    where\n        Op: OpText + OpBinary + PartialEq + std::fmt::Debug,\n    {\n        assert_op_line_round_trip(operation);\n        let encoded = operation.encode_op().unwrap_or_else(|error| panic!(\"op encode failed: {error}\"));\n        let encoded_again = operation.encode_op().unwrap_or_else(|error| panic!(\"op re-encode failed: {error}\"));\n        assert_eq!(encoded, encoded_again, \"op binary encoding is not deterministic\");\n        let decoded = Op::decode_op(&encoded).unwrap_or_else(|error| panic!(\"op decode failed: {error}\"));\n        assert_eq!(&decoded, operation, \"op-binary round trip diverged from source operation\");\n    }\n\n    /// ⚖️ Asserts command text and command binary are two encodings of the SAME command:\n    /// `ArtifactCommand::decode_command(&c.encode_command()) == parse_command(print_command(c)) == c`, and the\n    /// binary encoding is deterministic. The compile-time validation ground truth for\n    /// `ArtifactCommand`'s text/binary pair — the command-level mirror of\n    /// `assert_op_text_binary_equivalence`.\n    pub async fn assert_command_text_binary_equivalence<P, Op>(command: &ArtifactCommand<Op>)\n    where\n        Op: OpText + OpBinary + self::Mutation<P> + PartialEq + std::fmt::Debug,\n    {\n        let printed = print_command(command).await.unwrap_or_else(|error| panic!(\"command print failed: {error}\"));\n        let parsed: ArtifactCommand<Op> = parse_command::<P, Op>(&printed).await.unwrap_or_else(|error| panic!(\"command parse failed: {error}\"));\n        assert_eq!(&parsed, command, \"command text round trip diverged; printed:\\n{printed}\");\n        let encoded = command.encode_command().unwrap_or_else(|error| panic!(\"command encode failed: {error}\"));\n        let encoded_again = command.encode_command().unwrap_or_else(|error| panic!(\"command re-encode failed: {error}\"));\n        assert_eq!(encoded, encoded_again, \"command binary encoding is not deterministic\");\n        let decoded: ArtifactCommand<Op> = ArtifactCommand::<Op>::decode_command::<P>(&encoded).unwrap_or_else(|error| panic!(\"command decode failed: {error}\"));\n        assert_eq!(&decoded, command, \"command binary round trip diverged from source command\");\n    }\n\n    /// 📄️ Asserts that printing a store's envelope to text and parsing it back keeps its whole shared log — every edit\n    /// and every history transition — and hydrates to the canonical trunk tip (the `.ops` text is the shared log and\n    /// carries no viewer head, ticket 26/10/01 PER-VIEWER-ALTERNATIVE-HEAD); a store on the trunk tip gets back exactly the\n    /// envelope and live snapshot it holds. snapshot\");\n        }\n        retire_parsed_document(parsed);\n    }\n\n    /// 🧹️ Bounded retirement for a parse-produced document that belongs to no store.\n    /// Every terminal shell below released_bytes: 0 });\n            }\n            if self.0.take().is_some() {\n                return Ok(SnapshotRetirementStep::Pending { released_items: 1, released_bytes: 0 });\n            }\n PartialEq)]\npub struct PresenceRosterWire {\n    entries: [Option<Box<[u8]>>; PRESENCE_ROSTER_MAXIMUM_ITEMS],\n    len: usize,\n    bytes: usize,\n}\n\n#[derive(Debug)]\npub struct PresenceRosterPushRejected {\n    pub entry: Vec<u8>,\n    pub reason: &'static str,\n}\n\nimpl PresenceRosterWire {\n    pub fn empty() -> Self {\n        Self { entries: std::array::from_fn(|_| byte authority\" });\n        }\n        let bytes = entry.len();\n        self.entries[self.len] = Some(entry.into_boxed_slice());\n        self.len += 1;\n        self.bytes += bytes;\n 🔖️PresenceCommandCursor\npub const PRESENCE_COMMAND_MAXIMUM_BYTES: usize = PRESENCE_ROSTER_MAXIMUM_BYTES + PRESENCE_ROSTER_MAXIMUM_ITEMS * 10 + 32;\n\npub struct PresenceCommandCursor {\n    page: owner\", self.next_page as u64, \"next page has not been admitted\"))?;\n        self.remaining -= 1;\n        Ok(Some(entry))\n    }\n\n    pub fn next_len(&self) -> Result<Option<usize>, crate::os_spr::ProtocolError> {\n        if self.remaining == 0 {\n            return Ok(None);\n        }\n        Ok(self.page.as_ref().map(FixedCommandPage::len))\n    }\n\n    pub fn PagedRouteFieldsDecode {\n    fn new(tag: u8, plan: (usize, bool, usize)) -> Self {\n        let (leading, has_ops, trailing) = plan;\n        Self { tag, leading, has_ops, trailing, fields: usize::try_from(reader.read_varint()?).map_err(|_| semio_framework_diagnostic::Fault::new(semio_framework_diagnostic::FaultOrigin::Framework, semio_framework_diagnostic::FaultCode::new(\"plugin.transaction-prepared-ops\"), \"transaction prepared-ops count is not representable\"))?;\n            if count > TRANSACTION_PREPARED_OPS_MAXIMUM self.fields.push(reader.read_bounded_bytes(APP_COMMAND_FIELD_MAXIMUM_BYTES)?);\n        }\n        if self.fields.len() < self.leading + self.trailing || (self.has_ops && Result<AppCommand, semio_framework_diagnostic::Fault> {\n        let ops = std::mem::take(&mut self.ops);\n        let mut fields = std::mem::take(&mut self.fields).into_iter();\n        let built = match self.tag {\n            10 => Self::text(&mut fields).map(|port| AppCommand::MediaIn { seq, port, descriptor: fields.next().expect(\"retained media descriptor\"), data: fields.next().expect(\"retained media data\") }),\n            11 => Self::text(&mut fields).map(|port| AppCommand::MediaOut { seq, port, request: fields.next().expect(\"retained media request\") }),\n            12 => Self::text(&mut fields).map(|port| AppCommand::MediaFingerprint { seq, port }),\n            17 => Self::text(&mut fields).and_then(|txn_id| {\n                let mutation_id = Self::text(&mut fields)?;\n                let payload = fields.next().expect(\"retained transaction payload\");\n                let label = Self::text(&mut fields)?;\n                let origin = fields.next().expect(\"retained transaction origin\");\n                Ok(AppCommand::TransactionPrepare { seq, txn_id, mutation_id, payload, prepared_ops: ops, label, origin, prepared_child_ops: fields.next().expect(\"retained transaction child op groups\") })\n            }),\n            18 => Self::text(&mut fields).map(|txn_id| AppCommand::TransactionCommit { seq, txn_id }),\n            19 => Self::text(&mut fields).map(|txn_id| AppCommand::TransactionRollback { seq, txn_id }),\n            20 => Self::text(&mut fields).map(|group_id| AppCommand::TransactionUndo { seq, group_id }),\n Presence is the app-defined `ArtifactPack` payload;\n    /// generations let hosts skip unchanged renderer work while transient remains local-only.\n    /// `interaction` (trailing field, CHANNEL_VERSION 12 wire addition, contract-freeze §C7.6) is the\n    /// output of `encode_presence_interaction` over the app's own declared broadcast domains — empty\n    /// bytes when the app declares no interaction domains or nothing is selected/hovered right now.\n    /// `tool_run` (trailing field) is `encode_presence_tool_run` of the instance's tool run summary — empty\n    /// bytes without a run (`📋️tool-run-contract.md` §3.4). `history_edit` (trailing field) is\n    /// `encode_presence_history_edit` of the instance's open history edit — empty bytes while none is open.\n    Ephemeral {\n        presence: Vec<u8>,\n        presence_generation: u64,\n        transient_generation: u64,\n        interaction: Vec<u8>,\n        tool_run: Vec<u8>,\n        history_edit: Vec<u8>,\n    },\n    /// 🧾️ Full history patch for initial host projection and gap recovery.\n    HistorySnapshot {\n        in_reply_to: u64,\n        history_patch: Vec<u8>,\n    },\n    /// 📣️ A guest's dispatch touched a foreign artifact — the host mints `txn_id`, resolves each\n    /// opaque `ForeignStep` in `foreign` (one `store::pack_rt::encode_wire_value`-encoded serde\n    /// form per element; not decoded at this layer), and drives the transaction protocol (contract\n    /// freeze §5). CHANNEL_VERSION 9 wire addition.\n    TransactionProposal {\n        in_reply_to: u64,\n        proposal_id: String,\n        local_ops: Vec<Vec<u8>>,\n        description: String,\n        coalesce_key: String,\n        foreign: Vec<Vec<u8>>,\n    },\n    /// 🤝️ Phase-1 reply — empty `rejection` means the member is prepared. CHANNEL_VERSION 9 wire addition.\n    TransactionPrepared {\n        txn_id: String,\n        foreign: Vec<Vec<u8>>,\n        rejection: Vec<u8>,\n    },\n    /// ✅️ Phase-2 commit succeeded for a member. CHANNEL_VERSION 9 wire addition.\n    TransactionCommitted {\n        txn_id: String,\n        edit_id: String,\n    },\n    /// ↩️ A member rolled back its not-yet-committed transaction. CHANNEL_VERSION 9 wire addition.\n    TransactionRolledBack {\n        txn_id: String,\n    },\n    /// ⚔️ Pushed unsolicited (next to `DocumentChanged`) after every ingest: one packed `MergeReport`\n    /// describing how the batch was resolved. CHANNEL_VERSION 11 wire addition.\n    MergeReport {\n        in_reply_to: Option<u64>,\n        report: Vec<u8>,\n    },\n    /// ⚔️ Pushed unsolicited (next to `DocumentChanged`) after every ingest, and the reply to\n    /// `AppCommand::ReadConflicts`: one packed `Vec<Conflict>`. CHANNEL_VERSION 11 wire addition.\n    Conflicts {\n        in_reply_to: Option<u64>,\n        conflicts: Vec<u8>,\n    },\n    /// 🎨️ Revisioned UI patch batch for one surface — replaces `UiSection`'s cache-probe push. The\n    /// reactor ABI's guest returns `turn-result.ui-patches` (`semio_framework::kernel::UiPatch`,\n    /// `📓️design-abi.md` §2 \"`exchange` collapse\"); the host re-frames each one as this channel\n    /// frame to reach a UI client. `surface`/`kind`/`revision`/`base_revision` mirror\n    /// `kernel::UiPatch` field-for-field; `ops` is `kernel::PatchOp` — reused from\n    /// `semio_framework::kernel`, never redefined here — pack-encoded via\n    /// `store::pack_rt::encode_wire_value` (`Vec<PatchOp>`), same \"nested payload stays opaque\n    /// bytes\" convention every other structured field in this file already uses.\n    /// `base_revision` lets the client detect a stale diff and fall back to a full body instead of\n    /// reconciling a diff it can't trust. `in_reply_to` is `None` for an unsolicited push (the\n    /// common case — surfaces render lazily off `surface-visible`/timers, not off a command reply).\n    /// CHANNEL_VERSION 12 wire addition.\n    UiPatch {\n        in_reply_to: Option<u64>,\n        surface: String,\n        kind: String,\n        revision: u64,\n        base_revision: u64,\n        ops: Vec<u8>,\n    },\n    /// 🏁️ Marks the end of one surface's initial full-body snapshot burst, so a client that just\n    /// subscribed (`surface-visible`) knows when it has seen a complete tree and can start applying\n    /// incremental `UiPatch` frames instead of buffering. CHANNEL_VERSION 12 wire addition.\n    UiSnapshotEnd {\n        revision: u64,\n    },\n    /// 🏁️ One mounted typed operation reached its terminal result. Unsolicited and NEVER a reply:\n    /// the command that started the operation already returned its \"started\" `Invocation` long\n    /// before the retained job finished, so no `in_reply_to` sequence exists to correlate against —\n    /// `operation` (the host-allocated `semio_framework_job::OperationId`) is the correlation key\n    /// instead. `revision` is the artifact store's content revision at completion; `ui_scope` is the\n    /// operation's final `kernel::UiDirtyScope` and `history_patch` its command-log delta (empty\n    /// bytes when the operation recorded nothing), both `store::pack_rt::encode_wire_value`-encoded\n    /// exactly like `Invocation`'s same-named fields. CHANNEL_VERSION 15 wire addition.\n    OperationCompleted {\n        operation: u64,\n        revision: u64,\n        ui_scope: Vec<u8>,\n        history_patch: Vec<u8>,\n    },\n    /// 📃️ ACK-owned local-only pages are independent of ordinary command outcomes.\n    LocalInteractionQuery {\n        reply: protocol::LocalInteractionQueryReply,\n    },\n    /// 🗃️ Complete generation-fenced recursive document archive. CHANNEL_VERSION 16 wire addition.\n    DocumentArchive {\n        in_reply_to: u64,\n        archive: DocumentArchivePack,\n    },\n    /// 📊️ Progress or terminal state for one ACK-owned archive load.\n    DocumentArchiveLoad {\n        in_reply_to: u64,\n        status: DocumentArchiveLoadStatus,\n    },\n    MediaExportSubmitted {\n        in_reply_to: u64,\n        handle: MediaExportHandleWire,\n    },\n    MediaExportStatus {\n        in_reply_to: u64,\n        handle: MediaExportHandleWire,\n        state: MediaExportStateWire,\n        applied_progress: u64,\n MediaExportHandleWire,\n        data: Vec<u8>,\n        terminal: bool,\n    },\n    DocumentIdentity { in_reply_to: u64, identity: AppDocumentIdentity },\n}\n//#endregion 🔖️AppFrame\n\n//#region 🔖️DocumentArchiveLoadHost\n/// 🏁️ How one host-driven whole-document load ended (`📓️api-stepped-document-load.md` §2.3, ticket\n/// 26/09/30/NON-DESTRUCTIVE-HISTORY-EDITING). `Cancelled` and `Fault` both left the previous document exactly as it was;\n/// `Fault` carries the guest's encoded fault.\n#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum DocumentArchiveLoadOutcome {\n    Ready,\n    Cancelled,\n    Fault(Vec<u8>),\n}\n\n/// 🧭️ What a host does next with one [`DocumentArchiveLoadHost`]: send this command, stamped with the sequence the host minted\n/// for it, or stop, because the load reached its acknowledged terminal or was cancelled before it was ever admitted.\n#[derive(Debug, PartialEq)]\npub enum DocumentArchiveLoadStep {\n    Send { seq: u64, command: AppCommand },\n    Finished(DocumentArchiveLoadOutcome),\n}\n\n/// 🚧️ An answer a load cannot go on from: the guest refused the admission, a poll or an acknowledgement (its encoded fault), or the\n/// frame handed back answers some other command.\n#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum DocumentArchiveLoadRefusal {\n    Refused(Vec<u8>),\n    Unanswered,\n}\n\n#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]\nenum DocumentArchiveLoadSent {\n    Admit,\n    Poll,\n    Cancel,\n    Acknowledge,\n}\n\n/// 🗃️ The host half of the stepped, ACK-owned whole-document load (`📓️api-stepped-document-load.md` §2): a transport-free state\n/// machine every Rust host drives with its own exchange — the MCP gateway, the `🏃️run` batch runner, the wgpu bridge — so\n/// admit → poll* → (cancel → poll*) → acknowledge exists once. TS twin: `AppChannelClient.loadDocumentArchive` (`💻️os/🟦️.ts`).\n/// Corpus: `🧫️fixtures/🧫️document-archive-load-host/🔣️.json` (schema `🧬️schema/🔣️document-archive-load-host/🔣️.json`).\n///\n/// 🔢️ The operation is the admission's own sequence, which is how the guest keys the load. A host's sequence is minted only for\n/// a command that is sent, never for the step that finishes. Steps and answers alternate: every [`Self::step`] that sends is\n/// answered by exactly one [`Self::answer`] under the same sequence.\n///\n/// 🛑️ A cancel requested before admission sends nothing and finishes `Cancelled`. After admission it sends\n/// `CancelDocumentArchiveLoad` once and keeps polling: only the guest's terminal status says whether the previous document was\n/// restored or the load won the race (a refused cancel is that race, and the next poll answers it). A cancelled terminal whose\n/// acknowledgement is refused still owns retained input, so it is polled again before the next acknowledgement.\npub struct DocumentArchiveLoadHost {\n    archive: Option<DocumentArchivePack>,\n    operation: Option<u64>,\n    sent: Option<(u64, DocumentArchiveLoadSent)>,\n    cancel_requested: bool,\n    cancel_sent: bool,\n    terminal: Option<DocumentArchiveLoadStatus>,\n    outcome: Option<DocumentArchiveLoadOutcome>,\n}\n\nimpl DocumentArchiveLoadHost {\n    pub fn new(archive: DocumentArchivePack) -> Self {\n        Self { archive: Some(archive), operation: None, sent: None, cancel_requested: false, cancel_sent: false, terminal: None, outcome: None }\n    }\n\n    /// 🔢️ The admitted operation, once the admission was sent.\n    pub fn operation(&self) -> Option<u64> {\n        self.operation\n    }\n\n    /// 🛑️ Asks for the load to stop; idempotent, and a no-op once a terminal status is known.\n    pub fn request_cancel(&mut self) {\n        self.cancel_requested = true;\n        if self.operation.is_none() && self.outcome.is_none() {\n            self.archive = None;\n            self.outcome = Some(DocumentArchiveLoadOutcome::Cancelled);\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// ➡️ The next command, stamped with a sequence from `next_seq`, or the outcome once the load is over.\n    pub fn step(&mut self, next_seq: impl FnOnce() -> u64) -> DocumentArchiveLoadStep {\n        if let Some(outcome) = &self.outcome {\n            return DocumentArchiveLoadStep::Finished(outcome.clone());\n        }\n        let seq = next_seq();\n        let (sent, command) = match (self.operation, &self.terminal) {\n            (None, _) => (DocumentArchiveLoadSent::Admit, AppCommand::LoadDocumentArchive { seq, archive: self.archive.take().unwrap_or_default() }),\n            (Some(operation), Some(_)) => (DocumentArchiveLoadSent::Acknowledge, AppCommand::AcknowledgeDocumentArchiveLoad { seq, operation }),\n            (Some(operation), None) if self.cancel_requested && !self.cancel_sent => (DocumentArchiveLoadSent::Cancel, AppCommand::CancelDocumentArchiveLoad { seq, operation }),\n            (Some(operation), None) => (DocumentArchiveLoadSent::Poll, AppCommand::PollDocumentArchiveLoad { seq, operation }),\n        };\n        if sent == DocumentArchiveLoadSent::Admit {\n            self.operation = Some(seq);\n        }\n        self.sent = Some((seq, sent));\n        DocumentArchiveLoadStep::Send { seq, command }\n    }\n\n    /// 📬️ Takes the guest's answer to the command sent under `seq`; a poll answers its status for the host's progress.\n    pub fn answer(&mut self, seq: u64, frame: &AppFrame) -> Result<Option<DocumentArchiveLoadStatus>, DocumentArchiveLoadRefusal> {\n        let (sent, operation) = match (self.sent.take(), self.operation) {\n            (Some((sent_seq, sent)), Some(operation)) if sent_seq == seq => (sent, operation),\n            _ => return Err(DocumentArchiveLoadRefusal::Unanswered),\n        };\n        match (sent, frame) {\n            (DocumentArchiveLoadSent::Admit, AppFrame::Done { in_reply_to }) if *in_reply_to == seq => Ok(None),\n            (DocumentArchiveLoadSent::Cancel, AppFrame::Done { in_reply_to }) if *in_reply_to == seq => {\n                self.cancel_sent = true;\n                Ok(None)\n            }\n            (DocumentArchiveLoadSent::Poll, AppFrame::DocumentArchiveLoad { in_reply_to, status }) if *in_reply_to == seq && status.operation == operation => {\n                if matches!(status.state, DocumentArchiveLoadState::Ready | DocumentArchiveLoadState::Cancelled | DocumentArchiveLoadState::Fault) {\n                    self.terminal = Some(status.clone());\n                }\n                Ok(Some(status.clone()))\n            }\n            (DocumentArchiveLoadSent::Acknowledge, AppFrame::Done { in_reply_to }) if *in_reply_to == seq => {\n                let terminal = self.terminal.take().ok_or(DocumentArchiveLoadRefusal::Unanswered)?;\n                self.outcome = Some(match terminal.state {\n                    DocumentArchiveLoadState::Ready => DocumentArchiveLoadOutcome::Ready,\n                    DocumentArchiveLoadState::Cancelled => DocumentArchiveLoadOutcome::Cancelled,\n                    _ => DocumentArchiveLoadOutcome::Fault(terminal.fault),\n                });\n                Ok(None)\n            }\n            (DocumentArchiveLoadSent::Cancel, AppFrame::Error { in_reply_to: Some(reply), .. }) if *reply == seq => {\n                self.cancel_sent = true;\n                Ok(None)\n            }\n            (DocumentArchiveLoadSent::Acknowledge, AppFrame::Error { in_reply_to: Some(reply), .. }) if *reply == seq && self.terminal.as_ref().is_some_and(|terminal| terminal.state == DocumentArchiveLoadState::Cancelled) => {\n                self.terminal = None;\n                Ok(None)\n            }\n            (_, AppFrame::Error { in_reply_to: Some(reply), fault, .. }) if *reply == seq => Err(DocumentArchiveLoadRefusal::Refused(fault.clone())),\n            _ => Err(DocumentArchiveLoadRefusal::Unanswered),\n        }\n    }\n}\n//#endregion 🔖️DocumentArchiveLoadHost\n\n//#region 🔖️Codec\n// Hand-rolled binary frame encode/decode: `tag: u8 | fields...` — see the module-level docstring.\n// `crate::os_spr::wire::🔖️WireCodec` supplies the primitives; this crate adds only the option/vec\n// combinators the frame shapes need plus the tag-dispatch match arms below.\n\n// 🚫️async: R9 pure accessor — most call sites are inside `.ok_or_else`'s sync closure\n// (Option::ok_or_else requires sync FnOnce); no suspension point exists in the body either.\nfn malformed(what: &'static str, offset: u64, detail: &str) -> crate::os_spr::ProtocolError {\n    crate::os_spr::ProtocolError::Malformed { what, offset, detail: detail.to_string() }\n}\n\n//#region 🔖️Combinators\nasync fn write_opt_u64(out: &mut Vec<u8>, value: &Option<u64>) {\n    crate::os_spr::write_bool(out, value.is_some());\n    if let Some(v) = value {\n        crate::os_spr::write_varint_u64(out, *v);\n    }\n}\n\nasync fn read_opt_u64(bytes: &[u8], pos: &mut usize) -> Result<Option<u64>, crate::os_spr::ProtocolError> {\n    if crate::os_spr::read_bool(bytes, pos)? {\n        Ok(Some(crate::os_spr::read_varint_u64(bytes, pos)?))\n    } else {\n        Ok(None)\n    }\n}\n\nfn read_invocation_result_pack(bytes: &[u8], pos: &mut usize) -> Result<Vec<u8>, crate::os_spr::ProtocolError> {\n    let start = *pos;\n    let length = usize::try_from(crate::os_spr::read_varint_u64(bytes, pos)?).map_err(|_| malformed(\"channel invocation result pack\", start as u64, \"packed mutations or inverse group length does not fit this host\"))?;\n    if length > INVOCATION_RESULT_PACK_MAXIMUM_BYTES {\n        return Err(malformed(\"channel invocation result pack\", start as u64, \"packed mutations or inverse group exceed command transport authority\"));\n    }\n    let end = pos.checked_add(length).ok_or_else(|| malformed(\"channel invocation result pack\", start as u64, \"packed mutations or inverse group length overflow\"))?;\n    let value = bytes.get(*pos..end).ok_or_else(|| malformed(\"channel invocation result pack\", start as u64, \"packed mutations or inverse group are truncated\"))?.to_vec();\n    *pos = end;\n    Ok(value)\n}\n\n/// 🎞️ `presence u8 | byte` — an `Option<u8>` (`AppCommand::Presence.own_color`), the same\n/// presence-byte convention as {@link write_opt_u64} above.\nasync fn write_opt_u8(out: &mut Vec<u8>, value: &Option<u8>) {\n    crate::os_spr::write_bool(out, value.is_some());\n    if let Some(v) = value {\n        out.push(*v);\n    }\n}\n\nasync fn read_opt_u8(bytes: &[u8], pos: &mut usize) -> Result<Option<u8>, crate::os_spr::ProtocolError> {\n    if crate::os_spr::read_bool(bytes, pos)? {\n        let byte = *bytes.get(*pos).ok_or_else(|| malformed(\"channel app-command opt-u8\", *pos as u64, \"truncated\"))?;\n        *pos += 1;\n        Ok(Some(byte))\n    } else {\n        Ok(None)\n    }\n}\n\nasync fn write_vec_bytes(out: &mut Vec<u8>, values: &[Vec<u8>]) {\n    crate::os_spr::write_varint_u64(out, values.len() as u64);\n    for value in values {\n        crate::os_spr::write_bytes(out, value);\n    }\n}\n\nasync fn read_vec_bytes(bytes: &[u8], pos: &mut usize) -> Result<Vec<Vec<u8>>, crate::os_spr::ProtocolError> {\n    let count = crate::os_spr::read_varint_u64(bytes, pos)?;\n    // 🚫️async: R10 shape 2 — `read_bytes` is async but `Iterator::map`'s closure is sync; hoisted\n    // into a plain loop so each element can be awaited.\n    let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(count as usize);\n    for _ in 0..count {\n        out.push(crate::os_spr::read_bytes(bytes, pos)?);\n    }\n    Ok(out)\n}\n\nasync fn write_presence_roster(out: &mut Vec<u8>, roster: &PresenceRosterWire) {\n    crate::os_spr::write_varint_u64(out, roster.len() as u64);\n    for entry in roster.iter() {\n        crate::os_spr::write_bytes(out, entry);\n    }\n}\n\nasync fn write_vec_envelope(out: &mut Vec<u8>, values: &[crate::os_spr::causal::MutationEnvelope]) {\n    crate::os_spr::write_varint_u64(out, values.len() as u64);\n    for value in values {\n        crate::os_spr::causal::encode_envelope(value, out);\n    }\n}\n\nasync fn read_vec_envelope(bytes: &[u8], pos: &mut usize) -> Result<Vec<crate::os_spr::causal::MutationEnvelope>, crate::os_spr::ProtocolError> {\n    let count = crate::os_spr::read_varint_u64(bytes, pos)?;\n    // 🚫️async: R10 shape 2 — `decode_envelope` is async but `Iterator::map`'s closure is sync;\n    // hoisted into a plain loop so each element can be awaited.\n    let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(count as usize);\n    for _ in 0..count {\n        out.push(crate::os_spr::causal::decode_envelope(bytes, pos)?);\n    }\n    Ok(out)\n}\n//#endregion 🔖️Combinators\n\n/// 📤️ Encodes one `AppCommand`: `tag u8 | fields`.\n\nstruct CommandPageWriter {\n    pages: CommandPageSet,\n    current: [u8; COMMAND_PAGE_MAXIMUM_BYTES],\n    current_len: usize,\n    bytes: usize,\n}\n\nimpl CommandPageWriter {\n    /// ✍️ The generic encoder is the ONE authority that cannot declare its page count up front — it\n    /// discovers it while writing — so it declares the whole 64-page ceiling. It runs on a host, not\n    /// on the guest's fixed linear memory: the guest never encodes, it only admits pages.\n    fn try_new() -> Result<Self, semio_framework_diagnostic::Fault> {\n        Ok(Self { pages: CommandPageSet::try_new(COMMAND_MAXIMUM_PAGES)?, current: [0; COMMAND_PAGE_MAXIMUM_BYTES], current_len: 0, bytes: 0 })\n    }\n\n    fn flush(&mut self) -> Result<(), semio_framework_diagnostic::Fault> {\n        let current = std::mem::replace(&mut self.current, [0; COMMAND_PAGE_MAXIMUM_BYTES]);\n        let page = FixedCommandPage::try_from_array(current, self.current_len as u32)?;\n        self.current_len = 0;\n        self.pages.try_push(page).map_err(|(fault, _page)| fault)\n    }\n\n    fn write(&mut self, mut bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<(), semio_framework_diagnostic::Fault> {\n        while !bytes.is_empty() {\n            if self.current_len == COMMAND_PAGE_MAXIMUM_BYTES {\n                self.flush()?;\n            }\n            let take = bytes.len().min(COMMAND_PAGE_MAXIMUM_BYTES - self.current_len);\n            self.current[self.current_len..self.current_len + take].copy_from_slice(&bytes[..take]);\n            self.current_len += take;\n            bytes = &bytes[take..];\n            self.bytes += take;\n        }\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    fn byte(&mut self, byte: u8) -> Result<(), semio_framework_diagnostic::Fault> {\n        self.write(&[byte])\n    }\n\n    fn varint(&mut self, mut value: u64) -> Result<(), semio_framework_diagnostic::Fault> {\n        loop {\n            let mut byte = (value & 0x7f) as u8;\n            value >>= 7;\n            if value != 0 {\n                byte |= 0x80;\n            }\n            self.byte(byte)?;\n            if value == 0 {\n                return Ok(());\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    fn bytes(&mut self, bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<(), semio_framework_diagnostic::Fault> {\n        self.varint(bytes.len() as u64)?;\n        self.write(bytes)\n    }\n\n    fn string(&mut self, value: &str) -> Result<(), semio_framework_diagnostic::Fault> {\n        self.bytes(value.as_bytes())\n    }\n\n    fn envelope(&mut self, value: &crate::os_spr::causal::MutationEnvelope) -> Result<(), semio_framework_diagnostic::Fault> {\n        self.string(&value.mutation_id.0)?;\n        self.string(&value.document_id.0)?;\n        self.string(&value.actor.0)?;\n        self.varint(value.dependencies.len() as u64)?;\n        for dependency in &value.dependencies {\n            self.string(&dependency.0)?;\n        }\n        match &value.observed {\n            Some(observed) => {\n                self.varint(1)?;\n                self.string(&observed.0)?;\n            }\n            None => self.varint(0)?,\n        }\n        self.varint(value.target.len() as u64)?;\n        for segment in &value.target {\n            self.string(segment)?;\n        }\n        self.string(&value.diff.schema.0)?;\n        self.bytes(&value.diff.payload)?;\n        self.string(&value.inverse.schema.0)?;\n        self.bytes(&value.inverse.payload)?;\n        self.varint(value.timestamp.actor)?;\n        self.varint(value.timestamp.physical_ms)?;\n        self.varint(value.timestamp.logical)?;\n        match &value.transaction {\n            Some(transaction) => {\n                self.varint(1)?;\n                self.string(&transaction.id)?;\n                self.string(&transaction.tool)\n            }\n            None => self.varint(0),\n        }\n    }\n\n    fn finish(mut self) -> Result<PagedCommand, semio_framework_diagnostic::Fault> {\n        if self.current_len != 0 {\n            self.flush()?;\n        }\n        PagedCommand::try_from_pages(self.pages).map_err(|(fault, _pages)| fault)\n    }\n}\n\nfn write_media_export_handle_paged(out: &mut CommandPageWriter, handle: &MediaExportHandleWire) -> Result<(), semio_framework_diagnostic::Fault> {\n    out.varint(u64::from(handle.app_instance_id))?;\n    out.string(&handle.parent_document_id)?;\n    out.varint(handle.operation_id)?;\n    out.varint(handle.base_revision)?;\n    out.varint(handle.generation)\n}\n\nfn write_media_export_handle(out: &mut Vec<u8>, handle: &MediaExportHandleWire) {\n    crate::os_spr::write_varint_u64(out, u64::from(handle.app_instance_id));\n    crate::os_spr::write_str(out, &handle.parent_document_id);\n    crate::os_spr::write_varint_u64(out, handle.operation_id);\n    crate::os_spr::write_varint_u64(out, handle.base_revision);\n    crate::os_spr::write_varint_u64(out, handle.generation);\n}\n\nfn read_media_export_handle(bytes: &[u8], pos: &mut usize) -> Result<MediaExportHandleWire, crate::os_spr::ProtocolError> {\n    let app_instance_id = u32::try_from(crate::os_spr::read_varint_u64(bytes, pos)?).map_err(|_| malformed(\"media export app instance\", *pos as u64, \"app instance exceeds u32\"))?;\n    Ok(MediaExportHandleWire {\n        app_instance_id,\n        parent_document_id: crate::os_spr::read_str(bytes, pos)?,\n        operation_id: crate::os_spr::read_varint_u64(bytes, pos)?,\n        base_revision: crate::os_spr::read_varint_u64(bytes, pos)?,\n        generation: crate::os_spr::read_varint_u64(bytes, pos)?,\n    })\n}\n\n/// 📄️ Produces the exact pre-admitted page owner consumed by reactor command batches.\npub async fn encode_app_command(command: &AppCommand) -> Result<PagedCommand, semio_framework_diagnostic::Fault> {\n    if let AppCommand::Presence { own_color, peers, .. } = command {\n        let mut pages = CommandPageSet::try_new(peers.len().max(1))?;\n        for peer in peers.iter() {\n            pages.try_push(FixedCommandPage::try_copy_from(peer)?).map_err(|(fault, _page)| fault)?;\n        }\n        if pages.is_empty() {\n            pages.try_push(FixedCommandPage::try_copy_from(&[])?).map_err(|(fault, _page)| fault)?;\n        }\n        return PagedCommand::try_from_presence_pages(*own_color, pages, 🔖️DocumentArchiveLoadHost\n/// 🏁️ How one host-driven whole-document load ended (`📓️api-stepped-document-load.md` §2.3, ticket\n/// 26/09/30/NON-DESTRUCTIVE-HISTORY-EDITING). `Cancelled` and `Fault` both left the previous document exactly as it was;\n/// `Fault` carries the guest's encoded fault.\n#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum DocumentArchiveLoadOutcome {\n    Ready,\n    Cancelled,\n    Fault(Vec<u8>),\n}\n\n/// 🧭️ What a host does next with one [`DocumentArchiveLoadHost`]: send this command, stamped with the sequence the host minted\n/// for it, or stop, because the load reached its acknowledged terminal or was cancelled before it was ever admitted.\n#[derive(Debug, PartialEq)]\npub enum DocumentArchiveLoadStep {\n    Send { seq: u64, command: AppCommand },\n    Finished(DocumentArchiveLoadOutcome),\n}\n\n/// 🚧️ An answer a load cannot go on from: the guest refused the admission, a poll or an acknowledgement (its encoded fault), or the\n/// frame handed back answers some other command.\n#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum DocumentArchiveLoadRefusal {\n    Refused(Vec<u8>),\n    Unanswered,\n}\n\n#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]\nenum DocumentArchiveLoadSent {\n    Admit,\n    Poll,\n    Cancel,\n    Acknowledge,\n}\n\n/// 🗃️ The host half of the stepped, ACK-owned whole-document load (`📓️api-stepped-document-load.md` §2): a transport-free state\n/// machine every Rust host drives with its own exchange — the MCP gateway, the `🏃️run` batch runner, the wgpu bridge — so\n/// admit → poll* → (cancel → poll*) → acknowledge exists once. TS twin: `AppChannelClient.loadDocumentArchive` (`💻️os/🟦️.ts`).\n/// Corpus: `🧫️fixtures/🧫️document-archive-load-host/🔣️.json` (schema `🧬️schema/🔣️document-archive-load-host/🔣️.json`).\n///\n/// 🔢️ The operation is the admission's own sequence, which is how the guest keys the load. A host's sequence is minted only for\n/// a command that is sent, never for the step that finishes. Steps and answers alternate: every [`Self::step`] that sends is\n/// answered by exactly one [`Self::answer`] under the same sequence.\n///\n/// 🛑️ A cancel requested before admission sends nothing and finishes `Cancelled`. After admission it sends\n/// `CancelDocumentArchiveLoad` once and keeps polling: only the guest's terminal status says whether the previous document was\n/// restored or the load won the race (a refused cancel is that race, and the next poll answers it). A cancelled terminal whose\n/// acknowledgement is refused still owns retained input, so it is polled again before the next acknowledgement.\npub struct DocumentArchiveLoadHost {\n    archive: Option<DocumentArchivePack>,\n    operation: Option<u64>,\n    sent: Option<(u64, DocumentArchiveLoadSent)>,\n    cancel_requested: bool,\n    cancel_sent: bool,\n    terminal: Option<DocumentArchiveLoadStatus>,\n    outcome: Option<DocumentArchiveLoadOutcome>,\n}\n\nimpl DocumentArchiveLoadHost {\n    pub fn new(archive: DocumentArchivePack) -> Self {\n        Self { archive: Some(archive), operation: None, sent: None, cancel_requested: false, cancel_sent: false, terminal: None, outcome: None }\n    }\n\n    /// 🔢️ The admitted operation, once the admission was sent.\n    pub fn operation(&self) -> Option<u64> {\n        self.operation\n    }\n\n    /// 🛑️ Asks for the load to stop; idempotent, and a no-op once a terminal status is known.\n    pub fn request_cancel(&mut self) {\n        self.cancel_requested = true;\n        if self.operation.is_none() && self.outcome.is_none() {\n            self.archive = None;\n            self.outcome = Some(DocumentArchiveLoadOutcome::Cancelled);\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// ➡️ The next command, stamped with a sequence from `next_seq`, or the outcome once the load is over.\n    pub fn step(&mut self, next_seq: impl FnOnce() -> u64) -> DocumentArchiveLoadStep {\n        if let Some(outcome) = &self.outcome {\n            return DocumentArchiveLoadStep::Finished(outcome.clone());\n        }\n        let seq = next_seq();\n        let (sent, command) = match (self.operation, &self.terminal) {\n            (None, _) => (DocumentArchiveLoadSent::Admit, AppCommand::LoadDocumentArchive { seq, archive: self.archive.take().unwrap_or_default() }),\n            (Some(operation), Some(_)) => (DocumentArchiveLoadSent::Acknowledge, AppCommand::AcknowledgeDocumentArchiveLoad { seq, operation }),\n            (Some(operation), None) if self.cancel_requested && !self.cancel_sent => (DocumentArchiveLoadSent::Cancel, AppCommand::CancelDocumentArchiveLoad { seq, operation }),\n            (Some(operation), None) => (DocumentArchiveLoadSent::Poll, AppCommand::PollDocumentArchiveLoad { seq, operation }),\n        };\n        if sent == DocumentArchiveLoadSent::Admit {\n            self.operation = Some(seq);\n        }\n        self.sent = Some((seq, sent));\n        DocumentArchiveLoadStep::Send { seq, command }\n    }\n\n    /// 📬️ Takes the guest's answer to the command sent under `seq`; a poll answers its status for the host's progress.\n    pub fn answer(&mut self, seq: u64, frame: &AppFrame) -> Result<Option<DocumentArchiveLoadStatus>, DocumentArchiveLoadRefusal> {\n        let (sent, operation) = match (self.sent.take(), self.operation) {\n            (Some((sent_seq, sent)), Some(operation)) if sent_seq == seq => (sent, operation),\n            _ => return Err(DocumentArchiveLoadRefusal::Unanswered),\n        };\n        match (sent, frame) {\n            (DocumentArchiveLoadSent::Admit, AppFrame::Done { in_reply_to }) if *in_reply_to == seq => Ok(None),\n            (DocumentArchiveLoadSent::Cancel, AppFrame::Done { in_reply_to }) if *in_reply_to == seq => {\n                self.cancel_sent = true;\n                Ok(None)\n            }\n            (DocumentArchiveLoadSent::Poll, AppFrame::DocumentArchiveLoad { in_reply_to, status }) if *in_reply_to == seq && status.operation == operation => {\n                if matches!(status.state, DocumentArchiveLoadState::Ready | DocumentArchiveLoadState::Cancelled | DocumentArchiveLoadState::Fault) {\n                    self.terminal = Some(status.clone());\n                }\n                Ok(Some(status.clone()))\n            }\n            (DocumentArchiveLoadSent::Acknowledge, AppFrame::Done { in_reply_to }) if *in_reply_to == seq => {\n                let terminal = self.terminal.take().ok_or(DocumentArchiveLoadRefusal::Unanswered)?;\n                self.outcome = Some(match terminal.state {\n                    DocumentArchiveLoadState::Ready => DocumentArchiveLoadOutcome::Ready,\n                    DocumentArchiveLoadState::Cancelled => DocumentArchiveLoadOutcome::Cancelled,\n                    _ => DocumentArchiveLoadOutcome::Fault(terminal.fault),\n                });\n                Ok(None)\n            }\n            (DocumentArchiveLoadSent::Cancel, AppFrame::Error { in_reply_to: Some(reply), .. }) if *reply == seq => {\n                self.cancel_sent = true;\n                Ok(None)\n            }\n            (DocumentArchiveLoadSent::Acknowledge, AppFrame::Error { in_reply_to: Some(reply), .. }) if *reply == seq && self.terminal.as_ref().is_some_and(|terminal| terminal.state == DocumentArchiveLoadState::Cancelled) => {\n                self.terminal = None;\n                Ok(None)\n            }\n            (_, AppFrame::Error { in_reply_to: Some(reply), fault, .. }) if *reply == seq => Err(DocumentArchiveLoadRefusal::Refused(fault.clone())),\n            _ => Err(DocumentArchiveLoadRefusal::Unanswered),\n        }\n    }\n}\n//#endregion 🔖️DocumentArchiveLoadHost\n\n//#region 🔖️Codec\n// Hand-rolled binary frame encode/decode: `tag: u8 | fields...` — see the module-level docstring.\n// `crate::os_spr::wire::🔖️WireCodec` supplies the primitives; this crate adds only the option/vec\n// combinators the frame shapes need plus the tag-dispatch match arms below.\n\n// 🚫️async: R9 pure accessor — most call sites are inside `.ok_or_else`'s sync closure\n// (Option::ok_or_else requires sync FnOnce); no suspension point exists in the body either.\nfn malformed(what: &'static str, offset: u64, detail: &str) -> crate::os_spr::ProtocolError {\n    crate::os_spr::ProtocolError::Malformed { what, offset, detail: detail.to_string() }\n}\n\n//#region 🔖️Combinators\nasync fn write_opt_u64(out: &mut Vec<u8>, value: &Option<u64>) {\n    crate::os_spr::write_bool(out, value.is_some());\n    if let Some(v) = value {\n        crate::os_spr::write_varint_u64(out, *v);\n    }\n}\n\nasync fn read_opt_u64(bytes: &[u8], pos: &mut usize) -> Result<Option<u64>, crate::os_spr::ProtocolError> {\n    if crate::os_spr::read_bool(bytes, pos)? {\n        Ok(Some(crate::os_spr::read_varint_u64(bytes, pos)?))\n    } else {\n        Ok(None)\n    }\n}\n\nfn read_invocation_result_pack(bytes: &[u8], pos: self.current_len as u32)?;\n        self.current_len = 0;\n        self.pages.try_push(page).map_err(|(fault, _page)| fault)\n    }\n\n    fn write(&mut self, mut bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<(), semio_framework_diagnostic::Fault> {\n        while !bytes.is_empty() {\n            if self.current_len == COMMAND_PAGE_MAXIMUM_BYTES {\n                self.flush()?;\n            }\n            let take = bytes.len().min(COMMAND_PAGE_MAXIMUM_BYTES - self.current_len);\n            self.current[self.current_len..self.current_len + take].copy_from_slice(&bytes[..take]);\n            self.current_len += take;\n            bytes = &bytes[take..];\n            self.bytes += take;\n        }\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    fn byte(&mut self, byte: u8) -> Result<(), semio_framework_diagnostic::Fault> {\n        self.write(&[byte])\n    }\n\n    fn varint(&mut self, mut value: u64) -> Result<(), semio_framework_diagnostic::Fault> {\n        loop {\n            let mut byte = (value & 0x7f) as u8;\n            value >>= 7;\n            if value != 0 {\n                byte |= 0x80;\n            }\n            self.byte(byte)?;\n            if value == 0 {\n self.bytes(&value.diff.payload)?;\n        self.string(&value.inverse.schema.0)?;\n        self.bytes(&value.inverse.payload)?;\n        self.varint(value.timestamp.actor)?;\n        self.varint(value.timestamp.physical_ms)?;\n        self.varint(value.timestamp.logical)?;\n        match &value.transaction {\n            Some(transaction) => {\n                self.varint(1)?;\n _pages)| fault)\n    }\n}\n\nfn write_media_export_handle_paged(out: &mut CommandPageWriter, handle: &MediaExportHandleWire) -> Result<(), semio_framework_diagnostic::Fault> {\n       "inverse": "//! 🎞️ Protocol app-engine channel: the `AppCommand`/`AppFrame` binary frame taxonomy every app,\n//! once turned into a headless engine driven by bidirectional streaming of typed binary commands,\n//! exchanges with its client (a UI or a headless runner) — every UI interaction becomes a\n//! forwarded `AppCommand`, every engine reaction a returned `AppFrame`. Ticket:\n//! `.🧬semio/🦑️repo/🎫️tickets/🎆️26/🌙️08/☀️01/HEADLESS-APP-ENGINE-BINARY-COMMAND-PROTOCOL-FOUNDATIONS/`.\n//!\n//! 🎯️ Mirrors `protocol_wire`'s W5 hand-rolled binary layout exactly: `tag: u8` (assigned\n//! sequentially in match-arm declaration order below, NOT the enum's own discriminant) followed by\n//! its fields in declaration order, no per-field tags, no body-length prefix — one frame per\n//! channel message. `crate::os_spr::wire::🔖️WireCodec` supplies the primitive codec\n//! (`write_varint_u64`/`write_str`/`write_bytes`/`write_bool` and their `read_*` twins); this crate\n//! adds only the option/vec combinators and the two enums' tag dispatch below. Unlike\n//! `crate::os_spr::wire::ClientFrame`/`ServerFrame`, `AppCommand`/`AppFrame` carry no `Lane` byte —\n//! the app-engine channel is a single logical stream, not split into causally-ordered vs.\n//! best-effort lanes.\n\n//#region 🔖️Version\n/// 🔢️ The channel wire format's own version, pinned against the shared cross-language\n/// fixture `🔖️channel-version.json` so a half-done bump fails a test instead of drifting silently.\n/// Channel v12 (`📓️design-abi.md` §2 \"`exchange` collapse\") retires the `AppCommand::Hello` /\n/// `AppFrame::Welcome` handshake entirely — lifecycle now D) -> Result<Option<String>, D::Error> {\n    serde::Deserialize::deserialize(deserializer)\n}\n\n//#region 🔖️MediaExportWire\n#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub struct MediaExportHandleWire {\n    pub app_instance_id: u32,\n    pub parent_document_id: String,\n    pub operation_id: u64,\n    pub base_revision: u64,\n    pub generation: u64,\n}\n\n#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, own. Nothing here chooses a\n/// ceiling: [`semio_framework_trace::GUEST_HOST_ANSWER_CEILING_BYTES`] already says what a guest may\n/// be handed for ONE outstanding request before it answers with a typed fault instead of allocating.\npub const COMMAND_MAXIMUM_BYTES: usize = semio_framework_trace::GUEST_HOST_ANSWER_CEILING_BYTES;\n\n/// 📄️ Pages that budget occupies — the assembled ceiling over the page extent, not a chosen number.\n///\n/// 🧊️ A page authority's spine is `COMMAND_MAXIMUM_PAGES * size_of::<FixedCommandPage>()`, and a\n/// page slot is a POINTER to its own 4 KiB block (see [`FixedCommandPage`]), never the block itself\n/// — so the spine stays inside [`semio_framework_trace::GUEST_CONTIGUOUS_REQUEST_CEILING_BYTES`]\n/// while the command it assembles is free to be as long as the host-answer budget allows. Storing\n/// the blocks INLINE is what forced a 64-page ceiling: 64 inline pages are 262 272 contiguous bytes,\n/// four times what a fragmented guest can be relied on to serve, and the ceiling that bought that\n/// reservation also refused every command past 262 144 bytes — a 272 089-char contributions pack\n/// among them (ticket 26/09/09/PROCEDURAL-3D-END-TO-END).\npub const COMMAND_MAXIMUM_PAGES: usize = COMMAND_MAXIMUM_BYTES / COMMAND_PAGE_MAXIMUM_BYTES;\npub const COMMAND_BATCH_MAXIMUM_ITEMS: usize = 64;\npub const INVOCATION_RESULT_PACK_MAXIMUM_BYTES: usize = COMMAND_MAXIMUM_BYTES;\n\n/// 🧱️ One command page's own 4 KiB block, reserved fallibly so an exhausted guest heap answers with\n/// a `Fault` the host can display rather than `handle_alloc_error` → semio_framework_diagnostic::FaultCode::new(\"plugin.command-page-allocation\"), \"a command page could not reserve its exact 4096-byte block\"))?;\n    block.resize(COMMAND_PAGE_MAXIMUM_BYTES, 0);\n byte authority\" });\n        }\n        let bytes = entry.len();\n        self.entries[self.len] = Some(entry.into_boxed_slice());\n        self.len += 1;\n        self.bytes += bytes;\n   }\n        (true, 0)\n    }\n}\n\n#[derive(Debug, Default)]\nstruct PagedMediaExportHandleDecode {\n    stage: u8,\n    app_instance_id: u32,\n    parent_document_id: Option<String>,\n CHANNEL_VERSION 9 wire addition.\n    TransactionProposal {\n        in_reply_to: u64,\n        proposal_id: String,\n        local_ops: Vec<Vec<u8>>,\n        description: String,\n        coalesce_key: String,\n        foreign: Vec<Vec<u8>>,\n    },\n    /// 🤝️ Phase-1 reply — empty `rejection` means the member is prepared. CHANNEL_VERSION 9 wire addition.\n    TransactionPrepared {\n        txn_id: String,\n        foreign: Vec<Vec<u8>>,\n        rejection: Vec<u8>,\n    },\n    /// ✅️ Phase-2 commit succeeded for a member. CHANNEL_VERSION 9 wire addition.\n    TransactionCommitted {\n        txn_id: String,\n        edit_id: String,\n    },\n    /// ↩️ A member rolled back its not-yet-committed transaction. CHANNEL_VERSION 9 wire addition.\n    TransactionRolledBack {\n        txn_id: String,\n    },\n    /// ⚔️ Pushed unsolicited (next to `DocumentChanged`) after every ingest: one packed `MergeReport`\n    /// describing how the batch was resolved. CHANNEL_VERSION 11 wire addition.\n    MergeReport {\n        in_reply_to: Option<u64>,\n        report: Vec<u8>,\n    },\n    /// ⚔️ Pushed unsolicited (next to `DocumentChanged`) after every ingest, and the reply to\n    /// `AppCommand::ReadConflicts`: one packed `Vec<Conflict>`. CHANNEL_VERSION 11 wire addition.\n    Conflicts {\n        in_reply_to: Option<u64>,\n        conflicts: Vec<u8>,\n    },\n    /// 🎨️ Revisioned UI patch batch for one surface — replaces `UiSection`'s cache-probe push. The\n    /// reactor ABI's guest returns `turn-result.ui-patches` (`semio_framework::kernel::UiPatch`,\n    /// `📓️design-abi.md` §2 \"`exchange` collapse\"); the host re-frames each one as this channel\n    /// frame to reach a UI client. `surface`/`kind`/`revision`/`base_revision` mirror\n    /// `kernel::UiPatch` field-for-field; `ops` is `kernel::PatchOp` — reused from\n    /// `semio_framework::kernel`, never redefined here — pack-encoded via\n    /// `store::pack_rt::encode_wire_value` (`Vec<PatchOp>`), same \"nested payload stays opaque\n    /// bytes\" convention every other structured field in this file already uses.\n    /// `base_revision` lets the client detect a stale diff and fall back to a full body instead of\n    /// reconciling a diff it can't trust. `in_reply_to` is `None` for an unsolicited push (the\n    /// common case — surfaces render lazily off `surface-visible`/timers, not off a command reply).\n    /// CHANNEL_VERSION 12 wire addition.\n    UiPatch {\n        in_reply_to: Option<u64>,\n        surface: String,\n        kind: String,\n        revision: u64,\n        base_revision: u64,\n        ops: Vec<u8>,\n    },\n    /// 🏁️ Marks the end of one surface's initial full-body snapshot burst, so a client that just\n    /// subscribed (`surface-visible`) knows when it has seen a complete tree and can start applying\n    /// incremental `UiPatch` frames instead of buffering. CHANNEL_VERSION 12 wire addition.\n    UiSnapshotEnd {\n        revision: u64,\n    },\n    /// 🏁️ One mounted typed operation reached its terminal result. Unsolicited and NEVER a reply:\n    /// the command that started the operation already returned its \"started\" `Invocation` long\n    /// before the retained job finished, so no `in_reply_to` sequence exists to correlate against —\n    /// `operation` (the host-allocated `semio_framework_job::OperationId`) is the correlation key\n    /// instead. `revision` is the artifact store's content revision at completion; `ui_scope` is the\n    /// operation's final `kernel::UiDirtyScope` and `history_patch` its command-log delta (empty\n    /// bytes when the operation recorded nothing), both `store::pack_rt::encode_wire_value`-encoded\n    /// exactly like `Invocation`'s same-named fields. CHANNEL_VERSION 15 wire addition.\n    OperationCompleted {\n        operation: u64,\n        revision: u64,\n        ui_scope: Vec<u8>,\n        history_patch: Vec<u8>,\n    },\n    /// 📃️ ACK-owned local-only pages are independent of ordinary command outcomes.\n    LocalInteractionQuery {\n        reply: protocol::LocalInteractionQueryReply,\n    },\n    /// 🗃️ Complete generation-fenced recursive document archive. CHANNEL_VERSION 16 wire addition.\n    DocumentArchive {\n        in_reply_to: u64,\n        archive: DocumentArchivePack,\n    },\n    /// 📊️ Progress or terminal state for one ACK-owned archive load.\n    DocumentArchiveLoad {\n        in_reply_to: u64,\n        status: DocumentArchiveLoadStatus,\n    },\n    MediaExportSubmitted {\n        in_reply_to: u64,\n        handle: MediaExportHandleWire,\n    },\n    MediaExportStatus {\n        in_reply_to: u64,\n        handle: MediaExportHandleWire,\n        state: MediaExportStateWire,\n        applied_progress: u64,\n MediaExportHandleWire,\n        data: Vec<u8>,\n        terminal: bool,\n    },\n    DocumentIdentity { in_reply_to: u64, identity: AppDocumentIdentity },\n}\n//#endregion 🔖️AppFrame\n\n//#region 🔖️DocumentArchiveLoadHost\n/// 🏁️ How one host-driven whole-document load ended (`📓️api-stepped-document-load.md` §2.3, ticket\n/// 26/09/30/NON-DESTRUCTIVE-HISTORY-EDITING). `Cancelled` and `Fault` both left the previous document exactly as it was;\n/// `Fault` carries the guest's encoded fault.\n#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum DocumentArchiveLoadOutcome {\n    Ready,\n    Cancelled,\n    Fault(Vec<u8>),\n}\n\n/// 🧭️ What a host does next with one [`DocumentArchiveLoadHost`]: send this command, stamped with the sequence the host minted\n/// for it, or stop, because the load reached its acknowledged terminal or was cancelled before it was ever admitted.\n#[derive(Debug, PartialEq)]\npub enum DocumentArchiveLoadStep {\n    Send { seq: u64, command: AppCommand },\n    Finished(DocumentArchiveLoadOutcome),\n}\n\n/// 🚧️ An answer a load cannot go on from: the guest refused the admission, a poll or an acknowledgement (its encoded fault), or the\n/// frame handed back answers some other command.\n#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum DocumentArchiveLoadRefusal {\n    Refused(Vec<u8>),\n    Unanswered,\n}\n\n#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]\nenum DocumentArchiveLoadSent {\n    Admit,\n    Poll,\n    Cancel,\n    Acknowledge,\n}\n\n/// 🗃️ The host half of the stepped, ACK-owned whole-document load (`📓️api-stepped-document-load.md` §2): a transport-free state\n/// machine every Rust host drives with its own exchange — the MCP gateway, the `🏃️run` batch runner, the wgpu bridge — so\n/// admit → poll* → (cancel → poll*) → acknowledge exists once. TS twin: `AppChannelClient.loadDocumentArchive` (`💻️os/🟦️.ts`).\n/// Corpus: `🧫️fixtures/🧫️document-archive-load-host/🔣️.json` (schema `🧬️schema/🔣️document-archive-load-host/🔣️.json`).\n///\n/// 🔢️ The operation is the admission's own sequence, which is how the guest keys the load. A host's sequence is minted only for\n/// a command that is sent, never for the step that finishes. Steps and answers alternate: every [`Self::step`] that sends is\n/// answered by exactly one [`Self::answer`] under the same sequence.\n///\n/// 🛑️ A cancel requested before admission sends nothing and finishes `Cancelled`. After admission it sends\n/// `CancelDocumentArchiveLoad` once and keeps polling: only the guest's terminal status says whether the previous document was\n/// restored or the load won the race (a refused cancel is that race, and the next poll answers it). A cancelled terminal whose\n/// acknowledgement is refused still owns retained input, so it is polled again before the next acknowledgement.\npub struct DocumentArchiveLoadHost {\n    archive: Option<DocumentArchivePack>,\n    operation: Option<u64>,\n    sent: Option<(u64, DocumentArchiveLoadSent)>,\n    cancel_requested: bool,\n    cancel_sent: bool,\n    terminal: Option<DocumentArchiveLoadStatus>,\n    outcome: Option<DocumentArchiveLoadOutcome>,\n}\n\nimpl DocumentArchiveLoadHost {\n    pub fn new(archive: DocumentArchivePack) -> Self {\n        Self { archive: Some(archive), operation: None, sent: None, cancel_requested: false, cancel_sent: false, terminal: None, outcome: None }\n    }\n\n    /// 🔢️ The admitted operation, once the admission was sent.\n    pub fn operation(&self) -> Option<u64> {\n        self.operation\n    }\n\n    /// 🛑️ Asks for the load to stop; idempotent, and a no-op once a terminal status is known.\n    pub fn request_cancel(&mut self) {\n        self.cancel_requested = true;\n        if self.operation.is_none() && self.outcome.is_none() {\n            self.archive = None;\n            self.outcome = Some(DocumentArchiveLoadOutcome::Cancelled);\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// ➡️ The next command, stamped with a sequence from `next_seq`, or the outcome once the load is over.\n    pub fn step(&mut self, next_seq: impl FnOnce() -> u64) -> DocumentArchiveLoadStep {\n        if let Some(outcome) = &self.outcome {\n            return DocumentArchiveLoadStep::Finished(outcome.clone());\n        }\n        let seq = next_seq();\n        let (sent, command) = match (self.operation, &self.terminal) {\n            (None, _) => (DocumentArchiveLoadSent::Admit, AppCommand::LoadDocumentArchive { seq, archive: self.archive.take().unwrap_or_default() }),\n            (Some(operation), Some(_)) => (DocumentArchiveLoadSent::Acknowledge, AppCommand::AcknowledgeDocumentArchiveLoad { seq, operation }),\n            (Some(operation), None) if self.cancel_requested && !self.cancel_sent => (DocumentArchiveLoadSent::Cancel, AppCommand::CancelDocumentArchiveLoad { seq, operation }),\n            (Some(operation), None) => (DocumentArchiveLoadSent::Poll, AppCommand::PollDocumentArchiveLoad { seq, operation }),\n        };\n        if sent == DocumentArchiveLoadSent::Admit {\n            self.operation = Some(seq);\n        }\n        self.sent = Some((seq, sent));\n        DocumentArchiveLoadStep::Send { seq, command }\n    }\n\n    /// 📬️ Takes the guest's answer to the command sent under `seq`; a poll answers its status for the host's progress.\n    pub fn answer(&mut self, seq: u64, frame: &AppFrame) -> Result<Option<DocumentArchiveLoadStatus>, DocumentArchiveLoadRefusal> {\n        let (sent, operation) = match (self.sent.take(), self.operation) {\n            (Some((sent_seq, sent)), Some(operation)) if sent_seq == seq => (sent, operation),\n            _ => return Err(DocumentArchiveLoadRefusal::Unanswered),\n        };\n        match (sent, frame) {\n            (DocumentArchiveLoadSent::Admit, AppFrame::Done { in_reply_to }) if *in_reply_to == seq => Ok(None),\n            (DocumentArchiveLoadSent::Cancel, AppFrame::Done { in_reply_to }) if *in_reply_to == seq => {\n                self.cancel_sent = true;\n                Ok(None)\n            }\n            (DocumentArchiveLoadSent::Poll, AppFrame::DocumentArchiveLoad { in_reply_to, status }) if *in_reply_to == seq && status.operation == operation => {\n                if matches!(status.state, DocumentArchiveLoadState::Ready | DocumentArchiveLoadState::Cancelled | DocumentArchiveLoadState::Fault) {\n                    self.terminal = Some(status.clone());\n                }\n                Ok(Some(status.clone()))\n            }\n            (DocumentArchiveLoadSent::Acknowledge, AppFrame::Done { in_reply_to }) if *in_reply_to == seq => {\n                let terminal = self.terminal.take().ok_or(DocumentArchiveLoadRefusal::Unanswered)?;\n                self.outcome = Some(match terminal.state {\n                    DocumentArchiveLoadState::Ready => DocumentArchiveLoadOutcome::Ready,\n                    DocumentArchiveLoadState::Cancelled => DocumentArchiveLoadOutcome::Cancelled,\n                    _ => DocumentArchiveLoadOutcome::Fault(terminal.fault),\n                });\n                Ok(None)\n            }\n            (DocumentArchiveLoadSent::Cancel, AppFrame::Error { in_reply_to: Some(reply), .. }) if *reply == seq => {\n                self.cancel_sent = true;\n                Ok(None)\n            }\n            (DocumentArchiveLoadSent::Acknowledge, AppFrame::Error { in_reply_to: Some(reply), .. }) if *reply == seq && self.terminal.as_ref().is_some_and(|terminal| terminal.state == DocumentArchiveLoadState::Cancelled) => {\n                self.terminal = None;\n                Ok(None)\n            }\n            (_, AppFrame::Error { in_reply_to: Some(reply), fault, .. }) if *reply == seq => Err(DocumentArchiveLoadRefusal::Refused(fault.clone())),\n            _ => Err(DocumentArchiveLoadRefusal::Unanswered),\n        }\n    }\n}\n//#endregion 🔖️DocumentArchiveLoadHost\n\n//#region 🔖️Codec\n// Hand-rolled binary frame encode/decode: `tag: u8 | fields...` — see the module-level docstring.\n// `crate::os_spr::wire::🔖️WireCodec` supplies the primitives; this crate adds only the option/vec\n// combinators the frame shapes need plus the tag-dispatch match arms below.\n\n// 🚫️async: R9 pure accessor — most call sites are inside `.ok_or_else`'s sync closure\n// (Option::ok_or_else requires sync FnOnce); no suspension point exists in the body either.\nfn malformed(what: &'static str, offset: u64, detail: &str) -> crate::os_spr::ProtocolError {\n    crate::os_spr::ProtocolError::Malformed { what, offset, detail: detail.to_string() }\n}\n\n//#region 🔖️Combinators\nasync fn write_opt_u64(out: &mut Vec<u8>, value: &Option<u64>) {\n    crate::os_spr::write_bool(out, value.is_some());\n    if let Some(v) = value {\n        crate::os_spr::write_varint_u64(out, *v);\n    }\n}\n\nasync fn read_opt_u64(bytes: &[u8], pos: &mut usize) -> Result<Option<u64>, crate::os_spr::ProtocolError> {\n    if crate::os_spr::read_bool(bytes, pos)? {\n        Ok(Some(crate::os_spr::read_varint_u64(bytes, pos)?))\n    } else {\n        Ok(None)\n    }\n}\n\nfn read_invocation_result_pack(bytes: &[u8], pos: &mut usize) -> Result<Vec<u8>, crate::os_spr::ProtocolError> {\n    let start = *pos;\n    let length = usize::try_from(crate::os_spr::read_varint_u64(bytes, pos)?).map_err(|_| malformed(\"channel invocation result pack\", start as u64, \"packed mutations or inverse group length does not fit this host\"))?;\n    if length > INVOCATION_RESULT_PACK_MAXIMUM_BYTES {\n        return Err(malformed(\"channel invocation result pack\", start as u64, \"packed mutations or inverse group exceed command transport authority\"));\n    }\n    let end = pos.checked_add(length).ok_or_else(|| malformed(\"channel invocation result pack\", start as u64, \"packed mutations or inverse group length overflow\"))?;\n    let value = bytes.get(*pos..end).ok_or_else(|| malformed(\"channel invocation result pack\", start as u64, \"packed mutations or inverse group are truncated\"))?.to_vec();\n    *pos = end;\n    Ok(value)\n}\n\n/// 🎞️ `presence u8 | byte` — an `Option<u8>` (`AppCommand::Presence.own_color`), the same\n/// presence-byte convention as {@link write_opt_u64} above.\nasync fn write_opt_u8(out: &mut Vec<u8>, value: &Option<u8>) {\n    crate::os_spr::write_bool(out, value.is_some());\n    if let Some(v) = value {\n        out.push(*v);\n    }\n}\n\nasync fn read_opt_u8(bytes: &[u8], pos: &mut usize) -> Result<Option<u8>, crate::os_spr::ProtocolError> {\n    if crate::os_spr::read_bool(bytes, pos)? {\n        let byte = *bytes.get(*pos).ok_or_else(|| malformed(\"channel app-command opt-u8\", *pos as u64, \"truncated\"))?;\n        *pos += 1;\n        Ok(Some(byte))\n    } else {\n        Ok(None)\n    }\n}\n\nasync fn write_vec_bytes(out: &mut Vec<u8>, values: &[Vec<u8>]) {\n    crate::os_spr::write_varint_u64(out, values.len() as u64);\n    for value in values {\n        crate::os_spr::write_bytes(out, value);\n    }\n}\n\nasync fn read_vec_bytes(bytes: &[u8], pos: &mut usize) -> Result<Vec<Vec<u8>>, crate::os_spr::ProtocolError> {\n    let count = crate::os_spr::read_varint_u64(bytes, pos)?;\n    // 🚫️async: R10 shape 2 — `read_bytes` is async but `Iterator::map`'s closure is sync; hoisted\n    // into a plain loop so each element can be awaited.\n    let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(count as usize);\n    for _ in 0..count {\n        out.push(crate::os_spr::read_bytes(bytes, pos)?);\n    }\n    Ok(out)\n}\n\nasync fn write_presence_roster(out: &mut Vec<u8>, roster: &PresenceRosterWire) {\n    crate::os_spr::write_varint_u64(out, roster.len() as u64);\n    for entry in roster.iter() {\n        crate::os_spr::write_bytes(out, entry);\n    }\n}\n\nasync fn write_vec_envelope(out: &mut Vec<u8>, values: &[crate::os_spr::causal::MutationEnvelope]) {\n    crate::os_spr::write_varint_u64(out, values.len() as u64);\n    for value in values {\n        crate::os_spr::causal::encode_envelope(value, out);\n    }\n}\n\nasync fn read_vec_envelope(bytes: &[u8], pos: &mut usize) -> Result<Vec<crate::os_spr::causal::MutationEnvelope>, crate::os_spr::ProtocolError> {\n    let count = crate::os_spr::read_varint_u64(bytes, pos)?;\n    // 🚫️async: R10 shape 2 — `decode_envelope` is async but `Iterator::map`'s closure is sync;\n    // hoisted into a plain loop so each element can be awaited.\n    let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(count as usize);\n    for _ in 0..count {\n        out.push(crate::os_spr::causal::decode_envelope(bytes, pos)?);\n    }\n    Ok(out)\n}\n//#endregion 🔖️Combinators\n\n/// 📤️ Encodes one `AppCommand`: `tag u8 | fields`.\n\nstruct CommandPageWriter {\n    pages: CommandPageSet,\n    current: [u8; COMMAND_PAGE_MAXIMUM_BYTES],\n    current_len: usize,\n    bytes: usize,\n}\n\nimpl CommandPageWriter {\n    /// ✍️ The generic encoder is the ONE authority that cannot declare its page count up front — it\n    /// discovers it while writing — so it declares the whole 64-page ceiling. It runs on a host, not\n    /// on the guest's fixed linear memory: the guest never encodes, it only admits pages.\n    fn try_new() -> Result<Self, semio_framework_diagnostic::Fault> {\n        Ok(Self { pages: CommandPageSet::try_new(COMMAND_MAXIMUM_PAGES)?, current: [0; COMMAND_PAGE_MAXIMUM_BYTES], current_len: 0, bytes: 0 })\n    }\n\n    fn flush(&mut self) -> Result<(), semio_framework_diagnostic::Fault> {\n        let current = std::mem::replace(&mut self.current, [0; COMMAND_PAGE_MAXIMUM_BYTES]);\n        let page = FixedCommandPage::try_from_array(current, self.current_len as u32)?;\n        self.current_len = 0;\n        self.pages.try_push(page).map_err(|(fault, _page)| fault)\n    }\n\n    fn write(&mut self, mut bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<(), semio_framework_diagnostic::Fault> {\n        while !bytes.is_empty() {\n            if self.current_len == COMMAND_PAGE_MAXIMUM_BYTES {\n                self.flush()?;\n            }\n            let take = bytes.len().min(COMMAND_PAGE_MAXIMUM_BYTES - self.current_len);\n            self.current[self.current_len..self.current_len + take].copy_from_slice(&bytes[..take]);\n            self.current_len += take;\n            bytes = &bytes[take..];\n            self.bytes += take;\n        }\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    fn byte(&mut self, byte: u8) -> Result<(), semio_framework_diagnostic::Fault> {\n        self.write(&[byte])\n    }\n\n    fn varint(&mut self, mut value: u64) -> Result<(), semio_framework_diagnostic::Fault> {\n        loop {\n            let mut byte = (value & 0x7f) as u8;\n            value >>= 7;\n            if value != 0 {\n                byte |= 0x80;\n            }\n            self.byte(byte)?;\n            if value == 0 {\n                return Ok(());\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    fn bytes(&mut self, bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<(), semio_framework_diagnostic::Fault> {\n        self.varint(bytes.len() as u64)?;\n        self.write(bytes)\n    }\n\n    fn string(&mut self, value: &str) -> Result<(), semio_framework_diagnostic::Fault> {\n        self.bytes(value.as_bytes())\n    }\n\n    fn envelope(&mut self, value: &crate::os_spr::causal::MutationEnvelope) -> Result<(), semio_framework_diagnostic::Fault> {\n        self.string(&value.mutation_id.0)?;\n        self.string(&value.document_id.0)?;\n        self.string(&value.actor.0)?;\n        self.varint(value.dependencies.len() as u64)?;\n        for dependency in &value.dependencies {\n            self.string(&dependency.0)?;\n        }\n        match &value.observed {\n            Some(observed) => {\n                self.varint(1)?;\n                self.string(&observed.0)?;\n            }\n            None => self.varint(0)?,\n        }\n        self.varint(value.target.len() as u64)?;\n        for segment in &value.target {\n            self.string(segment)?;\n        }\n        self.string(&value.diff.schema.0)?;\n        self.bytes(&value.diff.payload)?;\n        self.string(&value.inverse.schema.0)?;\n        self.bytes(&value.inverse.payload)?;\n        self.varint(value.timestamp.actor)?;\n        self.varint(value.timestamp.physical_ms)?;\n        self.varint(value.timestamp.logical)?;\n        match &value.transaction {\n            Some(transaction) => {\n                self.varint(1)?;\n                self.string(&transaction.id)?;\n                self.string(&transaction.tool)\n            }\n            None => self.varint(0),\n        }\n    }\n\n    fn finish(mut self) -> Result<PagedCommand, semio_framework_diagnostic::Fault> {\n        if self.current_len != 0 {\n            self.flush()?;\n        }\n        PagedCommand::try_from_pages(self.pages).map_err(|(fault, _pages)| fault)\n    }\n}\n\nfn write_media_export_handle_paged(out: &mut CommandPageWriter, handle: &MediaExportHandleWire) -> Result<(), semio_framework_diagnostic::Fault> {\n    out.varint(u64::from(handle.app_instance_id))?;\n    out.string(&handle.parent_document_id)?;\n    out.varint(handle.operation_id)?;\n    out.varint(handle.base_revision)?;\n    out.varint(handle.generation)\n}\n\nfn write_media_export_handle(out: &mut Vec<u8>, handle: &MediaExportHandleWire) {\n    crate::os_spr::write_varint_u64(out, u64::from(handle.app_instance_id));\n    crate::os_spr::write_str(out, &handle.parent_document_id);\n    crate::os_spr::write_varint_u64(out, handle.operation_id);\n    crate::os_spr::write_varint_u64(out, handle.base_revision);\n    crate::os_spr::write_varint_u64(out, handle.generation);\n}\n\nfn read_media_export_handle(bytes: &[u8], pos: &mut usize) -> Result<MediaExportHandleWire, crate::os_spr::ProtocolError> {\n    let app_instance_id = u32::try_from(crate::os_spr::read_varint_u64(bytes, pos)?).map_err(|_| malformed(\"media export app instance\", *pos as u64, \"app instance exceeds u32\"))?;\n    Ok(MediaExportHandleWire {\n        app_instance_id,\n        parent_document_id: crate::os_spr::read_str(bytes, pos)?,\n        operation_id: crate::os_spr::read_varint_u64(bytes, pos)?,\n        base_revision: crate::os_spr::read_varint_u64(bytes, pos)?,\n        generation: crate::os_spr::read_varint_u64(bytes, pos)?,\n    })\n}\n\n/// 📄️ Produces the exact pre-admitted page owner consumed by reactor command batches.\npub async fn encode_app_command(command: &AppCommand) -> Result<PagedCommand, semio_framework_diagnostic::Fault> {\n    if let AppCommand::Presence { own_color, peers, .. } = command {\n        let mut pages = CommandPageSet::try_new(peers.len().max(1))?;\n        for peer in peers.iter() {\n            pages.try_push(FixedCommandPage::try_copy_from(peer)?).map_err(|(fault, _page)| fault)?;\n        }\n        if pages.is_empty() {\n            pages.try_push(FixedCommandPage::try_copy_from(&[])?).map_err(|(fault, _page)| fault)?;\n        }\n        return PagedCommand::try_from_presence_pages(*own_color, pages, peers.len()).map_err(|(fault, _pages)| fault);\n    }\n    let mut out = CommandPageWriter::try_new()?;\n    match command {\n        AppCommand::ConfigCommand { seq, command } => {\n }\n}\n\n#[semio_framework_async_macros::async_test]\nasync fn paged_recursive_archive_crosses_pages_and_decoded_owner_closes_one_field_per_grant() {\n    let mut archive = sample_document_archive();\n
