🔖️Corpus\n\n//#region 📥️CommandIngressPages\n/// 📥️ The cross-language paged command-ingress contract — the same rows the TypeScript host writer's\n/// twin reads (`🎭️actor/📮️shard-client/🧪️tests/📥️command-ingress-pages/🟦️.ts`).\n#[derive(serde::Deserialize)]\nstruct CommandIngressPagesFixture {\n    #[serde(rename = \"pageBytes\")]\n    page_bytes: usize,\n    #[serde(rename = \"commandMaximumBytes\")]\n    command_maximum_bytes: usize,\n    #[serde(rename = \"maximumPages\")]\n    maximum_pages: usize,\n    rows: Vec<CommandIngressPagesRow>,\n    refusals: Vec<CommandIngressPagesRefusal>,\n}\n\n#[derive(serde::Deserialize)]\nstruct CommandIngressPagesRow {\n    name: String,\n    bytes: usize,\n    pages: usize,\n}\n\n#[derive(serde::Deserialize)]\nstruct CommandIngressPagesRefusal {\n    name: String,\n    bytes: usize,\n}\n\nfn command_ingress_pages_fixture() -> CommandIngressPagesFixture {\n    serde_json::from_str(include_str!(\"../../../../../../../🔨️modules/🎭️actor/🧫️fixtures/📥️command-ingress-pages/🔣️.json\")).expect(\"📥️command-ingress-pages fixture parses\")\n}\n\n/// 🧱️ A deterministic command body — every byte a function of its offset, so a reassembly that\n/// duplicates, drops or reorders one page cannot compare equal.\nfn command_ingress_body(bytes: usize) -> Vec<u8> {\n    (0..bytes).map(|offset| (offset % 251 + 1) as u8).collect()\n}\n\n/// ⚖️ LAW: the transport's page and byte authorities are DERIVED from the guest linear-memory budget,\n/// and the spine that assembles a ceiling-sized command stays inside one guest growth unit.\n///\n/// 🧨️ This is the law the 64-page constant failed on both sides at once: it refused a 272 089-byte\n/// contributions pack outright, and the reservation it bought was 262 272 contiguous bytes — four\n/// times what a fragmented guest can be relied on to serve (ticket 26/09/09/PROCEDURAL-3D-END-TO-END).\n#[test]\nfn the_command_ingress_authorities_are_derived_from_the_guest_memory_budget() {\n    let fixture = command_ingress_pages_fixture();\n    assert_eq!(COMMAND_PAGE_MAXIMUM_BYTES, fixture.page_bytes);\n    assert_eq!(COMMAND_MAXIMUM_BYTES, fixture.command_maximum_bytes);\n    assert_eq!(COMMAND_MAXIMUM_PAGES, fixture.maximum_pages);\n    assert_eq!(COMMAND_MAXIMUM_BYTES, semio_framework_trace::GUEST_HOST_ANSWER_CEILING_BYTES, \"a command is an assembled host answer and is bound by that budget, not by one of its own\");\n    assert_eq!(COMMAND_MAXIMUM_PAGES, COMMAND_MAXIMUM_BYTES / COMMAND_PAGE_MAXIMUM_BYTES);\n    assert!(\n        CommandPageSet::reservation_bytes(COMMAND_MAXIMUM_PAGES) <= semio_framework_trace::GUEST_CONTIGUOUS_REQUEST_CEILING_BYTES,\n        \"a ceiling-sized page authority reserves {} B — over the {} B a routine per-command guest path may ask a fixed linear memory for\",\n        CommandPageSet::reservation_bytes(COMMAND_MAXIMUM_PAGES),\n        semio_framework_trace::GUEST_CONTIGUOUS_REQUEST_CEILING_BYTES\n    );\n    eprintln!(\n        \"command ingress authorities: pages={COMMAND_MAXIMUM_PAGES} bytes={COMMAND_MAXIMUM_BYTES} slot={} B spine={} B ceiling={} B\",\n        size_of::<FixedCommandPage>(),\n        CommandPageSet::reservation_bytes(COMMAND_MAXIMUM_PAGES),\n        semio_framework_trace::GUEST_CONTIGUOUS_REQUEST_CEILING_BYTES\n    );\n    assert!(\n        size_of::<FixedCommandPage>() < COMMAND_PAGE_MAXIMUM_BYTES,\n        \"a page slot must be a handle to its block, never the block — an inline page is what forced a fixed page ceiling\"\n    );\n}\n\n/// ⚖️ LAW: every fixture row splits into exactly the pages it declares and reassembles to the EXACT\n/// bytes it was cut from, with no page of a multi-page command left short of the page extent.\n#[test]\nfn every_command_ingress_row_reassembles_to_the_exact_bytes_it_was_cut_from() {\n    let fixture = command_ingress_pages_fixture();\n    for row in &fixture.rows {\n        let body = command_ingress_body(row.bytes);\n        let cut: Vec<&[u8]> = body.chunks(COMMAND_PAGE_MAXIMUM_BYTES).collect();\n        assert_eq!(cut.len(), row.pages, \"row {} cuts into {} pages, not the {} it declares\", row.name, cut.len(), row.pages);\n        let mut pages = CommandPageSet::try_new(row.pages).unwrap_or_else(|fault| panic!(\"row {} declares a page authority: {fault:?}\", row.name));\n        assert!(\n            CommandPageSet::reservation_bytes(row.pages) <= semio_framework_trace::GUEST_CONTIGUOUS_REQUEST_CEILING_BYTES,\n            \"row {} reserves {} B for its spine\",\n            row.name,\n            CommandPageSet::reservation_bytes(row.pages)\n        );\n        for (index, chunk) in cut.iter().enumerate() {\n            assert!(index + 1 == cut.len() || chunk.len() == COMMAND_PAGE_MAXIMUM_BYTES, \"row {} left a nonterminal page short\", row.name);\n            pages.try_push(FixedCommandPage::try_copy_from(chunk).expect(\"a cut page\")).unwrap_or_else(|(fault, _)| panic!(\"row {} admits page {index}: {fault:?}\", row.name));\n        }\n        let command = PagedCommand::try_from_pages(pages).unwrap_or_else(|(fault, _)| panic!(\"row {} assembles: {fault:?}\", row.name));\n        assert_eq!(command.page_len(), row.pages);\n        assert_eq!(command.byte_len(), row.bytes);\n        assert_eq!(command.kind(), body[0]);\n        let mut reader = PagedCommandReader::new(command);\n        let mut read = Vec::with_capacity(row.bytes);\n        for offset in 0..row.bytes {\n            read.push(reader.read_byte().unwrap_or_else(|fault| panic!(\"row {} ends inside byte {offset}: {fault:?}\", row.name)));\n        }\n        assert_eq!(read, body, \"row {} did not reassemble to its own bytes\", row.name);\n        assert!(reader.terminal_is_empty(), \"row {} left pages behind after its last byte\", row.name);\n        assert_eq!(reader.read_byte().expect_err(\"a fully read command has no further byte\").code.0, \"plugin.command-decode-truncated\");\n    }\n}\n\n/// ⚖️ LAW: an over-declaration and an over-push are refused with a `Fault` the host can display, and\n/// the page a saturated authority refuses is handed BACK rather than dropped.\n#[test]\nfn every_command_ingress_refusal_answers_a_fault_and_keeps_its_page() {\n    let fixture = command_ingress_pages_fixture();\n    for refusal in &fixture.refusals {\n        let declared = refusal.bytes.div_ceil(COMMAND_PAGE_MAXIMUM_BYTES);\n        assert_eq!(\n            CommandPageSet::try_new(declared).expect_err(&format!(\"refusal {} has no page authority\", refusal.name)).code.0,\n            \"plugin.command-page-count\",\n            \"refusal {} must be refused by the declaration, before one page is copied\",\n            refusal.name\n        );\n    }\n    let mut pages = CommandPageSet::try_new(2).expect(\"a two-page authority\");\n    for _ in 0..2 {\n        pages.try_push(FixedCommandPage::try_copy_from(&[7; COMMAND_PAGE_MAXIMUM_BYTES]).expect(\"a full page\")).expect(\"the declared pages are admitted\");\n    }\n    let (fault, returned) = pages.try_push(FixedCommandPage::try_copy_from(b\"third\").expect(\"a page\")).expect_err(\"a third page is over the declared authority\");\n    assert_eq!(fault.code.0, \"plugin.command-page-count\");\n    assert_eq!(returned.as_slice(), b\"third\", \"a refused page is handed back, never dropped\");\n}\n\n#[semio_framework_async_macros::async_test]\nasync fn 6, group_id: \"g\".to_string() }).await;\n}\n//#endregion 🔖️Transaction\n\n//#region 🔖️PagedRouteAdmission\n/// 🧵️ Drives the GUEST's own retained ingress — `PagedAppCommandDecodeCursor`, the decoder compiled\n/// into every component — rather than the flat host-side `decode_app_command` every round-trip law\n/// above uses. A route the flat decoder reads and the paged cursor refuses is exactly the gap this\n/// admission law exists to catch (`plugin.command-route-state-machine-required`).\nasync fn assert_paged_route_admits(command: &AppCommand) {\n    let encoded = encode_app_command(command).await.expect(\"route command encodes\");\n    let mut cursor = PagedAppCommandDecodeCursor::new(encoded);\n    for _ in 0..1024 {\n        match cursor.step().expect(\"paged route decode step\") {\n            Some(decoded) => {\n                assert_eq!(&decoded, command, \"paged ingress decodes the route byte for byte\");\n                return;\n            }\n            None => continue,\n        }\n    }\n    panic!(\"paged ingress never completed a route command within its step ceiling\");\n}\n\n#[semio_framework_async_macros::async_test]\nasync fn paged_ingress_admits_every_media_route() {\n    assert_paged_route_admits(&AppCommand::MediaIn { seq: 14, port: \"camera\".to_string(), descriptor: vec![1], data: vec![2, 3] }).await;\n    assert_paged_route_admits(&AppCommand::MediaOut { seq: 15, port: \"vector:out\".to_string(), request: Vec::new() }).await;\n    assert_paged_route_admits(&AppCommand::MediaFingerprint { seq: 16, port: \"camera\".to_string() }).await;\n}\n\n#[semio_framework_async_macros::async_test]\nasync fn paged_ingress_admits_every_transaction_route() {\n    assert_paged_route_admits(&AppCommand::TransactionPrepare { seq: 1, txn_id: \"t\".to_string(), mutation_id: \"m\".to_string(), payload: vec![9], prepared_ops: Vec::new(), label: String::new(), origin: Vec::new(), prepared_child_ops: Vec::new() }).await;\n    assert_paged_route_admits(&AppCommand::TransactionPrepare { seq: 2, txn_id: \"t\".to_string(), mutation_id: String::new(), payload: Vec::new(), prepared_ops: vec![vec![1], vec![2, 2]], label: \"l\".to_string(), origin: vec![9], prepared_child_ops: Vec::new() }).await;\n    assert_paged_route_admits(&AppCommand::TransactionPrepare { seq: 7, txn_id: \"t\".to_string(), mutation_id: String::new(), payload: Vec::new(), prepared_ops: vec![vec![1]], label: \"l\".to_string(), origin: vec![9], prepared_child_ops: vec![5, 6] }).await;\n    assert_paged_route_admits(&AppCommand::TransactionCommit { seq: 3, txn_id: \"t\".to_string() }).await;\n    assert_paged_route_admits(&AppCommand::TransactionRollback { seq: 4, txn_id: \"t\".to_string() }).await;\n    assert_paged_route_admits(&AppCommand::TransactionUndo { seq: 5, group_id: \"g\".to_string() }).await;\n    assert_paged_route_admits(&AppCommand::TransactionRedo { seq: 6, group_id: \"g\".to_string() }).await;\n}\n\n/// 🚪️ The routes that still require their own reserved ingress authority stay refused BY NAME, so\n/// \"admitted\" never becomes \"everything is admitted\": `Presence` (tag 28) owns\n/// `PresenceCommandCursor`'s one-exact-page-per-peer admission, and every tag no route declares is\n/// still a typed refusal rather than a silent drop.\n#[semio_framework_async_macros::async_test]\nasync fn paged_ingress_still_refuses_an_undeclared_route_by_name() {\n    let mut pages = CommandPageSet::try_new(1).expect(\"one fixed page\");\n    pages.try_push(FixedCommandPage::try_copy_from(&[22, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0]).expect(\"undeclared route page\")).unwrap_or_else(|(fault, _page)| panic!(\"admit undeclared route page: {fault:?}\"));\n    let command = PagedCommand::try_from_pages(pages).unwrap_or_else(|(fault, _pages)| panic!(\"admit undeclared route command: {fault:?}\"));\n    let mut cursor = PagedAppCommandDecodeCursor::new(command);\n    let fault = cursor.step().expect_err(\"an undeclared route is refused\");\n    assert_eq!(fault.code.0, \"plugin.command-route-state-machine-required\");\n}\n\n/// 🧹️ A refused route releases what it has already accumulated ONE field at a time under the\n/// caller's own grant — the same bounded-retirement contract `LoadDocumentArchive` keeps — so a\n/// faulted media command can never free a whole payload in one step.\n#[semio_framework_async_macros::async_test]\nasync fn a_cancelled_media_route_releases_one_field_at_a_time() {\n    let command = AppCommand::MediaIn { seq: 7, port: \"camera\".to_string(), descriptor: vec![1; 64], data: vec![2; 64] };\n    let encoded = encode_app_command(&command).await.expect(\"media route encodes\");\n    let mut cursor = PagedAppCommandDecodeCursor::new(encoded);\n    cursor.step().expect(\"port field\");\n    cursor.step().expect(\"descriptor field\");\n    let mut releases = 0;\n    for _ in 0..1024 {\n        let (empty, released) = cursor.close_step(COMMAND_PAGE_MAXIMUM_BYTES);\n        if released != 0 {\n            releases += 1;\n        }\n        if empty {\n            break;\n        }\n    }\n    assert!(releases >= 2, \"a cancelled media route released {releases} field(s), not one per step\");\n    assert!(cursor.terminal_is_empty(), \"a cancelled media route retires empty\");\n}\n//#endregion 🔖️PagedRouteAdmission\n\n//#region 🗃️DocumentArchiveLoadHost\n/// 🗃️ LAW (`🧫️fixtures/🧫️document-archive-load-host/🔣️.json`): the host half of the stepped whole-document load sends exactly the\n/// scripted commands — one admission, It hands every polled status back for the host's progress, and it ends in\n/// the scripted outcome. Every scripted status keeps `completed <= total`, monotonic within its case.\n#[test]\nfn the_document_archive_load_host_sends_the_scripted_commands_and_ends_in_the_scripted_outcome() {\n    let law: serde_json::Value = serde_json::from_str(include_str!(\"../../🧫️fixtures/🧫️document-archive-load-host/🔣️.json\")).unwrap();\n    let first = law[\"firstSequence\"].as_u64().unwrap();\n    let state = |name: &str| match name {\n        \"pending\" => DocumentArchiveLoadState::Pending,\n        \"running\" => DocumentArchiveLoadState::Running,\n        \"ready\" => DocumentArchiveLoadState::Ready,\n        \"cancelled\" => DocumentArchiveLoadState::Cancelled,\n        \"fault\" => DocumentArchiveLoadState::Fault,\n        other => panic!(\"unknown scripted state {other}\"),\n    };\n    let fault = |answer: &serde_json::Value| answer[\"fault\"].as_str().unwrap_or_default().as_bytes().to_vec();\n    let text = |bytes: Vec<u8>| String::from_utf8(bytes).expect(\"scripted faults are UTF-8\");\n    for case in law[\"cases\"].as_array().unwrap() {\n        let name = case[\"name\"].as_str().unwrap();\n        let exchanges = case[\"exchanges\"].as_array().unwrap();\n        let cancel_before = case[\"cancel\"][\"beforeStep\"].as_u64();\n        let cancel_in_flight = case[\"cancel\"][\"whileStepInFlight\"].as_u64();\n        let mut host = DocumentArchiveLoadHost::new(DocumentArchivePack { parent_pack: vec![7], parent_spr: vec![9], members: Vec::new() });\n        let mut seq = first;\n        let mut refusal = None;\n        let mut statuses: Vec<(u64, u64)> = Vec::new();\n        for (index, exchange) in exchanges.iter().enumerate() {\n            if cancel_before == Some(index as u64) {\n                host.request_cancel();\n            }\n            let command = match host.step(|| seq) {\n                DocumentArchiveLoadStep::Send { seq: stamped, command } => {\n                    assert_eq!(stamped, seq, \"{name}: step {index} is stamped with the minted sequence\");\n                    command\n                }\n                finished => panic!(\"{name}: step {index} finished early with {finished:?}\"),\n            };\n            let (sends, operation) = match &command {\n                AppCommand::LoadDocumentArchive { seq: sent, archive } => {\n                    assert_eq!((*sent, archive.parent_pack.as_slice(), merge-policy/conflict tests, written standalone (not depending on 1-D's\n// `📡️spr/🧫️fixtures` `🔖️Laws` helpers landing first).\n\n/// 🛰️ Builds a `MutationEnvelope` with an explicit HLC (bypassing target: Vec::new(),\n        diff: crate::os_spr::ArtifactDiff { schema: SchemaId(\"demo/v1\".to_string()), payload: operation.encode_op().expect(\"encode demo mutation\") },\n        inverse: crate::os_spr::InverseMutation { schema: SchemaId(\"demo/v1\".to_string()), payload: Vec::new() },\n        timestamp: hlc,\n        transaction: None, verb: None, line: None,\n    }\n}\n\nasync fn fresh_demo_store() -> ArtifactStore<DemoSnapshot, DemoMutation> {\n    ArtifactStore::new(create_document_envelope::<DemoSnapshot, DemoMutation>(\"demo/v1\", \"demo\", DemoSnapshot { n: Some(0) }, None)).await\n}\n\nasync fn owned_test_envelope<P, Mutation>(store: &ArtifactStore<P, Mutation>) -> ArtifactEnvelope<P, Mutation>\nwhere\n    P: Clone + ArtifactDsl + ArtifactPack + PartialEq + std::fmt::Debug + ToValue + FromValue + Send + 'static,\n    Mutation: Clone + OpText + OpBinary + super::Mutation<P> + PartialEq + ToValue + FromValue + Send + 'static,\n{\n    let files = print_document_pack(store.envelope()).await.expect(\"print owned test envelope\");\n    parse_document_pack::<P, Mutation>(&files.pack, &files.spr).await.expect(\"parse owned test envelope\").envelope\n}\n\n/// 🛰️ A `DeleteN` at an earlier HLC and a `SetN` at a later HLC — replayed in HLC order, the\n/// `SetN` lands on an already-deleted target and raises `mutation.target-missing` (Error).\nasync fn modify_vs_delete_envelopes() -> (crate::os_spr::MutationEnvelope, crate::os_spr::MutationEnvelope) {\n    let delete = mutation_envelope_at(\"deleter\", \"op-delete\", DemoMutation::DeleteN(DeleteN {}), HybridLogicalTimestamp::new(1, 100), Vec::new());\n    let modify = mutation_envelope_at(\"modifier\", \"op-modify\", DemoMutation::SetN(SetN { n: 42 }), HybridLogicalTimestamp::new(2, 200), Vec::new());\n    (delete, modify)\n}\n\n#[semio_framework_async_macros::async_test]\nasync fn modify_vs_delete_quarantines_under_normal_and_vigilant() {\n    for policy in [crate::os_spr::MergePolicy::Normal, crate::os_spr::MergePolicy::Vigilant] {\n        let mut store = fresh_demo_store().await;\n        store.set_merge_policy(policy);\n        let (delete, modify) = modify_vs_delete_envelopes().await;\n        store.ingest_remote(delete).await.expect(\"the delete alone raises no message and always applies\");\n        let pre_merge = store.snapshot().expect(\"pre-merge snapshot\");\n        let pre_merge_ids = store.applied_edit_ids().to_vec();\n        let report = store.ingest_remote(modify).await.expect(\"a policy rejection is a MergeReport, not an Err\");\n        assert!(!report.accepted, \"{policy:?} must reject an Error-level modify-vs-delete conflict\");\n        assert_eq!(report.worst, Some(semio_framework_diagnostic::Severity::Error));\n        assert_eq!(store.snapshot().expect(\"unchanged snapshot\"), pre_merge, \"{policy:?}: state stays pre-merge on reject\");\n        assert_eq!(store.applied_edit_ids(), pre_merge_ids.as_slice(), \"{policy:?}: applied_edit_ids stays pre-merge on reject\");\n        let conflict_id = report.conflict.clone().expect(\"a reject must raise a conflict\");\n        let conflict = store.conflicts().iter().find(|conflict| conflict.id == conflict_id).expect(\"conflict recorded on the store\");\n        assert_eq!(conflict.status, crate::os_spr::ConflictStatus::Open);\n        assert!(matches!(conflict.kind, crate::os_spr::ConflictKind::Quarantined { .. }), \"{policy:?}: a rejected batch quarantines, it never degrades\");\n        assert!(store.open_conflicts().any(|conflict| conflict.id == conflict_id));\n    }\n}\n\n#[semio_framework_async_macros::async_test]\nasync fn modify_vs_delete_applies_under_laissez_faire_with_a_degraded_conflict() {\n    let mut store = fresh_demo_store().await;\n    store.set_merge_policy(crate::os_spr::MergePolicy::LaissezFaire);\n    let store.ingest_remote(modify).await.expect(\"LaissezFaire only rejects Fatal\");\n    assert!(report.accepted);\n    assert_eq!(report.worst, Some(semio_framework_diagnostic::Severity::Error));\n    assert_eq!(store.snapshot().expect(\"snapshot\").n, None, \"the modify's part is absent — LAW 2 (an Error message ⇒ no change to its target)\");\n    assert!(report.replayed.iter().any(|edit_messages| must raise a Degraded conflict\");\n    let conflict = store.conflicts().iter().find(|conflict| conflict.id == conflict_id).expect(\"conflict recorded\");\n    assert!(matches!(conflict.kind, crate::os_spr::ConflictKind::Degraded { .. }));\n    assert_eq!(conflict.status, crate::os_spr::ConflictStatus::Open);\n}\n\n#[semio_framework_async_macros::async_test]\nasync fn 🔖️HistoryLaneTests\n#[semio_framework_async_macros::async_test]\nasync fn history_lane_defaults_to_document() {\n    assert_eq!(HistoryLane::default(), HistoryLane::Document);\n}\n\n/// 🛤️ The first (nearest Document entry in the redo stack),\n/// then doc2, never touching either interaction edit's own applied/redo membership; each lands\n/// back at its own HLC position in the applied order.\n#[semio_framework_async_macros::async_test]\nasync fn history_lane_default_undo_and_redo_skip_interaction_entries() {\n    let envelope = create_document_envelope(\"demo/v1\", \"demo\", doc2\");\n    let doc2_id = store.applied_edit_ids()[2].clone();\n    store.dispatch(ArtifactCommand::ApplyInLane { mutations: vec![DemoMutation::SetN(SetN { n: 200 })], description: None, lane: assert_eq!(store.envelope().lanes.get(&interaction1_id), Some(&HistoryLane::Interaction));\n    assert_eq!(store.envelope().lanes.get(&interaction2_id), Some(&HistoryLane::Interaction));\n assert_eq!(store.redo_edit_ids(), std::slice::from_ref(&doc2_id));\n    store.dispatch(ArtifactCommand::Redo).await.expect(\"redo doc2\");\n    assert_eq!(store.applied_edit_ids(), &[doc1_id.clone(), interaction1_id.clone(), doc2_id.clone(), interaction2_id.clone()]);\n    assert!(store.redo_edit_ids().is_empty());\n}\n\n/// 🛤️ The completing half of the mechanism: `UndoInLane`/`RedoInLane` walk a resolution.\n\n//#region 🔖️OpCodec\n/// 🎞️ Handcrafted OpText (P6).\nimpl OpText for TimestampedMutation {\n    fn parse_op(line: &str) -> Result<Self, TextError> {\n        let variants = <Self as crate::os_dsl::DslVariants>::variants();\n        for (keyword, spec_fn) in &variants {\n            let probe = format!(\"{} \", keyword);\n            if line == keyword.as_str() || line.starts_with(&probe) {\n                let record = crate::os_dsl::parse(line, &(spec_fn.ordinary)(), &crate::os_dsl::ParseOptions { limits: semio_framework_diagnostic::Limits::default(), mode: crate::os_dsl::SourceMode::Inline })?;\n                return <Self as crate::os_dsl::DslVariants>::from_named_record(keyword, &record);\n            }\n        }\n        Err(crate::os_dsl::__rt::field_error(format!(\"unknown operation line '{line}'\")))\n    }\n    fn print_op(&self) -> String {\n        let (keyword, record) = <Self as crate::os_dsl::DslVariants>::to_named_record(self);\n        let variants = <Self as crate::os_dsl::DslVariants>::variants();\n        let spec_fn = variants.iter().find(|(k, _)| k == &keyword).map(|(_, s)| *s).expect(\"variant spec must exist for its own keyword\");\n        crate::os_dsl::print(&record, &(spec_fn.ordinary)(), crate::os_dsl::JoinMode::Inline)\n    }\n}\n\n/// 🎯️ Handcrafted OpBinary (P6).\nimpl OpBinary for TimestampedMutation {\n    fn encode_op(&self) -> Result<Vec<u8>, crate::os_spr::ProtocolError> {\n        const OP_BINARY_FORMAT: u8 = 1;\n        let (keyword, record) = <Self as crate::os_dsl::DslVariants>::to_named_record(self);\n        let variants = <Self as crate::os_dsl::DslVariants>::variants();\n        let ordinal = variants.iter().position(|(k, _)| *k == keyword).ok_or(crate::os_spr::ProtocolError::Malformed { what: \"op variant\", offset: 0, detail: format!(\"keyword {keyword:?} is not a declared variant\") })?;\n        let spec = (variants[ordinal].1.ordinary)();\n        let body = crate::os_pack::encode_record_body(&spec, &record, &PackEncodeOptions::default()).map_err(crate::os_spr::ProtocolError::from)?;\n        let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(body.len() + 3);\n        out.push(OP_BINARY_FORMAT);\n        crate::os_pack::write_varint_u64(&mut out, ordinal as u64);\n        out.extend_from_slice(&body);\n        Ok(out)\n    }\n    fn decode_op(bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<Self, crate::os_spr::ProtocolError> {\n        const OP_BINARY_FORMAT: u8 = 1;\n        let mut reader = crate::os_pack::ByteReader::new(bytes);\n        let format = reader.read_u8()?;\n        if format != OP_BINARY_FORMAT {\n            return Err(crate::os_spr::ProtocolError::Malformed { what: \"op format\", offset: 0, detail: format!(\"unsupported op format {format}\") });\n        }\n        let ordinal = reader.read_varint_u64()?;\n        let variants = <Self as crate::os_dsl::DslVariants>::variants();\n        let (keyword, spec_fn) = variants.get(ordinal as usize).ok_or(crate::os_spr::ProtocolError::Malformed { what: \"op variant\", offset: 1, detail: format!(\"ordinal {ordinal} out of range for {} declared variants\", variants.len()) })?;\n        let spec = (spec_fn.ordinary)();\n        let body = &bytes[reader.position()..];\n        let (record, _report) = crate::os_pack::decode_record_body(body, &spec, &PackDecodeOptions::default()).map_err(crate::os_spr::ProtocolError::from)?;\n        let record_offset = reader.position() as u64;\n        <Self as crate::os_dsl::DslVariants>::from_named_record(keyword, &record).map_err(|error| crate::os_spr::ProtocolError::Malformed { what: \"op record\", offset: record_offset, detail: error.to_string() })\n    }\n}\n//#endregion 🔖️OpCodec\n\n/// 🪄️ Downcasts a registered `dyn SpaceMember` back to its concrete demo store.\nasync fn demo_member<'a, Mutation: self::Mutation<DemoSnapshot> + 'static, M:     let spec_fn = variants.iter().find(|(k, _)| k == &keyword).map(|(_, s)| *s).expect(\"variant spec must exist for its own keyword\");\n        crate::os_dsl::print(&record, &(spec_fn.ordinary)(),   const OP_BINARY_FORMAT: u8 = 1;\n        let (keyword, record) = <Self as crate::os_dsl::DslVariants>::to_named_record(self);\n        let variants = <Self as crate::os_dsl::DslVariants>::variants();\n        let ordinal = variants.iter().position(|(k, _)| *k == keyword).ok_or(crate::os_spr::ProtocolError::Malformed { what: \"op variant\", offset: 0, detail: format!(\"keyword {keyword:?} is not a declared variant\") })?;\n        let spec = (variants[ordinal].1.ordinary)();\n        let body = crate::os_pack::encode_record_body(&spec, &record, &PackEncodeOptions::default()).map_err(crate::os_spr::ProtocolError::from)?;\n        let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(body.len() + 3);\n        out.push(OP_BINARY_FORMAT);\n        crate::os_pack::write_varint_u64(&mut out, ordinal as u64);\n        out.extend_from_slice(&body);\n        Ok(out)\n    }\n    fn decode_op(bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<Self, crate::os_spr::ProtocolError> {\n        const OP_BINARY_FORMAT: u8 = 1;\n        let mut reader = crate::os_pack::ByteReader::new(bytes);\n        let format = reader.read_u8()?;\n        if format != OP_BINARY_FORMAT {\n            return Err(crate::os_spr::ProtocolError::Malformed { what: \"op format\", offset: 0, detail: format!(\"unsupported op format {format}\") });\n        }\n        let ordinal = reader.read_varint_u64()?;\n        let variants = <Self as crate::os_dsl::DslVariants>::variants();\n        let (keyword, spec_fn) = variants.get(ordinal as usize).ok_or(crate::os_spr::ProtocolError::Malformed { what: \"op variant\", offset: 1, detail: format!(\"ordinal {ordinal} out of range for {} declared variants\", variants.len()) })?;\n        let spec = (spec_fn.ordinary)();\n        let body = &bytes[reader.position()..];\n        let (record, _report) = crate::os_pack::decode_record_body(body, &spec, &PackDecodeOptions::default()).map_err(crate::os_spr::ProtocolError::from)?;\n        let record_offset = reader.position() as u64;\n        <Self as crate::os_dsl::DslVariants>::from_named_record(keyword, &record).map_err(|error| crate::os_spr::ProtocolError::Malformed { what: \"op record\", offset: record_offset, detail: error.to_string() })\n    }\n}\n\nimpl MemberStoreOwner<SeverityMutation> for DemoSnapshot {\n    type SnapshotOpen = UnsupportedMemberSnapshotOpen<Self>;\n\n    fn member_store_owners() -> DocumentStoreOwners<Self, }).await.expect(\"apply e2\");\n    let post_e2 = store.snapshot().expect(\"post-e2 snapshot\");\n    store.dispatch(ArtifactCommand::Undo).await.expect(\"undo e2\");\n    assert_eq!(store.snapshot().expect(\"live snapshot\"), post_e1, \"precondition: live store is back at post-e1\");\n    test_support::assert_live_equals_replay(&store).await;\n\n    let pack_files = assert_eq!(parsed.snapshot, post_e1, \"loaded snapshot must equal post-e1, proving undo position survived the save\");\n    let mut reloaded = ArtifactStore::new(parsed.envelope).await;\n    assert_eq!(reloaded.snapshot().expect(\"reloaded snapshot\"), post_e1, \"ArtifactStore::new must seed live state from the persisted cursor\");\n    assert_eq!(reloaded.applied_edit_ids(), 🔖️BackbonePorts\n#[semio_framework_async_macros::async_test]\nasync fn memory_backbone_port_round_trips_and_reports_a_missing_file() {\n    let port = MemoryBackbonePort::new().await;\n    let error = assert!(defaulted.read(\"local://a\").await.is_err(), \"Default constructs its own independent fallback store\");\n}\n\n//#endregion 🔖️BackbonePorts\n\n//#region 🔖️PackValueFixtures\nasync fn pack_value_fixture_corpus() -> Vec<(&'static str, DslValue)> {\n    vec![\n        (\"null\", DslValue::Null),\n        (\"bool_true\", DslValue::Bool(true)),\n        (\"bool_false\", DslValue::Bool(false)),\n        (\"int_zero\", DslValue::uint(0)),\n        (\"int_negative_one\", DslValue::int(-1)),\n        (\"float_pi\", DslValue::float(3.14)),\n        (\"float_whole_number\", DslValue::float(2.0)),\n        (\"string_empty\", DslValue::String(String::new())),\n        (\"string_escapes\", DslValue::String(\"hello\\nworld with \\\"quotes\\\"\".into())),\n        (\"array_empty\", DslValue::Array(vec![])),\n        (\"array_ints\", DslValue::Array(vec![DslValue::uint(1), DslValue::uint(2), DslValue::uint(3)])),\n        (\"object_empty\", DslValue::Object(vec![])),\n        (\"object_mixed\", DslValue::object([(\"a\".into(), DslValue::uint(1)), (\"b\".into(), DslValue::Array(vec![DslValue::Bool(true), DslValue::Null]))])),\n        (\n            \"nested_deep\",\n            DslValue::object([(\"a\".into(), DslValue::object([(\"b\".into(), DslValue::object([(\"c\".into(), DslValue::Array(vec![DslValue::uint(1), DslValue::uint(2), DslValue::object([(\"d\".into(), DslValue::String(\"leaf\".into()))])]))]))]))]),\n        ),\n    ]\n}\n\n/// 🎯️ Variant-exact `DslValue` equality. `Number`'s own `PartialEq` calls a fitting\n/// `UInt`/`Int` pair equal, so it cannot witness that the wire preserved the WRITER's variant —\n/// which is exactly what `TAG_UINT` versus `TAG_INT` decides, and what the canonical bytes and\n/// every hash over them depend on. `Float` compares by bits so `-0.0` and `NaN` are exact too.\n// 🚫️async: E1 pure recursive comparison consumed inside sync `.all()`/`.is_some_and()` closures\n// that cannot themselves be async — see R9/R10 residue shape 1\nfn dsl_value_variant_exact_eq(a: &DslValue, b: &DslValue) -> bool {\n    match (a, b) {\n        (DslValue::Number(crate::os_dsl::Number::UInt(x)), DslValue::Number(crate::os_dsl::Number::UInt(y))) => x == y,\n        (DslValue::Number(crate::os_dsl::Number::Int(x)), DslValue::Number(crate::os_dsl::Number::Int(y))) => x == y,\n        (DslValue::Number(crate::os_dsl::Number::Float(x)), DslValue::Number(crate::os_dsl::Number::Float(y))) => x.to_bits() == y.to_bits(),\n        (DslValue::Number(_), DslValue::Number(_)) => false,\n        (DslValue::Array(x), DslValue::Array(y)) => x.len() == y.len() && x.iter().zip(y).all(|(a, b)| dsl_value_variant_exact_eq(a, b)),\n        (DslValue::Object(x), DslValue::Object(y)) => x.len() == y.len() && x.iter().all(|(k, v)| y.iter().find(|(ok, _)| ok == k).is_some_and(|(_, ov)| dsl_value_variant_exact_eq(v, ov))),\n        _ => a == b,\n    }\n}\n\n/// 🔣️ Reads one `semio.pack.dynamic-integer/v1` value node — integers arrive as exact\n/// decimal STRINGS and floats as little-endian hex, so no fixture number ever passes through a\n/// JSON `f64` on its way into the corpus.\n// 🚫️async: E1 pure recursive fixture reader consumed inside sync iterator closures — see R9\nfn dynamic_integer_fixture_value(node: &serde_json::Value) -> DslValue {\n    if let Some(text) = node.get(\"uint\").and_then(|v| v.as_str()) {\n        return DslValue::uint(text.parse::<u64>().expect(\"corpus uint is an exact u64\"));\n    }\n    if let Some(text) = node.get(\"int\").and_then(|v| v.as_str()) {\n        return DslValue::int(text.parse::<i64>().expect(\"corpus int is an exact i64\"));\n    }\n    if let Some(text) = node.get(\"f64LeHex\").and_then(|v| v.as_str()) {\n        let mut bits = [0u8; 8];\n        for (index, byte) in bits.iter_mut().enumerate() {\n            *byte = u8::from_str_radix(&text[index * 2..index * 2 + 2], 16).expect(\"corpus f64LeHex byte\");\n        }\n        return DslValue::Number(crate::os_dsl::Number::Float(f64::from_le_bytes(bits)));\n    }\n    if let Some(items) = node.get(\"list\").and_then(|v| v.as_array()) {\n        return DslValue::Array(items.iter().map(dynamic_integer_fixture_value).collect());\n    }\n    if let Some(entries) = node.get(\"map\").and_then(|v| v.as_array()) {\n        return DslValue::Object(entries.iter().map(|entry| (entry[0].as_str().expect(\"corpus map key\").to_string(), dynamic_integer_fixture_value(&entry[1]))).collect());\n    }\n    panic!(\"unsupported corpus value node {node}\");\n}\n\n// 🚫️async: E1 pure hex reader consumed inside sync iterator closures — see R9\nfn dynamic_integer_fixture_bytes(hex: &str) -> Vec<u8> {\n    (0..hex.len() / 2).map(|index| u8::from_str_radix(&hex[index * 2..index * 2 + 2], 16).expect(\"corpus wireHex byte\")).collect()\n}\n\n/// 🧾️ Hex-dumps `pack_rt::encode_pack_value` over a representative `DslValue`\n/// corpus — ground truth for `HEADLESS-APP-ENGINE-BINARY-COMMAND-PROTOCOL-FOUNDATIONS`'s TS\n/// `PackValueCodec` mirror (`framework/product/os/ts/index.ts`). Run with `--nocapture` to\n/// capture the printed `name -> hex` lines; also asserts `decode_pack_value(encode_pack_value(v))\n/// == v` for every entry so the corpus is never accidentally out of date with the real codec.\n#[semio_framework_async_macros::async_test]\nasync fn pack_value_fixture_corpus_hex_dump() {\n    for (name, value) in pack_value_fixture_corpus().await {\n        let bytes = pack_rt::encode_pack_value(&value);\n        let hex: String = bytes.iter().map(|b| format!(\"{b:02x}\")).collect();\n        println!(\"[pack_value_fixture] {name} ({} bytes) -> {hex}\", bytes.len());\n        let decoded = pack_rt::decode_pack_value(&bytes).expect(\"decode_pack_value\");\n        assert!(dsl_value_variant_exact_eq(&decoded, &value), \"round-trip mismatch for fixture {name}: {decoded:?} != {value:?}\");\n    }\n}\n\n#[semio_framework_async_macros::async_test]\nasync fn interaction_state_pack_matches_first_party_value_and_json_oracle() {\n    let oracle: serde_json::Value = serde_json::from_str(include_str!(\"../../🎒️interaction-state-pack.json\")).unwrap();\n    let value = DslValue::from(&oracle);\n    let state = <protocol::InteractionState as FromValue>::from_value(value.clone()).unwrap();\n    let encoded = <protocol::InteractionState as ArtifactPack>::encode_pack(&state);\n    assert_eq!(encoded, <DslValue as ArtifactPack>::encode_pack(&value));\n    assert_eq!(encoded, <serde_json::Value as ArtifactPack>::encode_pack(&oracle));\n    let decoded = <protocol::InteractionState as ArtifactPack>::decode_pack(&encoded).unwrap();\n    assert_eq!(decoded, state);\n    assert_eq!(serde_json::Value::from(&<protocol::InteractionState as ToValue>::to_value(&decoded)), oracle);\n}\n\n/// 🪶️ Hex-dumps `pack_rt::encode_wire_value` over the SAME fixture corpus — ground\n/// truth for the container-less wire codec mirror in TS.\n#[semio_framework_async_macros::async_test]\nasync fn pack_wire_value_fixture_corpus_hex_dump() {\n    for (name, value) in pack_value_fixture_corpus().await {\n        let bytes = pack_rt::encode_wire_value(&value);\n        let hex: String = bytes.iter().map(|b| format!(\"{b:02x}\")).collect();\n        println!(\"[pack_wire_value_fixture] {name} ({} bytes) -> {hex}\", bytes.len());\n        let decoded = pack_rt::decode_wire_value(&bytes).expect(\"decode_wire_value\");\n        assert!(dsl_value_variant_exact_eq(&decoded, &value), \"round-trip mismatch for fixture {name}: {decoded:?} != {value:?}\");\n    }\n}\n\n/// 🔢️ Exact-variant law for the dynamic `Shape::Value` grammar over the shared,\n/// language-neutral `semio.pack.dynamic-integer/v1` corpus\n/// (`💻️os/🧫️fixtures/🎒️pack-dynamic-integer-v1`, whose `wireHex` is independently generated\n/// by a third-party LEB128 oracle). Asserts the emitted TAG, the exact `Number` variant, and\n/// byte equality — `DslValue` equality alone cannot witness any of the three, because\n/// `Number::PartialEq` calls `UInt(7)` and `Int(7)` equal while their wire tags differ.\n#[semio_framework_async_macros::async_test]\nasync fn pack_wire_value_preserves_integer_variants_at_u64_i64_boundaries() {\n    let corpus: serde_json::Value = serde_json::from_str(include_str!(\"../../../../🧫️fixtures/🎒️pack-dynamic-integer-v1/🔣️.json\")).expect(\"dynamic integer corpus parses\");\n    assert_eq!(corpus[\"schema\"].as_str(), Some(\"semio.pack.dynamic-integer/v1\"));\n    assert_eq!(corpus[\"version\"].as_u64(), Some(1));\n    let accept = corpus[\"accept\"].as_array().expect(\"accept rows\");\n    assert_eq!(accept.len(), 6, \"the corpus is bounded at six accept rows\");\n\n    for row in accept {\n        let id = row[\"id\"].as_str().expect(\"row id\");\n        let value = dynamic_integer_fixture_value(&row[\"value\"]);\n        let expected = dynamic_integer_fixture_bytes(row[\"wireHex\"].as_str().expect(\"row wireHex\"));\n        let bytes = pack_rt::encode_wire_value(&value);\n        assert_eq!(bytes, expected, \"{id}: encode_wire_value must be byte-exact against the neutral corpus\");\n        let tag = bytes[4];\n        let expected_tag = match row[\"variant\"].as_str() {\n            Some(\"uint\") => 0x04u8,\n            Some(\"int\") => 0x03,\n            Some(\"float\") => 0x05,\n            Some(\"map\") => 0x10,\n            other => panic!(\"{id}: unsupported corpus variant {other:?}\"),\n        };\n        assert_eq!(tag, expected_tag, \"{id}: the dynamic value's leading tag carries the writer's variant\");\n        let decoded = pack_rt::decode_wire_value(&bytes).expect(\"decode_wire_value\");\n        assert!(dsl_value_variant_exact_eq(&decoded, &value), \"{id}: {decoded:?} is not variant-exact against {value:?}\");\n        assert_eq!(pack_rt::encode_wire_value(&decoded), expected, \"{id}: re-encoding the decoded value is canonical and idempotent\");\n    }\n\n    assert!(matches!(pack_rt::decode_wire_value(&dynamic_integer_fixture_bytes(\"000101110403\")).expect(\"uint 3\"), DslValue::Number(crate::os_dsl::Number::UInt(3))));\n    assert!(matches!(pack_rt::decode_wire_value(&pack_rt::encode_wire_value(&DslValue::int(7))).expect(\"int 7\"), DslValue::Number(crate::os_dsl::Number::Int(7))), \"a positive Int keeps TAG_INT rather than collapsing onto TAG_UINT\");\n    assert_ne!(pack_rt::encode_wire_value(&DslValue::int(7)), pack_rt::encode_wire_value(&DslValue::uint(7)), \"Int(7) and UInt(7) are equal under Number::PartialEq but are distinct on the wire\");\n    let beyond_exact_f64 = 9_007_199_254_740_993u64;\n    assert_ne!(beyond_exact_f64 as f64 as u64, beyond_exact_f64, \"the f64 widening this law replaced is not injective past 2^53\");\n\n    for row in corpus[\"reject\"].as_array().expect(\"reject rows\") {\n        let id = row[\"id\"].as_str().expect(\"row id\");\n        let bytes = dynamic_integer_fixture_bytes(row[\"wireHex\"].as_str().expect(\"row wireHex\"));\n        match row[\"outcome\"].as_str() {\n            Some(\"decode-error\") => {\n                assert!(pack_rt::decode_wire_value(&bytes).is_err(), \"{id}: a truncated or overlong varint must fail the reader\");\n            }\n            Some(\"noncanonical\") => {\n                let &dynamic_integer_fixture_value(&row[\"decodes\"])), \"{id}: {decoded:?} is not the documented decode\");\n                assert_ne!(pack_rt::encode_wire_value(&decoded), bytes, \"{id}: a canonical-bytes caller rejects it because encode(decode(bytes)) != bytes\");\n            }\n            other => panic!(\"{id}: unsupported corpus outcome {other:?}\"),\n        }\n    }\n}\n//#endregion 🔖️PackValueFixtures\n\n//#region 🔖️CompositionTests\n\nimpl OpText for ValidatedMutation {\n    fn parse_op(line: &str) -> Result<Self, TextError> {\n        let variants = <Self as crate::os_dsl::DslVariants>::variants();\n        for (keyword, spec_fn) in &variants {\n            let probe = format!(\"{} \", keyword);\n            if line == keyword.as_str() || line.starts_with(&probe) {\n                let record = crate::os_dsl::parse(line, &(spec_fn.ordinary)(), &crate::os_dsl::ParseOptions { limits: semio_framework_diagnostic::Limits::default(), mode: crate::os_dsl::SourceMode::Inline })?;\n                return <Self as crate::os_dsl::DslVariants>::from_named_record(keyword, &record);\n            }\n        }\n        Err(crate::os_dsl::__rt::field_error(format!(\"unknown operation line '{line}'\")))\n    }\n    fn print_op(&self) -> String {\n        let (keyword, record) = <Self as crate::os_dsl::DslVariants>::to_named_record(self);\n        let variants = <Self as crate::os_dsl::DslVariants>::variants();\n        let spec_fn = variants.iter().find(|(k, _)| k == &keyword).map(|(_, s)| *s).expect(\"variant spec must exist for its own keyword\");\n        crate::os_dsl::print(&record, &(spec_fn.ordinary)(), crate::os_dsl::JoinMode::Inline)\n    }\n}\n\nimpl OpBinary for ValidatedMutation {\n    fn encode_op(&self) -> Result<Vec<u8>, crate::os_spr::ProtocolError> {\n        const OP_BINARY_FORMAT: u8 = 1;\n        let (keyword, record) = <Self as crate::os_dsl::DslVariants>::to_named_record(self);\n        let variants = <Self as crate::os_dsl::DslVariants>::variants();\n        let ordinal = variants.iter().position(|(k, _)| *k == keyword).ok_or(crate::os_spr::ProtocolError::Malformed { what: \"op variant\", offset: 0, detail: format!(\"keyword {keyword:?} is not a declared variant\") })?;\n        let spec = (variants[ordinal].1.ordinary)();\n        let body = crate::os_pack::encode_record_body(&spec, &record, &PackEncodeOptions::default()).map_err(crate::os_spr::ProtocolError::from)?;\n        let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(body.len() + 3);\n        out.push(OP_BINARY_FORMAT);\n        crate::os_pack::write_varint_u64(&mut out, ordinal as u64);\n        out.extend_from_slice(&body);\n        Ok(out)\n    }\n    fn decode_op(bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<Self, crate::os_spr::ProtocolError> {\n        const OP_BINARY_FORMAT: u8 = 1;\n        let mut reader = crate::os_pack::ByteReader::new(bytes);\n        let format = reader.read_u8()?;\n        if format != OP_BINARY_FORMAT {\n            return Err(crate::os_spr::ProtocolError::Malformed { what: \"op format\", offset: 0, detail: format!(\"unsupported op format {format}\") });\n        }\n        let ordinal = reader.read_varint_u64()?;\n        let variants = <Self as crate::os_dsl::DslVariants>::variants();\n        let (keyword, spec_fn) = variants.get(ordinal as usize).ok_or(crate::os_spr::ProtocolError::Malformed { what: \"op variant\", offset: 1, detail: format!(\"ordinal {ordinal} out of range for {} declared variants\", variants.len()) })?;\n        let spec = (spec_fn.ordinary)();\n        let body = &bytes[reader.position()..];\n        let (record, _report) = crate::os_pack::decode_record_body(body, &spec, &PackDecodeOptions::default()).map_err(crate::os_spr::ProtocolError::from)?;\n        let record_offset = reader.position() as u64;\n        <Self as crate::os_dsl::DslVariants>::from_named_record(keyword, &record).map_err(|error| crate::os_spr::ProtocolError::Malformed { what: \"op record\", offset: record_offset, detail: error.to_string() })\n    }\n}\n\n/// 🛂️ The composition fixture's negative value is a fatal outcome, so the dry-run\n/// rejects it before group dispatch can alter either member's history.\n\nimpl n: Some(9) }, None);\n    let orphan = vec![crate::os_spr::EditMessages { edit_id: \"edit-that-never-existed\".to_string(), messages: vec![crate::os_spr::MutationMessage::info(\"mutation.cascade\", ledger\"), \"the caller reads the refusal itself: {error:?}\");\n    assert_eq!(store.snapshot_ref().n, Some(3), \"the live store survives a refused reload unchanged\");\n    close_demo_artifact_store(&mut store);\n}\n//#endregion 🔖️RefusedReloadTests\n\n//#region 🔖️ErasedCloseDemandTests\n/// 🧱️ The ERASED close-byte demand a nested driver reads before it grants.\nstruct DemandingBufferRetirement {\n    buffer: Option<Vec<u8>>,\n}\n\nimpl ErasedSnapshotRetirement for DemandingBufferRetirement {\n    fn close_step(&mut self, maximum_items: usize, maximum_bytes: usize) -> Result<SnapshotRetirementStep, semio_framework_value::ValueError> {\n        let Some(buffer) = self.buffer.as_ref() else { return Ok(SnapshotRetirementStep::Complete) };\n        if maximum_items == 0 || maximum_bytes < buffer.capacity() {\n            return Ok(SnapshotRetirementStep::Blocked);\n        }\n        let released = self.buffer.take().expect(\"the physical owner is present\").capacity();\n        Ok(SnapshotRetirementStep::Pending { released_items: 1, released_bytes: released })\n    }\n\n    fn terminal_is_empty(&self) -> bool {\n        self.buffer.is_none()\n    }\n\n    fn next_close_byte_demand(&self) -> usize {\n        self.buffer.as_ref().map_or(0, Vec::capacity)\n    }\n}\n\n/// 🧱️ A driver that owns nothing but a `Box<dyn ErasedSnapshotRetirement>` and its own allocation\n/// admission — the shape `CopyCursor` and every other nested close ladder has.\nstruct NestedErasedDriver {\n    inner: Box<dyn ErasedSnapshotRetirement>,\n    allocation_admission: usize,\n}\n\nimpl NestedErasedDriver {\n    fn close(&mut self, payload_grant: usize) -> Result<SnapshotRetirementStep, semio_framework_value::ValueError> {\n        let demand = self.inner.next_close_byte_demand();\n        let paid = if demand > payload_grant { demand.min(self.allocation_admission) } else { payload_grant };\n        self.allocation_admission = self.allocation_admission.saturating_sub(paid.saturating_sub(payload_grant));\n        self.inner.close_step(1, paid)\n    }\n}\n\nstruct DefaultedDemandRetirement(bool);\n\nimpl ErasedSnapshotRetirement for DefaultedDemandRetirement {\n    fn close_step(&mut self, _maximum_items: usize, _maximum_bytes: usize) -> Result<SnapshotRetirementStep, semio_framework_value::ValueError> {\n        self.0 = true;\n        Ok(SnapshotRetirementStep::Complete)\n    }\n\n    fn terminal_is_empty(&self) -> bool {\n        self.0\n    }\n}\n\n/// ⚖️ LAW: a retirement that owes a physical allocation publishes the SMALLEST grant its next step\n/// can spend, through the erased trait, and a nested driver that reads it pays that demand out of\n/// its OWN allocation admission instead of spinning `Blocked` on the caller's payload page.\n///\n/// 🐛️ Without the erased demand, a `Box<dyn ErasedSnapshotRetirement>` holder had exactly two\n/// answers to choose between and no way to tell them apart: `Blocked` because the inner owner is\n/// waiting on someone else, and `Blocked` because the driver under-granted it. A heap allocation\n/// cannot be freed in pieces, so a cursor driving at a 1-byte payload granule could neither grant\n/// enough nor report truthfully — measured 2026-09-22 as the four `CopyCursor` laws of\n/// `semio-framework-artifact-flow-flow`'s `retained::*` suite, each spinning on\n/// `positive copy close grant blocked` (`📓️fp10-plugin-lib-and-lanes.md` §3).\n#[semio_framework_async_macros::async_test]\nasync fn an_erased_retirement_publishes_its_physical_close_demand_and_a_nested_driver_pays_it() {\n    let defaulted = DefaultedDemandRetirement(false);\n    assert_eq!(defaulted.next_close_byte_demand(), 1, \"a retirement that releases owners rather than buffers costs no bytes, and the default says exactly that\");\n\n    let mut buffer = Vec::with_capacity(8_192);\n    buffer.resize(8_192, 0u8);\n    let capacity = buffer.capacity();\n    let mut nested = NestedErasedDriver { inner: Box::new(DemandingBufferRetirement { buffer: Some(buffer) }), allocation_admission: 16_384 };\n    assert_eq!(nested.inner.next_close_byte_demand(), capacity, \"the physical demand is the whole allocation, published through the ERASED view\");\n\n    let step = nested.close(1).expect(\"a nested driver closes its foreign owner\");\n    assert_eq!(step, SnapshotRetirementStep::Pending { released_items: 1, released_bytes: capacity }, \"one payload byte of grant still frees the whole allocation, paid from the driver's own admission\");\n    assert_eq!(nested.allocation_admission, 16_384 - (capacity - 1), \"the demand is charged to the DRIVER's allocation admission, never to the caller's payload page\");\n    assert!(nested.inner.terminal_is_empty());\n    assert_eq!(nested.close(1).expect(\"a terminal owner still answers\"), SnapshotRetirementStep::Complete);\n    assert_eq!(nested.inner.next_close_byte_demand(), 0, \"a terminal owner owes no further physical grant\");\n}\n//#endregion 🔖️ErasedCloseDemandTests\n\n/// 🪪️ Fixture law `🧫️fixtures/🪪️replica-edit-identity.json`: fresh replicas that author identical\n/// gestures never share an edit or envelope_field_registry_capacity_and_contention_return_the_exact_decoder_before_adoption() {\n    let registry = ArtifactEnvelopeFieldDecoderRegistry::<(), ()>::new();\n    let mut leases = reissued.\n#[test]\nfn snapshot_read_double_return_is_counted_once_and_reclaimed_once() {\n    let registry = Arc::new(SnapshotReadLeaseRegistry::new());\n    let aliased_root = Arc::new(11u32);\n returned twice on the aliased path\");\n    assert_eq!(registry.returned.load(std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Acquire), 0, \"an aliased root is reclaimed on the returning thread, not charged to the pump\");\n    assert_eq!(Arc::strong_count(&aliased_root), 1, \"the aliased slot released its own owner alias in the same call\");\n    assert!(registry.try_take_one_returned::<u32>().expect(\"one the pump path\");\n    assert_eq!(registry.returned.load(std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Acquire), 1);\n    let mut reclaimed = None;\n    for _ in 0..SNAPSHOT_READ_LEASE_CAPACITY {\n        if let stale_snapshot_read_generation_cannot_aba_remove_a_reused_slot() {\n    let registry = Arc::new(SnapshotReadLeaseRegistry::new());\n    let owner = Arc::new(1u16);\n    let first = }), HybridLogicalTimestamp::new(2, 200), Vec::new());\n    (delete, modify)\n}\n\n#[semio_framework_async_macros::async_test]\nasync fn modify_vs_delete_quarantines_under_normal_and_vigilant() {\n assert_eq!(store.applied_edit_ids(), pre_merge_ids.as_slice(), \"{policy:?}: applied_edit_ids stays pre-merge on reject\");\n        let conflict_id = report.conflict.clone().expect(\"a reject must crate::os_spr::ConflictStatus::Open);\n        assert!(matches!(conflict.kind, crate::os_spr::ConflictKind::Quarantined { .. }), \"{policy:?}: a rejected batch quarantines, it never degrades\");\n assert_eq!(store.open_conflicts().count(), cap, \"fixture must actually be at capacity for this test to be meaningful\");\n\n    let before_edits = store.envelope().vcs.edits.len();\n    let before_snapshot = store.snapshot().expect(\"pre-attempt snapshot\");\n    let before_ids = store.applied_edit_ids().to_vec();\n\n    let error = store.ingest_remote(modify).await.expect_err(\"minting one more Open conflict past the cap must be a loud, typed refusal\");\n    assert!(matches!(&error, VcsError::ValidationFailed(message) if message.contains(\"capacity\")), \"got {error:?}\");\n    assert_eq!(store.envelope().vcs.edits.len(), before_edits, \"a refused mint must be fully atomic — nothing about the attempted batch applied\");\n    assert_eq!(store.snapshot().expect(\"snapshot\"), before_snapshot);\n    assert_eq!(store.applied_edit_ids(), before_ids.as_slice());\n    assert_eq!(store.open_conflicts().count(), cap, \"the backlog must stay exactly at capacity, never silently grow past it\");\n}\n\n/// ✂️ MEDIUM-3: resolved (`Accepted`/`Discarded`) conflicts are closed historical facts, so\n/// unlike `Open` ones they are prunable — oldest push order evicted first, capped, while an\n/// `Open` conflict is never touched no matter how far over cap the resolved backlog grows.\n#[semio_framework_async_macros::async_test]\nasync fn resolved_conflicts_are_pruned_oldest_first_once_the_ledger_exceeds_its_cap_while_open_ones_survive() {\n    let mut store = fresh_demo_store().await;\n    let cap = super::ArtifactStore::<DemoSnapshot, DemoMutation>::RESOLVED_CONFLICT_CAP;\n    let open = synthetic_open_conflict(u64::MAX).await;\n    store.0.envelope.conflicts.push(open.clone());\n    let overflow: u64 = 20;\n    let resolved_count = cap as u64 + overflow;\n    for seed in 0..resolved_count {\n        let mut resolved = synthetic_open_conflict(seed).await;\n        resolved.status = crate::os_spr::ConflictStatus::Accepted;\n        store.0.envelope.conflicts.push(resolved);\n    }\n    assert_eq!(store.conflicts().len(), resolved_count as usize + 1);\n\n    store.0.prune_resolved_conflicts().expect(\"bounded resolved-conflict retirement\");\n\n    assert_eq!(store.conflicts().len(), cap, \"pruning must bring the ledger back down to the cap\");\n    assert!(store.conflicts().iter().any(|conflict| conflict.id == open.id && conflict.status == crate::os_spr::ConflictStatus::Open), \"the Open conflict must never be evicted, no matter how far over cap the resolved backlog grows\");\n    let surviving_seeds: HashSet<u64> = store.conflicts().iter().filter(|conflict| conflict.status == crate::os_spr::ConflictStatus::Accepted).map(|conflict| conflict.timestamp.physical_ms).collect();\n    assert_eq!(surviving_seeds.len(), cap - 1);\n    for evicted_seed in 0..=overflow {\n        assert!(!surviving_seeds.contains(&evicted_seed), \"seed {evicted_seed} was among the oldest resolved conflicts and must be pruned first\");\n    }\n    assert!(surviving_seeds.contains(&(resolved_count - 1)), \"the newest resolved conflict must survive pruning\");\n}\n\n/// 🧼️ MEDIUM-4: one `ingest_remote` batch that quarantines BOTH a brand-new edit (`op-c`, never\n/// committed before) AND a previously-committed edit a rewind now retroactively invalidates\n/// (`op-a`, which carried a REAL non-empty `mutation.cascade` message from its first commit)\n/// — proving `replace_edit_messages(.., empty)` clears the stale ledger entry correctly even\n/// when it runs in the same pass as a never-populated one, regardless of which kind an id is.\n///\n/// `op-b` (earlier HLC than `op-a`) forces a rewind that replays `op-a` against a DELETED\n/// target the second time around. `op-c` (later HLC, brand new) is submitted FIRST but\n/// depends on `op-b`, so it buffers in the dag and is released alongside `op-b` in the SAME\n/// `ingest_remote` call/batch — the mixed-kind scenario MEDIUM-4 asks for.\n#[semio_framework_async_macros::async_test]\nasync fn quarantine_message_clearing_is_correct_for_a_mixed_new_and_retroactive_batch() {\n    let mut store = fresh_demo_store().await;\n    store.set_merge_policy(crate::os_spr::MergePolicy::Normal);\n\n    let a = mutation_envelope_at(\"actor-a\", \"op-a\", DemoMutation::AddN(AddN { delta: 5 }), HybridLogicalTimestamp::new(1, 100), Vec::new());\n    store.ingest_remote(a).await.expect(\"op-a commits cleanly the first time, on a fresh n=0 target\");\n    assert!(!store.messages_for_edit(\"op-a\").is_empty(), \"fixture must carry real prior ledger content for this test to be meaningful\");\n    assert_eq!(store.snapshot().expect(\"snapshot\"), DemoSnapshot { n: Some(5) });\n\n    let b = mutation_envelope_at(\"actor-b\", \"op-b\", DemoMutation::DeleteN(DeleteN {}), HybridLogicalTimestamp::new(1, 50), Vec::new());\n    let c = mutation_envelope_at(\"actor-c\", \"op-c\", DemoMutation::AddN(AddN { delta: 1 }), HybridLogicalTimestamp::new(2, 150), vec![MutationId(\"op-b\".into())]);\n    store.ingest_remote(c).await.expect(\"op-c buffers behind its unmet dependency on op-b\");\n    let report = store.ingest_remote(b).await.expect(\"op-b's arrival releases op-b and op-c into the same batch\");\n\n    assert!(!report.accepted, \"op-c never committed\");\n    assert_eq!(store.applied_edit_ids(), &[\"op-b\".to_string()], \"only op-b committed — op-a dropped out on retroactive invalidation, op-c never entered\");\n    assert_eq!(store.snapshot().expect(\"snapshot\"), DemoSnapshot { n: None });\n\n    assert!(store.messages_for_edit(\"op-a\").is_empty(), \"op-a's stale non-empty ledger entry must be cleared, not left stale, once it is retroactively quarantined\");\n    assert!(store.messages_for_edit(\"op-c\").is_empty(), \"op-c never committed, so it must never gain a ledger entry\");\n    assert!(store.envelope().edit_messages.iter().all(|entry| entry.edit_id != \"op-a\"), \"a cleared entry must be fully removed from the durable ledger, not left behind as an empty Vec\");\n    assert!(store.envelope().edit_messages.iter().all(|entry| entry.edit_id != \"op-c\"), \"op-c must never appear in the durable ledger at all\");\n\n    let conflict_id = report.conflict.expect(\"the mixed quarantine batch must raise one conflict\");\n    let conflict = store.conflicts().iter().find(|conflict| conflict.id == conflict_id).expect(\"conflict recorded on the store\");\n    assert_eq!(conflict.status, crate::os_spr::ConflictStatus::Open);\n    match &conflict.kind {\n        crate::os_spr::ConflictKind::Quarantined { envelopes } => assert_eq!(envelopes.len(), 2, \"both op-a (retroactive) and op-c (new) must be quarantined TOGETHER in one conflict\"),\n        other => panic!(\"expected a Quarantined conflict, got {other:?}\"),\n    }\n    assert_eq!(store.conflicts().len(), 1, \"op-a's clean first commit never raised a conflict of its own — only this one mixed-batch conflict must exist\");\n}\n//#endregion 🔖️RobustnessTests\n\n#[semio_framework_async_macros::async_test]\nasync fn }).await.expect(\"apply\");\n    store.dispatch(ArtifactCommand::CommitCheckpoint { message: Some(\"checkpoint\".into()), authors: Vec::new() }).await.expect(\"checkpoint\");\n    let 🔖️HistoryLaneTests\n#[semio_framework_async_macros::async_test]\nasync fn history_lane_defaults_to_document() {\n    assert_eq!(HistoryLane::default(), HistoryLane::Document);\n}\n\n/// 🛤️ The design's headline acceptance case: undoing after an interleaved run of\n/// document/interaction edits reverts the last DOCUMENT edit, skipping past trailing (and even\n/// mid-history) `Interaction`-lane entries in both directions, which stay applied throughout.\n///\n/// Default undo skips the TRAILING interaction2 edit to revert doc2 instead.\n///\n/// A second default undo reverts doc1 — the only remaining Document-lane entry — even though\n/// it now sits BEFORE two still-applied interaction edits in `applied_edit_ids`.\n///\n/// Default redo mirrors it: restores doc1 first (nearest Document entry in the redo stack),\n/// then doc2, never touching either interaction edit's own applied/redo membership; each lands\n/// back at its own HLC position in the applied order.\n#[semio_framework_async_macros::async_test]\nasync fn history_lane_default_undo_and_redo_skip_interaction_entries() {\n    let envelope = create_document_envelope(\"demo/v1\", \"demo\", DemoSnapshot { n: Some(0) }, None);\n    let mut store = ArtifactStore::new(envelope).await;\n    store.dispatch(ArtifactCommand::Apply { mutations: vec![DemoMutation::SetN(SetN { n: 1 })], description: None, transaction: None }).await.expect(\"apply doc1\");\n    let doc1_id = store.applied_edit_ids()[0].clone();\n    store.dispatch(ArtifactCommand::ApplyInLane { mutations: vec![DemoMutation::SetN(SetN { n: 100 })], description: None, lane: HistoryLane::Interaction, transaction: None }).await.expect(\"apply interaction1\");\n    let interaction1_id = store.applied_edit_ids()[1].clone();\n    store.dispatch(ArtifactCommand::Apply { mutations: vec![DemoMutation::SetN(SetN { n: 2 })], description: None, transaction: None }).await.expect(\"apply doc2\");\n    let doc2_id = store.applied_edit_ids()[2].clone();\n    store.dispatch(ArtifactCommand::ApplyInLane { mutations: vec![DemoMutation::SetN(SetN { n: 200 })], description: None, lane: HistoryLane::Interaction, transaction: None }).await.expect(\"apply interaction2\");\n    let interaction2_id = store.applied_edit_ids()[3].clone();\n\n    assert_eq!(store.envelope().lanes.get(&interaction1_id), Some(&HistoryLane::Interaction));\n    assert_eq!(store.envelope().lanes.get(&interaction2_id), Some(&HistoryLane::Interaction));\n    assert!(store.envelope().lanes.get(&doc1_id).is_none(), \"an ordinary Document-lane edit never gets a `lanes` entry (sparse ledger)\");\n    assert!(store.envelope().lanes.get(&doc2_id).is_none());\n\n    store.dispatch(ArtifactCommand::Undo).await.expect(\"undo skips interaction2 to revert doc2\");\n    assert_eq!(store.applied_edit_ids(), &[doc1_id.clone(), interaction1_id.clone(), interaction2_id.clone()], \"doc2 removed; both interaction edits remain applied\");\n    assert_eq!(store.redo_edit_ids(), std::slice::from_ref(&doc2_id));\n\n    store.dispatch(ArtifactCommand::Undo).await.expect(\"undo doc1 despite interaction edits between it and the tail\");\n    assert_eq!(store.applied_edit_ids(), &[interaction1_id.clone(), interaction2_id.clone()]);\n    assert_eq!(store.redo_edit_ids(), &[doc2_id.clone(), doc1_id.clone()]);\n\n    store.dispatch(ArtifactCommand::Redo).await.expect(\"redo doc1\");\n    assert_eq!(store.applied_edit_ids(), &[doc1_id.clone(), interaction1_id.clone(), interaction2_id.clone()]);\n    assert_eq!(store.redo_edit_ids(), std::slice::from_ref(&doc2_id));\n    store.dispatch(ArtifactCommand::Redo).await.expect(\"redo doc2\");\n    assert_eq!(store.applied_edit_ids(), &[doc1_id.clone(), interaction1_id.clone(), doc2_id.clone(), interaction2_id.clone()]);\n    assert!(store.redo_edit_ids().is_empty());\n}\n\n/// 🛤️ The completing half of the mechanism: `UndoInLane`/`RedoInLane` walk a NON-`Document`\n/// lane explicitly and independently of the document lane's own cursor position.\n///\n/// Explicit lane-scoped undo reverts ONLY the interaction edit, leaving the document edit\n/// applied — the mirror image of default `Undo` skipping it.\n///\n/// Redoing the Document lane from here has nothing to redo — only the Interaction lane's\n/// cursor moved, proving the two lanes' redo stacks are independent, not one shared position.\n#[semio_framework_async_macros::async_test]\nasync fn history_lane_undo_in_lane_and_redo_in_lane_walk_only_the_requested_lane() {\n    let envelope = create_document_envelope(\"demo/v1\", \"demo\", DemoSnapshot { n: Some(0) }, None);\n    let mut store = ArtifactStore::new(envelope).await;\n    store.dispatch(ArtifactCommand::Apply { mutations: vec![DemoMutation::SetN(SetN { n: 1 })], description: None, transaction: None }).await.expect(\"apply doc\");\n    store.dispatch(ArtifactCommand::ApplyInLane { mutations: vec![DemoMutation::SetN(SetN { n: 99 })], description: None, lane: HistoryLane::Interaction, transaction: None }).await.expect(\"apply interaction\");\n    let doc_id = store.applied_edit_ids()[0].clone();\n    let interaction_id = store.applied_edit_ids()[1].clone();\n\n    store.dispatch(ArtifactCommand::UndoInLane { lane: HistoryLane::Interaction }).await.expect(\"undo in interaction lane\");\n    assert_eq!(store.applied_edit_ids(), std::slice::from_ref(&doc_id));\n    assert_eq!(store.redo_edit_ids(), std::slice::from_ref(&interaction_id));\n    assert_eq!(store.snapshot().expect(\"snapshot\").n, Some(1), \"reverting the interaction edit restores the document edit's own value\");\n\n    assert_eq!(store.dispatch(ArtifactCommand::RedoInLane { lane: HistoryLane::Document }).await.unwrap_err(), VcsError::NothingToRedo);\n\n    store.dispatch(ArtifactCommand::RedoInLane { lane: HistoryLane::Interaction }).await.expect(\"redo in interaction lane\");\n    assert_eq!(store.applied_edit_ids(), &[doc_id.clone(), interaction_id.clone()]);\n    assert!(store.redo_edit_ids().is_empty());\n}\n\n/// 🛤️ Acceptance: a history made ENTIRELY of store.dispatch(ArtifactCommand::ApplyInLane { mutations: vec![DemoMutation::SetN(SetN { n: 2 })], description: None, lane: HistoryLane::Interaction, transaction: None }).await.expect(\"apply interaction2\");\n    assert_eq!(store.applied_edit_ids().len(), 2);\n\n    let error = store.dispatch(ArtifactCommand::Undo).await.unwrap_err();\n    assert_eq!(error, VcsError::NothingToUndo, \"no store.dispatch(ArtifactCommand::UndoInLane { lane: HistoryLane::Interaction }).await.expect(\"undo in interaction lane\");\n    assert_eq!(store.applied_edit_ids().len(), 1);\n    assert_eq!(store.snapshot().expect(\"snapshot\").n, Some(1));\n}\n\n/// 🛤️ `Interaction`-lane entries are ordinary persisted `Edit`s — they survive a plain\n/// owned pack+SPR round trip, and a }\n}\n\n/// 🧭️ One resolution per schema, in the hub's trusted-catalog order: the linked Rust codec whenever\n/// this binary links one — a mounted component owning the same kind never displaces it — register_component_document_codec(Arc::new(EchoComponentCodec { schema: \"test.kind-codec-component/v1\" })).expect(\"component codec registers\");\n\n    let resolved = document_kind_codec(\"test.kind-codec-component/v1\").await.expect(\"registry\").expect(\"component kind resolves\");\n    assert!(matches!(resolved, DocumentKindCodec::Component(_)));\n    assert_eq!(resolved.pack_schema_hash().await.expect(\"component identity\"), [9; 32]);\n    assert_eq!(resolved.print_mirror(&[1, 2, 3], &[4]).await.expect(\"component mirror\"), ArtifactTextFiles { (keyword, record) = <Self as crate::os_dsl::DslVariants>::to_named_record(self);\n        let variants = <Self as crate::os_dsl::DslVariants>::variants();\n        let ordinal = variants.iter().position(|(k, _)| *k == keyword).ok_or(crate::os_spr::ProtocolError::Malformed { what: \"op variant\", offset: 0, detail: format!(\"keyword {keyword:?} is not a declared variant\") spec = (spec_fn.ordinary)();\n        let body = &bytes[reader.position()..];\n        let (record, _report) = crate::os_pack::decode_record_body(body, &spec, crate::os_dsl::DslVariants>::from_named_record(keyword, &record).map_err(|error| crate::os_spr::ProtocolError::Malformed { what: \"op record\", offset: record_offset, detail: error.to_string() })\n pack_value_fixture_corpus() -> Vec<(&'static str, DslValue)> {\n    vec![\n        (\"null\", DslValue::Null),\n        (\"bool_true\", DslValue::Bool(true)),\n        (\"bool_false\", DslValue::Bool(false)),\n        (\"int_zero\", DslValue::uint(0)),\n        (\"int_negative_one\", DslValue::int(-1)),\n        (\"float_pi\", DslValue::float(3.14)),\n        (\"float_whole_number\", DslValue::float(2.0)),\n        (\"string_empty\", DslValue::String(String::new())),\n        (\"string_escapes\", DslValue::String(\"hello\\nworld with \\\"quotes\\\"\".into())),\n        (\"array_empty\", DslValue::Array(vec![])),\n        (\"array_ints\", DslValue::Array(vec![DslValue::uint(1), DslValue::uint(2), DslValue::uint(3)])),\n        (\"object_empty\", DslValue::Object(vec![])),\n        (\"object_mixed\", DslValue::object([(\"a\".into(), DslValue::uint(1)), (\"b\".into(), DslValue::Array(vec![DslValue::Bool(true), DslValue::Null]))])),\n        (\n            \"nested_deep\",\n            DslValue::object([(\"a\".into(), DslValue::object([(\"b\".into(), DslValue::object([(\"c\".into(), DslValue::Array(vec![DslValue::uint(1), DslValue::uint(2), DslValue::object([(\"d\".into(), DslValue::String(\"leaf\".into()))])]))]))]))]),\n        ),\n    ]\n}\n\n/// 🎯️ Variant-exact `DslValue` equality. `Number`'s own `PartialEq` calls a fitting\n/// `UInt`/`Int` pair equal, so it cannot witness that the wire preserved the WRITER's variant —\n/// which is exactly what `TAG_UINT` versus `TAG_INT` decides, and what the canonical bytes and\n/// every hash over them depend on. `Float` compares by bits so `-0.0` and `NaN` are exact too.\n// 🚫️async: E1 pure recursive comparison consumed inside sync `.all()`/`.is_some_and()` closures\n// that cannot themselves be async — see R9/R10 residue shape 1\nfn dsl_value_variant_exact_eq(a: &DslValue, b: &DslValue) -> bool {\n    match (a, b) {\n        (DslValue::Number(crate::os_dsl::Number::UInt(x)), DslValue::Number(crate::os_dsl::Number::UInt(y))) => x == y,\n        (DslValue::Number(crate::os_dsl::Number::Int(x)), DslValue::Number(crate::os_dsl::Number::Int(y))) => x == y,\n        (DslValue::Number(crate::os_dsl::Number::Float(x)), DslValue::Number(crate::os_dsl::Number::Float(y))) => x.to_bits() == y.to_bits(),\n        (DslValue::Number(_), DslValue::Number(_)) => false,\n        (DslValue::Array(x), DslValue::Array(y)) => x.len() == y.len() && x.iter().zip(y).all(|(a, b)| dsl_value_variant_exact_eq(a, b)),\n        (DslValue::Object(x), DslValue::Object(y)) => x.len() == y.len() && x.iter().all(|(k, v)| y.iter().find(|(ok, _)| ok == k).is_some_and(|(_, ov)| dsl_value_variant_exact_eq(v, ov))),\n        _ => a == b,\n    }\n}\n\n/// 🔣️ Reads one `semio.pack.dynamic-integer/v1` value node — integers arrive as exact\n/// decimal STRINGS and floats as little-endian hex, so no fixture number ever passes through a\n/// JSON `f64` on its way into the corpus.\n// 🚫️async: E1 pure recursive fixture reader consumed inside sync iterator closures — see R9\nfn dynamic_integer_fixture_value(node: &serde_json::Value) -> DslValue {\n    if let Some(text) = node.get(\"uint\").and_then(|v| v.as_str()) {\n        return DslValue::uint(text.parse::<u64>().expect(\"corpus uint is an exact u64\"));\n    }\n    if let Some(text) = node.get(\"int\").and_then(|v| v.as_str()) {\n        return DslValue::int(text.parse::<i64>().expect(\"corpus int is an exact i64\"));\n    }\n    if let Some(text) = node.get(\"f64LeHex\").and_then(|v| v.as_str()) {\n        let mut bits = [0u8; 8];\n        for (index, byte) in bits.iter_mut().enumerate() {\n            *byte = u8::from_str_radix(&text[index * 2..index * 2 + 2], 16).expect(\"corpus f64LeHex byte\");\n        }\n        return DslValue::Number(crate::os_dsl::Number::Float(f64::from_le_bytes(bits)));\n    }\n    if let Some(items) = node.get(\"list\").and_then(|v| v.as_array()) {\n        return DslValue::Array(items.iter().map(dynamic_integer_fixture_value).collect());\n    }\n    if let Some(entries) = node.get(\"map\").and_then(|v| v.as_array()) {\n        return DslValue::Object(entries.iter().map(|entry| (entry[0].as_str().expect(\"corpus map key\").to_string(), dynamic_integer_fixture_value(&entry[1]))).collect());\n    }\n    panic!(\"unsupported corpus value node {node}\");\n}\n\n// 🚫️async: E1 pure hex reader consumed inside sync iterator closures — see R9\nfn dynamic_integer_fixture_bytes(hex: &str) -> Vec<u8> {\n    (0..hex.len() / 2).map(|index| u8::from_str_radix(&hex[index * 2..index * 2 + 2], 16).expect(\"corpus wireHex byte\")).collect()\n}\n\n/// 🧾️ Hex-dumps `pack_rt::encode_pack_value` over a representative `DslValue`\n/// corpus — ground truth for `HEADLESS-APP-ENGINE-BINARY-COMMAND-PROTOCOL-FOUNDATIONS`'s TS\n/// `PackValueCodec` mirror (`framework/product/os/ts/index.ts`). Run with `--nocapture` to\n/// capture the printed `name -> hex` lines; also asserts `decode_pack_value(encode_pack_value(v))\n/// == v` for every entry so the corpus is never accidentally out of date with the real codec.\n#[semio_framework_async_macros::async_test]\nasync fn pack_value_fixture_corpus_hex_dump() {\n    for (name, value) in pack_value_fixture_corpus().await {\n        let bytes = pack_rt::encode_pack_value(&value);\n        let hex: String = bytes.iter().map(|b| format!(\"{b:02x}\")).collect();\n        println!(\"[pack_value_fixture] {name} ({} bytes) -> {hex}\", bytes.len());\n        let decoded = pack_rt::decode_pack_value(&bytes).expect(\"decode_pack_value\");\n        assert!(dsl_value_variant_exact_eq(&decoded, &value), \"round-trip mismatch for fixture {name}: {decoded:?} != {value:?}\");\n    }\n}\n\n#[semio_framework_async_macros::async_test]\nasync fn interaction_state_pack_matches_first_party_value_and_json_oracle() {\n    let oracle: Some(\"semio.pack.dynamic-integer/v1\"));\n    assert_eq!(corpus[\"version\"].as_u64(), Some(1));\n    let accept = corpus[\"accept\"].as_array().expect(\"accept rows\");\n    assert_eq!(accept.len(), }\n}\n//#endregion 🔖️PackValueFixtures\n\n//#region 🔖️CompositionTests\n\nimpl OpText for ValidatedMutation {\n    fn parse_op(line: &str) -> Result<Self, TextError> {\n        let variants = <Self as DemandingBufferRetirement {\n    buffer: Option<Vec<u8>>,\n}\n\nimpl ErasedSnapshotRetirement for DemandingBufferRetirement {\n    fn close_step(&mut self, maximum_items: usize, maximum_bytes: usize) -> Result<SnapshotRetirementStep, semio_framework_value::ValueError> {\n        let Some(buffer) = self.buffer.as_ref() else { return Ok(SnapshotRetirementStep::Complete) };\n        if maximum_items == 0 || maximum_bytes < buffer.capacity() {\n            return Ok(SnapshotRetirementStep::Blocked);\n        }\n        let released = self.buffer.take().expect(\"the physical owner is present\").capacity();\n        Ok(SnapshotRetirementStep::Pending { released_items: 1, released_bytes: released })\n    }\n\n    fn terminal_is_empty(&self) -> bool {\n        self.buffer.is_none()\n    }\n\n    fn next_close_byte_demand(&self) -> usize {\n        self.buffer.as_ref().map_or(0, Vec::capacity)\n    }\n}\n\n/// 🧱️ A driver that owns nothing but a `Box<dyn ErasedSnapshotRetirement>` and its own allocation\n/// admission — the shape `CopyCursor` and every other nested close ladder has.\nstruct NestedErasedDriver {\n    inner: Box<dyn ErasedSnapshotRetirement>,\n    allocation_admission: usize,\n}\n\nimpl NestedErasedDriver {\n    fn close(&mut self, payload_grant: usize) -> Result<SnapshotRetirementStep, semio_framework_value::ValueError> {\n        let demand = self.inner.next_close_byte_demand();\n        let paid = if demand > payload_grant { demand.min(self.allocation_admission) } else { payload_grant };\n        self.allocation_admission = self.allocation_admission.saturating_sub(paid.saturating_sub(payload_grant));\n        self.inner.close_step(1, paid)\n    }\n}\n\nstruct DefaultedDemandRetirement(bool);\n\nimpl ErasedSnapshotRetirement for DefaultedDemandRetirement {\n    fn close_step(&mut self, _maximum_items: usize, _maximum_bytes: usize) -> Result<SnapshotRetirementStep, semio_framework_value::ValueError> {\n        self.0 = true;\n        Ok(SnapshotRetirementStep::Complete)\n    }\n\n    fn terminal_is_empty(&self) -> bool {\n        self.0\n    }\n}\n\n/// ⚖️ LAW: a retirement that owes a physical allocation publishes the SMALLEST grant its next step\n/// can spend, through the erased trait, and a nested driver that reads it pays that demand out of\n/// its OWN allocation admission instead of spinning `Blocked` on the caller's payload page.\n///\n/// 🐛️ Without the erased demand, a `Box<dyn ErasedSnapshotRetirement>` holder had exactly two\n/// answers to choose between and no way to tell them apart: `Blocked` because the inner owner is\n/// waiting on someone else, and `Blocked` because the driver under-granted it. A heap allocation\n/// cannot be freed in pieces, so a cursor driving at a 1-byte payload granule could neither grant\n/// enough nor report truthfully — measured 2026-09-22 as the four `CopyCursor` laws of\n/// `semio-framework-artifact-flow-flow`'s `retained::*` suite, each spinning on\n/// `positive copy close grant blocked` (`📓️fp10-plugin-lib-and-lanes.md` §3).\n#[semio_framework_async_macros::async_test]\nasync fn an_erased_retirement_publishes_its_physical_close_demand_and_a_nested_driver_pays_it() {\n    let defaulted = DefaultedDemandRetirement(false);\n    assert_eq!(defaulted.next_close_byte_demand(), 1, \"a retirement that releases owners rather than buffers costs no bytes, and the default says exactly that\");\n\n    let mut buffer = Vec::with_capacity(8_192);\n    buffer.resize(8_192, 0u8);\n    let capacity = buffer.capacity();\n    let mut nested = NestedErasedDriver { inner: Box::new(DemandingBufferRetirement { buffer: Some(buffer) }), allocation_admission: 16_384 };\n    assert_eq!(nested.inner.next_close_byte_demand(), capacity, \"the physical demand is the whole allocation, published through the ERASED view\");\n\n    let step = nested.close(1).expect(\"a nested driver closes its foreign owner\");\n    assert_eq!(step, SnapshotRetirementStep::Pending { released_items: 1, released_bytes: capacity }, \"one payload byte of grant still frees the whole allocation, paid from the driver's own admission\");\n    assert_eq!(nested.allocation_admission, 16_384 - (capacity - 1), \"the demand is charged to the DRIVER's allocation admission, never to the caller's payload page\");\n    assert!(nested.inner.terminal_is_empty());\n    assert_eq!(nested.close(1).expect(\"a terminal owner still answers\"), SnapshotRetirementStep::Complete);\n    assert_eq!(nested.inner.next_close_byte_demand(), 0, \"a terminal owner owes no further physical grant\");\n}\n//#endregion 🔖️ErasedCloseDemandTests\n\n/// 🪪️ Fixture law `🧫️fixtures/🪪️replica-edit-identity.json`: fresh replicas that author identical\n/// gestures never share an edit or }).await.expect(\"author edit\");\n    author.dispatch(ArtifactCommand::Undo).await.expect(\"author undo\");\n    let events = author.event_log().expect(\"author event log\");\n    let mut replica = fresh_demo_store().await;\n    for event in events.clone() {\n        replica.ingest_remote(event).await.expect(\"replica ingests the author's events\");\n    }\n    assert_eq!(replica.snapshot().expect(\"replica snapshot\"), DemoSnapshot { n: Some(0) }, \"the replicated revert withdraws the edit\");\n    let before = owned_test_envelope(&replica).await;\n    let crate::os_spr::history_transition_from_envelope(&forged).expect(\"decode\").expect(\"a transition\") else { panic!(\"the last event is the revert\") };\n    forged.diff.payload = crate::os_spr::encode_history_transition(&crate::os_spr::HistoryTransition::Reinstate { mutation_ids });\n    let error = replica.ingest_remote(forged).await.expect_err(\"a known transition id may not carry another payload\");\n    assert!(matches!(error, VcsError::ValidationFailed(message) if message.contains(\"conflicts with its established payload\")));\n    assert_eq!(replica.envelope(), }).await.expect(\"a's own checkpoint\");\n    for event in a.event_log().expect(\"a's log\") {\n        b.ingest_remote(event).await.expect(\"b ingests a's checkpoint transition\");\n    }\n    for assert_eq!(store.envelope().vcs.checkpoints.len(), 2, \"both checkpoints are facts on every replica\");\n        for change in &store.envelope().vcs.changes {\n            for edit_id in HLC order is current on both replicas\");\n}\n\n//#region 🔖️MergePolicyTests\n// 🎯️ `26/08/16/MUTATION-OUTCOMES-MERGE-POLICIES-AND-FIRST-CLASS-CONFLICTS` §C6 acceptance —\n// two-peer
